etymology.text: From Middle English schewen, from Old English scēawian (“to look, look at, exhibit, display”), from Proto-West Germanic *skauwōn, from Proto-Germanic *skawwōną (“to look, see”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewh₁- (“to heed, look, feel, take note of”); see haw, gaum, caveat, caution.

senses.definition: To determine the number, amount, or value of [something].
To notice, discern. (Roughly, "can tell" means "know" but with a sense of direct perception.)
To reveal information in prose through outright expository statement — contrasted with show.
To have an effect, especially a noticeable one; to be apparent, to be demonstrated.
(of a fact) To support a certain position.
To pick up on a difference. (See tell apart for more.)
To narrate, to recount.
To convey by speech; to say.
To instruct or inform.
To order; to direct, to say to someone.
To use (beads or similar objects) as an aid to prayer.
To inform someone in authority about a wrongdoing.
To show, be showing, be revealed.
To reveal.

examples.text: Please tell me your phone number.
examples.translation: 請告訴我你的電話號碼。

examples.text: We cannot tell which is better.
examples.translation: 我們無法辨別哪個更好。

examples.text: She wanted him to tell her that he loved her.
examples.translation: 她想他跟她說我愛你。

examples.text: He promised me that he wouldn't tell anybody.
examples.translation: 他答應了我不會對任何人說。

examples.text: Could you tell me how to get to the station?
examples.translation: 能否告訴我去車站的路怎麼走？

examples.text: Can you tell me where the nearest bus stop is?
examples.translation: 你能把最近的公車站指給我看嗎?

etymology.text: From Middle English tellen (“to count, tell”), from Old English tellan (“to count, tell”), from Proto-West Germanic *talljan, from Proto-Germanic *taljaną, *talzijaną (“to count, enumerate”), from Proto-Germanic *talą, *talō (“number, counting”), from Proto-Indo-European *dol- (“calculation, fraud”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（tellen）「數、告訴」，來自古英語（tellan），經原始日耳曼語（*taljaną）「計數」，來自（*talą）「數目」，上溯至原始印歐語（*dol-）「計算、詐欺」。

senses.definition: To demonstrate that something is true or viable; to give proof for; to bear out; to testify.
To turn out; to manifest.
To turn out to be.
To put to the test, to make trial of.
To ascertain or establish the genuineness or validity of; to verify.
To determine by experiment which effects a substance causes when ingested.
senses.native: （藥理）以實驗確定（物質的作用）

senses.definition: To experience.
To take a trial impression of; to take a proof of.

examples.text: Mathematicians love to prove things.
examples.translation: 數學喜歡證明事物。

examples.text: Prove you're not a chicken.
examples.translation: 請證明你不是雞。

examples.text: Sam needed to prove that.
examples.translation: 山姆非證明這點不可。

examples.text: You can't prove that.
examples.translation: 你無法證明。

examples.text: Tom says that he can prove that Mary did that.
examples.translation: 湯姆說他能證明那是瑪麗做的。

examples.text: The facts proved that our worries were unnecessary.
examples.translation: 事實證明了我們的擔心是多餘的。

etymology.text: From Middle English proven, from Old English prōfian (“to esteem, regard as, evince, try, prove”) and Old French prover (“to prove”), both from Latin probō (“test, try, examine, approve, show to be good or fit, prove”, verb), from probus (“good, worthy, excellent”), from Proto-Indo-European *pro-bʰuH-s (“being in front, prominent”), from *pro-, *per- (“toward”) + *bʰuH- (“to be”). Displaced native Middle English sothen (“to prove”), from Old English sōþian (“to prove”). Doublet of probe. More at
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（proven），來自古英語（prōfian）「尊重、顯示、試驗、證明」與古法語（prover）「證明」，兩者皆源自拉丁語（probō）「試驗、檢查、認可、證明」，來自（probus）「好的、正直的」，最終源自原始印歐語。取代了中古英語原有的（sothen）「證明」。與（probe）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: To show how to use (something).
To show the steps taken to create a logical argument or equation.
To participate in or organize a demonstration.
To show, display, or present; to prove or make evident

examples.text: Can you demonstrate it?
examples.translation: 您可以示範一下嗎?

examples.text: Anything can be demonstrated using numbers.
I'll demonstrate how this machine works.
Allow me to demonstrate my invention to you.
All the students demonstrated against the war.
Souls have not been demonstrated to exist.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin dēmonstrātus, the perfect passive participle of dēmonstrō (“to show, point at”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix). Cognate with French démontrer.

senses.definition: Something that provides a definitive characterization or description of the nature and attributes of a specified entity.
Things that are or can be known about a given topic; communicable knowledge of something.
Any ordered sequence of symbols (or signals) (that could contain a message).
The act of informing or imparting knowledge; notification.

A statement of criminal activity brought before a judge or magistrate; in the UK, used to inform a magistrate of an offence and request a warrant; in the US, an accusation brought before a judge without a grand jury indictment.
The act of informing against someone, passing on incriminating knowledge; accusation.
The systematic imparting of knowledge; education, training.
The creation of form; the imparting of a given quality or characteristic; forming, animation.
The meaning that a human assigns to data by means of the known conventions used in its representation.
Divine inspiration.
A service provided by telephone which provides listed telephone numbers of a subscriber.
Any unambiguous abstract data, the smallest possible unit being the bit.
The output resulting from the systematic collection, manipulation and organization of raw data into a structured, interpretable format.

examples.text: That's an interesting piece of information.
examples.translation: 這是條有趣的資訊。

examples.text: Keep this information under your hat.
examples.translation: 不要把這些資料洩露出去。

examples.text: Please ask at the information desk.
examples.translation: 請向服務台詢問。

examples.text: He collected bits of information.
examples.translation: 他收集了一些訊息。

examples.text: We want to get more information.
examples.translation: 我們想要更多資訊。

examples.text: The information you gave me is of little use.
examples.translation: 你給我的資料沒有多大的用處。

etymology.text: From Middle English enformacioun, informacioun, borrowed from Anglo-Norman informacioun, enformation, Old French information, from Latin īnfōrmātiō (“formation, conception; education”), from the participle stem of īnformāre (“to inform”). Equivalent to inform + -ation.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（informacioun），借自英法語（informacioun）與古法語（information），來自拉丁語（īnfōrmātiō）「形成、構想、教育」，再來自（īnfōrmāre）「告知」。相當於（inform + -ation）。

senses.definition: To communicate knowledge to.
To impart information or knowledge.
To act as an informer; denounce.
To give form or character to; to inspire (with a given quality); to affect, influence (with a pervading principle, idea etc.).
To direct, guide.
To instruct, train (usually in matters of knowledge).
To make known, wisely and/or knowledgeably.
To take form; to become visible or manifest; to appear.

examples.text: We should inform them about that.
examples.translation: 我們應該把那件事情告知他們。

examples.text: Please inform me when to start.
examples.translation: 請通知我何時開始。

examples.text: Please keep me informed.
examples.translation: 請通知我。

examples.text: Has anyone informed Tom?
examples.translation: 有沒有人通知湯姆？

examples.text: Why wasn't I informed?
examples.translation: 怎麼沒人告訴我。

examples.text: Please inform me of the plan ahead of time.
examples.translation: 請你事先把計劃告訴我。

etymology.text: From Middle English informen, enformen, borrowed from Old French enformer, informer (“to train, instruct, inform”), from Latin īnfōrmō (“to shape, form, train, instruct, educate”), from in- (“into”) + fōrma (“form, shape”), equivalent to in- + form.

senses.definition: An act of pointing out or indicating.
A fact that shows that something exists or may happen.
A discovery made; information.

Any symptom or occurrence in a disease that serves to direct to suitable remedies; the problem that warrants and prompts the use of a diagnostic test, imaging mode, or treatment (e.g., medication, surgical procedure).
A declared approximation of the price at which a traded security is likely to commence trading.
A mark or another symbol used to represent something.
An explanation; a display.

examples.text: I see no indication of that ever happening.
There was no indication that anything was wrong.
Intelligence is not an indication of knowledgeability.
Is there any indication whether Tom wants to go?

The cursing tongue is an indication of a bad heart.

etymology.text: From Old French indication, from Latin indicātiō (“a showing, indicating the value of something; valuation”), from indicō (“point out, indicate, show; value”); see indicate; compare French indication, Spanish indicación, Italian indicazione. By surface analysis, indicate + -ion.

senses.definition: An item of information put into a temporary or permanent physical medium.
A set of data relating to a single individual or item.
A data structure similar to a struct, in some programming languages such as C and Java based on classes and designed for storing immutable data.
The most extreme known value of some variable, particularly that of an achievement in competitive events.
senses.native: 紀錄、最高記錄、最好成績

senses.definition: Any instance of a physical medium on which information was put for the purpose of preserving it and making it available for future reference.
A music album; broadly, any music released as a single, EP, etc.

examples.translation: 我有不低於一千片光碟。

展覽的物品陳列（展示會）
留聲機唱片；盛食物的盤子

etymology.text: From Middle English recorde, borrowed from Old French record, from recorder. See record.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（recorde），借自古法語（record），來自（recorder）。參見動詞（record）。

senses.definition: A visible fact that shows that something exists or may happen.
A mark or another symbol used to represent something.
A clearly visible object, generally flat, bearing a short message in words or pictures.
Positive or negative polarity, as denoted by the + or - sign.
A specific gesture or motion used to communicate by those with speaking or hearing difficulties; now specifically, a linguistic unit in sign language equivalent to word in spoken languages.
A military emblem carried on a banner or standard.
a perceptible indication of something not immediately apparent (as a visible clue that something has happened)
a public display of a message
any nonverbal action or gesture that encodes a message
structure displaying a board on which advertisements can be posted
(astrology) one of 12 equal areas into which the zodiac is divided
(medicine) any objective evidence of the presence of a disorder or disease
having an indicated pole (as the distinction between positive and negative electric charges)
An omen.
A property of the body that indicates a disease and, unlike a symptom, can be detected objectively by someone other than the patient.
Physical evidence left by an animal.
A wonder; miracle; prodigy.
An astrological sign.
Sign language in general.

A semantic unit, something that conveys meaning or information (e.g. a word of written language); (linguistics, semiotics) a unit consisting of a signifier and a signified concept. (See sign (semiotics).)
senses.native: 語意單位，傳達意義或資訊的單元（如書面語的詞）；（語言學、符號學）由能指與所指組成的符號單位

examples.text: Don't forget to sign your name.

examples.text: Do you think it's a sign?

examples.translation: 一切的跡象都表示她的狀況有所改善。

examples.text: Red, as opposed to green, is a sign of danger.
examples.translation: 紅色是危險的標誌，與綠色相對。

etymology.text: From Middle English signe, sygne, syng, seine, sine, syne, from Old English seġn (“sign; mark; token”) and Old French signe, seing (“sign; mark; signature”); both from Latin signum (“a mark; sign; token”); root uncertain. Doublet of signum and signal. Partially displaced native token.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 signe, sygne, syng, seine, sine, syne，來自古英語 seġn（「標記；符號」）及古法語 signe, seing（「標記；簽名」）；皆源自拉丁文 signum（「標記；符號」）；詞源不明。為 signum 與 signal 的同源詞，部分取代原生詞「token」。

senses.definition: An effort, process, or operation designed to establish or discover a fact or truth; an act of testing; a test; a trial.

The degree of evidence which convinces the mind of any truth or fact, and produces belief; a test by facts or arguments which induce, or tend to induce, certainty of the judgment; conclusive evidence; demonstration.
The quality or state of having been proved or tried; firmness or hardness which resists impression, or does not yield to force; impenetrability of physical bodies.
A proof sheet; a trial impression, as from type, taken for correction or examination.
A limited-run high-quality strike of a particular coin, originally as a test run, although nowadays mostly for collectors' sets.

A sequence of statements consisting of axioms, assumptions, statements already demonstrated in another proof, and statements that logically follow from previous statements in the sequence, and which concludes with a statement that is the object of the proof.
A process for testing the accuracy of an operation performed. Compare prove, transitive verb, 5.

A measure of the alcohol content of liquor. Originally, in Britain, 100 proof was defined as 57.1% by volume (no longer used). In the US, 100 proof means that the alcohol content is 50% of the total volume of the liquid; thus, perfectly pure absolute alcohol would be 200 proof.
Experience of something.
Firmness of mind; stability not to be shaken.
Armour of excellent or tried quality, and deemed impenetrable; properly, armour of proof.

etymology.text: From Middle English proof, from Old French prove, from Late Latin proba (“a proof”), from Latin probō (“to prove”); see prove; compare also the doublet probe.

senses.definition: A fact or statement used to support a proposition; a reason.
A series of propositions organized so that the final proposition is a conclusion which is intended to follow logically from the preceding propositions, which function as premises.
A process of reasoning; argumentation.

An abstract or summary of the content of a literary work such as a book, a poem or a major section such as a chapter, included in the work before the content itself; (figuratively) the contents themselves.
A verbal dispute; a quarrel.
Any of the phrases that bear a syntactic connection to the verb of a clause.
The independent variable of a function.
The phase of a complex number.
A quantity on which the calculation of another quantity depends.
A value, or a reference to a value, passed to a function.
A parameter at a function call; an actual parameter, as opposed to a formal parameter.
a fact or assertion offered as evidence that something is true
a contentious speech act; a dispute where there is strong disagreement
a discussion in which reasons are advanced for and against some proposition or proposal
a summary of the subject or plot of a literary work or play or movie
(computer science) a reference or value that is passed to a function, procedure, subroutine, command, or program
Any dispute, altercation, or collision.
A matter in question; a business in hand.
The subject matter of an artistic representation, discourse, or writing; a theme or topic.
Evidence, proof; (countable) an item of such evidence or proof.

etymology.text: From Middle English argument, from Anglo-Norman and Old French arguement, from Latin argumentum. The English word is analysable as argue + -ment. Doublet of argumentum.

senses.definition: present participle and gerund of mean

etymology.text: From Middle English mening, menyng, equivalent to mean + -ing. Cognate with Scots mening (“intent, purpose, sense, meaning”), West Frisian miening (“opinion, mind”), Dutch mening (“view, opinion, judgement”), German Meinung (“opinion, view, mind, idea”), Danish and Swedish mening (“meaning, sense, sentence, opinion”), Icelandic meining (“meaning”).

senses.definition: Having a (specified) intention.
Expressing some intention or significance; meaningful.

examples.text: I can't understand this sign's meaning.

etymology.text: From Middle English mening, menyng, equivalent to mean + -ing. Cognate with Scots mening (“intent, purpose, sense, meaning”), West Frisian miening (“opinion, mind”), Dutch mening (“view, opinion, judgement”), German Meinung (“opinion, view, mind, idea”), Danish and Swedish mening (“meaning, sense, sentence, opinion”), Icelandic meining (“meaning”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 mening、menyng，意為 mean + -ing。與蘇格蘭語 mening（意為「意圖、目的、意義」）、西弗里斯蘭語 miening（意為「意見、心思」）、荷蘭語 mening（意為「觀點、意見、判斷」）、德語 Meinung（意為「意見、觀點、心思、想法」）、丹麥語與瑞典語 mening（意為「意義、語意、句子、意見」）、冰島語 meining（意為「意義」）同源。

senses.definition: Signifying something; carrying meaning.
Having a noticeable or major effect.
Reasonably large in number or amount.
Having a covert or hidden meaning.
Having a low probability of occurring by chance (for example, having high correlation and thus likely to be related).
Of a digit or figure, see significant figure.

senses.definition: The extent to which something matters; importance
Meaning.

The results are full of significance.
I don't understand its significance.

senses.definition: Physical matter; material.
A form of matter that has constant chemical composition and characteristic properties.
The essential part of anything; the most vital part.
Substantiality; solidity; firmness.
Material possessions; estate; property; resources.
Drugs (illegal narcotics)
Ousia, essence; underlying reality or hypostasis in the philosophical sense.

Both Latin and Germanic from Proto-Indo-European *sent- (“

The original meaning of the verb is 'to sit before' in the sense of presiding at a meeting. A secondary meaning of the verb is 'to command, to govern'. So praesidēns means 'the presiding one on a meeting' or 'governor, co
etymology.native: 源自古法語（president），來自拉丁語（praesidēns）「主持、會長、領袖」（受格 praesidentem），是動詞（praesideō）「主持」的現在主動分詞的名詞化。該動詞由（prae）「在前」加（sedeō）「坐」組成，原義是「坐在前面」主持會議，引申為「指揮、統治」。

A plant that has been cut down until its main stem is close to the ground, resembling a stool, to promote new growth.
A close-stool; a seat used for urination and defecation: a chamber pot, commode, outhouse seat, or toilet.
Feces; excrement.
A production of feces or excrement; an act of defecation, stooling.
A small channel on the side of a vessel, for the deadeyes of the backstays.
Material, such as oyster shells, spread on the sea bottom for oyster spat to adhere to.
A decoy; a portable piece of wood to which a pigeon is fastened to lure wild birds.
senses.native: （古）誘鳥（將鴿子綁在木柱上以引誘野鳥）

senses.definition: An informer to the police.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: This stool needs to be repaired.
examples.translation: 這張矮凳需要修理。

examples.text: Bring a stool from the kitchen.
examples.translation: 從廚房拿一張矮凳來。

examples.text: He had a roundworm in his stool the other day.
examples.translation: 他前幾天大便裡有蛔蟲。

examples.text: She had toad-stools all over the front yard.
examples.translation: 她前院滿是鴨子糞。

examples.text: Stefan sat on one of the stools by the island.
examples.translation: 斯特凡坐在島邊的一張矮凳上。

examples.text: If you stand on this stool, you can reach the top of the closet.
examples.translation: 站在這個凳子上的話，你可以摸到衣櫃頂。

etymology.text: From Middle English stool, from Old English stōl (“chair, seat”), from Proto-West Germanic *stōl, from Proto-Germanic *stōlaz (“chair”), from Proto-Indo-European *stoh₂los (“frame, rack, stand”), from *steh₂- (“to stand”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 stool，來自古英語 stōl（意為「椅子、座位」），源自原始西日耳曼語 *stōl，再溯源自原始日耳曼語 *stōlaz（意為「椅子」），更上溯源自原始印歐語 *stoh₂los（意為「框架、支架」），來自 *steh₂-（意為「站立」）

senses.definition: A chair with supports for the arms or elbows.
An upholstered chair without armrests intended for the living room
A position from which a casual and inexpert perspective looks out on the world.

examples.text: He sprawled lazily on an armchair.
examples.translation: 他慵懶地躺在沙發椅上。

examples.text: My father fixes broken armchairs.
examples.translation: 我爸爸修壞了的沙發椅。

examples.text: We were sitting in the armchairs.
examples.translation: 我們坐在沙發椅上。

examples.text: We bought a comfortable new armchair.
examples.translation: 我們買了張舒適的扶手椅。

examples.text: Here's a comfortable armchair you can sit in.
examples.translation: 這是一張你可以坐的舒適沙發椅。

examples.text: Tom sat in his armchair, reading a magazine.
examples.translation: 湯姆坐在沙發椅上，看雜誌。

etymology.text: From arm + chair.
etymology.native: 由 arm 與 chair 組成。

senses.definition: To divide (a thing) into separate parts.
To disunite from a group or mass; to disconnect.
To cause (things or people) to be separate.
To divide itself into separate pieces or substances.
senses.native: 分開、分離，自行分成各個部分或物質

senses.definition: To set apart; to select from among others, as for a special use or service.
senses.native: 挑選出、另行安排（作為特殊用途）

examples.text: Separate the articles from the headings.
He separated the fighting children.
Separate the remaining pieces by color.
If the kids get too noisy, separate them for a few minutes.
The sauce will separate if you don't keep stirring.
She separated the eggs.
examples.translation: 她把蛋白和蛋黃分開。

etymology.text: From Middle English separaten (“to separate”), from separat (“separated”) + -en, from Latin sēparātus, perfect passive participle of sēparō (“to separate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from sē- (“apart”) + parō (“prepare”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *per- (“produce, procure, bring forward, bring forth”). Displaced Middle English scheden, from Old English scēadan (whence English shed).

senses.definition: To apply violent force to someone or something.
To aggressively challenge a person, idea, etc., with words (particularly in newspaper headlines, because it typesets into less space than "criticize" or similar).
(Of a chemical species) To approach a chemical species or bond in order to form a bond with it.
To begin to affect; to act upon injuriously or destructively; to begin to decompose or waste.
To deal with something in a direct way; to set to work upon.
To aim balls at the batsman’s wicket.
To set a field, or bowl in a manner designed to get wickets.
To bat aggressively, so as to score runs quickly.
To move forward in an active attempt to score a point, as opposed to trying not to concede.
To accelerate quickly in an attempt to get ahead of the other riders.

examples.text: We were attacked from both sides.
examples.translation: 我們被兩面夾擊了。

examples.text: The dog attacked the little boy.
examples.translation: 這隻狗攻擊了這個小男孩。

examples.text: Stop attacking yourself and go fight the fascists.
examples.translation: 不要再打擊自己了，給我去打擊法西斯。

examples.text: We were attacked by swarms of bees.
examples.translation: 我們被一大群蜜蜂攻擊。

examples.text: A swarm of hornets attacked the children.
examples.translation: 一窩黃蜂襲擊了孩子們。

examples.text: Our troops were constantly attacked by the guerrillas.
examples.translation: 我們軍隊總是被遊擊隊騷擾。

etymology.text: Borrowed from French attaque, derived from the verb attaquer, from Italian attaccare (“to join, attach”) (used in attaccare battaglia (“to join battle”)), from Frankish *stakkijan (“to stick, stick to, attach”). Doublet of attach. Displaced native Middle English onresen, from Old English onrǣsan (“to attack”); and Middle English resinge (“an assault, attack”) (compare Old English onrǣs (“an attack”)).
etymology.native: 借自法語（attaque），源自動詞（attaquer），來自義大利語（attaccare）「連接、附著」（用於 attaccare battaglia「開戰」），再源自法蘭克語（*stakkijan）「黏、附著」。與（attach）為雙式詞。取代了中古英語原有的（onresen，源自古英語 onrǣsan「攻擊」）與（resinge）「襲擊」。

senses.definition: Free of dirt, filth, or impurities (extraneous matter); not dirty, filthy, or soiled.
Of metal, having relatively few impurities.
Free of contamination, (unwanted) germs, infection, or disease.
Devoid of sexually transmitted diseases (STDs).
Of a route, ascended without falling.
Free from that which is useless or injurious; without defects.
In an unmarked condition; blank.
Pure, especially morally or religiously.
Not using drugs or alcohol.
Free from (or showing no signs of) corrupt, unlawful, and/or sinister conduct or connections (and (of criminal, driving, etc. records) therefore without restrictions or penalties).
Free of infiltration by covert listening or recording devices (bugs), enemy spies, etc.
Empty.
Smooth, exact, and performed well.
That does not damage the environment (as much as some alternative).
Allowing an uninterrupted flow over surfaces, without protrusions such as racks or landing gear.
Having the undercarriage and flaps in the up position.
Not muscular due to steroid use.
Of a victory or performance: without any blemishes such as submission holds, disqualification, interference, etc.
Not in possession of weapons or contraband such as drugs.
Devoid of profanity.

examples.text: Mother made me clean the bathroom.
examples.translation: 母親讓我打掃洗手間。

examples.text: I want everyone to help me clean the house.
examples.translation: 我希望所有人都來幫我打掃房子。

examples.text: If Ted were here, he could help us clean our room.
It is the students' duty to clean their classrooms.
examples.translation: 學生有清掃教室的責任。

examples.text: Bring me a clean plate and take the dirty one away.
examples.translation: 請拿一個新的盤子給我並把這個髒的拿走.

examples.text: You may take this book as long as you keep it clean.
examples.translation: 你可以拿走這本書，但可別把它弄髒了。

etymology.text: From Middle English clene, from Old English clāne, clǣne (“clean; pure; clear”), from Proto-West Germanic *klainī (“dainty, fine, small; clean”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *glēy- (“gleaming”), from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to gleam”).

senses.definition: Exhibiting social ability or cleverness.
An acronym for remembering desirable characteristics for goal-setting: specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, timebound. (See SMART criteria on Wikipedia.Wikipedia)
Exhibiting intellectual knowledge, such as that found in books.
Equipped with intelligent behaviour (digital/computer technology).
Good-looking; well dressed; fine; fashionable.
Cleverly shrewd and humorous in a way that may be rude and disrespectful.
Sudden and intense.
Causing sharp pain; stinging.
Sharp; keen; poignant.
Intense in feeling; painful. Used usually with the adverb intensifier right.
Efficient; vigorous; brilliant.
Pretentious; showy; spruce.
Brisk; fresh.
Hard-working.

examples.text: Mary may not be as smart as you think she is.
examples.translation: 瑪麗可能沒有你想的那麼聰明。

examples.text: That cast on his leg chaffs him right smart.

etymology.text: From Middle English smerten, from Old English *smeortan (“to smart”), from Proto-West Germanic *smertan, from Proto-Germanic *smertaną (“to hurt, ache”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)merd- (“to bite, sting”). Cognate with Scots smert, Dutch smarten, German schmerzen, Danish smerte, Swedish smärta.

senses.definition: Newly made, formed or evolved; having no precedent; of recent origin; new.
Original, especially in an interesting way; new and striking; not of the typical or ordinary type.

examples.text: It wasn't a very interesting novel.
examples.translation: 這不是一個很有趣的小說。

examples.text: Yesterday, he read the most interesting novel.
examples.translation: 他昨天看了一部最有趣的小說。

relations.native: 不按傳統手法寫的小說
美國網路產品公司名稱

etymology.text: From Middle English novel, from Old French novel (“new, fresh, recent, recently made or done, strange, rare”) (modern nouvel, nouveau), from Latin novellus (“new, fresh, young, modern”), diminutive of novus (“new”). Doublet of nouveau.

senses.definition: Showing good judgement or the benefit of experience.
Disrespectful.
Aware, informed (to something).

examples.text: He is more clever than wise.
examples.translation: 與其說他有智慧，不如說他聰明。

examples.text: She is older and wiser now.
examples.translation: 她現在更加年長也更加有智慧。

examples.text: Don't get older, get wiser.
examples.translation: 衰老不得，智慧不得不得。

examples.text: The old man looked wise.
examples.translation: 老人看起來明智。

examples.text: A wise leader knows when to listen to others.
examples.translation: 聰明的領袖知道什麼時候要聽取他人意見。

examples.text: Although he may be clever, he is not wise.
examples.translation: 他只不過是有點小聰明。

etymology.text: From Middle English wys, wyse, from Old English wīs (“wise”), from Proto-Germanic *wīsaz (“knowledgeable, wise”), from Proto-Indo-European *wéydos (“seeing; knowledge”), from *weyd- (“to see”).

senses.definition: Relating to the origin or beginning; preceding all others.
First in a series of copies or versions.
Newly created.
Fresh, different.
Pioneering.
Having a specified place or time as its origin.
Unseasoned, unflavored, plain, or having a standard or typical flavor; classic, traditional

examples.text: You shouldn't forget your original intentions.
examples.translation: 不能忘記自己的初衷。

examples.text: He adhered to the original plan.
examples.translation: 他堅持原來的計畫。

examples.text: That's an original idea.
examples.translation: 那是原創的想法。

examples.text: The original qipao was wide and loose.
examples.translation: 最初的旗袍是寬鬆的。

examples.text: Tom makes his own original Christmas cards every year.
examples.translation: 湯姆每年都會製作自己獨創的聖誕節賀卡。

examples.text: He has a lot of original ideas.
examples.translation: 他有很多獨到的見解。

etymology.text: From Middle English original, from Old French original, from Late Latin orīginālis (“primitive, original”), from Latin orīgō (“beginning, source, origin”), equivalent to origin + -al; see origin.

senses.definition: Situated toward or at the front of something.
Situated toward or near the enemy lines.
Acting in or pertaining to the direction in which someone or something is facing.
Acting in or pertaining to the direction of travel or movement.
Moving in the desired direction of progress.
Having the usual order or sequence.
Expected or scheduled to take place in the future.
Advanced beyond the usual degree; advanced for the season; precocious.
Without customary restraint or modesty; bold, cheeky, pert, presumptuous or pushy.
Prominent, emphasized (or, in combinations, emphasizing).
Ready; prompt; ardently inclined; in a bad sense, eager or hasty.

examples.text: The forward battalion took a hammering.
examples.translation: 前線營遭受重創。

examples.translation: 我的正前方視力很好，但周邊視力很差。

examples.translation: 這是國家向前邁出的重要一步。

examples.text: The price for forward delivery is presently higher than the spot price.
examples.translation: 目前遠期交貨的價格高於現貨價。

examples.text: The grass is forward, or forward for the season. We have a forward spring.
examples.translation: 草長得早，以這個季節來說算早。今年春天來得早。

relations.native: （故事的）未來場景；倒敘的反向

etymology.text: From Middle English foreward, from Old English foreweard (“forward, inclined to the front, fore, early, former”), from Proto-Germanic *fura- (“fore-”), *warþaz (“turned”), equivalent to fore + -ward. Cognate with Dutch voorwaarts (“forward”), German vorwärts (“forward”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（foreward），來自古英語（foreweard）「向前、在前、早期、以前」，由原始日耳曼語（*fura-）「前」加（*warþaz）「轉向」組成，相當於（fore）加（-ward）。與荷蘭語（voorwaarts）、德語（vorwärts）同源。

senses.definition: A device that generates light, heat, or other electromagnetic radiation. Especially an electric light bulb.
A device containing oil, burnt through a wick for illumination; an oil lamp.
A piece of furniture holding one or more electric light sockets.
An eye.

examples.text: She turned off her desk lamp.

examples.translation: 你在賣這些燈嗎？

examples.translation: 燈籠在樹枝上吊著。

examples.translation: 愛迪生發明了電燈。

examples.translation: 我想把閱讀燈關了，行嗎？

etymology.text: From Middle English laumpe, lampe, from Old French lampe (“lamp, light”), from Latin lampas (“torch, lamp, light”), from Ancient Greek λαμπάς (lampás, “torch, lamp, beacon, light, meteor”), from Proto-Indo-European *leh₂p- (“to shine”). Cognate with Lithuanian lópė (“light”), Welsh llachar (“bright”). Displaced native Old English lēohtfæt (literally “light-vat”).

senses.definition: To hunt at night using a lamp, during which bright lights are used to dazzle the hunted animal or to attract insects for capture.

etymology.text: From Middle English laumpe, lampe, from Old French lampe (“lamp, light”), from Latin lampas (“torch, lamp, light”), from Ancient Greek λαμπάς (lampás, “torch, lamp, beacon, light, meteor”), from Proto-Indo-European *leh₂p- (“to shine”). Cognate with Lithuanian lópė (“light”), Welsh llachar (“bright”). Displaced native Old English lēohtfæt (literally “light-vat”).

senses.definition: A sudden, short, temporary burst of light.
A very short amount of time.
A sudden and brilliant burst, as of genius or wit.
Pizzazz, razzle-dazzle.
Material left around the edge of a moulded part at the parting line of the mould.
The strips of bright cloth or buttons worn around the collars of market traders.
A pattern where each prop is thrown and caught only once.
A language, created by a minority to maintain cultural identity, that cannot be understood by the ruling class.
A form of military insignia.
Any of various lycaenid butterflies of the genera Artipe, Deudorix and Rapala.
A tattoo flash (example design on paper to give an idea of a possible tattoo).
The sudden sensation of being "high" after taking a recreational drug.
Synonym of flashback (“recurrence of the effects of a hallucinogenic drug”).
A brief exposure or making visible (of a smile, badge, etc).
The (intentional or unintentional) exposure of an intimate body part or undergarment in public.
A flashlight; an electric torch.
A preparation of capsicum, burnt sugar, etc., for colouring liquor to make it look stronger.
A newsflash.
A pool of water, in some areas especially one that is marshy, and/or one formed by subsidence of the ground due to mining. (Compare flush (“marsh; pool”).)
A reservoir and sluiceway beside a navigable stream, just above a shoal, so that the stream may pour in water as boats pass, and thus bear them over the shoal.

examples.text: Jonas started noticing the flashes again.
I left your flash drive at home.
examples.translation: 我把你的優盤忘在家裡了。

examples.text: I saw a flash of lightning far in the distance.
He had a flash of intuition.

etymology.text: In some senses, from Middle English flasshen, a variant of flasken, flaskien (“to sprinkle, splash”), which was likely of imitative origin; in other senses probably of North Germanic origin akin to Swedish dialectal flasa (“to burn brightly, blaze”), related to flare. senses.definition: A collection of sheets of paper bound together to hinge at one edge, containing printed or written material, pictures, etc.
A record of betting (from the use of a notebook to record what each person has bet).
A list of all players who have been booked (received a warning) in a game.
The list of mares that a stallion will breed in a given season.
A list of the races that a jockey is scheduled to ride in.
The twenty-sixth Lenormand card.
Any source of instruction.
The accumulated body of knowledge passed down among black pimps.
The sum of chess knowledge in the opening or endgame.
A long work fit for publication, typically prose, such as a novel or textbook, and typically published as such a bound collection of sheets, but now sometimes electronically as an e-book.
A major division of a long work.
A bookmaker (a person who takes bets on sporting events and similar); bookie; turf accountant.
A convenient collection, in a form resembling a book, of small paper items for individual use.
The script of a musical or opera.
Records of the accounts of a business.
A book award, a recognition for receiving the highest grade in a class (traditionally an actual book, but recently more likely a letter or certificate acknowledging the achievement).
Six tricks taken by one side.
Four of a kind.
A document, held by the referee, of the incidents that happened in a game.
senses.native: （比賽中由裁判持有的）記錄單（記錄比賽事件）

senses.definition: A portfolio of one's previous work in the industry.

examples.text: This book contains forty photographs.

examples.text: Are you reading an interesting book?

examples.text: Have you finished reading the book?
examples.translation: 你讀完這本書了嗎？

examples.text: This book isn't interesting at all.
examples.translation: 這本書一點也不有趣。

examples.text: I ordered those books from Germany.
examples.translation: 我從德國訂購了那些書。

examples.text: I have to give back the book before Saturday.
examples.translation: 我必須在禮拜六之前把書還回去。

etymology.text: From Middle English bok, book, from Old English bōc, from Proto-West Germanic *bōk, from Proto-Germanic *bōks. Bookmaker sense by clipping.
etymology.native: 「book」源自中世英文 bok，來自古英文 bōc，再溯源自原始西日耳曼語 *bōk，更上溯至原始日耳曼語 *bōks。其「賭博」義項則由剪切形成。

senses.definition: To reserve (something) for future use.
To write down, to register or record in a book or as in a book.
senses.native: 登記、記錄（於簿冊或類似的紀錄中）

senses.definition: To add a name to the list of people who are participating in something.
To record the name and other details of a suspected offender and the offence for later judicial action.
senses.native: 記錄嫌疑人的姓名、資料及違法事由，以供日後司法追訴

senses.definition: To issue a caution to, usually a yellow card, or a red card if a yellow card has already been issued.
senses.native: 對（球員）出示警告（通常為黃牌，若已有黃牌則出示紅牌）

senses.definition: To travel very fast.
To record bets as bookmaker.
To receive the highest grade in a class.
To move or leave, often hurriedly and abruptly.

examples.text: The policeman booked her when she tried to solicit a man.
examples.translation: 警察在她試圖勾引男子時將她逮捕。

etymology.text: From Middle English bok, book, from Old English bōc, from Proto-West Germanic *bōk, from Proto-Germanic *bōks. Bookmaker sense by clipping.
etymology.native: 「book」源自中世英文 bok，來自古英文 bōc，再溯源自原始西日耳曼語 *bōk，更上溯至原始日耳曼語 *bōks。其「賭博」義項則由剪切形成。

senses.definition: Something actual as opposed to invented.
Something concrete used as a basis for further interpretation.
An objective consensus on a fundamental reality that has been agreed upon by a substantial number of experts.
Information about a particular subject, especially actual conditions and/or circumstances.
Something which is real.
An individual value or measurement at the lowest level of granularity in a data warehouse.
A wrongful or criminal deed.
Action; the realm of action.
A feat or meritorious deed.

examples.text: We have overlooked this important fact.
examples.translation: 我們看漏了這件重要的事。

examples.text: There is no denying the fact.
examples.translation: 這是無可否認的事實。

examples.text: This story is based on facts.
examples.translation: 這個故事是根據真人真事寫成的。

examples.text: Are you sure of your facts?
examples.translation: 你確定你的資料屬實嗎？

examples.text: We want to know the facts.
examples.translation: 我們想知道真相。

examples.text: I don't really like him, in fact, I hate him.
examples.translation: 我不太喜歡他，其實我討厭他。

etymology.text: From Old French fact, from Latin factum (“an act, deed, feat, etc.”); also Medieval Latin for “state, condition, circumstance”; neuter of factus (“done or made”), perfect passive participle of faciō (“do, make”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to put, place, set”). etymology.native: 源自古法語（fact），來自拉丁語（factum）「行為、事蹟」，是（faciō）「做」的完成被動分詞中性形式，上溯至原始印歐語（*dʰeh₁-）「放、置」。與（feat）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: A set of items or amount of material procured, gathered or presented together.
A set of pitch classes used by a composer.
The activity of collecting.
A set of sets; used because such a thing is in general too large to comply with the formal definition of a set.
A gathering of money for charitable or other purposes, as by passing a contribution box for donations.
Debt collection.
The jurisdiction of a collector of excise.
A set of college exams generally taken at the start of the term.
The quality of being collected; calm composure.
The act of inferring or concluding from premises or observed facts; also, that which is inferred.

examples.text: The flat front trouser was a staple of that fashion designer's collections.
The attic contains a remarkable collection of antiques, oddities, and random junk.
The asteroid belt consists of a collection of dust, rubble, and minor planets.
This year's Summer Collection will include a wide range of evening wear.
He has a big collection of stamps.
He has a superb coin collection.

Synonym of Chinese whispers (“a game for several players in which a phrase, whispered by each person in turn to their neighbour, is often unwittingly misunderstood as it is transferred, to humorous effect by the time it reaches the last person and is compared with the original phrase; (figurative) a situation where something is changed or misunderstood as a result of passing through successive people or processes”).

etymology.text: The noun is derived from tele- (prefix meaning ‘from a distance’) + -phone (suffix denoting a device which makes a sound), modelled after German Telephon (“early apparatus converting sound into electrical signals”) (dated) (now German Telefon). The word was first used to refer to the modern device in 1876 by the Scottish-born Canadian-American engineer Alexander Graham Bell (1847–1922).
etymology.native: 這個名詞源自 tele-（表示「從遠處」的前綴）＋ -phone（表示「發出聲音的裝置」的後綴），仿照德語 Telephon（「早期將聲音轉換為電信號的裝置」）（舊用語）（現為德語 Telefon）。1876年，蘇格蘭出生的加拿大裔美國工程師亞歷山大·格雷厄姆·貝爾（1847–1922）首次用此詞指稱現代裝置。

Germanic cognates include Scots gowd, Dutch goud, German Gold, Faroese, Icelandic, Norwegian Bokmål, and Norwegian Nynorsk gull, Danish and Swedish guld, and cognates from other Indo-European languages include Latvian zelts, Russian зо

senses.definition: Any of several shrubs or trees of the genus Citrus in the family Rutaceae.

etymology.text: First appears c. 1655, in the English translation Álvaro Semedo’s writings. From Dutch thee, from Hokkien 茶 (tê) (Amoy dialect), from Old Chinese, ultimately from Proto-Sino-Tibetan *s-la (「leaf, tea」). Introduced to English and other Western European languages by the Dutch East India Company, who sourced their tea in Amoy; compare Malay teh along the same trade route. Doublet of chai and cha (and, distantly, the first element of lahpet), from same Proto-Sino-Tibetan root; see discussion of cogn
etymology.native: 最早出現於1655年左右，源自荷蘭人譯本Álvaro Semedo的著作。來自荷蘭語thee，源自 Hokkien 茶（tê）（同安腔），源自古漢語，最終源自原始漢藏語 *s-la（「葉，茶」）。由荷蘭東印度公司引入英文及其他西歐語言，他們從同安供應茶葉；可與馬來語teh 比較，沿同一貿易路線。與chai及cha為同源詞（且遠源與lahpet之首字同源），詳見相關詞源討論。

Usually regarded as a borrowing of Late Latin catīllus (“small bowl”), diminutive of Latin catinus (“deep bowl, vessel for cooking up or serving food”), however, the word may be Germanic confused with the Latin: compare Old English cete (“cooking pot”)
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 ketel，亦作 chetel，來自古英語 ċietel（「鍋、大鍋」），中古英語時可能受古諾斯語 ketill 影響，皆源自原始日耳曼語 *katilaz（「鍋、桶、容器」），起源與構成不明。通常認為是拉丁語 catīllus（「小碗」）的借詞，此詞為拉丁語 catinus（「深碗、烹煮或盛食之器」）之縮小形，但此詞也可能因德語與拉丁語混淆而產生；可參照古英語 cete（「烹煮鍋」）

Cognate with Dutch schop (“shed”), German Schuppen (“shed”), German Schober (“barn”), French échoppe (“booth, shop”) (< Germanic). The verb is denominal. etymology.text: First attested in c. 1646 in a publication by Thomas Browne. etymology.text: From Middle English screw, scrue (“screw”); apparently, despite the difference in meaning, from Old French escroue (“nut, cylindrical socket, screwhole”), from Latin scrōfa (“female pig”) through comparison with the corkscrew shape of a pig's penis. There is also the Old French escruve (“screw”), from Old Dutch *scrūva ("screw"; whence Middle Dutch schruyve (“screw”)), which probably influenced or conflated with the aforementioned, resulting in the Middle English word.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 screw，scrue（「螺絲」）；儘管意義不同，可能來自舊法語 escroue（「螺母、圓柱形插座、螺紋孔」），再經拉丁語 scrōfa（「母豬」）與豬陰莖螺旋槳形狀的比較。另有舊法語 escruve（「螺絲」），源自舊荷蘭語 *scrūva（「螺絲」；由此衍生中古荷蘭語 schruyve（「螺絲」）」），可能影響或與前述詞彙合併，形成中古英語此詞。

Displaced native Middle English wis, iwis (“certain, sure”) (from Old English ġewiss (“certain, sure”)) and alternative Middle English spelling sertane (“some, certain”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（certeyn、certain），借自古法語（certain），來自通俗拉丁語推測形式（*certānus），是拉丁語（certus）「固定的、確定的」的延伸形式，與（cernere）「分開、察覺、決定」的過去分詞（cretus）同源。取代了中古英語原有的（wis、iwis）「確定的」。

etymology.text: From Middle English comun, from Anglo-Norman comun, from Old French comun (rare in the Gallo-Romance languages, but reinforced as a Carolingian calque of Proto-West Germanic *gamainī (“common”) in Old French), from Latin commūnis (“common, public, general”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱom-moy-ni-s (“held in common”), from Proto-Indo-European *mey- (“to exchange, change”). Displaced native Middle English imene, ȝemǣne (“common, general, universal”) (from Old English ġemǣne (“common, universal”)),
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（comun），來自英法語與古法語（comun），在古法語中又作為原始西日耳曼語（*gamainī）「共同的」的仿譯而強化，最終來自拉丁語（commūnis）「共同的、公共的」，源自原始印歐語（*mey-）「交換」。取代了中古英語原有的（imene），其源自古英語（ġemǣne）。

etymology.text: From Middle English standard, from Old French estandart (“gathering place, battle flag”), from Frankish *standahard (literally “stand firm, stand hard”), equivalent to stand + -ard. Merged with Middle English standar, stander, standere
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（standard），來自古法語（estandart）「集合地點、戰旗」，再源自法蘭克語（*standahard）「站穩」，相當於（stand）加（-ard）。另一說認為第二部分來自法蘭克語（*oʀd）「點、地方」。後與中古英語（standar、stander）合流。

senses.definition: A female.
An ethnic group in southern China.
A language of the Hmong-Mien language family spoken by very few She people.

examples.text: Everyone hoped that she would win.
examples.translation: 每個人都希望她會獲勝。

examples.text: Jane insisted that she was right.
examples.translation: 珍堅持她是對的。

examples.text: All the signs are that she is getting better.
examples.translation: 一切的跡象都表示她的狀況有所改善。

examples.text: It seems to me that she is a little selfish.
examples.translation: 我覺得她有點自私。

examples.text: The doctor told her that she should take a rest.
examples.translation: 醫生告訴她要靜養。

examples.text: I have known her since she was a little girl.
examples.translation: 我從她還是個小女孩兒的時候就認識她。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English sche, scho, hyo, ȝho (“she”), whence also Yorkshire dialectal shoo (“she”), Scots she, sho (“she”).
etymology.native: 承襲自中古英語（sche、scho）「她」；約克郡方言與蘇格蘭語的「她」也源自此。

senses.definition: A companion; a comrade.
An animal which is a member of a breed or species, or a flock, herd, etc.
An object which is associated with another object; especially, as part of a set.
One comparable in characteristics with another; especially, as belonging to the same class or group.
One with abilities, achievements, skills, etc., equal to those of another; a thing with characteristics, worth, etc., equal to those of another thing.
One in the same condition, or situation of need, as another.
An academic who constitutes an educational institution (such as a college or university); now particularly, a senior member involved in teaching, research, and management of the institution.
A (senior) member of a learned or professional society.
A senior member of an Inn of Court.
An honorary title bestowed by an educational instutition upon a distinguished person (often an alumna or alumnus).
A scholar appointed to a fellowship, that is, a paid academic position held for a certain period which usually requires the scholar to conduct research.
A physician undergoing a fellowship (supervised subspecialty medical training) after having completed a residency (specialty training program).
A member of a college or university who manages its business interests.
A senior researcher or technician in a corporation, especially one engaged in research and development.
An individual regardless of gender; usually qualified by an adjective or used in the plural.
An equal in character, power, rank, etc.; a peer.
One living at the same time, or about the same age as another, especially when in the same field of study or work.
A male person; a bloke, a chap, a guy, a man; also, preceded by a modifying word, sometimes with a sense of mild reproach: used as a familiar term of address to a man.
An animal or object.
One of a pair of things suited to each other or used together; a counterpart, a mate.

examples.text: What a disagreeable fellow he is!
examples.translation: 他可真是個讓人討厭的傢伙！

examples.text: We're fellow countrymen.
examples.translation: 我們是同胞。

examples.text: Fred is a lazy fellow.
examples.translation: 弗雷德是一個懶惰的傢伙。

examples.text: He is a good fellow.
examples.translation: 他是個好人。

examples.text: Tom's a good fellow.
examples.translation: 湯姆這人不錯。

examples.text: Who's the fellow that just said hello to you?

etymology.text: From Middle English felawe, felowe (“companion, good friend”) from Old English fēolaga, from Old Norse félagi, derived from félag (“joint venture; partnership”, literally “a laying together of property”), from fé (“livestock, property; money”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *peḱ- (“livestock; wealth”)) + lag (“something laid down; right position; arrangement; companionship, fellowship; partnership”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *legʰ- (“to lie down”)).

senses.definition: To enter in a register; to enlist.
To sign-up, especially to vote.
To record, especially in writing.
To buy the full version of trial software by providing one's details and payment.
To express outward signs.
To record officially and handle specially.
To make or adjust so as to be properly or precisely aligned.
To place one's name, or have one's name placed in a register.
To make an impression.
To be in proper alignment; to align or correspond exactly.
To voluntarily sign over for safe keeping, abandoning complete ownership for partial.
To perceive or comprehend; pick up on.
To occur; become realised or noticed; dawn on.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: All participants must be registered.
examples.translation: 所有的參加者都得註冊。

examples.text: What do I have to do now that I'm registered?
examples.translation: 我註冊了，現在該幹什麼呢？

examples.text: I want to have this letter registered.
examples.translation: 我想要用掛號寄這封信。

examples.text: Sir, please present your passport or identity card, so I can register it.
examples.translation: 先生，請出示護照或者身份證，讓我登記一下。

examples.text: Neither Tom nor Mary has registered to vote.
The thermometer registered minus ten last night.

etymology.text: From Medieval Latin registrum, from Late Latin regesta (“list, items recorded”), from Latin regerō (“to record, to carry back”), from re- + gerō (“to carry, bear”). Compare Latin registoria (“a treasurer”). Some senses influenced by association with unrelated Latin regō (“to rule”).

senses.definition: To attack using one or more bombs; to bombard.
To attack or annoy in the manner of a bombing.
To jump into water in a squatting position, with the arms wrapped around the legs, in order to maximise the resulting splash.
To add an excessive amount of chlorine to a pool when it has not been maintained properly.
To move at high speed.
To make oneself drunk.
To cover an area in many graffiti tags.
To fail dismally.
To crash.
To make a smelly mess in (a toilet).
Synonym of parachute (“wrap illicit drugs in a covering before swallowing them”).
To sound; to boom; to make a humming or buzzing sound.

examples.text: London was bombed several times.
examples.translation: 倫敦被轟炸過許多次。

examples.text: The Americans bombed Dresden.
They defused the bomb before it could blow up.
examples.translation: 他們趁炸彈還沒有爆炸的時候就把它拆掉了。

examples.text: This bomb can kill many people.
examples.translation: 這個炸彈可以炸死很多人。

etymology.text: From French bombe, from Italian bomba, from Latin bombus (“a booming sound”), from Ancient Greek βόμβος (bómbos, “booming, humming, buzzing”), imitative of the sound itself. Doublet of bombe. Compare boom.

senses.definition: An instance of plucking or pulling sharply.
The lungs, heart with trachea and often oesophagus removed from slaughtered animals.
senses.native: 宰殺動物後取出的肺、心臟及氣管（有時含食道）

senses.definition: Guts, nerve, fortitude or persistence.
Cheap wine.

examples.text: Those tiny birds are hardly worth the tedious pluck.

relations.native: 滾動的行為、結果或狀態

etymology.text: From Middle English plucken, plukken, plockien, from Old English pluccian, ploccian (“to pluck, pull away, tear”), also Old English plyċċan ("to pluck, pull, snatch; pluck with desire"), from Proto-West Germanic *plukkōn, from Proto-Germanic *plukkōną, *plukkijaną (“to pluck”), of uncertain and disputed origin.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 plucken、plukken 或 plockien，來自古英語 pluccian 與 ploccian（「拔取、拉扯、撕扯」），亦見古英語 plyċċan（「拔取、拉扯；渴望地拔取」），源自日耳曼語族原初 *plukkōn，其起源不明且存在爭議。

senses.definition: To examine critically or carefully; especially, to search out problems or determine condition; to scrutinize.
To examine officially.
To observe the status or nature of an object beyond what is found obvious upon its initial presentation; to 'view within' the object.

examples.text: The cadres inspected our school.
examples.translation: 幹部們視察了我們的學校。

examples.text: The sniffing dog inspects everywhere.
examples.translation: 那隻嗅探犬到處檢查。

examples.text: Government officials inspected all factories.
examples.translation: 政府官員檢查了所有工廠。

examples.text: For years Marina had been inspecting houses.
examples.translation: 瑪麗娜多年來一直在做房屋檢查。

examples.text: People love to inspect each other's houses.
examples.translation: 人們喜歡參觀彼此的房子。

examples.text: "I need to inspect the wound," said the doctor.
examples.translation: 「我必須檢查下傷口，」醫生說道。

relations.native: 仔細檢視，尋找隱藏或隱晦的瑕疵
仔細檢視，尋找隱藏或隱晦的瑕疵

etymology.text: From Latin inspectum, past participle of inspicere (“to look into”), from in (“in”) + specere (“to look at”), equivalent to in- + -spect.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語「察看」的過去分詞，由「向內」加「看」組成，相當於「內」加「看」的構詞成分。

senses.definition: Movement in people or things characterized with a continuous motion, involving either a non solid mass or a multitude.
senses.native: 人或物持續運動的特徵，涉及非固體物質或眾多事物

senses.definition: The movement of a real or figurative fluid.
A formalization of the idea of the motion of particles in a fluid, as a group action of the real numbers on a set.
senses.native: 粒子在流體中運動概念的正式化，即實數對集合的群體作用

senses.definition: The rising movement of the tide.
Smoothness or continuity.
The amount of a fluid that moves or the rate of fluid movement.
senses.native: 流體的移動量或流動速率

senses.definition: A flow pipe, carrying liquid away from a boiler or other central plant (compare with return pipe which returns fluid to central plant).
senses.native: 輸送液體遠離鍋爐或其他中央設施的管道（與將液體送回中央設施的回流管相對）

senses.definition: A mental state characterized by concentration, focus, and enjoyment of a given task.
senses.native: 專注、專注力並享受特定任務的心理狀態

senses.definition: The emission of blood during menstruation.
The ability to skillfully rap along to a beat.
senses.native: 有技巧地隨節奏說唱的能力

senses.definition: The sequence of steps taken in a piece of software to perform some action.
senses.native: 軟體執行某項動作所採取的步驟序列

senses.definition: A bog or mire, especially a rough, waterlogged one.
senses.native: 沼澤或泥沼（尤指多水而崎嶇者）

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: The river flows under the bridge.
examples.translation: 河從橋下流過。

examples.text: The Seine flows through Paris.
examples.translation: 塞納河穿越了巴黎。

examples.text: This river flows quickly.
examples.translation: 這條河水流湍急。

examples.text: The Rhine flows between France and Germany.
examples.translation: 萊茵河流經法國和德國國界。

examples.text: The river that flows through London is the Thames.
examples.translation: 流經倫敦的河是泰晤士河。

examples.text: That river flows into the Pacific.
examples.translation: 這條河匯入太平洋。

relations.native: 工作進程中的步驟序列
流體中持續運動的特徵，涉及非固體物質或眾多事物

etymology.text: From Middle English flowe, from the verb (see below). The psychology sense “state of focus” was coined by Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi in 1975.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 flowe，來自動詞（見下文）。心理學意義「專注狀態」由米哈里·契克森米哈賴於 1975 年提出。

senses.definition: Money or other items used to facilitate transactions.
Paper money.
The state of being current; general acceptance, recognition or use.
Current value; general estimation; the rate at which anything is generally valued.
Fluency; readiness of utterance.

examples.text: What is the currency of Taiwan?
examples.translation: 台灣的貨幣是什麼 ?

examples.text: Algeria needs more foreign currency reserves.
The Algerian dinar is Algeria's currency.
The exchange rates for foreign currency change daily.
examples.translation: 外幣的匯率天天都變。

examples.text: What currency do you use in England?
examples.translation: 你在英國用什麼錢買東西？

examples.text: The ringgit is the currency of which country?

etymology.text: Borrowed from Medieval Latin currentia. By surface analysis, current + -cy.

senses.definition: A piece of currency, usually metallic and in the shape of a disc, but sometimes polygonal, or with a hole in the middle.
A token used in a special establishment like a casino.
That which serves for payment or recompense.
Something in broad circulation or use.
One of the suits of minor arcana in tarot, or a card of that suit.
A corner or external angle.
A small circular slice of food.
Money in general, not limited to coins.

examples.text: My hobby is collecting old coins.
examples.translation: 我的嗜好是收集古錢幣。

examples.text: He likes collecting old coins.
examples.translation: 他喜歡珍藏古幣。

examples.text: She gave me these old coins.
examples.translation: 這些舊硬幣是她給我的。

examples.text: Chris gets 7 gold coins!
examples.translation: 克里斯取得了七枚金幣！

examples.text: He thrust some coins into my pocket.
examples.translation: 他把數枚硬幣強行塞進了我的口袋中。

examples.text: Where did you get those old coins?
examples.translation: 你從哪裡得到這些古錢的？

etymology.text: From Middle English coyn, from Old French coigne (“wedge, cornerstone, die for stamping”), from Latin cuneus (“wedge”). Doublet of coign and cuneus. See also quoin (“cornerstone”). Displaced Middle English mynt, from Old English mynet (whence modern English mint), which was derived from Latin monēta.

senses.definition: The inner flight muscle (pectoralis minor) of poultry.
A specialized rail wagon hauled behind a steam engine to carry fuel and water.
A naval ship that functions as a mobile base for other ships.
A smaller boat used for transportation between a large ship and the shore.
A member of a diving team who assists a diver during a dive but does not themselves go underwater.
Someone who tends or waits on something or someone.
Anything which is offered, proffered, put forth or bid with the expectation of a response, answer, or reply.
A means of payment such as a check or cheque, cash or credit card.
A formal offer to buy or sell something.
Any offer or proposal made for acceptance.
Care, kind concern, regard.

examples.text: Seashells were the legal tender in the Shang dynasty.
examples.translation: 在商朝，貝朋為通用貨幣。

examples.text: Algeria regularly launches large oil tenders.
Your credit card has been declined so you need to provide some other tender such as cash.
We will submit our tender to you within the week.

etymology.text: From Middle English tender, tendere, from Anglo-Norman tendre, Old French tendre, from Latin tener, tenerum (“soft, delicate”).

senses.definition: To assign or be assigned a particular rank or level.
To evaluate or estimate the value of.
To consider or regard.
To deserve; to be worth.
To determine the limits of safe functioning for a machine or electrical device.
senses.native: 規定（機器或電器的）額定值

senses.definition: To evaluate a property's value for the purposes of local taxation.
senses.native: 評定房地產價值（以課地方稅）

senses.definition: To like; to think highly of.
To take action to slow down the pace of the horse one is riding.
To have position (in a certain class).
To have value or standing.
To ratify.
To ascertain the exact rate of the gain or loss of (a chronometer) as compared with true time.
To berate, scold.
To cause (hay, hemp, flax, etc) to decay (whether in an injurious way, or—as retting—in a useful way) by exposure to weather, particularly wetness.

examples.text: What's the postage rate for packages?
examples.translation: 包裹的郵資是多少？

examples.text: Canada's crime rate is decreasing.
examples.translation: 加拿大的犯罪率下降了。

examples.text: What's the exchange rate today?
examples.translation: 今天的匯率是多少？

examples.text: I've heard that if you default on the water rates your water supply will be suspended, is that true?
examples.translation: 聽說不交水費就會被停水，是真的嗎？

examples.text: The transformer is rated at 10 watts.
examples.translation: 這台變壓器的額定功率為 10 瓦。

etymology.text: From Middle English rate, from Old French rate, from Medieval Latin rata, from Latin prō ratā parte (“according to a fixed part”), from ratus (“fixed”), from rērī (“think, deem, judge, estimate", originally "reckon, calculate”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（rate），來自古法語（rate），再源自中世紀拉丁語（rata），來自拉丁語（prō ratā parte）「按固定比例」，源自（ratus）「固定的」，來自（rērī）「認為、估算」。

senses.definition: To pull along a surface or through a medium, sometimes with difficulty.
To proceed heavily, laboriously, or slowly; to advance with weary effort; to go on lingeringly.
To act or proceed slowly or without enthusiasm; to be reluctant.
To draw along (something burdensome); hence, to pass in pain or with difficulty.
To serve as a clog or hindrance; to hold back.
To operate a pointing device by moving it with a button held down; to move, copy, etc. (an item) in this way.
To unintentionally rub or scrape on a surface.
To hit or kick off target.
To fish with a dragnet.
To search for something, as a lost object or body, by dragging something along the bottom of a body of water.
To break (land) by drawing a drag or harrow over it; to harrow.
To search exhaustively, as if with a dragnet.
To play at a slower tempo than one is supposed to or than the other musicians one is playing with, or to inadvertently gradually decrease tempo while one is playing.
To roast, say negative things about, or call attention to the flaws of (someone).
To inhale from a cigarette, cigar, etc.
To drag something on.
To perform as a drag queen or drag king.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Michael was dragging something behind him.
William dragged Sandra to the bathroom.
James dragged Amanda to a restaurant.
I'm not going to drag their suitcases around.
I dragged myself out of bed and went to work.
I'm sorry that you got dragged into all this.

etymology.text: From Middle English draggen (“to drag”), early Middle English dragen (“to draw, carry”), confluence of Old English dragan (“to drag, draw, draw oneself, go, protract”) and Old Norse draga (“to draw, attract”); both from Proto-Germanic *draganą (“to draw, drag”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰregʰ- (“to draw, drag”).

senses.definition: A wind instrument consisting of a tube, often lined with holes to allow for adjustment in pitch, sounded by blowing into the tube.
A tube used to produce sound in an organ; an organ pipe.
The key or sound of the voice.
A high-pitched sound, especially of a bird.
A rigid tube that transports water, steam, or other fluid, as used in plumbing and numerous other applications.
A water pipe.
A tubular passageway in the human body such as a blood vessel or the windpipe.
A large container for storing liquids or foodstuffs; now especially a vat or cask of cider or wine. (See a diagram comparing cask sizes.)
The contents of such a vessel, as a liquid measure, sometimes set at 126 wine gallons; half a tun.
Decorative edging stitched to the hems or seams of an object made of fabric (clothing, hats, curtains, pillows, etc.), often in a contrasting color; piping.
A vertical conduit through the Earth's crust below a volcano through which magma has passed, often filled with volcanic breccia.
One of the goalposts of the goal.
An elongated or irregular body or vein of ore.
A mechanism that enables one program to communicate with another by sending its output to the other as input.
The character |.
A hollow stem with a bowl at one end used for smoking, especially a tobacco pipe but also including various other forms such as a water pipe.
A man's penis.
A type of pasta similar to macaroni.
senses.native: 一種類似通心粉的義大利麵（筆管麵）

senses.definition: An anonymous satire or essay, insulting and frequently libellous, written on a piece of paper which was rolled up and left somewhere public where it could be found and thus spread, to embarrass the author's enemies.
A data backbone, or broadband Internet access.

examples.text: Water poured from the broken pipe.
examples.translation: 水從破裂的水管傾瀉而出。

examples.text: The sewage pipe is obstructed.
examples.translation: 下水道堵了。

examples.text: This pipe is carved from meerschaum.
He was sitting there with a pipe in his mouth.
examples.translation: 他口裡含著菸斗,坐在那兒.

examples.text: Grandfather talked to me with a pipe in his mouth.
examples.translation: 爺爺叼著煙管跟我說話。

examples.text: The woodwind section includes both pipes and reeds.
examples.translation: 木管樂器組中包含無簧片管樂器與簧片管樂器。

etymology.text: From Middle English pīpe, pype (“hollow cylinder or tube used as a conduit or container; duct or vessel of the body; musical instrument; financial records maintained by the English Exchequer, pipe roll”), from Old English pīpe (“pipe (musical instrument); the channel of a small stream”), from Proto-West Germanic *pīpā. Reinforced by Vulgar Latin *pīpa, from Latin pipire, pipiare, pipare, from pīpiō (“to chirp, peep”), of imitative origin. Displaced native Old English fealh and Old English þrūh.

senses.definition: To criticise harshly; to reprove.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Don't rebuke him for that.
examples.translation: 不要因為那件事責備他。

examples.text: Mary is rebuking Tom.
examples.translation: 瑪麗正在責備湯姆。

examples.text: He who rebukes the world is rebuked by the world.
examples.translation: 責備世界的人，會被世界責備。

examples.text: Even Satan rebukes you.
examples.translation: 連撒旦也在責備你。

examples.text: He was rebuked for writing such a rough report.
examples.translation: 他因寫了一份如此粗糙的報告而被責備。

examples.text: The minister was rebuked in public.
examples.translation: 該部長在公眾面前受到了斥責。

etymology.text: From Middle English rebuken, from Anglo-Norman rebuker (“to beat back, repel”), from re- + Old French *buker, buchier, buschier (“to strike, hack down, chop”), from busche (“wood”), from Vulgar Latin *busca (“wood, grove”), from Frankish *busk (“grove”), from Proto-Germanic *buskaz (“bush”); equivalent to re- + bush.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 rebuken，來自盎格魯 - 諾曼語 rebuker（「擊退、抵禦」），由前綴 re- 加上古法語 *buker, buchier, buschier（「打擊、砍伐」）組成，後者源於 busche（「樹木」），再源自通俗拉丁語 *busca（「樹木、叢林」），最終來自弗蘭克語 *busk（「叢林」），與原始日耳曼語 *buskaz（「灌木叢」）相當。

senses.definition: Of, or relating to glaciers.
Very slow.
Cold and icy.
Having the appearance of ice.
Cool and unfriendly.

examples.text: Glacial water gets its colour from rock flour.
examples.translation: 冰川水因其顏色來自岩石粉塵而呈現色澤。

examples.text: There are three glacial fjords in Ireland.
examples.translation: 愛爾蘭有三個冰川峽灣。

examples.text: Glacial meltwater is not purer than other types of water.
examples.translation: 冰川融水不如其他類型的水純淨。

examples.text: The melted snowpack seeps down to fill mountainside indentations to form glacial lakes.
examples.translation: 融化的積雪滲透下去，填滿山邊的凹陷處，形成冰川湖。

examples.text: This project runs at a glacial pace.
examples.translation: 這個專案進展緩慢如冰川。

examples.text: In front of the fireplace, they shared stories to forget the glacial winter nights.
examples.translation: 壁爐前，他們分享故事以忘卻那寒冷無情的冬夜。

relations.native: 與礦床或開採地有關的

etymology.text: Borrowed from French glacial, from Latin glaciālis, from glaciēs (“ice”). The sense "slow" refers to the speed of actual glaciers, typically around 1 meter per day.
etymology.native: 借自法語 glacial，源於拉丁語 glaciālis，來自 glaciēs（冰）。「緩慢」之意指實際冰川的速度，通常每天約一米。

senses.definition: A hard growth of keratin that protrudes from the top of the head of certain animals, usually paired.
An instrument resembling a musical horn and used to signal others.
A loud alarm, especially one on a motor vehicle.
A sound signaling the expiration of time.
A conical device used to direct waves.
A peninsula or projecting tract of land.

Any similar real or imaginary growth or projection such as the elongated tusk of a narwhal, the eyestalk of a snail, the pointed growth on the nose of a rhinoceros, or the hornlike projection on the head of a demon or similar.
An antler.
The hard substance from which animals' horns are made, sometimes used by man as a material for making various objects.
A vessel made from a horn, to contain drink, ink, gunpowder, etc.
One of the two corners of a crescent, particularly of the crescent moon
The high pommel of a saddle; also, either of the projections on a lady's saddle for supporting the leg.
The Ionic volute.

Cognate with Norwegian flak (“slice, sliver”, literally “piece torn off”), Swedish flak (“a thin slice”), Danish flage (“flake”), German Flocke (“flake”), Dutch vlak (“smooth surface, plain”) and vlok (“flake”), as well as with La
etymology.native: 「flake」源自中世英文 flake（雪片），來自古英語 flacca 和／或古諾斯語 flak（鬆散或撕裂的碎片），又源自原始日耳曼語 *flaką（扁平之物），再溯源自原始印歐語 *pleh₂-（平坦、寬廣）。與挪威語 flak（切片、薄片，字面為「撕下的碎片」）、瑞典語 flak（薄片）、丹麥語 flage（碎屑）、德語 Flocke（碎屑）、荷蘭語 vlak（平滑表面）及 vlok（碎屑）同源，亦與拉丁語相關。

senses.definition: To trouble aggressively, to harass.

To be irritated; to fret.

Her continuous chatter vexes me.

senses.definition: To puzzle, perplex, baffle, bewilder (somebody); to afflict by being complicated, contradictory, or otherwise difficult to understand.
To mix up, muddle up (one thing with another); to mistake (one thing for another).
To mix thoroughly; to confound; to disorder.
To be confused.
To make uneasy and ashamed; to embarrass.
To rout; discomfit.

examples.text: We're still a little confused.
examples.translation: 我們還是有點疑惑。

examples.text: I was awfully confused by his question.
examples.translation: 我對他的問題感到非常困惑。

etymology.text: Back-formation from confused, from Middle English confused (“frustrated, ruined”), from Anglo-Norman confus, from Latin cōnfūsus, past participle of cōnfundō.

senses.definition: To campaign.
To get a batsman out stumped.
To bowl down the stumps of (a wicket).
To walk heavily or clumsily, plod, trudge.
To reduce to a stump; to truncate or cut off a part of.

examples.text: He’s been stumping for that reform for months.
examples.translation: 他已經為那項改革競選了數月之久。

examples.text: Tom and Mary are really stumped.
examples.translation: 湯姆和瑪麗真的被難倒了。

examples.text: Tom was stumped by the problem.
examples.translation: 湯姆被這個問題難住了。

examples.translation: 這個問題讓我難住了。

etymology.text: From Middle English stumpe, stompe (“stump”), from or akin to Middle Low German stump (“stump”) or Middle Dutch stomp, from Old Saxon or Old Dutch *stump, from Proto-West Germanic *stump, from Proto-Germanic *stumpaz (“stump, blunt, part cut off”). Displaced native Old English stofn.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 stump, stompe（樹樁），與中古低地德語 stump 或中古荷蘭語 stomp 相近，來自古薩克森語或古荷蘭語 *stump，源自原始西日耳曼語 *stump，再源自原始日耳曼語 *stumpaz（樹樁、鈍物、被切下的部分）。

senses.definition: To speak ambiguously or enigmatically.
To solve, answer, or explicate a riddle or question.
To put something through a riddle or sieve; to sieve; to sift.
To fill with holes like a riddle.
To fill or spread throughout; to pervade (with something destructive or weakening).
senses.native: 充斥、瀰漫（破壞或削弱性的事物）

senses.definition: To plait.

examples.text: If you solve this riddle, you're a genius.
Riddle me this.
You have to riddle the gravel before you lay it on the road.
Your argument is riddled with errors.
The shots from his gun began to riddle the targets.

etymology.text: From Middle English redel, redels, from Old English rǣdels, rǣdelse (“counsel, opinion, imagination, riddle”), from Proto-West Germanic *rādislī (“counsel, conjecture”). Analyzable as rede (“advice”) + -le. Akin to Old English rǣdan (“to read, advise, interpret”). Cognate with Dutch raadsel, German Rätsel.

senses.definition: To provide with a surface; to apply a surface to.
To rise to the surface.
To bring to the surface.
To come out of hiding.
come to the surface
put a coat on; cover the surface of; furnish with a surface
appear or become visible; make a showing
To become known or apparent; to appear or be found; to come to light.
To make (information, facts, content, etc) known.
To work a mine near the surface.

examples.text: Fadil's body surfaced under the bridge.
examples.translation: 法迪爾的屍體在橋下浮現。

examples.text: The crew surfaced the road with bitumen.
examples.translation: 船員用瀝青鋪平道路。

examples.text: There was great relief when the missing diver finally surfaced.
examples.translation: 當失蹤的潛水員終於浮上水面時，大家鬆了一口氣。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French surface. By surface analysis, sur- + face. Doublet of superficies.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀法語的表面。由表面分析可知，sur- + face。是 superficies 的同義詞。

senses.definition: on the surface

examples.text: Surface materials of the moon.
examples.translation: 月球表面物質。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French surface. By surface analysis, sur- + face. Doublet of superficies.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀法語的表面。由表面分析可知，sur- + face。是 superficies 的同義詞。

senses.definition: Located above, especially over the head.

senses.definition: Kicked over one's own head.
senses.native: 把東西踢過自己的頭頂

examples.text: Place your luggage in the overhead lockers.

etymology.text: From Middle English owerheved, over-hed, over hede (adverb), from Old English oferhēafod (adverb), equivalent to over- + head. Compare German Low German overhoopt, överhoopt, German überhaupt. Piecewise doublet of overchief.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 owerheved，由 over- 加上 head 組成。與德語低地德語 überhoopt 相當。

senses.definition: To come or be in sight; to be in view; to become visible.
To come before the public.
To stand in presence of some authority, tribunal, or superior person, to answer a charge, plead a cause, etc.; to present oneself as a party or advocate before a court, or as a person to be tried.
To seem; to have a certain semblance; to look.
To become visible to the apprehension of the mind; to be known as a subject of observation or comprehension, or as a thing proved; to be obvious or manifest.
To bring into view

examples.text: It would appear that you're wrong.
examples.translation: 你似乎錯了。

examples.text: She appears to have many friends.
examples.translation: 她看起來好像有很多朋友。

examples.text: It appears that he is mistaken.
examples.translation: 看來他搞錯了。

examples.text: She appears to have a headache.
examples.translation: 她看起來頭痛的樣子。

examples.text: That house appears deserted.
examples.translation: 那幢房子看起來被遺棄了。

examples.text: The king will appear in person tomorrow evening.
examples.translation: 國王明晚會親自出現。

etymology.text: From Middle English apperen, aperen, borrowed from Old French aparoir (French apparoir), from Latin appāreō (“to appear”), from ad (“to”) + pāreō (“to come forth, to become visible”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂-s- (“watch, see”), s-present of *peh₂- (“protect”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（apperen、aperen），借自古法語（aparoir），來自拉丁語（appāreō）「出現」，由（ad）「向」加（pāreō）「顯現」組成，最終可溯至原始印歐語（*peh₂-s-）「觀看」。

senses.definition: To issue forth, as water from the earth; to flow; to spring.
To have something seep out of the surface.

examples.text: Tears welled in Mary's eyes as Tom told her about his sad childhood.

etymology.text: From Middle English wel, wal, wol, wele, from Old English wel (“well, abundantly, very, very easily, very much, fully, quite, nearly”), from Proto-Germanic *wela, *wala (“well”, literally “as wished, as desired”), from Proto-Indo-European *welh₁- (“wish, desire”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（wel、wele），來自古英語（wel）「好、豐富地、非常、完全」，經原始日耳曼語（*wela）「如願地」，上溯至原始印歐語（*welh₁-）「希望、想要」。

senses.definition: The terminal point of something in space or time.
Death.
The most extreme point of an object, especially one that is longer than it is wide.
A single warp thread.
A key that when pressed causes the cursor to go to the last character of the current line.
Share of joint responsibility.
The cessation of an effort, activity, state, or motion.
Result.
A purpose, goal, or aim.
One of the two parts of the ground used as a descriptive name for half of the ground.
The position at the end of either the offensive or defensive line, a tight end, a split end, a defensive end.
A period of play in which each team throws eight rocks, two per player, in alternating fashion.
An ideal point of a graph or other complex. See End (graph theory)
That which is left; a remnant; a fragment; a scrap.
Money.

examples.text: The meeting will end tomorrow.
examples.translation: 會議明天就結束了。

examples.text: What time does your class end?
examples.translation: 您幾點下課？

examples.text: Everyone must learn on their own in the end.
examples.translation: 到了最後，大家一定要靠自己學習。

examples.text: You must put an end to this foolish behavior.
examples.translation: 你該結束這種愚蠢的行為了。

examples.text: I was at my wit's end when I heard the news.
examples.translation: 當我聽到這個消息時, 我束手無策。

examples.text: You must complete the treatment until the end.
examples.translation: 你必須堅持完成治療。

etymology.text: From Middle English ende, from Old English ende, from Proto-West Germanic *andī, from Proto-Germanic *andijaz (“end”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂entíos (“forehead; front”), from *h₂ent- (“face; forehead; front”), from *h₂en- (“on, onto”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語與古英語（ende），經原始日耳曼語（*andijaz）「末端」，上溯至原始印歐語（*h₂entíos）「前額、前面」，再來自（*h₂ent-）「臉、前面」。

senses.definition: A bounding straight edge of a two-dimensional shape.
One half (left or right, top or bottom, front or back, etc.) of something or someone.
One surface of a sheet of paper (used instead of "page", which can mean one or both surfaces.)
Sidespin; english
A line of descent traced through a particular relative, usually a parent or spouse, as distinguished from that traced through another.
The batters faced in an inning by a particular pitcher.
A written monologue or part of a scene to be read by an actor at an audition.
A person who prefers not to engage in anal sex during same-sex sexual activity.
A flat surface of a three-dimensional object; a face.
A region in a specified position with respect to something.
The portion of the human torso usually covered by the arms when they are not raised; the areas on the left and right between the belly or chest and the back.
One possible aspect of a concept, person, or thing.
One set of competitors in a game.
A sports team.
A group of morris dancers who perform together.
A group having a particular allegiance in a conflict or competition.
A recorded piece of music; a record, especially in jazz.
A television channel, usually as opposed to the one currently being watched (from when there were only two channels).
A dish that accompanies the main course; a side dish.
An unjustified air of self-importance; a conceited attitude.

examples.text: This medicine doesn't have side effects.
