examples.text: This medicine has no side effects.
examples.translation: 這藥沒有副作用。

examples.text: We were attacked from both sides.
examples.translation: 我們被兩面夾擊了。

examples.text: First, I should hear both sides.
examples.translation: 首先，我要聽聽雙方的意見。

examples.text: He always takes sides with her.
examples.translation: 他總是支持她。

examples.text: Many thousands on both sides had been wounded.
examples.translation: 雙方都有幾千人受傷。

etymology.text: From Middle English side, from Old English sīde (“side, flank”), from Proto-Germanic *sīdǭ (“side, flank, edge, shore”), derived from *sīdaz, probably from Proto-Indo-European *seh₁- (“long, lasting”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian Siede (“side”), West Frisian side (“side”), Dutch zijde, zij (“side”), German Low German Sied (“side”), German Seite (“side”), Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, and Norwegian Nynorsk side (“side”), Swedish sida (“side”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（side），來自古英語（sīde）「側邊、腰側」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*sīdǭ）「側面、邊緣、岸」，可能最終來自原始印歐語（*seh₁-）「長的」。與荷蘭語（zijde）、德語（Seite）、瑞典語（sida）同源。

senses.definition: The boundary line of a surface.
The thin cutting side of the blade of an instrument, such as an ax, knife, sword, or scythe; that which cuts as an edge does, or wounds deeply, etc.
A connected pair of vertices in a graph.
A one-dimensional face of a polytope. In particular, the joining line between two vertices of a polygon; the place where two faces of a polyhedron meet.
An advantage.
A sharp terminating border; a margin; a brink; an extreme verge.
Sharpness; readiness or fitness to cut; keenness; intenseness of desire.
The border or part adjacent to the line of division; the beginning or early part (of a period of time)
A shot where the ball comes off the edge of the bat, often unintentionally.
A level of sexual arousal that is maintained just short of reaching the point of inevitability, or climax.
The point of data production in an organization (the focus of edge computing), as opposed to the cloud.

examples.text: Will you please hold this edge?

examples.text: Who has the edge now?

examples.text: The bedroom curtains have faded at the edges.

examples.text: She's been feeling a little on edge recently.

examples.text: The sidebar is displayed on the edge of the page below the site logo.

examples.text: A great Empire, like a great Cake, is most easily diminished at the Edges.
examples.translation: 一個偉大的帝國, 就像是一個大蛋糕, 最容易消失的地方就在邊緣。

etymology.text: From Middle English egge, from Old English eċġ, from Proto-West Germanic *aggju, from Proto-Germanic *agjō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp”).
etymology.native: 「蛋」源自中世紀英文 egge，來源為古英語 eċġ，再溯自古西日耳曼語 *aggju，更上溯自古德語 *agjō，最終源自印歐語系 *h₂eḱ-（意為「鋭利」）

senses.definition: To move an object slowly and carefully in a particular direction.

senses.definition: To trim the margin of a lawn where the grass meets the sidewalk, usually with an electric or gas-powered lawn edger.
senses.native: 修剪草坪與人行道交界處的草邊（以電動或汽油修邊機）

senses.definition: To furnish with an edge; to construct an edging.

senses.definition: To form a border to; to enclose, to border.

senses.native: （俚，比喻）因不斷拖延而使（某人）煩躁、惱火

examples.text: That night will be forever edged in my memory.

etymology.text: From Middle English egge, from Old English eċġ, from Proto-West Germanic *aggju, from Proto-Germanic *agjō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp”).
etymology.native: 「蛋」源自中世紀英文 egge，來源為古英語 eċġ，再溯自古西日耳曼語 *aggju，更上溯自古德語 *agjō，最終源自印歐語系 *h₂eḱ-（意為「鋭利」）

senses.definition: To walk with long, regular strides, as a soldier does.
To cause someone to walk somewhere.
To go to war; to make military advances.
To make steady progress.
To have common borders or frontiers

examples.text: A brass band is marching along the street.
examples.translation: 一個銅管樂隊沿著路前進。

examples.text: They marched northwest into the Shenandoah Valley.
examples.translation: 他們向西北方向進軍，進入了謝南多厄河谷。

examples.text: We marched under a hail of bullets.
examples.translation: 我們在槍林彈雨之下行進。

examples.text: The march toward progress is really more of a haphazard stagger.
examples.translation: 邁向進步的行軍，其實更像是漫無章法的跌跌撞撞。

etymology.text: From Middle English marchen, from Middle French marcher (“to march, walk”), from Old French marchier (“to stride, to march, to trample”), from Frankish *markōn (“to mark, mark out, to press with the foot”), from Proto-Germanic *markōną (“to mark”). Akin to Old English mearc, ġemearc (“mark, boundary”). Compare mark, from Old English mearcian.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語，來自中古法語「行進、走」，來自古法語「大步走、行軍、踐踏」，來自法蘭克語「做記號、用腳踩壓」，上溯至原始日耳曼語「做記號」。與古英語「標記、邊界」同源；可比較「記號」。

senses.definition: A boundary, the border which one must cross in order to enter or leave a territory.
A value which is known to be greater or smaller than a given set of values.
A sizeable jump, great leap.
A spring from one foot to the other in dancing.
senses.native: 舞蹈中從一腳跳到另一腳

senses.definition: A bounce; a rebound.

examples.text: He boarded a plane bound for Los Angeles.
examples.translation: 他登上了前往洛杉磯的飛機。

examples.text: The plane bound for Beijing is going to take off soon.
examples.translation: 飛往北京的飛機就要起飛了。

examples.text: I'm sorry, I didn't mean to overstep my bounds.
Your naivety knows no bounds.
The deer crossed the stream in a single bound.

etymology.text: From Middle English bound, bund (preterite) and bounden, bunden, ibunden, ȝebunden (past participle), from Old English bund- and bunden, ġebunden respectively. See bind.

senses.definition: To advance very slowly, or by a small amount (in a particular direction).
To drive by inches, or small degrees.
To deal out by inches; to give sparingly.
to burn (to insult); to speak in a cocky and cheeky manner

examples.text: Lukas inched his way closer to the front door.

etymology.text: From Middle English ynche, enche, from Old English ynċe, borrowed from Latin ū̆ncia (“Roman inch, various similar units”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *óynos (“one”). Doublet of ounce, uncia, onça, onza, oka, ouguiya, and awqiyyah.

senses.definition: Either of the two fleshy protrusions around the opening of the mouth.
A part of the body that resembles a lip, such as the edge of a wound or the labia.
The projecting rim of an open container or a bell, etc.; a short open spout.
The edge of a high spot of land.
The sharp cutting edge on the end of an auger.
One of the two opposite divisions of a labiate corolla.
A distinctive lower-appearing of the three true petals of an orchid.
One of the edges of the aperture of a univalve shell.
Backtalk; verbal impertinence.
Embouchure: the condition or strength of a wind instrumentalist's lips.

examples.text: You've got something on your lip.

examples.translation: 每年冬天，我的嘴唇都會乾裂。

examples.text: Read my lips, no new taxes!
examples.translation: 聽好了，不加稅！

examples.text: You have beautiful lips.
examples.translation: 你的嘴唇很漂亮。

examples.text: I have chapped lips.
examples.translation: 我的嘴裂開了。

examples.text: Lips that touch liquor shall not touch mine.
examples.translation: 碰過酒的嘴唇就別想碰我的唇。

senses.definition: A restriction; a bound beyond which one may not go or proceed.

A value to which a sequence converges. Equivalently, the common value of the upper limit and the lower limit of a sequence: if the upper and lower limits are different, then the sequence has no limit (i.e., does not converge).
Any of several abstractions of this concept of limit.
The cone of a diagram through which any other cone of that same diagram can factor uniquely.
Fixed limit.
The final, utmost, or furthest point; the border or edge.
A determining feature; a distinguishing characteristic.
The first group of riders to depart in a handicap race.

senses.definition: A person who is exasperating, intolerable, astounding, etc.
The space or thing defined by limits.
That terminates a period of time; hence, the period itself; the full time or extent.
A restriction; a check or curb; a hindrance.

examples.text: They've upped my limit.
examples.translation: 他們把我的限制提高了。

examples.text: Don't go beyond the speed limit.
examples.translation: 不要超速。

examples.text: My patience is nearing its limit.

etymology.native: 源自中古英語（limit），來自古法語（limit），再源自拉丁語（līmes、līmit-）「田間小徑、邊界、界線」。取代了古英語原有的（ġemǣre）。與（limes）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: The part of the human torso forming a relatively horizontal surface running away from the neck.

A cut of meat comprising the upper joint of the foreleg and the surrounding muscle.
The portion of a garment where the shoulder is clothed.
Anything forming a shape resembling a human shoulder.
A usually unsealed strip of land bordering a road, where vehicles can drive or park in an emergency.
The portion of a hill or mountain just below the peak.
A lateral protrusion of a hill or mountain.
The angle of a bastion included between the face and flank.
An abrupt projection which forms an abutment on an object, or limits motion, etc., such as the projection around a tenon at the end of a piece of timber.

senses.definition: To become attached or fixed; to adhere.

examples.text: There's bamboo growing in the garden.
examples.translation: 花園裡有竹子在生長。

examples.text: Tom grows strawberries in his garden.
examples.translation: 湯姆在他的院子裡種著草莓。

examples.text: Great oaks from little acorns grow.
examples.translation: 高大的橡樹是從一顆小小的橡子成長而來的。

examples.text: My father's hobby is growing roses.
examples.translation: 我父親的嗜好是種玫瑰花。

examples.text: I didn't have a bicycle when I was growing up.
examples.translation: 小時候我沒有腳踏車。

examples.text: We didn't have computers when I was growing up.
examples.translation: 我小時候的時候還沒有電腦。

etymology.text: From Middle English growen, from Old English grōwan (“to grow, increase, flourish, germinate”), from Proto-West Germanic *grōan, from Proto-Germanic *grōaną (“to grow, grow green”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰreh₁- (“to grow, become green”).
etymology.native: 此詞源於中古英語 growen，再追溯至古英語 grōwan，意指生長、增加或繁茂。

senses.definition: Covered with leaves.
Containing much foliage.
In the form of leaves (of some material).
Resembling a leaf.
Wealthy, middle- or upper-class.

examples.text: Algiers needs more beautiful and leafy trees.
examples.translation: Algiers 需要更多美麗且蔥鬱的樹木。

examples.text: There are many avenues in this leafy part of town.
examples.translation: 這片蔥鬱的社區裡有很多林蔭大道。

examples.text: Try to eat more leafy green vegetables.
examples.translation: 試著多吃一些綠葉蔬菜。

examples.text: I was surprised that when I heard that people really don't eat leafy vegetables.
examples.translation: 我驚訝地發現，有人真的不吃綠葉蔬菜。

examples.text: That insect can only be found in very dense leafy forests.
examples.translation: 這種昆蟲只能在非常茂密的蔥鬱森林中找到。

examples.text: The deer only ate the leafy tips of the bush, not the branches.
examples.translation: 那隻鹿只吃灌木的蔥鬱頂端，不啃枝幹。

etymology.text: From leaf + -y.
etymology.native: 由葉子加上-y構成。

senses.definition: The act or process by which something is built; construction.
A closed structure with walls and a roof.
Synonym of Tits building.

examples.text: New York bristles with towering buildings.
examples.translation: 紐約充滿著高樓大廈。

examples.text: This building is LEED Platinum certified.
examples.translation: 該建築已獲 LEED 白金認證。

examples.text: Special forces surrounded the building.
examples.translation: 特種部隊包圍了建築物。

examples.text: The building is seven stories high.
examples.translation: 這棟建築物有七層樓高。

examples.text: The soldiers occupied the building.
examples.translation: 士兵們佔領了這個建築。

examples.text: I wonder when this building was constructed.
examples.translation: 我很好奇那個建築物是什麼時候建造的。

etymology.text: From Middle English byldynge, buyldyng, byldyng, buldynge, buldyng, boldyng, equivalent to build + -ing. Compare also related Middle English bold (“edifice, castle, mansion”), from Old English bold (“building, dwelling, house”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 byldynge、buyldyng、byldyng、buldynge、buldyng、boldyng，意為 build + -ing。亦可參照中古英語 bold（意為建築物、城堡、大宅），源自古英語 bold（意為建築、居所、房屋）。

senses.definition: present participle and gerund of build

examples.text: They shone like stars in the dark, dirty building.
examples.translation: 在又黑又髒的大廈裏，它們就像星星一樣地閃耀著。

etymology.text: From Middle English byldynge, buyldyng, byldyng, buldynge, buldyng, boldyng, equivalent to build + -ing. Compare also related Middle English bold (“edifice, castle, mansion”), from Old English bold (“building, dwelling, house”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 byldynge、buyldyng、byldyng、buldynge、buldyng、boldyng，意為 build + -ing。亦可參照中古英語 bold（意為建築物、城堡、大宅），源自古英語 bold（意為建築、居所、房屋）。

senses.definition: Persons forming or belonging to a particular group, such as a nation, class, ethnic group, country, family, etc.
A group of persons regarded as being servants, followers, companions or subjects of a ruler or leader.
One's colleagues or employees.
A person's ancestors, relatives or family.
The mass of a community as distinguished from a special class (elite); the commonalty; the populace; the vulgar; the common crowd; the citizens.
People in general, humans, by extension sentient beings real or fictional.
senses.native: 人類；泛指人，包括真實或虛構的有感生物

examples.text: People established churches and schools there.
examples.translation: 人們在那裡建立了教堂和學校。

examples.text: The Japanese people have renounced war.
examples.translation: 日本人放棄了戰爭。

examples.text: The Japanese are an industrious people.
examples.translation: 日本人是勤奮的國民。

examples.text: He liberated the people from bondage.
examples.translation: 他讓人們擺脫了奴役。

examples.text: People who will lie for you, will lie to you.
examples.translation: 會為你說謊的人，就會對你說謊。

examples.text: Two hundred people died of cholera last year.
examples.translation: 去年有兩百人因霍亂死亡。

etymology.text: From Middle English puple, peple, peeple, from Anglo-Norman people, from Old French pueple, peuple, pople, from Latin populus (“a people, nation”), from Old Latin populus, from earlier poplus, from even earlier poplos, from Proto-Italic *poplos (“army”) of unknown origin. Doublet of pueblo. Gradually ousted native English lede and, partially, folk.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 puple、peple 或 peeple，來自盎格魯 - 諾曼人的 people，再源自舊法語的 pueple、peuple 等，最終來自拉丁語 populus（「人民、民族」），其詞源可追溯至更早的拉丁語 poplus 及原始義大利語 *poplos（意為「軍隊」），具體起源不明。它與 pueblo 同源，逐漸取代了本土英語中的 lede 和 folk。

senses.definition: An institution dedicated to teaching and learning; an educational institution.
An educational institution providing primary and secondary education, prior to tertiary education (college or university).
An art movement, a community of artists.
The followers of a particular doctrine; a particular way of thinking or particular doctrine; a school of thought.
At Eton College, a period or session of teaching.
Within a larger educational institution, an organizational unit, such as a department or institute, which is dedicated to a specific subject area.
The time during which classes are attended or in session in an educational institution.
The room or hall in English universities where the examinations for degrees and honours are held.
The canons, precepts, or body of opinion or practice, sanctioned by the authority of a particular class or age.
An establishment offering specialized instruction, as for driving, cooking, typing, coding, etc.
A group of fish or a group of marine mammals such as porpoises, dolphins, or whales.
A multitude.

examples.text: This school supplies students with textbooks.
examples.translation: 這所學校為學生提供教科書。

examples.text: People established churches and schools there.
examples.translation: 人們在那裡建立了教堂和學校。

examples.text: School starts in September in Europe.
examples.translation: 歐洲的學校在九月開學。

examples.text: I miss my elementary school teachers.
examples.translation: 我很想念我小學的老師。

examples.text: Dave never returned to school again.
examples.translation: 大衛再也沒有回到學校了。

examples.text: You didn't come to school yesterday, did you?
examples.translation: 你昨天沒來學校, 是嗎?

etymology.text: From Middle English scole, from Old English scōl (“place of education”), from Proto-West Germanic *skōlu, from Late Latin schola, scola (“learned discussion or dissertation, lecture, school”), from Ancient Greek σχολή (skholḗ, “spare time, leisure”), from Proto-Indo-European *seǵʰ- (“to hold, have, possess”). Doublet of schola and shul.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（scole），來自古英語（scōl）「教育場所」，來自後期拉丁語（schola）「學術討論、講課、學校」，再來自古希臘語（skholḗ）「閒暇」，上溯至原始印歐語（*seǵʰ-）「持有」。

senses.definition: An establishment that provides accommodation and other services for paying guests; normally larger than a guesthouse, and often one of a chain.
A large town house or mansion; a grand private residence, especially in France.
A public house or pub.
A restaurant; any dining establishment.
The larger red property in the game of Monopoly, in contradistinction to houses.
The guest accommodation and dining section of a cruise ship.

examples.text: This hotel has accommodations for 1,000 guests.
examples.translation: 這家飯店可以容納一千人。

examples.text: Tom broke into Mary's hotel room.
examples.translation: 湯姆闖進了瑪麗的飯店房間。

examples.text: Are you staying at this hotel?
examples.translation: 你住在這家旅館嗎？

examples.text: I am staying at the hotel for the time being.
examples.translation: 目前我待在飯店。

examples.text: How far is it from the airport to the hotel?
examples.translation: 從機場到旅館多遠？

examples.text: I'd like to put some things in the hotel safe.
examples.translation: 我想在飯店的保險櫃裡存點東西。

relations.native: 度假勝地、度假村、渡假村

etymology.text: Borrowed from French hôtel, from Middle French hostel, from Old French ostel, from Late Latin hospitālis (“hospice, shelter, guesthouse”), from Latin hospitālis (“hospitable”). Doublet of hostel and hospital.
etymology.native: 借自法語（hôtel），來自中古法語（hostel）、古法語（ostel），再源自晚期拉丁語（hospitālis）「招待所、庇護所」，來自拉丁語（hospitālis）「好客的」。與（hostel）、（hospital）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: A corridor; a hallway.
A large meeting room.
A manor house (originally because a magistrate's court was held in the hall of his mansion).
A building providing student accommodation at a university.
The principal room of a secular medieval building.
A place for special professional education, or for conferring professional degrees or licences.
A living room.
A college's canteen, which is often but not always coterminous with a traditional hall.
A meal served and eaten at a college's hall.
Hall class, a class of steam locomotive used on the GWR.
Cleared passageway through a crowd, as for dancing.

examples.text: There's a telephone in the hall.
examples.translation: 走廊裡有一部電話。

examples.text: Leave your umbrella in the hall.
examples.translation: 把你的雨傘放在走廊裡。

examples.text: This hall can hold 5,000 people.
examples.translation: 這個大廳可以容納5000個人。

examples.text: Can we speak in the hall?
examples.translation: 我們能在走廊裡說話嗎？

examples.text: Where is the city hall?
examples.translation: 市政府在哪裡?

examples.text: The number of the chairs in the hall is 80.
examples.translation: 大廳裡有八十張椅子。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English halle (“hall”), from Old English heall (“hall, dwelling, house, palace, temple, law-court”), from Proto-West Germanic *hallu (“hall”), from Proto-Germanic *hallō (“hall”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱel- (“to hide, conceal”).

senses.definition: The part of the forelimb below the forearm or wrist in humans and other primates, and the corresponding part in many other animals.
An index or pointer on a dial; such as the hour and minute hands on the face of an analog clock, which are used to indicate the time of day.
A side; part, camp; direction, either right or left.
A performer more or less skilful.
An instance of helping.
Handwriting; style of penmanship.
A person's autograph or signature.
Promise, word; especially of a betrothal.
Personal possession; ownership.
Management, domain, control.
A limb of certain animals, such as the foot of a hawk, or any one of the four extremities of a monkey.
The set of cards held by a player.
A round of a card game.
A bundle of tobacco leaves tied together.
A bunch of bananas, a typical retail amount, where individual fruits are fingers.
Four inches, a hand's breadth.
Three inches.
Power of performance; means of execution; ability; skill; dexterity.
An agent; a servant, or manual laborer; a workman, trained or competent for special service or duty.
senses.native: 代理人；僕役或雇工；受過專業訓練、能勝任特定工作的工人

senses.definition: A hand which is free to assist; especially due to having one's hands full or otherwise fully preoccupied.

examples.text: All the students clapped their hands.
examples.translation: 所有的學生都拍手。

examples.text: Wash your hands before each meal.
examples.translation: 飯前洗手

examples.text: She greeted him waving her hand.
examples.translation: 她揮著手向他打招呼。

examples.text: You haven't washed your hands yet, have you?
examples.translation: 你還沒洗手，不是嗎？

examples.text: I entered the room and shook hands with him.
examples.translation: 我走進了房間與他握手。

examples.text: My right hand is Uighur, and my left is Han.
examples.translation: 我的右手是維族的，左手是漢族的。

etymology.text: From Middle English hond, hand, from Old English hand, from Proto-West Germanic *handu, from Proto-Germanic *handuz.
etymology.native: 「hand」源自中世紀英文 hond，來自古英文 hand，再溯源自原始西日耳曼語 *handu，更上溯至原始日耳曼語 *handuz。

senses.definition: To give, pass or transmit with the hand, literally or figuratively.
To lead, guide, or assist with the hand; to conduct.
To furl (a sail).
To manage.
To seize; to lay hands on.
To pledge by the hand; to handfast.
To cooperate.

examples.text: Have you handed in your homework?
examples.translation: 你交功課了嗎？

examples.text: Tom handed the envelope full of cash to Mary.
examples.translation: 湯姆把裝滿現金的信封遞給瑪麗。

etymology.text: From Middle English hond, hand, from Old English hand, from Proto-West Germanic *handu, from Proto-Germanic *handuz.
etymology.native: 「hand」源自中世紀英文 hond，來自古英文 hand，再溯源自原始西日耳曼語 *handu，更上溯至原始日耳曼語 *handuz。

senses.definition: The act or process of writing done with the hand, rather than typed or word-processed.
The characteristic writing of a particular person.
Text that was written by hand.
A characteristic trait or hallmark by which somebody may be recognised.

examples.text: She has very nice-looking handwriting.
examples.translation: 她的筆跡很美。

examples.text: Your handwriting is really good!
examples.translation: 你的字寫得真漂亮！

examples.text: My mother has good handwriting.
examples.translation: 我母親的筆跡很好看。

examples.text: She's got terrible handwriting.
examples.translation: 她寫的字很難看。

examples.text: She has beautiful handwriting.
examples.translation: 她的筆跡很美。

examples.text: Do you know whose handwriting this is?
examples.translation: 你知道這是誰的字嗎？

etymology.text: From hand + writing, equal to handwrite + -ing.
etymology.native: 由「手」與「寫」組成，意即手寫加上動名詞尾。

senses.definition: The soft foot of a mammal or other animal, generally a quadruped, that has claws or nails; comparable to a human hand or foot.
A hand.

examples.text: The cat was licking its paws.
examples.translation: 貓正在舔它的爪子。

examples.text: David bandaged the dog's paw.
examples.translation: 戴維給小狗的爪子包紮了。

examples.text: Get your dirty paws off me.
examples.translation: 別用你那髒手碰我。

examples.text: Cookie, sit! Paw! Down! Roll over! Good girl!
examples.translation: 坐好！趴下！滾過來！乖女孩！

examples.text: Boris noticed the paw prints around the camp.
examples.translation: 鮑里斯注意到營地周圍的爪印。

examples.text: The cat was touching the mouse with its paw.
examples.translation: 貓用爪子觸碰著老鼠。

etymology.text: From Middle English pawe, from Old French poue, poe, from Vulgar Latin *pauta. Further origin unknown, perhaps from Frankish *pōta, from Frankish *pōtōn (“to put, stick, plant”), from Proto-Germanic *putōną, whence also Old English potian (“to push”), pȳtan (“to put out, poke out”). See more at put. Doublet of pote, put, and putt.
etymology.native: 詞源不明，可能來自日耳曼語族 *pōta，意為「放置、插入、種植」。

senses.definition: That which complies with justice, law or reason.
A legal, just or moral entitlement.
The right side or direction.
The right hand or fist.
The authority to perform, publish, film, or televise a particular work, event, etc.; a copyright.
The ensemble of right-wing political parties; political conservatives as a group.
The outward or most finished surface, as of a coin, piece of cloth, a carpet, etc.
A wave breaking from right to left (viewed from the shore).

examples.text: Let's discuss the matter right now.
examples.translation: 讓我們馬上討論這個問題吧。

examples.text: This law will deprive us of our basic rights.
examples.translation: 這項法律會剝奪我們的基本權利。

examples.text: He has no right to interfere in our family affairs.
examples.translation: 他無權干涉我們的家庭事務。

examples.text: My right hand is numb.
examples.translation: 我的右手麻了。

etymology.text: From Middle English reȝt, right, righte, riht, riȝt, riȝte, ryght, ryȝt, from Old English reht, reoht, rieht, riht, ryht (“right,” also the word for “straight” and “direct”), from Proto-West Germanic *reht, from Proto-Germanic *rehtaz (“right, straight; just, morally upright”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃reǵtós (“right, straightened”), from *h₃reǵ- (“to straighten; to righten”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（right、riht），來自古英語（riht）「正確的、直的」，經原始日耳曼語（*rehtaz）「正確、筆直、正直」，上溯至原始印歐語（*h₃reǵ-）「弄直」。

senses.definition: The left side or direction.
The left-wing political parties as a group; citizens holding left-wing views as a group.
The left hand or fist.
A punch delivered with the left fist.
A wave breaking from left to right (viewed from the shore).
location near or direction toward the left side; i.e. the side to the north when a person or object faces east
those who support varying degrees of social or political or economic change designed to promote the public welfare
the hand that is on the left side of the body
the piece of ground in the outfield on the catcher's left
a turn toward the side of the body that is on the north when the person is facing east

examples.text: The Left left workers behind, thinking they had a winning demographic coalition. It hasn't really worked out for them yet.

etymology.text: From Middle English left, luft, leoft, lift, lyft, from Old English left, lyft (“weak, clumsy, foolish”), attested in Old English lyftādl (“palsy, paralysis”), from Proto-Germanic *luft-, from *lubjaną (“to castrate, lop off”) (compare dialectal English lib, West Frisian lobje, Dutch lubben), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)lewp-, *(s)lup- (“hanging limply”). Compare Scots left (“left”), North Frisian lefts, leeft, leefts (“left”), West Frisian lofts (“left”), obsolete Dutch lucht, leftsch, lefts,

senses.definition: To let go of; to cease to hold or contain.
To free or liberate; to set free.
To make available to the public.
To discharge.
(of a call) To hang up.
To let go, quit (a legal claim); to discharge or relinquish a right to (lands or buildings) by conveying to another who has some right or estate in possession.
senses.native: 放棄（法律權利）；讓渡（土地權利）

senses.definition: To loosen; to relax; to remove the obligation of.
To set up; to provide with a goalscoring opportunity.
To set free a chemical substance.
To launch; to come out; to become available.
To lease again; to grant a new lease of; to let back.

examples.text: Tom will be released Monday.
examples.translation: 湯姆將於週一釋放。

examples.text: Tom was released in 2013.
examples.translation: 湯姆2013年的時候被釋放了。

examples.text: She'll be released.
examples.translation: 她會被釋放。

examples.text: The first Macintosh PC was released in 1984.
examples.translation: 第一台麥金塔電腦於 1984 年發布。

examples.text: I was three years old when Windows XP was released.
examples.translation: （Windows XP）發行時我三歲。

examples.text: The girl released the birds from the cage.
examples.translation: 女孩把鳥兒從籠中放了出來。

etymology.text: From Middle English relesen, relessen, from Old French relaisser (variant of relascher).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（relesen、relessen），來自古法語（relaisser，relascher 的變體）。

senses.definition: The atmosphere above a given point, especially as visible from the surface of the Earth as the place where the sun, moon, stars, and clouds are seen.
With a descriptive word: the part of the sky which can be seen from a specific place or at a specific time; its climate, condition, etc.
Usually preceded by the: the abode of God or the gods, angels, the souls of deceased people, etc.; heaven; also, powers emanating from heaven.
The set of all lightlike lines (or directions) passing through a given point in space-time.
In an art gallery: the upper rows of pictures that cannot easily be seen; also, the place where such pictures are hung.
A cloud.
A disagreeable person; an enemy.

examples.text: The sky was filled with aeroplanes.
examples.translation: 天上滿是飛機。

examples.text: The sky was ablaze with fireworks.
examples.translation: 天空被焰火點亮。

examples.text: The sky became darker and darker.
examples.translation: 天空變得越來越暗了。

examples.text: The clouds floating in the sky are beautiful.
examples.translation: 天空飄的雲很美。

examples.text: Not a single cloud could be seen in the sky.
examples.translation: 天上萬里無雲。

examples.text: Do you know the reason why the sky looks blue?
examples.translation: 你知道為什麼天看起來這麼藍嗎？

etymology.text: The noun is derived from Middle English sky (“sky; cloud; mist”), also spelled ski, skie, [and other forms], from Old Norse ský (“cloud”), from Proto-Germanic *skiwją (“cloud; sky”), from *skiwô (“cloud; cloud cover, haze; sky”) (whence Old English sċēo (“cloud”) and Middle English skew (“air; sky; (rare) cloud”)), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewH- (“to cover; to conceal, hide”).
etymology.native: 這個名詞源自中古英語 sky（天空、雲霧），也寫作 ski、skie 等，來自古諾斯語 ský（雲），再溯源自原始日耳曼語 *skiwją（雲、天空），來自 *skiwô（雲、霧氣、天空），進而影響古英語 sċēo 與中古英語 skew（空氣、天空、罕見的雲）；而這些詞根又來自原始印歐語 *(s)kewH-（覆蓋、隱藏）

senses.definition: The gases surrounding the Earth or any astronomical body.
The air in a particular place.
The conditions (such as music, illumination, etc.) that can influence the mood felt in an environment.
A unit of measurement for pressure equal to 101325 Pa (symbol: atm), approximately the atmospheric pressure at sea level.
The apparent mood felt in an environment.
senses.native: 環境中感受到的明顯情緒氛圍

senses.definition: Extras in a scene who have no spoken lines.
senses.native: 場景中沒有對白線的配角

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Over 95% of Titan's atmosphere is nitrogen.
examples.translation: 泰坦大氣層超過百分之九十五是氮氣。

examples.text: The atmosphere protects us from meteors.
examples.translation: 大氣層保護我們免受流星撞擊。

examples.text: Can we make Mars' atmosphere breathable?
examples.translation: 我們能讓火星大氣層變得可呼吸嗎？

examples.text: This place has a mysterious atmosphere to it.
examples.translation: 這個地方的氣氛很神秘。

examples.text: The atmosphere in the room was hot and smoky.
examples.translation: 房間裡的大氣層又熱又多煙。

examples.text: The atmosphere is always extremely lively when eating hot pot.
examples.translation: 吃火鍋的時候 ,氣氛往往是非常熱鬧的.

etymology.text: Borrowed from French atmosphère, from New Latin atmosphaera, from Ancient Greek ἀτμός (atmós, “steam”) + σφαῖρα (sphaîra, “sphere”); corresponding to atmo- + -sphere.
etymology.native: 源自法語 atmosphère，來自新拉丁語 atmosphaera，源自古希臘語 ἀτμός（蒸汽）與 σφαῖρα（球體），對應於 atmo- 加上 -sphere。

senses.definition: A rampart of earth, stones etc. built up for defensive purposes.
A structure built for defense surrounding a city, castle etc.
Each of the substantial structures acting either as the exterior of or divisions within a structure.
A fictional bidder used to increase the price at an auction.
A line of defenders set up between an opposing free-kick taker and the goal.
Two or more blockers skating together so as to impede the opposing team.
Any of the surfaces of rock enclosing the lode.
A personal notice board listing messages of interest to a particular user.
A character that has high defenses, thereby reducing the amount of damage taken from the opponent’s attacks.
Face-down tiles arranged in stacked rows from which players draw new tiles.
A point of desperation.
A point of defeat or extinction.
An impediment to free movement.
The butterfly Lasiommata megera.
A barrier.
Something with the apparent solidity, opacity, or dimensions of a building wall.
A means of defence or security.
One of the vertical sides of a container.
senses.native: 容器的垂直側面之一（牆）

senses.definition: A dividing or containing structure in an organ or cavity.
senses.native: 器官或腔室中的分隔或包覆結構（壁）

senses.definition: A doctor who tries to admit as few patients as possible.

examples.text: She decorated the wall with pictures.
examples.translation: 她用繪畫來裝飾牆。

examples.translation: 他們正在拆這面牆。

examples.text: We're going to paint the wall.
examples.translation: 我們準備刷牆。

examples.text: He painted the picture which is on the wall.
examples.translation: 他畫了牆上的那幅畫。

etymology.text: From Middle English wal, from Old English weall (“wall, dike, earthwork, rampart, dam, rocky shore, cliff”), from Proto-West Germanic *wall (“wall, rampart, entrenchment”), from Latin vallum (“wall, rampart, entrenchment, palisade”), from Proto-Indo-European *welH- (“to turn, wind, roll”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 wal，來自古英語 weall（意為「牆、堤壩、土壩、防禦工事、水壩、岩岸、峭壁」），源自古西日耳曼語 *wall（意為「牆、防禦工事、壕溝」），源自拉丁語 vallum（意為「牆、防禦工蹟、木柵欄」），源自印歐語系原始詞 *welH-（意為「轉動、旋轉、滾動」）

senses.definition: To enclose with, or as if with, a wall or walls.
To use a wallhack.
To wallbang.
senses.native: （俚）在遊戲中失控地持續開火（亂射）

senses.definition: To boil.
To well, as water; spring.
To make a wall knot on the end of (a rope).
senses.native: 在繩索末端打出繩結（繩頭結）

examples.text: Put these pictures up us for wall, please.

etymology.text: From Middle English wal, from Old English weall (“wall, dike, earthwork, rampart, dam, rocky shore, cliff”), from Proto-West Germanic *wall (“wall, rampart, entrenchment”), from Latin vallum (“wall, rampart, entrenchment, palisade”), from Proto-Indo-European *welH- (“to turn, wind, roll”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 wal，來自古英語 weall（意為「牆、堤壩、土壩、防禦工事、水壩、岩岸、峭壁」），源自古西日耳曼語 *wall（意為「牆、防禦工事、壕溝」），源自拉丁語 vallum（意為「牆、防禦工蹟、木柵欄」），源自印歐語系原始詞 *welH-（意為「轉動、旋轉、滾動」）

senses.definition: To encircle something or simultaneously extend in all directions.
To enclose or confine something on all sides so as to prevent escape.
To pass around; to travel about; to circumnavigate.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Special forces surrounded the building.
examples.translation: 特種部隊包圍了建築物。

examples.text: This place is surrounded by hills.
examples.translation: 這裡的周圍都是山岡。

examples.text: I'm surrounded by linguaphiles!
examples.translation: 我被各國語言及文字的愛好者所圍繞。

examples.text: Japan is surrounded by sea.
examples.translation: 日本被海環繞著。

examples.text: We were surrounded.
examples.translation: 我們被包圍了。

examples.text: He was surrounded by a throng of reporters.
examples.translation: 他被一大群記者包圍著。

etymology.text: From Middle English sourrounden (“to submerge, overflow”), from Middle French souronder, suronder, from Late Latin superundō, from super + undō (“to rise in waves”), from unda (“wave”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語「淹沒、溢流」，來自中古法語，來自後期拉丁語「溢出」，由「在上」加「起浪」組成，源自「波浪」。

senses.definition: The outermost shape, view, or edge of an object.
The shape, view, or shadow of a person's head from the side; a side view.
A summary or collection of information, especially about a person.
A specific page or field in which users can provide various types of personal information in software or Internet systems.
Reputation, prominence; noticeability.
The amount by which something protrudes.

A smoothed (e.g., troweled or brushed) vertical surface of an excavation showing evidence of at least one feature or diagnostic specimen; the graphic recording of such as by sketching, photographing, etc.
Character; totality of related characteristics; signature; status (especially in scientific, technical, or military uses).
A section of any member, made at right angles with its main lines, showing the exact shape of mouldings etc.
A drawing exhibiting a vertical section of the ground along a surveyed line, or graded work, as of a railway, showing elevations, depressions, grades, etc.
A user's preferences.
An exemption from certain types of duties due to injury or disability.

examples.text: Is my profile picture beautiful?
examples.translation: 我的頭像漂亮嗎？

examples.text: I like your profile picture.
examples.translation: 我喜歡你的頭像。

examples.text: Claudio's Instagram profile had five followers.
Tom always has the cutest profile pictures.
examples.translation: 湯姆永遠有最可愛的頭像。

examples.text: Have you changed your profile picture recently?
examples.translation: 你最近更改過你的頭像嗎？

examples.text: Mary looked nothing like her profile picture.

etymology.text: From French profil, from Italian profilo (“a border”), later also proffilo (“a side-face, profile”), from Latin pro (“before”) + filo (“a line, stroke, thread”), from filum (“a thread”); see file. Doublet of purfle.

senses.definition: A thing that has physical existence but is not alive.
Objective; goal, end or purpose of something.
A person or thing toward which an emotion is directed.
An instantiation of a class or structure.
The noun phrase which is an internal complement of a verb phrase or a prepositional phrase. In a verb phrase with a transitive action verb, it is typically the receiver of the action.
A cause for attention or concern.
An instance of one of the two kinds of entities that form a category, the other kind being the arrows (also called morphisms).
Sight; show; appearance; aspect.

examples.text: UFO stands for unidentified flying object.
examples.translation: 不明飛行物這個縮寫代表無法辨識的飛行物體。

examples.text: Watch out for falling objects!
examples.translation: 當心墜落的東西!

examples.text: I wouldn't object if you wanted to go with her.
examples.translation: 如果你想和她一起去，我不會反對。

examples.text: The house was full of colorful art objects.
examples.translation: 房子裡放滿了五顏六色的藝術品。

examples.text: His main object in life was to become rich.
examples.translation: 他主要的人生目標就是成為一個有錢人。

examples.text: The surface of the object is fairly rough.
examples.translation: 這件物件的表面頗為粗糙。

etymology.text: From Old French object, from Medieval Latin obiectum (“object”, literally “thrown against”), from obiectus, perfect passive participle of obiciō (“to throw against”), from ob- (“against”) + iaciō (“to throw”), as a calque of Ancient Greek ἀντικείμενον (antikeímenon). Doublet of objectum and objet.
etymology.native: 源自古法語，來自中世紀拉丁語「物體」（字面意為「被擲於前方之物」），為「對著…投擲」的完成被動分詞，由「對著」加「投擲」組成，仿譯自古希臘語「對立之物」。與「客體」、「物件（法語）」為同源異形詞。

senses.definition: The state of being difficult, or hard to do.
An obstacle that hinders achievement of a goal.
Physical danger from the environment, especially with risk of drowning
An objection.
That which cannot be easily understood or believed.
An awkward situation or quarrel.

examples.text: He encountered difficulties in his work.
examples.translation: 他在工作上遇到了麻煩。

examples.text: He is confronted by many difficulties.
examples.translation: 他面臨著許多困難。

examples.text: We're not afraid of any difficulties.
examples.translation: 我們不畏懼任何困難。

examples.text: We're having difficulty locating Tom.
examples.translation: 我們找湯姆不容易。

examples.text: He is facing many difficulties.
examples.translation: 他面臨著許多困難。

examples.text: He succeeded in the face of great difficulties.
examples.translation: 面對巨大的困難，他成功了。

etymology.text: From Middle English difficulte, from Middle French and Anglo-Norman difficulte and their etymon Latin difficultas, from difficul, older form of difficilis (“hard to do, difficult”), from dis- + facilis (“easy”); see difficile and difficult. Equivalent to dis- + facile + -ty. Also analysable as difficult + -y, though the adjective is historically a backformation from the noun.

senses.definition: Decorative paper-like material used to cover the inner walls of buildings.
An image or tiled pattern used as the background of a computer desktop.
senses.native: 電腦桌布、電腦壁紙、桌面背景

senses.definition: A roll of such paper.
A style or design of such material.
senses.native: 這種材料的樣式或設計

senses.definition: Anything that serves as a background or part of the surroundings.
senses.native: 任何可作為背景或環境一部分的東西

senses.definition: Generic footage of a building or location that may be used in the background of a related news report.
senses.native: 建築或地點的通用影像，可用於相關新聞報導的背景中

senses.definition: Gaudy mass-produced stamps, typically of little or no value and only produced for sale to collectors.
senses.native: 花哨的大批量生產郵票，通常價值極低，僅為賣給收藏家而製造

senses.definition: A radio operator's collection of awards and QSL cards.
senses.native: 無線電操作員的獎盃與 QSL 卡片收藏

examples.text: The walls were covered with wallpaper.

senses.definition: The feel or shape of a surface or substance; the smoothness, roughness, softness, etc. of something.
The quality given to a work of art by the composition and interaction of its parts.
An image applied to a polygon to create the appearance of a surface.
The act or art of weaving.
Something woven; a woven fabric; a web.
A tissue.

examples.text: Avocados have a buttery texture.

examples.translation: 我真的很喜歡鴨脷的脆口感。

examples.translation: 味道還算不錯，但口感很糟糕。

senses.definition: To create or apply a texture.

examples.translation: 用鏟子在灰泥上拖曳，以製造牆面紋理。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French texture, borrowed from Latin textūra (“a weaving, web, texture, structure”), from textus, past participle of texere (“to weave”). See text. Doublet of tessitura.

senses.definition: The surroundings, circumstances, environment, background or settings that determine, specify, or clarify the meaning of an event or other occurrence.

The trama or flesh of a mushroom.
For a formula: a finite set of variables, which set contains all the free variables in the given formula.
The data (register contents, program counter value, etc.) needed to switch to another thread of execution.

examples.text: It depends on the context.
examples.translation: 這要看情況。

examples.text: Everything in its right context.

examples.text: If I know the context, I understand the text.

senses.definition: Evoking positive feelings regarding gender, like gender euphoria or gender envy.

examples.text: This outfit I'm wearing feels gender as hell. It's incredible that I get to look this hot.

etymology.text: From Middle English gendre, borrowed from Old French gendre, borrowed from Latin genere (“type, kind”). Doublet of genre and genus. The verb developed after the noun. Displaced native Old English hād (“sex, gender”).

senses.definition: Flowing freely like water; fluid; not solid and not gaseous; composed of particles that move freely among each other on the slightest pressure.
Easily sold or disposed of without losing value.
Having sufficient trading activity to make buying or selling easy.
Flowing or sounding smoothly or without abrupt transitions or harsh tones.
Belonging to a class of consonants comprising the laterals and the rhotics, which in many languages behave similarly.
Fluid and transparent.

examples.translation: 你應該喝大量的液體。

examples.translation: 水是液體。凍起來就成了固體。

examples.translation: 一種物質可以是固態、氣態或液態。

senses.definition: filled or brimming with tears
applied to a fish depicted horizontally

etymology.text: From Middle English swymmynge. Equivalent to swim (“to move through water”, verb) + -ing (suffix forming gerunds).

senses.definition: Any of a class of organic compounds (such as ethanol) containing a hydroxyl functional group (-OH).
Beverages containing ethanol, collectively.
Ethanol.
Any very fine powder.

examples.translation: 未經許可，我不能喝酒。

examples.text: Do you drink alcohol every day?
examples.translation: 你每天都喝酒嗎？

examples.translation: 他從不喝酒。

examples.text: I don't drink alcohol.
examples.translation: 我不會喝酒。

examples.text: Don't drive under the influence of alcohol.
examples.translation: 酒後別開車 。

senses.definition: The material of the surrounding environment, e.g. solid, liquid, gas, vacuum, or a specific substance such as a solvent.
A format for communicating or presenting information.
Someone who conveys information from the spirit world.
Anything of a middle rank or position.
One of several common sizes to which an item may be manufactured, smaller than a large but larger than a small.
An item labelled or denoted as being that size.
One who fits an item of that size.
The materials or empty space through which signals, waves, or forces pass.
A nutrient substance, commonly a solution or solid, for the growth of cells in vitro.
A substance, structure, or environment in which living organisms subsist, grow or are cultured.
senses.native: （生物生存或培養的）環境；培養基

senses.definition: A means, channel, agency or go-between through which communication, commerce, etc is conveyed or carried on, or by which an aim is achieved.
The materials used to finish a workpiece using a mass finishing or abrasive blasting process.
A liquid base which carries pigment in paint.
A means of expression, in the arts, such as a material (oil, pastel, clay, etc) or method or style (expressionism, jazz, etc).
The mean or middle term of a syllogism, that by which the extremes are brought into connection.
A middle place or degree.
An average; sometimes the mathematical mean.
A half-pint serving of Guinness (or other stout in some regions).

examples.text: Television is obsolete as a medium in any case.
examples.translation: 無論如何，電視作為媒介已經過時了。

examples.text: It’s a communication medium, not a substance or specific activity.
examples.translation: 網路是一個相通的渠道，而不是物質或具體的活動。

etymology.native: 借自拉丁語（medium），是（medius）「中間的」的中性形式，最終來自原始印歐語（*médʰyos）「在……之間」。比較（middle）。與（mid）、（medio）、（media）、（meson）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: A pigment (or dye)-based fluid used for writing, printing etc.
The black or dark-colored fluid ejected by squid, octopus etc, as a protective strategy.
A particular type, color or container of this fluid.
senses.native: 此流體的特定類型、顏色或容器

senses.definition: Publicity.
Tattoo work.
Cheap red wine.

examples.text: This blotting paper absorbs ink well.
The black ink stained the paper.
She was asked to write her name in ink.
examples.translation: 她被要求用墨水寫下她的名字。

examples.text: An octopus can release ink when it gets into danger.
examples.translation: 章魚遇到危險時會噴出墨汁。

examples.text: My ballpoint pen just ran out of ink.

senses.definition: Of, belonging or relating to music, or to its performance or notation.

Fond of music; discriminating with regard to music; gifted or skilled in music.
Pertaining to a class of games in which players move while music plays, but have to take a fixed position when it stops; by extension, any situation where people repeatedly change positions.

Mozart: one of the great musical prodigies of all time.

senses.definition: A container.

senses.definition: An organ that receives and holds a secretion.
