To bring into disrepute.

examples.text: Tom deserves to be blamed.
examples.translation: 湯姆應當被責備。

examples.text: It is no use blaming him for the accident now.
examples.translation: 事情已經發生了，現在怪他也沒有用。

examples.text: They blamed Tom for causing the accident.
examples.translation: 他們指責湯姆造成了事故。

examples.text: They blamed George for the failure.
examples.translation: 他們把失敗歸咎於喬治。

examples.text: After what happened at the wedding, I wouldn't blame you if you never spoke to them again.

etymology.text: From Middle English blame, borrowed from Old French blame, blasme, produced from the verb blasmer, which in turn is derived from Late Latin blastēmāre, variant of blasphēmāre, from Ancient Greek βλασφημέω (blasphēméō). Doublet of blaspheme. Displaced native Old English tǣling (“blame”) and tǣlan (“to blame”).

senses.definition: To forgive; to pardon; to overlook.
To allow to leave, or release from any obligation.
To provide an excuse for; to justify.
To relieve of an imputation by apology or defense; to make apology for as not seriously evil; to ask pardon or indulgence for.

examples.text: You'll have to make up some kind of excuse.
examples.translation: 你不得不製造一些藉口。

examples.text: Excuse me, do you have any of these in your store?
examples.translation: 請問，這款你們店裡有嗎？

examples.text: I excused myself from the proceedings to think over what I'd heard.

etymology.text: From Middle English excusen (verb) and excuse (noun), borrowed from Old French escuser (verb) and excuse (noun), from Latin excūsō, excūsāre (“to excuse, allege in excuse, literally, free from a charge”), from ex (“out”) + causa (“a charge”); see cause, accuse and recuse. Displaced native Old English lād (“an excuse”) and lādian (“to excuse”).

senses.definition: Followed by of: to free (oneself or someone, or a place) from an annoyance or hindrance.
Followed by away, from, or out of: to remove (oneself or someone, or something, that is annoying, troublesome, or unwanted).
Often followed by from, of, or out of: to free or release, or to rescue or save, (oneself or someone, or something).
To clear (a place or way); especially, to clear (land) of trees, undergrowth, etc.
Sometimes followed by away: to destroy or kill (someone).
Sometimes followed by up: to remove obstacles or refuse from (a place); to clean, to clear out; specifically, to clear or empty (the stomach).
Followed by up: to eradicate (something); to root out, to uproot.
Sometimes followed by away or off: to complete or get through (a task, or work).
Often followed by up: to put (a place, such as a room or a table) in order; to clear, to tidy.
To dismiss (someone) who has attended on a person; (reflexive) to remove (oneself) from a person's presence after attending to them.
To settle (a disagreement).
Followed by of: to deprive (oneself or someone) of something; to strip.
To get away from or get out of (a place); to escape.
To clear land or some other place.
To clear or empty the stomach; also, to clear the throat.
Of work: to be completed.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: How can I rid myself of my inferiority complex?
examples.translation: 我有什麼辦法可以脫離我的自卑情結嗎？

examples.text: This poison is very effective in getting rid of roaches.
examples.translation: 這毒藥用來治蟑螂很有效。

examples.text: I'm trying to rid myself of this bad habit.
We’re trying to rid the world of poverty.
"Get rid of it, of course!" answered the farmer.
examples.translation: 「擺脫它, 當然!」 這個農夫回答。

examples.text: All of us would like to get rid of nuclear weapons.
examples.translation: 我們所有的人都想除掉核子武器。

etymology.text: The verb is derived from Middle English ridden (“to remove debris, obstructions, etc., from (a place), to clear; to complete (something unfinished); to free (someone or something); to relieve (someone); etc.”), probably from Old English *ryddan (“to remove debris, obstructions, etc., from (a place), to clear”) (the past participle form ġeryd is attested), from Proto-Germanic *riudijaną (“to clear”), from Proto-Indo-European *Hrewdʰ- (“to clear land”), or possibly from *Hrew- (“to dig out, tear o

senses.definition: To relinquish (a right etc.); to give up claim to; to forgo.
To relinquish claim on a payment or fee which would otherwise be due.
senses.native: 放棄本應收取的款項或費用

senses.definition: To release [a player] onto the waiver wire
To put aside, avoid.
To outlaw (someone).
To abandon, give up (someone or something).
To move from side to side; to sway.
To stray, wander.

examples.text: Tom and Mary waived their rights.
examples.translation: 湯姆和瑪麗放棄了他們的權利。

examples.text: Has Tom waived his rights?
examples.translation: 湯姆已經放棄他的權利了嗎？

examples.text: They waived their rights.
examples.translation: 他們放棄了權利。

examples.text: We waived those requirements so you can graduate.
examples.translation: 我們免除了那些要求，讓你畢業。

examples.text: Tom does not want to waive his right to a jury trial.
examples.translation: 湯姆不願放棄他的陪審團審判權利。

examples.text: By signing this contract, he waives all rights to his work.
examples.translation: 簽訂這份合約後，他放棄了對作品的所有權利。

etymology.text: From Middle English weyven (“to avoid, renounce”), from Anglo-Norman weyver (“to abandon, allow to become a waif”), from Old French waif (“waif”), from gaiver (“to abandon”), ultimately of Scandinavian/North Germanic origin; see weyver.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 weyven（「避免、放棄」），來自盎格魯 - 諾曼語 weyver（「放棄、成為流浪兒」），再源自舊法語 waif，最終可追溯至斯堪的納維亞或北日耳曼語系。

senses.definition: An ongoing winner in a game or contest.
Someone who is chosen to represent a group of people in a contest.
Someone who fights for a cause or status.
Someone who fights on another's behalf.
A particularly notable member of a plant species, such as one of great size.

examples.text: Politicians are the champions of promises.
The world champions were the Swedes.
He's an Algerian taekwondo champion.
He was an Olympic champion in weightlifting.
Magnus Carlsen is the world chess champion.
The one hundred meter champion is Jamaican.

etymology.text: From Middle English champioun, from Old French champion, from Medieval Latin campio (“combatant in a duel, champion”), from Frankish *kampijō (“fighter”), from Proto-West Germanic *kampijō (“combat soldier”), a derivative of *kampijan (“to battle, to campaign”), itself a derivative of *kamp (“battlefield, battle”), ultimately a borrowing in West-Germanic from Latin campus (“a field, a plain, a place of action”).

senses.definition: The money originally invested or loaned, on which basis interest and returns are calculated.
The chief administrator of a school.
The chief executive and chief academic officer of a university or college.
A legal person that authorizes another (the agent) to act on their behalf; or on whose behalf an agent or gestor in a negotiorum gestio acts.
The primary participant in a crime.
Either party in a duel.
A partner or owner of a business.
A type of stop on a pipe organ consisting of flue pipes with a bright tonal quality. They are also sometimes referred to as a diapason.
The construction that gives shape and strength to a roof, generally a truss of timber or iron; or, loosely, the most important member of a piece of framing.
The first two long feathers of a hawk's wing.
One of the turrets or pinnacles of waxwork and tapers with which the posts and centre of a funeral hearse were formerly crowned
A dancer at the highest rank within a professional dance company, particularly a ballet company.
A security principal.
A main character or lead actor.
An essential point or rule; a principle.

examples.text: Our school's principal is very old.
examples.translation: 我校校長很老了。

examples.text: He has just become a principal.
examples.translation: 他剛成為一名校長。

examples.text: He must be the principal.
examples.translation: 他一定是校長。

examples.text: I have lost both principal and interest.
examples.translation: 我本金和利息都沒了。

examples.text: The principal severely reproved the students whenever they made a mess in the hallway.
examples.translation: 每次學生把走廊弄得一團糟的時候，校長都會嚴厲地訓斥他們。

examples.text: The visitor was none other than the principal.

etymology.text: From Middle English principal, from Old French principal, from Latin prīncipālis.

senses.definition: To do (something); to execute.
To do (something) in front of an audience, such as acting or music, often in order to entertain.
To exhibit an expected pattern of behavior; to function; to work.
senses.native: 表現、運作，發揮預期功能

senses.definition: Of a man, to be able to initiate or fulfill an act of sexual intercourse.
To act in accordance with (a contract); to fulfill one’s terms of (a contract).
To fulfill contractually agreed-to terms.
senses.native: 履約，履行契約約定的條款

senses.definition: To behave theatrically so as to give the impression of (a quality, character trait, etc.); to feign.
senses.native: 做作地表現（某種特質），假裝

senses.definition: To behave in accordance with, and thereby in turn shape, (a social notion or role).
senses.native: 依照（社會角色）行事，從而塑造它

senses.definition: To behave in ways that carry meaning in social contexts.
senses.native: （社會學）以具有社會意義的方式表現

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: They will perform it.
examples.translation: 他們會執行它。

senses.definition: To spend time idly, absent-mindedly.
To expose to the rays of the Moon.
To adorn with moons or crescents.
To rise in price rapidly or suddenly. (from to the moon)
To shoot the moon.
To display one's buttocks to, typically as a jest, insult, or protest.
To gaze at lovingly or in adoration.
To fuss over something adoringly; to be infatuated with someone.

examples.text: Rick was over the moon about passing the exam.
The hooligans mooned the riot police.

etymology.text: From Middle English mone, from Old English mōna (“moon”), from Proto-West Germanic *mānō, from Proto-Germanic *mēnô (“moon”), from Proto-Indo-European *mḗh₁n̥s (“moon; month”), probably from *meh₁- (“to measure”).

senses.definition: To furnish with galaxies.
To gather together into a luminous whole.

etymology.text: From Middle English galaxye, galaxie, from Old French galaxie, from Latin galaxias, from Ancient Greek γαλαξίας (galaxías, “Milky Way”), shortening of γαλαξίας κύκλος (galaxías kúklos, “milky circle”), from γάλα (gála, “milk”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 galaxye，galaxie，來自古法文 galaxie，源自拉丁文 galaxias，來自古希臘文 γαλαξίας（galaxías，「銀河」），是 γαλαξίας κύκλος（galaxías kúklos，「銀河圈」）的縮寫，而 γάλα（gála，「牛奶」）是其語源。

senses.definition: The status or position of a performer acknowledged to be a star; fame; celebrity.

examples.text: She rose to stardom when she was just twelve.
examples.translation: 她十二歲時便已成名。

examples.text: He was catapulted to international stardom.
examples.translation: 他被推舉至國際巨星之列。

examples.text: Sills' stardom stretched from the highbrow world of the Metropolitan Opera to the playful world of the Muppets on television.
examples.translation: 西爾斯的成名之路從大都會歌劇院的高雅世界延伸至電視上馬戲團的歡樂世界。

examples.text: Stardom meant nothing to her.
examples.translation: 成名對她來說毫無意義。

examples.text: She wants to achieve stardom by singing at the local festival.
examples.translation: 她想透過在當地節日演唱來獲得成名。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Many people dream of reaching stardom through their hard work.
examples.translation: 許多人夢想著透過努力而達到成名。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From star + -dom.
etymology.native: 由星加上後綴 -dom 組成。

senses.definition: An act or instance of purging.
An evacuation of the bowels or the stomach; a defecation or vomiting.
Something which or someone who purges; especially, a medicine that evacuates the intestines; a cathartic.
senses.native: 具清腸效果的人或事物；尤指瀉劑（瀉藥）

senses.definition: A forcible removal of people, for example, from political activity.
senses.native: 強制驅逐（如政治活動中的人員）；清洗

senses.definition: An act or instance of the cleansing of pipes.
A red or reddish liquid that seeps out from raw muscular meat consisting mostly of water and protein; "meat juice".
senses.native: 生肉滲出的紅色或帶紅色的液體（肉汁，主要為水與蛋白質）

senses.definition: The temporarily worsening of acne due to the introduction of skincare products that increase cell turnover, bringing underlying blemishes to the surface more quickly.
senses.native: 使用促進細胞更新的保養品後，原有的暗瘡暫時惡化、浮現的現象（肌膚適應期）

senses.definition: A period of time in which normal rules supposedly do not apply; especially, a time for violence and gang war.
senses.native: （俚）傳說中正常法律不適用的時段（淨化之夜，尤指暴力與幫派火拚）

examples.text: He died in a purge by Stalin.
examples.translation: 他在斯大林的清洗中去世。

etymology.text: From Middle English purgen, from Old French purgier, from Latin pūrgō (“to make pure, to cleanse”), from pūrus (“clean, pure”) + agō (“to make, to do”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 purgen，來自古法文 purgier，源自拉丁文 pūrgō（意為「使純淨、清潔」），由 pūrus（意為「清潔、純淨」）與 agō（意為「使、做」）組成。

senses.definition: To clean, polish, or wash (something) by rubbing and scrubbing it vigorously, frequently with an abrasive or cleaning agent.
To remove debris and dirt (from something) by purging; to sweep along or off by a current of water.
senses.native: 以水流沖刷清除雜物與灰塵；用水流沖刷或掃去

senses.definition: To clear the digestive tract (of an animal) by administering medication that induces defecation or vomiting; to purge.
senses.native: 給予藥物使動物排便或嘔吐，以清理其消化系統；催吐或瀉下

senses.definition: To (cause livestock to) suffer from diarrhoea or dysentery.
To search an area thoroughly.
To run with speed; to scurry.
To move swiftly over; to brush along.
To cleanse (something) without rubbing.

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: The cadaver dogs scoured the woods.
examples.translation: 死狗在森林中奔竄搜尋。

examples.text: I need to scour the city.
examples.translation: 我需要搜尋整座城市。

examples.text: The police scoured every building in town.
examples.translation: 警察搜尋了鎮上每一棟建築。

examples.text: How our cat loves to scour someone else's dishes!
examples.translation: 「我們的貓多愛幫別人的碗盤清潔！」

examples.text: Detective Dan Anderson scoured the scene for evidence.
examples.translation: 偵探丹·安德森在現場搜尋證據。

examples.text: I scoured the neighborhood.
examples.translation: 我搜尋了整個社區。

etymology.text: From Middle English scǒuren (“to polish, scour; to clean; to beat, whip”), from Middle Dutch scuren, schuren (“to clean; to polish”) or Middle Low German schǖren, of uncertain origin but probably from Old French escurer, from Medieval Latin scūrō, escūrō, excūrō (“to clean off”), from ex- (“thoroughly”) + cūrō (“to arrange, see to, take care of”), from cūra (“care, concern”) (from Proto-Indo-European *kʷeys- (“to heed”)) + -ō.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語，意為「拋光、清潔」，可能來自中世紀拉丁語，最終源自印歐語根。

senses.definition: A session of crying.
A sob.
A red or reddish liquid that seeps out from raw muscular meat during storage, consisting mostly of water and protein; "meat juice".
A lapwing; wipe, especially, a northern lapwing (Vanellus vanellus).

examples.text: My mother did nothing but weep.
examples.translation: 我的母親只是默默地哭泣。

examples.text: He that laughs in the morning weeps at night.
examples.translation: 清晨一笑，夜半一哭。

examples.text: To weep is to make less the depth of grief.
examples.translation: 哭泣是減輕悲傷的深度。

examples.text: Aren't there times when you overwhelmingly want to weep?
examples.translation: 有沒有時候你強烈地想要大哭一場？

examples.text: She began to grumble and then to weep.
examples.translation: 她開始抱怨，然後哭泣。

examples.text: Sometimes you just have to have a good weep.
examples.translation: 有時候你只是需要好好大哭一場。

etymology.text: From Middle English wepen, from Old English wēpan (“to weep, complain, bewail, mourn over, deplore”), from Proto-West Germanic *wōpijan, from Proto-Germanic *wōpijaną (“to weep”), from Proto-Indo-European *weh₂b- (“to call, cry, complain”).
etymology.native: 「哭泣」一詞源於中古英語 wepen，再追溯至古英語 wēpan（意為哀悼、悲嘆），其後經日耳曼語族各階段演變，最終源自印歐語系原初詞根 *weh₂b-（意為呼喊、叫喊）。

senses.definition: The process or manner of treating someone or something.
Medical care for an illness or injury.
The use of a substance or process to preserve or give particular properties to something.
A treatise; a formal written description or characterization of a subject.
A brief, third-person, present-tense summary of a proposed film.
harsh punishment; retribution
entertainment; treat

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Tom needed treatment.
examples.translation: 湯姆需要接受治療。

examples.text: Algiers needs many sewage treatment plants.
Algeria needs more sewage treatment plants.
You should stay in the hospital for treatment.
examples.translation: 你應該留在醫院，接受治療。

examples.text: You must complete the treatment until the end.
examples.translation: 你必須堅持完成治療。

examples.text: He asked her to give him preferential treatment.
examples.translation: 他請求她給予優待。

etymology.text: From treat + -ment. Compare French traitement.

senses.definition: To completely remove, get rid of, put an end to.
To render (a facility) unusable, to destroy it; to disable (a soldier), make them unable to fight (typically but not necessarily by killing)
To excrete (waste products).
To exclude (from investigation or from further competition).
To record amounts in a consolidation statement to remove the effects of inter-company transactions.
To kill (a person or animal).

examples.text: We've already eliminated half the possibilities.
Algeria needs to eliminate its deficits.
They have eliminated all imperfections.
Germany was eliminated by South Korea.
examples.translation: 德國被韓國淘汰。

examples.text: Belgium eliminated Brazil from the World Cup.
He was eliminated before he got to the finals.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin ēlīminātus, perfect passive participle of ēlīminō (“to turn out of doors, banish”), from ē- + līmen (“a threshold”, līmin- in compounds) + -ō (first conjugation verb-forming suffix) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), akin to Latin līmes (“a boundary”); see also English limit and limen.

senses.definition: A cloud in outer space consisting of gas or dust (e.g. a cloud formed after a star explodes).
A white spot or slight opacity of the cornea.
A cloudy appearance in the urine.

examples.text: Do you know what a nebula is?
examples.translation: 你知道星雲是什麼嗎？

examples.text: Stars are born in massive clouds of gas and dust called nebulas.
examples.translation: 星星是在稱為星雲的大量氣體與塵埃雲中誕生的。

examples.text: We don't yet know which stars were formed in the same nebula as our sun.
examples.translation: 我們尚不清楚哪些星星是在與太陽同源的星雲中誕生的。

examples.text: A nebula is an interstellar cloud of dust, hydrogen, helium and other ionized gases.
examples.translation: 星雲是太空中的塵埃、氫、氦及其他電離氣體雲。

examples.text: That nebula doesn't look like a crab to me.
examples.translation: 那片星雲在我看來不像螃蟹。

examples.text: Some suspected that fuzzy patches of light known as nebulas were actually distant "islands of stars" far beyond our galaxy.
examples.translation: 有些人懷疑那些稱為星雲的模糊光斑，其實是遠遠超出銀河系的「星星島」。

etymology.text: Learned borrowing from Latin nebula (“little cloud, mist”). First attested in 1655. Akin to Ancient Greek νεφέλη (nephélē, “cloud”), German Nebel (“mist, nebula”), Old Norse nifl, Polish niebo (“sky, heaven”), Russian не́бо (nébo, “sky”).
etymology.native: 從拉丁語 nebula（「小雲、霧」）借入，最早見於1655年。與古希臘語 νεφέλη（nephélē，「雲」）、德語 Nebel（「霧、星雲」）、古挪威語 nifl、波蘭語 niebo（「天空、天堂」）、俄語 не́бо（nébo，「天空」）相關。

senses.definition: A perceived change in some function, sensation or appearance of a person that indicates a disease or disorder, such as fever, headache or rash; strictly, a symptom is felt or experienced by the patient, while a sign can be detected by an observer.
A signal; anything that indicates, or is characteristic of, the presence of something else, especially of something undesirable.

examples.text: Do you have coronavirus symptoms?
examples.translation: 你有新冠病毒的症狀嗎？

examples.text: Dan began displaying symptoms of Alzheimer's.
For how long will I continue to have these symptoms?
examples.translation: 這種癥狀在我身上將會持續多久？

examples.text: Like most diseases, it has its own symptoms.
Being on time is a symptom of a boring life.
Do you know what the symptoms of the flu are?

etymology.text: From Middle English sinthoma, from Medieval Latin sinthoma, altered by Late Latin symptoma, from Ancient Greek σύμπτωμα (súmptōma, “a happening, accident, symptom of disease”), from stem of συμπίπτω (sumpíptō, “Ι befall”), from συν- (sun-, “together”) + πίπτω (píptō, “to fall”). See also syn-, -oma, -ome.

senses.definition: Inflicted by oneself.

examples.text: Tom died from self-inflicted injuries.
examples.translation: 湯姆因自傷身亡。

examples.text: Tom's wounds weren't self-inflicted.
examples.translation: 湯姆的傷口並非自傷所致。

examples.text: Do you really think Tom's wounds are self-inflicted?
examples.translation: 你真的認為湯姆的傷口是自傷所致嗎？

examples.text: A lot of Algeria's economic problems are self-inflicted.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞許多經濟問題皆為自製。

examples.text: Tom was the victim of a self-inflicted gunshot wound.
examples.translation: 湯姆遭自傷槍傷致死。

examples.text: Tom died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound to the head.
examples.translation: 湯姆因自傷頭部槍傷身亡。

etymology.text: From self- + inflicted.
etymology.native: 來自 self- + inflicted。

senses.definition: One who enters into, or offers themselves for, any service of their own free will, especially when done without pay.
One who enters into military service voluntarily (but who, when in service, is subject to discipline and regulations like other soldiers), as opposed to a conscript.
A voluntary member of the organized militia of a country, as distinguished from a regular or member of the standing army.
A person who acts out of their own will without a legal obligation, such as a donor.
A plant that grows spontaneously, without being cultivated on purpose; see volunteer plant in Wikipedia.
A native or resident of the American state of Tennessee.
a native or resident of Tennessee
(military) a person who freely enlists for service
a person who performs voluntary work

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Volunteers distributed tea in disposable cups.
Volunteers have saved thousands of people.
Just don't volunteer any new information.
The babies are taken care of by volunteers.
examples.translation: 嬰兒被志願者們照顧著。

examples.text: Tom was the first person to volunteer.
examples.translation: 湯姆是第一個志願參與的人。

examples.text: I spent the whole day working as a volunteer.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French voluntaire, from Latin voluntārius (“willing, voluntary”); or from voluntary + -eer.

senses.definition: Done, given, or acting of one's own free will.
Done by design or intention; intentional.
Working or done without payment.
Endowed with the power of willing.
Of or relating to voluntarism.

examples.text: Donations are voluntary.
This is not voluntary.
It's not voluntary.
But there's a big difference between forced and voluntary labor.
She can only go to the company to do voluntary work on Sundays.
examples.translation: 她星期天也只能去公司做義務勞動了。

examples.text: He made a voluntary contribution to the school.

etymology.text: From Middle English voluntarie, from Old French volontaire, from Latin voluntārius (“willing, of free will”), from voluntās (“will, choice, desire”), from volēns, present participle of volo (“to will”). Displaced native Old English selfwille (literally “self-willed”).

senses.definition: Responsible for a dishonest act.
Judged to have committed a crime.
Having a sense of guilt.
Blameworthy.

examples.text: He confessed that he was guilty.
examples.translation: 他承認有罪。

examples.text: You make me feel so guilty.
examples.translation: 你讓我感到很內疚。

examples.text: I knew that Tom was guilty.
examples.translation: 我知道湯姆有罪。

examples.text: Tom felt very guilty.
examples.translation: 湯姆非常愧疚。

examples.text: She declared that she was not guilty.
examples.translation: 她聲稱自己沒罪。

examples.text: Actually, you're the guilty one.
examples.translation: 其實，有罪的人是你。

etymology.text: From Middle English gilty, gulty, from Old English gyltiġ (“offending, guilty”); equivalent to guilt + -y.

senses.definition: The primary income-earner in a household.
senses.native: 養家活口的人、養家糊口的人、養家的人

examples.text: She's the breadwinner in this family.
examples.translation: 她是這個家庭的經濟支柱。

examples.text: My father is the breadwinner.
examples.translation: 我父親是這個家庭的經濟支柱。

examples.text: Tom is the sole breadwinner for the family.
examples.translation: Tom 是這個家庭唯一的經濟支柱。

examples.text: She's the sole breadwinner for the family.
examples.translation: 她是這個家庭唯一的經濟支柱。

examples.text: Tom is his family's main breadwinner.
examples.translation: Tom 是他家庭的主要經濟支柱。

examples.text: Tom became the breadwinner of the family when his father died.
examples.translation: 當他父親去世後，Tom 成為家庭的經濟支柱。

etymology.text: From bread + winner, where to win = to earn. Compare West Frisian breawinning (“livelihood”, literally “bread-winning”), Dutch broodwinning (“livelihood”).
etymology.native: 由 bread 與 winner 組成，意為「賺錢」。可與西弗里斯蘭語 breawinning（意為「維生」，字面為「賺麵包」）及荷蘭語 broodwinning（意為「維生」）相比。

senses.definition: A group of people who are closely related to one another (by blood, marriage or adoption); kin; in particular, a set of parents and their children; an immediate family.
A group of related animals, usually a mother and offspring, a mating pair or larger lineages in some species.
A (close-knit) group of people related by blood, friendship, marriage, law, or custom, especially if they live or work together.
A category in the classification of organisms, ranking below order and above genus; a taxon at that rank.
A group of languages believed to have descended from the same ancestral language.
An extended family: a group of people who are related to one another by blood or marriage.
A nuclear family: a mother and father who are married and cohabiting and their child or children.
Members of one's family collectively.
The gay community.
Lineage, especially honorable or noble lineage.
Any group or aggregation of things classed together as kindred or related from possessing in common characteristics which distinguish them from other things of the same order.
A collection of sets, especially of subsets of a given set.
A group of instruments having the same basic method of tone production.

examples.text: Our family always celebrates Christmas together.
examples.translation: 我們家一直都是一起過聖誕節。

examples.text: She knows nothing about her family.
examples.translation: 她對她的家人一無所知。

examples.text: Please say hello to your family.
examples.translation: 帶我向你家人問好。

examples.text: Kate made her family leave home.
examples.translation: 凱特使她的家人離家出走。

examples.text: The family is too poor to pay back the debts.
examples.translation: 這個家庭非常貧窮以至於無法償還貸款。

examples.text: Tom wants to spend more time with his family.
examples.translation: 湯姆想多把時間花在他的家庭上。

etymology.text: From Late Middle English famylye, from Latin familia (“a household”). Displaced native Old English hīred and hād. Doublet of familia.
etymology.native: 源自晚期中古英語（famylye），來自拉丁語（familia）「家庭、家眷」。取代了古英語本土詞（hīred、hād）。與（familia）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: A person who raises a child (which they have made, adopted, fostered, taken as their own, etc.).
A third person who has provided DNA samples in an IVF procedure in order to alter faulty genetic material.
A person who has had a baby; this person in relation to their child or children.
A surrogate parent.
The source or origin of something.
An organism from which a plant or animal is immediately biologically descended.
Sponsor, supporter, owner, protector.
A parent company.
The object from which a child or derived object is descended; a node superior to another node.
senses.native: （程式、資料結構的）父物件；父節點

senses.definition: The nuclide that decays into a daughter nuclide.
A relative.

examples.text: Please don't tell your parents this.
examples.translation: 請不要告訴你父母。

examples.text: Your parents didn't come, did they?
examples.translation: 你的父母沒來，是嗎？

examples.text: How are your parents getting along?
examples.translation: 你的父母是如何相處的？

examples.text: When my parents get old, I will support them.
examples.translation: 等父母老了，我會贍養他們。

examples.text: My parents' generation went through the war.
examples.translation: 我父母那一代經歷過戰爭。

examples.text: She wrote to her parents at least once a week.
examples.translation: 他給父母寫信至少一週一次。

etymology.text: From Middle English parent, borrowed from Anglo-Norman parent, Middle French parent, from Latin parentem, accusative of parēns (“parent”), present participle of pariō (“to breed, bring forth”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（parent），借自英法語與中古法語（parent），來自拉丁語（parentem），是（parēns）「父母」的受格，為（pariō）「生育」的現在分詞。

senses.definition: A person who supports, promotes, advocates or champions a cause, movement, or political party; an adherent.
A person who provides moral or physical support to another; an attendant participating in a ceremony or procession.
Someone who is a fan of a certain sports team or sportsperson.
Something that supports another thing.
Something that supports a structure such as a building or a sculpture.
An animal or figure that supports a shield in a coat of arms.
A garter worn around the leg to support a sock or stocking.

examples.text: We are looking for supporters.
examples.translation: 我們正在尋找支持者。

examples.text: That team's supporters are really fanatical.
Rev. King and his supporters were threatened.
examples.translation: 金牧師和他的支持者們受到威脅。

examples.text: We search supporters.
examples.translation: 我們尋找支持者。

examples.text: The latter view has many supporters in Japan.
Tom is a Christian supporter of Palestine.

etymology.text: From Middle English supporter, supportour, equivalent to support + -er.

senses.definition: A person or organization with some sort of responsibility for another person or organization, especially where the responsibility has a religious, legal, or financial aspect.
A senior member of a twelve step or similar program chosen to guide an initiate and form a partnership with them.
A person or organization that pays all or part of the cost of an event, publication, media program, etc., usually in exchange for advertising.

examples.text: This program has the following sponsors.
I don't think this sponsor is very suitable.
examples.translation: 我覺得這個贊助不太合適。

examples.text: Prospectuses must be signed by two sponsor representatives.
examples.translation: 招股說明書必須由兩名保薦代表人簽字。

examples.text: If only we could find a company to sponsor our race.
My sponsor was willing to agree to my suggestion.
Would you like to sponsor our project?

etymology.text: Learned borrowing from Latin spōnsor (“a surety", in Late Latin "a sponsor in baptism”).

senses.definition: One who supplies; a provider.
Someone who assists (sets up) a goal.

examples.text: SEAAL is Algiers's drinking water supplier.
I'm thinking about changing my supplier.
You should choose this supplier.
We face competition from foreign suppliers.
They have cooperated with this supplier before.
Algeria is a safe gas supplier for Spain.

etymology.text: From supply + -er.

senses.definition: A tool used to moor a vessel to the bottom of a sea or river to resist movement.
An anchorman or anchorwoman.
A metal tie holding adjoining parts of a building together.
A screw anchor.
Carved work, somewhat resembling an anchor or arrowhead; part of the ornaments of certain mouldings. It is seen in the echinus, or egg-and-anchor (called also egg-and-dart, egg-and-tongue) ornament.
One of the anchor-shaped spicules of certain sponges.
One of the calcareous spinules of certain holothurians, as in species of Synapta.
The thirty-fifth Lenormand card.
A defensive player, especially one who counters the opposition's best offensive player.
An iron device so shaped as to grip the bottom and hold a vessel at her berth by the chain or rope attached.
The combined anchoring gear (anchor, rode, bill/peak and fittings such as bitts, cat, and windlass.)
Representation of the nautical tool, used as a heraldic charge.

Any instrument serving a purpose like that of a ship's anchor, such as an arrangement of timber to hold a dam fast; a device to hold the end of a bridge cable etc.; or a device used in metalworking to hold the core of a mould in place.
A marked point in a document that can be the target of a hyperlink.
A line of code in a program which acts as a reference point for further code to be added immediately before or after, usually via copy and paste.
The final runner in a relay race.
A point that is touched by the draw hand or string when the bow is fully drawn and ready to shoot.
A superstore or other facility that serves as a focus to bring customers into an area.
That which gives stability or security.
senses.native: 使人穩定或有安全感的人或事物

senses.definition: The brake of a vehicle.

examples.text: Gabriel heard an anchor dropping.
examples.translation: 蓋比爾聽見錨繩放下的聲音。

examples.text: The skipper is weighing anchor.
examples.translation: 船長正在解開錨。

examples.text: Tom has an anchor tattooed on his right arm.
examples.translation: 湯姆的右臂上刺著一個錨形紋身。

examples.text: A large number of boats lay at anchor in the bay.
examples.translation: 許多船隻停泊在灣內。

examples.text: The anchor is stuck. Back up and see if it comes out.
examples.translation: 錨卡住了，請倒車看看能否脫困。

examples.text: I have a tattoo of an anchor on my right arm.
examples.translation: 我右臂上有一隻錨的刺青。

etymology.text: From Middle English anker, from Old English ancor, ancra, from Latin ancora, from (or cognate with) Ancient Greek ἄγκυρα (ánkura). The modern form is a sixteenth-century modification after the Medieval Latin spelling anchora. Doublet of ancora, anker, angora, and Ankara.
etymology.native: 此詞源於古希臘語 ἄγκυρα，經拉丁語與中古英語演變而成現代拼寫。

senses.definition: Of, pertaining to, or in accordance with the (usually high) standards of a profession.
Expert.
Of an occupation, paid, especially so as to provide a livelihood.
Engaging in persistent behaviour that is exaggeratedly implied to be a full-time, paid occupation.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: They're professional singers.
examples.translation: 他們是職業歌手。

examples.text: Professional cyclists usually ride in pelotons.
My son wants to become a professional golf player.
examples.translation: 我的兒子想成為一個專業高爾夫球手。

examples.text: Amateurs talk strategy, professionals talk logistics.
examples.translation: 外行談策略，內行談後勤。

examples.text: I've always wanted to be a professional basketball player.
examples.translation: 我一直想成為一名職業籃球運動員。

examples.text: I'm a professional photographer.
examples.translation: 我是專業攝影師。

etymology.text: From Middle English professhennalle, professhynalle; equivalent to profession + -al.

senses.definition: Any of the collections of many millions or billions of stars, galactic dust, black holes, etc. existing as independent and coherent systems, of which there are billions in the known universe.
An assemblage of things or people seen as luminous or brilliant.
Any print or pattern reminiscent of a galaxy, generally consisting of blending, semiopaque patches of vibrant color on a dark background.
The Milky Way; the apparent band of concentrated stars which appears in the night sky over earth.

examples.text: She really wants a Samsung Galaxy.
examples.translation: 她真的想要一台三星 Galaxy。

examples.text: She wondered about other galaxies.
examples.translation: 她對其他星系感到好奇。

examples.text: Jonas departed to another galaxy.
examples.translation: 約納斯前往另一個星系。

examples.text: We might well be the only ones in our Galaxy.
examples.translation: 我們很可能就是銀河系中唯一的生物。

examples.text: You know nothing about the Andromeda galaxy.
examples.translation: 你對仙女座星系一無所知。

examples.text: Do other intelligent beings live in our Galaxy?
examples.translation: 其他智慧生命是否居住在銀河系中？

etymology.text: From Middle English galaxye, galaxie, from Old French galaxie, from Latin galaxias, from Ancient Greek γαλαξίας (galaxías, “Milky Way”), shortening of γαλαξίας κύκλος (galaxías kúklos, “milky circle”), from γάλα (gála, “milk”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 galaxye，galaxie，來自古法文 galaxie，源自拉丁文 galaxias，來自古希臘文 γαλαξίας（galaxías，「銀河」），是 γαλαξίας κύκλος（galaxías kúklos，「銀河圈」）的縮寫，而 γάλα（gála，「牛奶」）是其語源。

senses.definition: The sum of everything that exists in the cosmos.
An entity similar to our universe; one component of a larger entity known as the multiverse.
Everything under consideration.
The set of all things considered.
The set of all admissible observations.
A sample taken from the population.
An imaginary collection of worlds; the general imaginary world within which a work of fiction takes place, broader than its immediate setting.
A collection of stories with characters and settings that typically share a continuity but are less interrelated than those of sequels or prequels.
A whole world, in the sense of perspective or social setting.
A deity who is equivalent to the sum of everything that exists in the cosmos.
The Earth, the sphere of the world.

examples.text: But the universe is infinite.
examples.translation: 但宇宙無限。

examples.text: How was the universe formed?
examples.translation: 宇宙是怎樣形成的？

examples.text: Spirituality connects us to the universe.
How many galaxies are there in the universe?
examples.translation: 宇宙裡有多少個星系呀？

examples.text: Our world is only a small part of the universe.
examples.translation: 我們的世界只不過是宇宙的一小部分。

examples.text: There's no doubt that the universe is infinite.
examples.translation: 宇宙毫無疑問是無限的。

etymology.text: From Middle English universe, from Old French univers, from Latin universum (“all things, as a whole, the universe”), neuter of universus (“all together, whole, entire, collective, general, literally turned or combined into one”), from uni-, combining form of unus (“one”) + versus (“turned”), perfect passive participle of vertō (“to turn”). Analyzable as uni- + -verse through backformation of -verse.

senses.definition: Synonym of decamillennium: a period of 10000 years.
A countless number or multitude (of specified things)
Ten thousand; 10,000

examples.text: The night sky was filled with a myriad of stars.
examples.translation: 夜空裡佈滿了無數顆星星。

examples.text: Designs are available in a myriad of colors.
examples.translation: 設計款式有無數種顏色可供選擇。

examples.text: Tom made attempts to burnish his public image after a myriad of scandals.
examples.translation: 湯姆嘗試在眾多醜聞後擦亮他的公眾形象。

examples.text: There are a myriad of meats at the deli on the corner of Fifth and Harvey Street.
examples.translation: 街角第五街與哈維街交界的熟食店裡，有各式各樣的肉品。

examples.text: The Way produces one, one produces two, two produces three, and three produces the myriad things.
examples.translation: 道生一，一生二，二生三，三生萬物。

examples.text: Earth hosts a myriad of animals.
examples.translation: 地球上有無數種動物。

etymology.text: From French myriade, from Late Latin mȳriadem (accusative of mȳrias), from Ancient Greek μυριάς (muriás, “number of 10,000”), from μυρίος (muríos, “numberless, countless, infinite”). By surface analysis, myria- + -ad.
etymology.native: 源出法語 myriade，後者來自晚拉丁語 mȳriadem，再源自古希臘語 μυριάς（一萬之數），其後又源自 μυρίος（無盡、無數）。

senses.definition: In a shape of, or reminding of, an ellipse; oval.
Of, or showing ellipsis; having a word or words omitted.
Concise, condensed.
relating to or containing an instance of ellipsis.
Elliptic.

examples.text: The planets follow elliptical orbits.
examples.translation: 行星沿橢圓軌道運行。

examples.text: The orbit around Sirius is elliptical.
examples.translation: 天狼星周圍的軌道是橢圓形的。

examples.text: Mercury travels around the Sun in an elliptical orbit.
examples.translation: 水星繞太陽沿橢圓軌道運行。

examples.text: Pluto's orbit is highly elliptical.
examples.translation: 冥王星的軌道非常橢圓。

examples.text: Since the orbits are elliptical, the planets do not always have the same distance from the Sun.
examples.translation: 由於軌道是橢圓形的，行星和太陽之間的距離不會總是相同。

examples.text: Mercury has the most elliptical orbit of any planet in the Solar System.
examples.translation: 水星擁有太陽系中任何行星最橢圓的軌道。

etymology.text: From elliptic + -al, from Ancient Greek ἐλλειπτικός (elleiptikós), from ἐλλείπω (elleípō, “I leave out, omit”).
etymology.native: 源自希臘文，意為「遺漏」或「省略」。

senses.definition: An elliptical movement of an object about a celestial object or Lagrange point, especially a periodic elliptical revolution.
One complete circuit round an orbited body.
The state of moving in an orbit.
The path of an electron around an atomic nucleus.
A path for the ball on the outer edge of the playfield, usually connected so that the ball entering in one end will come out of the other.
A sphere of influence; an area or extent of activity, interest, or control.
The bony cavity in the skull of a vertebrate containing the eyeball.
The area around the eye of a bird or other animal.
A collection of points related by the evolution function of a dynamical system.
The subset of elements of a set X to which a given element can be moved by members of a specified group of transformations that act on X.
senses.native: 變換群作用下可達元素集合

senses.definition: The number of hands such that each player at the table has posted the big blind once.
A state of increased excitement, activity, or anger.
senses.native: （非正式）激動、活躍或憤怒的狀態（發飆）

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: They managed to put a satellite into orbit.
examples.translation: 他們成功將衛星送入軌道。

examples.text: Since the orbits are elliptical, the planets do not always have the same distance from the Sun.
examples.translation: 由於軌道是橢圓形的，行星和太陽之間的距離不會總是相同。

examples.text: Pioneer 10 crossed Pluto's orbit in 1983.
examples.translation: 先驅者10號於1983年穿越冥王星軌道。

examples.text: Comets follow eccentric orbits.
examples.translation: 彗星沿橢圓軌道運行。

examples.text: A rocket was used to orbit the satellite.
examples.translation: 火箭被用來將衛星送入軌道。

examples.text: He plotted the orbit of the moon.
examples.translation: 他繪製了月亮的軌道。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English orbite, orbita, from Latin orbita (“course, track, impression, mark”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 orbite、orbita，來自拉丁文 orbita（意為軌道、痕跡、印記）。

senses.definition: To circle or revolve around another object or position.
To place an object (e.g. a satellite) into an orbit around a planet.
senses.native: 將（衛星等）送入環繞行星的軌道

senses.definition: To move around the general vicinity of something.
senses.native: 在某事物附近徘徊、繞行

senses.definition: To move in a circle.
To center (around).
To continue to follow or engage with someone by means of social media after breaking up with them.
senses.native: 分手後仍在社群媒體上持續追蹤、關注對方（社群追蹤）

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: John Glenn orbited the Earth three times in 1962.
examples.translation: 約翰·格倫於1962年繞地球三圈。

examples.text: Bennu is a primordial artifact preserved in the vacuum of space, orbiting among planets and moons and asteroids and comets.
examples.translation: 貝努是一塊保存於太空真空中的原始遺物，穿行於行星、衛星、小行星與彗星之間。

examples.text: The Earth orbits the Sun.
examples.translation: 地球繞太陽公轉。

examples.text: The planets are orbiting the sun.
examples.translation: 行星圍繞太陽運行。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English orbite, orbita, from Latin orbita (“course, track, impression, mark”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 orbite、orbita，來自拉丁文 orbita（意為軌道、痕跡、印記）。

senses.definition: The breadth, depth or reach of a subject; the extent of applicability or relevance; a domain, purview or remit.
A device used in aiming a projectile, through which the person aiming looks at the intended target.
Potential range of action; degree of freedom; opportunity.
The region of program source code in which a given identifier is meaningful, or a given object can be accessed.
The shortest sub-wff of which a given instance of a logical connective is a part.
The region of an utterance to which some modifying element applies.
Any medical procedure that ends in the suffix -scopy, such as endoscopy, colonoscopy, bronchoscopy, etc.
A bundle, as of twigs.

examples.text: What was the scope?
This is beyond the scope of my imagination.
examples.translation: 這超出了我的想像範圍。

examples.text: We need to understand the scope of the problem.
That goes beyond the scope of this course.
She can only view things in a narrow scope.
This subject is outside the scope of our inquiry.

etymology.text: From Italian scopo (“purpose”), from Latin scopus (“target”), from Ancient Greek σκοπός (skopós), from σκέπτομαι (sképtomai), from Proto-Indo-European *speḱ-. Etymologically related to skeptic and spectrum.

senses.definition: A range of values or locations.
The space, area, volume, point, or abstract location, to which something extends.
A contiguous area of storage in a file system.
senses.native: （電腦）區段，檔案系統中連續的儲存區塊

senses.definition: The valuation of property.
A writ directing the sheriff to seize the property of a debtor, for the recovery of debts of record due to the Crown.
senses.native: （法律）查封令，命執行官查封債務人財產以追償欠官方之款項

examples.text: A good book can completely absorb your attention, to the extent that you forget your surroundings and even your existence.
examples.translation: 一本好書會令你全神貫注，甚至忘掉周圍和自己。

senses.definition: A hollow area within the body.
A small or large hole in a tooth caused by caries; often also a soft area adjacent to the hole also affected by caries.
The female part of a mold: the depression itself or (metonymically) the half of the mold that contains it.

examples.text: Remember, brushing keeps cavities away!
examples.translation: 請記住，刷牙能預防蛀牙！

examples.text: Brushing your teeth will help prevent cavities.
examples.translation: 刷牙有助於預防蛀牙。

examples.text: If we care for our teeth we won't have cavities.
examples.translation: 若我們好好照顧牙齒，就不會患蛀牙。

examples.text: The guards performed a body cavity search.
examples.translation: 警衛人員對其進行了身體腔隙檢查。

examples.text: I ate too many sweets and now I've got a cavity.
examples.translation: 我吃了太多甜食，現在得了蛀牙。

examples.text: If he has a cavity in his tooth, I want to know about it.
examples.translation: 若他牙齒有蛀洞，我想了解詳情。

etymology.text: From Middle French cavité or Late Latin cavitās, from cav(i) (“hollow, excavated, concave”) + -tās (“-ity”, nominal suffix). First attested in the Mid-16th c.
etymology.native: 源於中古法語 cavité 或晚拉丁語 cavitās，由 cav(i)（空洞、挖掘、凹）加上 -tās（-ity，名詞綴）組成。最早見於十六世紀中葉。

senses.definition: A region of the earth or of a continent; a district or country.
An administrative subdivision of certain countries, including Canada and China.
An area under the jurisdiction of an archbishop, typically comprising a number of adjacent dioceses.
An area under the jurisdiction of a provincial within a monastic order.
The parts of a country outside its national capital.
A major region defined by common geologic attributes and history.
An area of activity, responsibility or knowledge; the proper concern of a particular person or concept.
An area outside Italy which is administered by a Roman governor or prefect.

examples.text: Canada has thirteen provinces and territories.
Ontario is Canada's most populous province.
Alsace is a very beautiful province of France.
I was in an Algerian province called Bejaia.
He lives in the Algerian province of Bejaia.
The typhoon caused damage across several provinces.
examples.translation: 颱風的破壞跨越了好幾個省。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English provynce, from Anglo-Norman province, Old French province, from Latin prōvincia, seemingly corresponding to prō- (“forward”) + vinciō (“to bind, bind about, fetter, tie, fasten, surround, encircle”). Displaced Old English boldġetæl.

senses.definition: The degree of this difference.
A control on a television, etc, that adjusts the amount of contrast in the images being displayed.
A difference between two objects, people or concepts.
Something that is opposite of or strikingly different from something else.
Antithesis.
Contrast medium

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Red contrasts well with blue.
What a contrast between them!
The picture is colorful in contrast with this one.
examples.translation: 和這幅比起上來，那幅畫的色彩鮮艷多了。

examples.text: She seemed very happy in contrast to the man.
Compare and contrast Cantonese with Mandarin.
The explanation below was achieved by comparing and contrasting a variety of different theories.
examples.translation: 下面的解釋是通過比較和對比各種不同的理論。

etymology.text: From French contraster, from Latin contrāstāre (“to resist", "to withstand”), from contrā (“against”) + stō, stāre (“to stand”).

senses.definition: Between the stars.
Among the stars.

examples.text: Voyager 1 has finally reached interstellar space.
examples.translation: 旅行者一號終於進入了星際空間。

examples.text: Voyager 1 entered interstellar space.
examples.translation: 旅行者一號已進入星際空間。

examples.text: The interstellar journey was filled with unknown dangers.
examples.translation: 這趟星際旅程充滿了未知的危險。

examples.text: Tom designed the first engine capable of fast interstellar travel.
examples.translation: 湯姆設計了第一台能實現快速星際旅行的引擎。

examples.text: A nebula is an interstellar cloud of dust, hydrogen, helium and other ionized gases.
examples.translation: 星雲是塵埃、氫、氦及其他電離氣體組成的星際雲。

examples.text: Scientists have detected for the first time an interstellar asteroid passing through our solar system.
examples.translation: 科學家首次發現一顆星際小行星穿越了太陽系。

etymology.text: From inter- + stellar.
etymology.native: 來自 inter- 與 stellar 的組合。

senses.definition: Something which is emitted or sent out; issue.
The act of emitting; the act of sending forth or putting into circulation.
A show; a program.

examples.text: Can Algiers become a zero-emissions metropolis?
examples.translation: Algiers 能否成為零排放的都市？

examples.text: Cars are equipped with emission-control filters.
examples.translation: 汽車裝有排氣控制過濾器。

examples.text: Australia had no such emission controls.
examples.translation: 澳洲當時並無這樣的排氣控制措施。

examples.text: Algeria needs to decrease its emission levels.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞需降低其排氣水平。

examples.text: This graph shows the CO2 emissions by country.
examples.translation: 此圖表顯示各國二氧化碳排放量。

examples.text: Filters stop emission of gas into the atmosphere.
examples.translation: 過濾器可阻止氣體排入大氣。

etymology.text: First attested in 1607. From Middle French émission, from Latin ēmissiō (“sending forth”), from ēmittō (“send out”), from ex (“from, out of”) + mittō (“send”).
etymology.native: 最早見於1607年，源自中世紀法語émission，來源為拉丁語ēmissiō（「發出」），由ēmittō（「送出」）衍生，由ex（「從、出自」）+ mittō（「送出」）組成。

senses.definition: A number of things that follow on one after the other or are connected one after the other.
A television or radio program consisting of several episodes that are broadcast at regular intervals.
senses.native: 電視連續劇、電視劇、連續劇

senses.definition: Synonym of season (“one of the groups of episodes that together make up a whole series”).
The sequence of partial sums ∑ᵢ₌₁ⁿa_i of a given sequence aᵢ.
A subdivision of a genus, a taxonomic rank below that of section (and subsection) but above that of species.
A group of matches between two sides, with the aim being to win more matches than the opposition.
The optional taxonomic rank above order/subseries, but below superorder.
senses.native: （生物分類）系：目或亞系之上、總目之下的選用階元

senses.definition: The optional taxonomic rank above group, but below epifamily.
senses.native: （生物分類）系：群之上、上科之下的選用階元

senses.definition: A parcel of rough diamonds of assorted qualities.
A set of consonants that share a particular phonetic or phonological feature.
senses.native: （語音）一組具有共同特徵的子音

senses.definition: A period, stretch of time.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: They watched a TV series tonight.
examples.translation: 他們今晚看了電視連續劇。

examples.text: I like watching Korean TV series.
examples.translation: 我很喜歡看韓國的電視劇。

examples.text: They gave a series of concerts.
examples.translation: 他們辦了一系列的音樂會。

examples.text: Lucario is a creature in the Pokémon series.
examples.translation: 路卡利歐是《神奇寶貝》系列中的一種生物。

examples.text: She made a series of medical discoveries.
examples.translation: 她提出了一連串的醫學發現。

examples.text: Which drama series do you like best?
examples.translation: 你最喜歡什麼電視劇？

relations.native: 展覽的物品陳列（展示會）
展覽的物品陳列（展示會）

etymology.text: Attested from the 1610s; borrowed from Latin seriēs, from serere (“to join together, bind”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ser- (“to bind, put together, to line up”). Related to desert, insert, sermon, and sorcerer.
etymology.native: 自 1610 年代起有記載；借自拉丁語（seriēs），來自（serere）「連接、綁」，最終源自原始印歐語（*ser-）「綁、排列」。與（desert）、（insert）、（sermon）、（sorcerer）有關。

senses.definition: The outflow of a bodily fluid, particularly (now rare) in abnormal amounts.
The entire set of some item printed and disseminated during a certain period, particularly (publishing) a single printing of a particular edition of a work when contrasted with other print runs.
The entire set of something; all of something.
Any financial instrument issued by a company.
The loan of a book etc. from a library to a patron; all such loans by a given library during a given period.
The means or opportunity by which something flows or comes out, particularly
The action or an instance of sending something out, particularly
A small incision, tear, or artificial ulcer, used to drain fluid and usually held open with a pea or other small object.
The production or distribution of something for general use.
The distribution of something (particularly rations or standardized provisions) to someone or some group.
The action or an instance of a company selling bonds, stock, or other securities.
Any question or situation to be resolved, particularly
A point of law or fact in dispute or question in a legal action presented for resolution by the court.
Anything in dispute, an area of disagreement whose resolution is being debated or decided.
A psychological or emotional difficulty, (now informal, figurative and usually euphemistic) any problem or concern considered as a vague and intractable difficulty.
The end result of an event or events, any result or outcome, particularly
Offspring: one's natural child or children.
Progeny: all one's lineal descendants.
A single edition of a newspaper or other periodical publication.
A Monacan Indian; a member of a Mestee group originating in Amherst County, Virginia.

examples.text: We have important issues to discuss.
examples.translation: 我們有些重要的事要談。

examples.text: Viviana has important issues to discuss.
examples.translation: 薇薇安娜有重要的事情要討論。

examples.text: I don't know how she should deal with that issue.
examples.translation: 不知道她應該怎麼處理那個問題。

examples.text: I want to avoid phones that have too many issues.
examples.translation: 我想要避免問題太多的手機。

examples.text: She has dropped out of school due to health issues.
examples.translation: 她因為健康因素休學了。

examples.text: This issue has nothing to do with you.
examples.translation: 這件事與你無關。

etymology.text: From Middle English issue, from Old French issue (“an exit, a way out”), feminine past participle of issir (“to exit”), from Latin exeō (“go out, exit”), from prefix ex- (“out”) + eō (“go”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（issue），來自古法語（issue）「出口、出路」，是（issir）「出去」的陰性過去分詞，來自拉丁語（exeō）「出去」，由「向外」（ex-）加「走」（eō）組成。

senses.definition: A transmission of a radio or television programme intended to be received by anyone with a receiver.
A programme (bulletin, documentary, show, etc.) so transmitted.
The act of scattering seed; a crop grown from such seed.

examples.text: We broadcast news on the hour.
examples.translation: 我們正點播報新聞。

examples.text: Television stations broadcast 24 hours a day.
This programme is broadcast fortnightly.
His death was broadcast all over the world.
examples.translation: 他去世的消息在世界各地播出。

examples.text: That program is now being broadcast.
examples.translation: 那個節目現在正在播出。

examples.text: The fight was only broadcast on pay-per-view.

etymology.text: From broad + cast. First attested in the mid 18th century, in the agricultural use of spreading seeds.

senses.definition: The act, process, or result of reducing.
The amount or rate by which something is reduced, e.g. in price.
A reaction in which electrons are gained and valence is reduced; often by the removal of oxygen or the addition of hydrogen.
The process of rapidly boiling a sauce to concentrate it.
The rewriting of an expression into a simpler form.
A transformation of one problem into another problem, such as mapping reduction or polynomial-time reduction.
An arrangement for a far smaller number of parties, e.g. a keyboard solo based on a full opera.
A philosophical procedure intended to reveal the objects of consciousness as pure phenomena. (See phenomenological reduction.)
A medical procedure to restore a fracture or dislocation to the correct alignment, usually with a closed approach but sometimes with an open approach (surgery).
A reduced price of something by a fraction or decimal.
The ratio of a material's change in thickness compared to its thickness prior to forging and/or rolling.
A religious settlement created during a mission by Spanish or Portuguese colonists with the intent of evangelizing Christianity to the local population.

examples.text: He advocated the reduction of taxes.
examples.translation: 他提倡減稅。

examples.text: It's not about cost reduction.
examples.translation: 這與減少開支無關。

examples.text: It isn't about cost reduction.
examples.translation: 這與減少開支無關。

examples.text: Harm reduction saves lives.
examples.translation: 減少傷害，拯救生命。

examples.text: Survival analysis showed a significant reduction.
examples.translation: 存活分析顯示，機率顯著減少。

examples.text: They demand a reduction in working hours.
examples.translation: 他們要求減少工作時長。

etymology.text: From Middle English reduccion, a borrowing from Old French reducion, from Latin reductiō, reductiōnem. Equivalent to reduce + -tion.

senses.definition: A disposition; an arrangement, categorization, or classification of things.
A kick or a handball of the ball during a game.

A sexual paraphilia, as in art, fiction, and role-playing, that involves a character consuming and digesting another and disposing their remains as bodily fluids, typically as via ejaculation or defecation.
senses.native: 一種性偏好，涉及角色吞食並消化他人，將其殘骸以精液或排洩物形式排出

senses.definition: The power to use something or someone.
senses.native: 使用某物或某人的權力

senses.definition: A garbage disposal

examples.text: Her elegant disposal of these artifacts constitutes a rare classification worthy of scholarly admiration.

An electronic home entertainment device equipped with a screen and a speaker for receiving television signals and displaying them in audio-visual form.
Collectively, the programs broadcast via the medium of television.
Vision at a distance.

examples.text: My little brother is watching television.
examples.translation: 我弟弟在看電視。

examples.text: What's your favorite television program?
examples.translation: 你最喜歡看哪個電視節目？

examples.text: There's nothing good on television now.
examples.translation: 現在電視上沒有甚麼好看的。

examples.text: He likes watching tennis on television.
examples.translation: 他喜歡在電視上看網球。

examples.text: Do you know how high the television tower is?
examples.translation: 你知道那座電視塔有多高嗎？

examples.text: Turn off the television. I can't concentrate.

To result in specific machine instructions or bytecode when compiled.

examples.text: Why doesn't it emit any light?
examples.translation: 為什麼它不發出任何光呢？

examples.text: The dog emitted grunts.
examples.translation: 狗發出了低吼聲。

examples.text: Planets don't emit light by themselves.
examples.translation: 行星本身不會發出光線。

examples.text: I like the light that candles emit.
examples.translation: 我喜歡蠟燭發出的光。

examples.text: Lightbulbs emit heat.
examples.translation: 燈泡會散發熱量。

examples.text: The motor overheated and is now emitting smoke.
examples.translation: 馬達過熱，現在正在冒煙。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin ēmittō.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 ēmittō。

senses.definition: A person's daughter or son; a person's child.
Any of a person's descendants, including of further generations.
An animal or plant's progeny or young.
Anything produced; the result of an entity's efforts.
A process launched by another process.

examples.text: What's stopping you from having offspring?
examples.translation: 什麼在阻止你生兒育女？

examples.text: An otter's offspring are called pups.
examples.translation: 水獺的幼崽稱為幼獸。

examples.text: Rabbits have a lot of offspring.

examples.text: Some animals are producing offspring in zoos.
examples.translation: 有些動物在動物園裡產下幼崽。

examples.text: Books are the offspring of someone's brains.
examples.translation: 書是人腦的產物。

examples.text: She sacrificed her own life for her offspring.
examples.translation: 她為其幼崽犧牲了自己的生命。

etymology.text: From Middle English ofspring, from Old English ofspring (“offspring, descendants, posterity”), equivalent to off- + spring. Compare Icelandic afspringur (“offspring”). More at off, spring.
etymology.native: 「offspring」源自中世紀英文，來自古英文「ofspring」，意為「後代、子孫」，由「off-」與「spring」組成。可參照冰島語「afspringur」（子孫）。詳見「off」與「spring」。

senses.definition: plural of child

examples.text: Children should drink milk every day.
examples.translation: 孩子們應該每天喝牛奶。

examples.text: Tom wants children, but Mary doesn't.
examples.translation: 湯姆想要孩子，但瑪麗不想。

examples.text: The children were well looked after.
examples.translation: 孩子們被照顧得很好。

examples.text: The children already went to school.
examples.translation: 孩子們已經去上學了。

examples.text: I heard the children's happy voices.
examples.translation: 我聽到孩子們開心的聲音。

examples.text: Won't somebody please think of the children?!
examples.translation: 拜託不會有人想到孩子們嗎?!

examples.text: Two children are sitting on top of the fence.
examples.translation: 兩個孩子在柵欄上坐著。

examples.text: Tom was always different from other children.
examples.translation: 湯姆總是跟別的小孩不一樣。

examples.text: There are four lovely children in this photo.
examples.translation: 這張照片上有四個可愛的孩子。

examples.text: The couple have no less than seven children.
examples.translation: 這對夫婦有七個子女之多。

examples.text: We prayed that our children would forgive us.
examples.translation: 我們祈禱孩子們會原諒我們。

examples.text: American children grow up hearing those words.
examples.translation: 美國的小孩聽著這些話長大。

examples.text: Children of six and above should attend school.
examples.translation: 六歲及以上的小孩應該上學。

examples.text: I believe it my duty to protect these children.
examples.translation: 我認為我有義務保護這些孩子。

examples.text: She was ashamed of her children's behavior.
examples.translation: 她為自己孩子的行為感到羞恥。

examples.text: I've known Jim ever since we were children.
examples.translation: 從我們是兒童開始，我就認識吉姆了。

examples.text: Young children are often fascinated by science.
examples.translation: 小孩常常對科學很有熱情。

examples.text: Many children die of starvation in Africa.
examples.translation: 在非洲有許多孩子死於飢餓。

examples.text: The children haven't studied division yet.
examples.translation: 孩子們還沒上過除法。

examples.text: We should ban advertising aimed towards children.
examples.translation: 我們應該禁止針對兒童的廣告。

examples.text: Children were apt to invent their own games.
examples.translation: 孩子們總愛創作自己的遊戲。

examples.text: Parents often sacrifice themselves to ensure that their children receive a good education.
examples.translation: 父母為了確保孩子受到良好的教育常常犧牲自己。

examples.text: Pioneer men and women had a hard life, and so did their children.
examples.translation: 先驅的男女過著艱苦的生活，他們的孩子也一樣。

examples.text: But if we were wholly rational, would we want children at all?
examples.translation: 但如果我們完全理性，我們會想要孩子嗎？

examples.text: Youth is such a priceless commodity that it is a shame to waste it on children.
examples.translation: 青春是如此珍貴的資產，竟把牠浪費在孩子身上，真令人遺憾。

examples.text: The children of American soldiers staying in Japan and Japanese women were disparagingly called half-breeds.
examples.translation: 留在日本的美國士兵與日本女性所生的孩子，被諷刺地稱為「混血兒」。

etymology.text: From Middle English children, alteration of earlier childre ("children"; > English dialectal childer), from Old English ċildru, ċildra (“children”), nominative and accusative plural of ċild (“child”), equivalent to child + -ren.
etymology.native: 「children」源自中世紀英文的「children」，是更早「childre」的變體，而「childre」來自古英語「ċildru」、「ċildra」，意為「孩子們」，是「ċild」（孩子）的 nominative 與 accusative 複數形式，等於「child + -ren」。

senses.definition: A male parent, especially of a human; a male who parents a child (which he has sired, adopted, fostered, etc.).
A term of respectful address for a priest.
A title given to the personification of a force of nature or abstract concept, such as Father Time or Father Frost.
A senator of Ancient Rome.
A male ancestor more remote than a parent; a progenitor; especially, a first ancestor.
A term of respectful address for an elderly man.
senses.native: （對年長男性的敬稱）老爹；老先生

senses.definition: A person who plays the role of a father in some way.
A pioneering figure in a particular field.
Something that is the greatest or most significant of its kind.
senses.native: 同類中最大或最重要的事物

senses.definition: Something inanimate that begets.
A member of a church council.
The archived older version of a file that immediately precedes the current version, and was itself derived from the grandfather.
A title given to priests.
One of the chief ecclesiastical authorities of the first centuries after Christ.
senses.native: 教父（基督教早期的教會權威）

examples.text: My father caught three fish yesterday.

examples.text: Peter isn't anything like his father.

examples.text: Father takes the 7:00 subway to work.
examples.translation: 爸爸乘早上7點的捷運去上班。

examples.text: My father traveled all over the world by air.
examples.translation: 我的父親坐飛機環遊了世界。

examples.text: My father graduated from Harvard University.
examples.translation: 我爸爸是哈佛大學畢業的。

examples.text: My father always speaks in a very loud voice.
