senses.definition: An instance of applying pressure; an instance of pressing.
A device used to apply pressure to an item.
A crowd.
A printing machine.
The print-based media (both the people and the newspapers).
A publisher.
An enclosed storage space (e.g. closet, cupboard).
An exercise in which weight is forced away from the body by extension of the arms or legs.
An additional bet in a golf match that duplicates an existing (usually losing) wager in value, but begins even at the time of the bet.
Pure, unfermented grape juice.
A commission to force men into public service, particularly into the navy.
In personology, any environmental factor that arouses a need in the individual.
senses.native: （人格心理學）任何引起個人需求的環境因素（壓力、需求刺激）

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Put the ironing in the linen press.

etymology.text: From Middle English presse (“throng, crowd, clothespress”), partially from Old English press (“clothespress”) (from Medieval Latin pressa) and from Old French presse (Modern French presse) from Old French presser (“to press”), from Latin pressāre, from pressus, past participle of premere (“to press”). Chiefly displaced native Middle English thring (“press, crowd, throng”) (from Old English þring (“a press, crowd, anything that presses or confines”)).

senses.definition: The act, or an instance, of swinging.
The manner in which something is swung.
The sweep or compass of a swinging body.
A line, cord, or other thing suspended and hanging loose, upon which anything may swing.
A hanging seat that can swing back and forth, in a children's playground, for acrobats in a circus, or on a porch for relaxing.
An energetic and acrobatic late-1930s partner-based dance style, also known as jitterbug and lindy-hop.
The genre of music associated with this dance style.
The amount of change towards or away from something.
In an election, the increase or decrease in the number of votes for opposition parties compared with votes for the incumbent party.
Sideways movement of the ball as it flies through the air.
Capacity of a turning lathe, as determined by the diameter of the largest object that can be turned in it.
In a musical theater production, a performer who understudies several roles.
A basic dance step in which a pair link hands and turn round together in a circle.
The maximum amount of change that has occurred or can occur; the sum of the maximum changes in any direction.
Influence or power of anything put in motion.
A type of hook with the arm more extended.
Free course; unrestrained liberty.

examples.text: Swingers and swing dancers are different.
Who swings too high, achieves nothing.
The negotiations are in full swing.
My emotions swing wildly, leaving me exhausted.
"I am too old to swing on branches," said the boy.
Tom sat on the porch swing, smoking his pipe.

etymology.text: From Middle English swyngen, from Old English swingan, from Proto-West Germanic *swingan, from Proto-Germanic *swinganą (compare Low German swingen, German schwingen, Dutch zwingen, Swedish svinga), from Proto-Indo-European *swenk-, *sweng- (compare Scottish Gaelic seang (“thin”)). Related to swink.

senses.definition: A young goat.
A child, adolescent, or (loosely) a young adult.
A person whose childhood took place in a particular time period or area.
One's son or daughter, regardless of age.
Used as a form of address for a child, teenager or young adult.
An inexperienced person or one in a junior position.
Kidskin.
The meat of a young goat.
A young antelope.
A deception; an act of kidding somebody.
A small wooden mess tub in which sailors received their food.
A seed pod, usually of a leguminous plant.
Synonym of faggot (“bundle of heath and furze”).

examples.text: He treated the oxen like they didn't exist, but he treated the goat kid like a puppy.
examples.translation: 他對那些牛視若無睹，卻把小山羊當小狗一樣對待。

examples.text: Most of the kids are foreigners.
examples.translation: 小朋友多是外國人。

examples.text: Tom's kids were in the attic.
examples.translation: 湯姆孩子們在閣樓。

examples.text: Tom was always different from the other kids.
examples.translation: 湯姆總是跟別的小孩不一樣。

examples.text: Kids open their presents in Christmas morning.
examples.translation: 孩子們在聖誕節的早上打開禮物。

examples.text: Tom was a little overweight when he was a kid.
examples.translation: 湯姆小時候有一點點超重。

etymology.text: From Middle English kide, from Old Norse kið (“young goat”), from Proto-Germanic *kidją, *kittīną (“goatling, kid”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *gʰaydn-, *ǵʰaydn- (“goat”) or Proto-Indo-European *gidʰ- (“kid, goatling, little goat”). Compare Swedish and Danish kid, German Kitz and Kitze, Albanian kedh and kec. The sense of child has been in use since the 1590s as slang, and since the 1840s in informal use.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（kide），來自古諾斯語（kið）「小山羊」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*kidją），可能來自原始印歐語（*gʰaydn-）「山羊」。比較瑞典語和丹麥語（kid）、德語（Kitz）。「小孩」之義自 1590 年代起作為俚語使用，自 1840 年代起作為口語使用。

senses.definition: A child, a person who has not reached the age of majority, consent, etc. and is legally subject to fewer responsibilities and less accountability and entitled to fewer legal rights and privileges.
A lesser person or thing, a person, group, or thing of minor rank or in the minor leagues.
A formally recognized secondary area of undergraduate study, requiring fewer course credits than the equivalent major.
A person who is completing or has completed such a course of study.
A determinant of a square matrix obtained by deleting one or more rows and columns.
Synonym of behind: a one-point kick.
Any of various noctuid moths in Europe and Asia, chiefly in the Oligia and Mesoligia genera.
A leaf-cutter worker ant intermediate in size between a minim and a media.
Changes rung on six bells.
An adolescent, a person above the legal age of puberty but below the age of majority.
Synonym of subtrahend, the amount subtracted from a number.
The younger brother of a pupil.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: She's still a minor.
examples.translation: 她還未成年。

examples.text: In such a strict community, even minor rebellion was seen as deviant.
He plays in the minors.
She hasn't won a minor since the Sichuan Open.
The play is considered one of his minors.

etymology.text: From Middle English minor, menor, menour, etc., from Latin minor (“lesser; young; young person”) both directly and via Norman and Middle French menor, menour, etc. Doublet of minus but not mini-. Cognate with minister, minify, Minorca, Menshevik, and possibly minnow. Compare Latin minimum and minuō, Old High German minniro, Cornish minow.

senses.definition: A prepubescent child.
A person younger than the age of majority; a minor.
A person younger than the age of full criminal responsibility, such that the person either cannot be held criminally liable or is subject to less severe forms of punishment.
A publication for young adult readers.
An actor playing a child's role.
A sexually immature animal.
A two-year-old racehorse.

examples.text: The juvenile of the species was small.
examples.translation: 這個物種的幼體很小。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin iuvenīlis (“youthful; juvenile”), from iuvenis (“young; a youth”) + -īlis (suffix forming adjectives indicating a relationship or a pertaining to). Iuvenis is ultimately derived from Proto-Indo-European *h₂yuh₁en- (“young”), from *h₂óyu (“long life; lifetime”) (from *h₂ey- (“age; life”)) + *h₁én (“in”).
etymology.native: 借自拉丁語 iuvenīlis（意為「青春的；少年的」），由 iuvenis（意為「年輕的；青年」）+ -īlis（構成形容詞的後綴，表示與某事物相關）組成。iuvenis 最終源自原始印歐語 *h₂yuh₁en-（意為「年輕的」），來自 *h₂óyu（意為「長壽；一生」）（來自 *h₂ey-（意為「年齡；生命」））+ *h₁én（意為「在」）。

senses.definition: A young child (typically between one and three years old) who has started walking but not fully mastered it.
One unsteady on their feet.
Any young child (typically before preadolescence) who is capable of walking.
senses.native: 能行走的幼兒（通常指青春期前）

examples.text: The toddler's socks are bright red.
examples.translation: 托德爾的襪子是鮮紅色的。

examples.text: Toddlers often throw tantrums.
examples.translation: 學步兒經常發脾氣。

examples.text: Leonid and Anna met when they were toddlers.
examples.translation: 列奧尼德和安娜在他們還是學步兒時相遇。

examples.text: How can I get my toddler to eat vegetables?
examples.translation: 我該如何讓我的學步兒吃蔬菜？

examples.text: The toddler wobbled when he first stood up.
examples.translation: 托德爾第一次站起來時搖晃了一下。

examples.text: I can't believe I just got rick rolled by a toddler.
examples.translation: 我無法相信一個學步兒就騙了我。

etymology.text: From toddle (“to walk unsteadily”) + -er – literally “one who walks unsteadily”, hence a young child.
etymology.native: 「蹣跚」加上「-er」字尾，意即「蹣跚行走者」，故指幼兒。

senses.definition: A smaller amount or quantity.

examples.text: It is no less than two hours' walk from here.
examples.translation: 從這開始走用不了兩小時。

examples.text: The couple have no less than seven children.
examples.translation: 這對夫婦有七個子女之多。

examples.text: She has faults, but I love her none the less.
examples.translation: 雖然她有些缺點，但我始終還是愛她。

examples.text: I love him none the less for his faults.
examples.translation: 他有他的缺點，但是我愛他。

etymology.text: Adverb From Middle English les, lesse, leasse, lasse, from Old English lǣs (“smaller, less”), from Proto-Germanic *laisiz, from Proto-Indo-European *leys- (“to shrink, grow thin, be gentle”). Cognate with Old Frisian lēs (“less”), Old Saxon lēs (“less”). According to Kroonen (2013), from a northern Indo-European root Proto-Indo-European *leh₂is- or *leh₃is-, which he connects to Lithuanian liesas (“lean”).
etymology.native: 副詞源自中古英語（les、lesse），來自古英語（lǣs）「較小、較少」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*laisiz），最終可能來自原始印歐語（*leys-）「縮小、變瘦」。與古弗里斯語（lēs）、古撒克遜語（lēs）同源。

senses.definition: The process of imparting knowledge, skill and judgment.
Facts, skills and ideas that have been learned, especially through formal instruction.
Upbringing, rearing.

examples.text: Education in this world disappoints me.
examples.translation: 世界上的教育都讓我失望。

examples.text: Education starts at home.
examples.translation: 教育從家庭開始。

examples.text: Education begins at home.
examples.translation: 教育從家庭開始。

examples.text: The parents value their children's education.
examples.translation: 父母很重視孩子的教育。

examples.text: You have the advantage of a good education.
examples.translation: 你受過良好教育，這是你的優勢。

examples.text: Kelly cut physical education and went home.
examples.translation: 凱莉沒上體育課就回家了。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French éducation, from Latin ēducātiō (“a breeding, bringing up, rearing”), from ēducō (“to educate, train”), from ēdūcō (“to lead forth, to take out; to raise up, to erect”). See educate.
etymology.native: 借自中古法語（éducation），來自拉丁語（ēducātiō）「養育、撫養」，源自（ēducō）「教育、訓練」，與（ēdūcō）「帶出、扶起」有關。參見（educate）。

senses.definition: Any of a wide variety of articles, usually made of fabrics, animal hair, animal skin, or some combination thereof, used to cover the human body for warmth, to preserve modesty, or for fashion.
An act or instance of putting clothes on.
A covering of non-conducting material on the outside of a boiler, or steam chamber, to prevent radiation of heat.
The art or process of making cloth.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: What's your favorite item of clothing?
examples.translation: 你最喜歡哪類的衣服？

examples.text: Santiago was wearing very expensive clothing.
examples.translation: 聖地牙哥穿著非常昂貴的衣服。

examples.text: This store doesn't sell women's clothing.
examples.translation: 這家店不賣女裝。

examples.text: You can't judge a person based on clothing.
examples.translation: 不能根據服裝來判斷一個人。

examples.text: I can provide my family with food and clothing.
examples.translation: 我可以給我的家庭提供衣食。

examples.text: This clothing is my coworker's, not mine.
examples.translation: 這衣服是我同事的，不是我的。

etymology.text: From Middle English clothing, clathing, from Old English *clāþung, from Proto-West Germanic *klaiþungu (“clothing”), equivalent to clothe + -ing. Cognate with Scots clathing, claithing (“clothing”), Saterland Frisian Klodenge (“clothing”), West Frisian klaaiïng (“clothing”), Dutch kleding (“clothing”), German Kleidung (“clothing”), Danish klædning (“clothing, dress, attire”), Swedish kläding, klädning (“clothing, dress”). Doublet of the dialectal English term cleading, from Middle English clethi
etymology.native: 源自中古英語，來自古英語，上溯至原始西日耳曼語「衣物」，相當於「穿衣」加名詞字尾。與蘇格蘭語、弗里斯蘭語、荷蘭語、德語、丹麥語、瑞典語的同義字同源。

senses.definition: A period of rest or soothing.
A period of reduced activity; a respite.
A period without waves or wind.
An extended pause between sets of waves.

examples.text: The rains entered a lull.
examples.translation: 雨勢稍歇。

examples.text: Where did you lull them?
examples.translation: 你怎麼讓他們安靜下來？

examples.text: Lull your baby to sleep.
examples.translation: 讓寶寶安穩入睡。

examples.text: The sound of crickets chirping and frogs croaking lulls me to sleep.
examples.translation: 蟋蟀的叫聲與蛙鳴催我入眠。

examples.text: The murmur of the brook lulls me to sleep.
examples.translation: 溪流潺潺，催我入眠。

examples.text: There was a momentary lull in the violence as the leaders of the two sides parleyed.
examples.translation: 雙方領袖談判時，暴力暫時平息。

etymology.text: From Middle English lullen, lollen. Originally, perhaps expressive in origin from la-la-la or lu-lu-lu sounds made in calming a child. Compare Finnish laulaa (“to sing”) and Hiligaynon lala (“to sing a lullaby”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 lullen, lollen，可能原本是用來安撫孩童的la-la-la或lu-lu-lu聲音。可與芬蘭語 laulaa（唱歌）及希利蓋翁語 lala（唱搖籃曲）相對照。

senses.definition: To cause to rest by soothing influences; to compose; to calm
To become gradually calm; to subside; to cease or abate.
To give somebody a false sense of security so that an unpleasant situation takes the person by surprise.
senses.native: 假裝安全使人措手不及

examples.text: The teacher lulled us into thinking that we had won.
examples.translation: 老師讓我們誤以為贏了。

examples.text: The sweet lulling beauty of the birch.
examples.translation: 白樺樹那種甜美安撫的美。

examples.text: The sound of the stream lulled me to sleep.
examples.translation: 溪水聲讓我入睡。

examples.text: The fighting lulled for a moment.
examples.translation: 戰鬥暫時平息了一瞬。

examples.text: Don't be lulled into a false sense of security.
examples.translation: 別被假象的安心感迷惑。

examples.text: The storm lulled.
examples.translation: 風暴稍歇。

etymology.text: From Middle English lullen, lollen. Originally, perhaps expressive in origin from la-la-la or lu-lu-lu sounds made in calming a child. Compare Finnish laulaa (“to sing”) and Hiligaynon lala (“to sing a lullaby”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 lullen, lollen，可能原本是用來安撫孩童的la-la-la或lu-lu-lu聲音。可與芬蘭語 laulaa（唱歌）及希利蓋翁語 lala（唱搖籃曲）相對照。

senses.definition: To calm down, to quiet.
To cause to fall by drops.
To expel spirit from by heat, or to evaporate and condense in a refrigeratory; to distill.
senses.native: 以加熱方式提取精華，或蒸發後冷凝（蒸餾）

senses.definition: To trickle, drip.

examples.text: Even though he apologized, I'm still furious.
examples.translation: 即使他道歉了，我還是很憤怒。

etymology.text: From Middle English stille (“motionless, stationary”), from Old English stille (“still, quiet”), from Proto-West Germanic *stillī, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)telH- (“to be silent; to be still”). Cognate with Scots stil (“still”), Saterland Frisian stil (“motionless, calm, quiet”), West Frisian stil (“quiet, still”), Dutch stil (“quiet, silent, still”), Low German still (“quiet, silent, still”), German still (“still, quiet, tranquil, silent”), Swedish stilla (“quiet, silent, peaceful”), Iceland
etymology.native: 「still」源自中古英語 stille（意為「靜止、不動」），來自古英語 stille（意為「靜謐、安靜」），再溯源自原始西日耳曼語 *stillī，來自原始印歐語 *(s)telH-（意為「保持沉默、靜止」）。與蘇格蘭語 stil（靜止）、薩特蘭弗里斯蘭語 stil（靜止、平靜）、西弗里斯蘭語 stil（安靜、靜止）、荷蘭語 stil（安靜、沉默、靜止）、低地德語 still（安靜、沉默、靜止）、德語 still（靜謐、安靜、平和、沉默）、瑞典語 stilla（安靜、沉默、平靜）、冰島語 stilla 相關。

senses.definition: The absence of sound; quietness.
The absence of disturbance or trouble; peace, security.
a period of calm weather
an untroubled state; free from disturbances
the absence of sound
a disposition free from stress or emotion
The absence of movement; stillness, tranquility.

examples.text: He prefers the quiet.

etymology.text: From Middle English quiete, from Old French quiet (adjective) and quiete (noun), from Latin quiētus, past participle of quiēscere (“to keep quiet, rest”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kʷyeh₁- (“rest”). Doublet of coy, quit, quite, and quietus. Largely displaced native English still in the sense of "with little or no sound".
etymology.native: 源自中古英語，來自古法語形容詞「安靜的」與名詞「安寧」，來自拉丁語「平靜的」，為「保持安靜、休息」的過去分詞，最終來自原始印歐語「休息」的字根。與「矜持」、「離開」、「相當」為同源異形詞。在「無聲」一義上大致取代了本土字「靜」。

senses.definition: To make calm.
To become calm.

examples.text: Whatever happens, keep calm.
examples.translation: 無論發生甚麼事也要保持冷靜。

etymology.text: From Middle English calm, calme, from Middle French calme, probably from Old Italian calma, of uncertain origin. Calma may derive from Late Latin cauma (“heat of the midday sun”), from Ancient Greek καῦμα (kaûma, “heat, especially of the sun”), from καίω (kaíō, “to burn”), or possibly from Latin caleō. Compare also Lombardic *chalm, *chalma (“frozenness”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *kalmaz (“frozenness, cold”).

senses.definition: A temporary stop or rest; an intermission of action; interruption; suspension; cessation.
A short time for relaxing and doing something else.
Hesitation; suspense; doubt.
In writing and printing, a mark indicating the place and nature of an arrest of voice in reading; a punctuation mark.
A break or paragraph in writing.
A sign indicating continuance of a note or rest.
A button whose functions are pausing and resuming something, such as a DVD player, a video game or a computer.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: He spoke for ten minutes without a pause.
examples.translation: 他不停頓地說了十分鐘。

examples.text: What's drinking? A mere pause from thinking!
examples.translation: 喝酒是什麼？不過是暫停思考罷了！

examples.text: We pause for station identification.
I believe that anyone who pauses to contemplate nature cannot be an atheist.
examples.translation: 我相信，任何停下來沉思大自然的人都不可能是無神論者。

examples.text: Teach the pupil to mind the pauses.
examples.translation: 教學生注意停頓。

etymology.text: From Middle French pause, from Latin pausa, from Ancient Greek παῦσις (paûsis), from Ancient Greek παύω (paúō, “stop”), of uncertain origin. Doublet of pausa.
etymology.native: 源自中古法語（pause），來自拉丁語（pausa），再源自古希臘語（παῦσις），來自（παύω）「停止」，來源不明。與（pausa）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: To become quiet.
To make quiet.
To appease; to allay; to soothe.
To rush, to gush.
To send forth a rush of water over (some ground) so as to clear off the soil and other materials overlying, and thus uncover or separate out, ore.
senses.native: 用水沖洗地表，以揭露或分離礦物

examples.text: She hushed her baby to sleep.
examples.translation: 她輕聲哄著嬰兒入睡。

examples.text: All became hushed and still on board the ship.
examples.translation: 船上的所有人變得安靜寂靜。

examples.text: She got into the room with hushed steps.
examples.translation: 她輕輕地走進房間。

examples.text: Many politicians are believed to accept hush money.
examples.translation: 許多政治人物被認為接受封口費。

examples.text: The room became slightly hushed.
examples.translation: 房間變得稍微安靜了一些。

examples.text: Don’t mention that the girl is adopted; her family is very hush-hush about it.
examples.translation: 別提那個女孩是養女的事；她的家人對此守口如瓶。

etymology.text: From Middle English huschen (“to hush”) (as past participle husht (“silent; hushed”) and interjection husht (“quiet!”)). Cognate with Low German huschen, hüssen (“to hush; lull”), German huschen (“to shoo; scurry”), Danish hysse (“to hush”), and maybe Albanian hesht.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語，與低地德語、德語等語言同源。

senses.definition: Lack of difficulty; the ability to do something easily.
Freedom from pain, hardship, and annoyance, sometimes (derogatory, archaic) idleness, sloth.
Freedom from worry and concern; peace; sometimes (derogatory, archaic) indifference.
Freedom from effort; leisure, rest.
Freedom from financial effort or worry; affluence.
Freedom from embarrassment or awkwardness; grace.
Followed by of or from: release from or reduction of pain, hardship, or annoyance.
Release from constraint, obligation, or a constrained position.
Additional space provided to allow greater movement.
Release from intestinal discomfort: defecation.
A convenience; a luxury.
A relief; an easement.

examples.text: She solved the problem with ease.
examples.translation: 她不費吹灰之力就把問題解決了。

examples.text: I never felt at ease in my father's company.
examples.translation: 我在我爸的公司一直感覺不自在。

examples.text: When I speak Chinese, I start to feel at ease.
examples.translation: 我說中文的時候，開始感到自在了。

examples.text: My mind is at ease believing you'll keep the secret.
examples.translation: 我十分安心，因為我知道你會保守秘密。

examples.text: I am very ill at ease with strangers.
examples.translation: 我面對陌生人很不自在。

examples.text: Tom is ill at ease among strangers.

Sometimes ascribed to Vulgar Latin *āsia or *āsium, possibly from Latin ānsa (“handle, haft”) or Frankish *ansiju (“handle, loophole, eyelet; cup-handle; arms akimbo, elbow room”), but more often derived from Vulgar Latin *adjace(m), from Latin adj

senses.definition: Appropriate for ordinary use, rather than for special occasions.

etymology.native: 「place」源自中古英語，融合古英語 plæċe（意為「地方、開闊空間、街道」）與古法語 place（意為「廣場、開闊空間」），二者皆源自拉丁語 platēa（意為「廣場、寬闊街道」），再溯源自古希臘語 πλατεῖα（plateîa），為 πλατεῖα ὁδός（plateîa hodós，意為「寬闊道路」）之縮寫，而古希臘語則源自原始印歐語 *pleth₂-（意為「延展」），其由 *pleh₂-（意為「平坦」）延伸而來。此詞取代了古英語 stōw 與 stede（部分）之用法。亦可參見英文 pleck（意為「一塊土地」）與西弗里斯蘭語 plak（意為「廣場」）

etymology.text: From Middle English noricerie, norserye (“children's nursery; state of being fostered or nursed; education, upbringing”) [and other forms], from Old French norricerie, nourricerie, from norrice, nourrice (modern French nourrice (“childminder, nanny; wet nurse”)) + -erie (suffix forming feminine nouns). Norrice and nourrice are derived from Late Latin nūtrīcia (“wet nurse”), from Latin nūtrīcius (“that nurses or suckles; nourishing”), from nūtriō (“to breastfeed, nurse, suckle”), possibly ultimat
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 noricerie、norserye（意為「孩童育養之地；被撫養或哺乳的狀態；教育、育養」），來自古法文 norricerie、nourricerie，源自 norrice、nourrice（現代法文 nourrice，意為「育兒保姆、哺乳母」）＋-erie（構成女性名詞的後綴）。norrice 與 nourrice 來自拉丁文 nūtrīcia（意為「哺乳母」），源自拉丁文 nūtrīcius（意為「哺乳或餵養者；餵養之物」），來自 nūtriō（意為「哺乳、餵養」），可能源自最古老的詞源。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English prudent, from Old French prudent, from Latin prūdēns, contracted from prōvidēns (“foresight”) (English providence), the present participle of prōvideō (“to forsee; to provide for”). Unrelated to prude. Doublet of provident. Displaced native Old English glēaw.
etymology.native: 「prudent」源自中世紀英文，來源為古法文 prudens，再源自拉丁文 prūdēns，是 prōvideō（意為「預見、提供」）的現在分詞，與「prude」無關，是「provident」的同源詞，取代了古英語 glēaw。

senses.definition: Taking a long time to move or go a short distance, or to perform an action; not quick in motion; proceeding at a low speed.
Not happening in a short time; spread over a comparatively long time.
Not hasty; not tending to hurry; acting with deliberation or caution.
Behind in time; indicating a time earlier than the true time.
Lacking spirit; deficient in liveliness or briskness.
Not busy; lacking activity.
Of reduced intellectual capacity; not quick to comprehend.

examples.text: Your watch is ten minutes slow.
examples.translation: 你的錶慢了10分鐘。

examples.text: My watch is five minutes slow.
examples.translation: 我的錶慢了五分鐘。

examples.text: If you do it a bit slower, it goes quicker.
examples.translation: 如果你做慢一點, 它就會進行的快一點。

examples.text: When PC problems slow you down, what can you do?
examples.translation: 當電腦出現問題導致您的工作速度變慢時，您該怎麼辦？

examples.text: Can you speak a little slower please?
examples.translation: 你們能稍微講慢點麼？

examples.text: The slow blue puma slides under the diligent cat.
examples.translation: 行動遲緩的藍色美洲獅從勤奮的貓身下滑過。

etymology.text: From Middle English slaw, slow, from Old English slāw (“lazy; inert, slow”), from Proto-West Germanic *slaiw, from Proto-Germanic *slaiwaz (“blunt; dull; exhausted, faint, sluggish, weak, weary; listless, torpid; dim-witted, slow; lazy, slack”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *sleyH-u- (“bad”).

senses.definition: Low or reduced in price.
Of poor quality.
Of little worth.
Trading at a price level which is low relative to historical trends, a similar asset, or (for derivatives) a theoretical value.
Taking little of system time or resources.
Underhanded or unfair.
Stingy; mean; excessively frugal.

examples.text: Oranges aren't as cheap as bananas.
examples.translation: 柳橙沒有香蕉便宜。

examples.text: Cheap meat doesn't make good soup.
examples.translation: 便宜的肉做不出好湯。

examples.text: Is it cheaper to call after 9:00?
examples.translation: 九點以後打電話比較便宜嗎？

examples.text: Show me a cheaper one, please.
examples.translation: 請給我看看便宜一點的。

examples.text: Is Warsaw cheaper than London?
examples.translation: 華沙比倫敦便宜嗎？

examples.text: This kind of cloth is both cheap and sturdy.
examples.translation: 這種布既便宜又結實。

etymology.text: As a noun, from Middle English chep, from Old English cēap (“trade, market, value”), from Proto-West Germanic *kaup. As a verb, from Middle English chepen, from Old English ċēapian (“to buy, bargain, trade”), from Proto-West Germanic *kaupōn, from Proto-Germanic *kaupōną, a verbal derivative of *kaupô (“trader”), from Latin caupō.

senses.definition: Taking care; attentive to potential danger, error or harm; cautious.
Conscientious and painstaking; meticulous.
Full of care or grief; sorrowful, sad.
Full of cares or anxiety; worried, troubled.

examples.text: Be careful when taking the taxi!
examples.translation: 大家搭車要注意喔！

examples.text: Be careful. It's slippery here.
examples.translation: 小心地滑。

examples.text: Tom needs to be very careful.
examples.translation: 湯姆需要很小心。

examples.text: You ought to be more careful.
examples.translation: 你應該要更小心。

examples.text: You must be careful in choosing your friends.
examples.translation: 交友須謹慎。

examples.text: Be careful. He's not an easy one to swindle.
examples.translation: 要留神，他不容易受騙。

etymology.text: From Middle English careful, from Old English carful; equivalent to care + -ful.

senses.definition: Characterized by very precise, conscientious attention to details.
Timid, fearful, overly cautious.

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: Tom is very meticulous about everything.
examples.translation: 湯姆對每件事都極為細心。

examples.text: She's very meticulous in her work.
examples.translation: 她在工作上非常細心。

examples.text: He's very meticulous in his work.
examples.translation: 他在工作上非常細心。

examples.text: Tom is so meticulous about the food he eats.
examples.translation: 湯姆對他所吃的食物極為講究細節。

examples.text: You think in a way that is very meticulous.
examples.translation: 你的思維方式非常講究細節。

examples.text: Tom is so meticulous in his choice of food.
examples.translation: 湯姆對他所選擇的食物極為講究細節。

etymology.text: Learned borrowing from Latin meticulōsus (“full of fear, timid, fearful, terrible, frightful”), from metus (“fear”) and -culōsus, extracted from perīculōsus (“perilous”). Sense of “characterized by very precise, conscientious attention to details” is a semantic loan from French méticuleux.
etymology.native: 此詞源自拉丁語 meticulōsus，由 metus（恐懼）與 -culōsus 組成。其「極度細心、注重細節」的含義是借自法語 méticuleux。

senses.definition: Enjoying good health; free from disease or disorder.
Conducive to health.
Evincing health.
Significant, hefty; beneficial.

examples.text: So, will this mean healthier cities?
examples.translation: 那麼，這代表更健康的城市嗎？

examples.text: To all appearances, she is healthy.
examples.translation: 無論從哪方面看，她很健康。

examples.text: Tom's grandmother looks healthy.
examples.translation: 湯姆的祖母好像身體很好。

examples.text: My grandfather is very healthy.
examples.translation: 我的祖父非常健康。

examples.text: His grandmother looks healthy.
examples.translation: 他祖母看起來很健康。

examples.text: Some of them are healthy, but others are not.
examples.translation: 他們中的一些人身體健康，但是其他人不是。

etymology.text: From health + -y.

senses.definition: An agent or representative; a reseller or distributor (sometimes with a private label); a consignee.
One of the elements, circumstances, or influences which contribute to produce a result.
Any of various objects multiplied together to form some whole.
A resource used in the production of goods or services, a factor of production.
A commission agent.
A person or business organization that provides money for another's new business venture; one who finances another's business.
A business organization that lends money on accounts receivable or buys and collects accounts receivable.
Influence; a phenomenon that affects the nature, the magnitude, and/or the timing of a consequence.
A steward or bailiff of an estate.
A doer, maker; a person who does things for another person or organization.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: There are many complicating factors.
examples.translation: 有許多複雜的因素。

examples.text: Several factors operated to help prices go up.
examples.translation: 物價上漲是多方因素造成的。

examples.text: What was the determining factor in this case?
examples.translation: 這個案子的決定性因素是什麼？

examples.text: So many factors were adduced in this sentence.
examples.translation: 這個句子舉出了這麼多因素。

examples.text: Honesty was the most important factor in his success.
examples.translation: 誠實是他成功最重要的因素。

examples.text: She considers environmental factors.
examples.translation: 她考慮環境因素。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English factour, from Middle French facteur, Anglo-Norman factour, and their etymon Latin factor (“a doer, maker, performer”), from factus (“done or made”), perfect passive participle of faciō (“do, make”).
etymology.native: 承襲自中古英語（factour），來自中古法語（facteur）、英法語（factour）及其源頭拉丁語（factor）「做者、製作者、執行者」，源自（faciō）「做」的完成式被動分詞（factus）。

senses.definition: Having the faculty of sensation; pertaining to the senses.
Responsive to stimuli.
Easily offended, upset, or hurt.
Capable of offending, upsetting, or hurting.
Meant to be concealed or kept secret.
Being aware of the feelings of others and taking care not to offend them.
Important, intricate, and requiring great delicacy.
Accurate; able to register small changes in some property.
Having paranormal abilities that can be controlled through mesmerism.

examples.text: She's very sensitive to cold.
examples.translation: 她非常怕冷。

examples.text: He is very sensitive.
examples.translation: 他很敏感。

examples.text: I am clever, sensitive and imaginative.
Cats' eyes are very sensitive to light.
examples.translation: 貓的眼睛對光很敏感。

examples.text: She is sensitive to the heat.
examples.translation: 她很怕熱。

examples.text: I am very sensitive to heat.
examples.translation: 我對熱氣很敏感。

etymology.text: From Middle French sensitif, from Medieval Latin sensitivus. By surface analysis, sense + -ite + -ive.

senses.definition: Firm in standing or position; not tottering or shaking; fixed; firm.
Constant in feeling, purpose, or pursuit; not fickle, changeable, or wavering; not easily moved or persuaded to alter a purpose; resolute.
Smooth and not bumpy or with obstructions.
Phlegmatic, calm; not easily upset, excited, or disturbed.
Regular and even.
Slow.
Confident and cool-headed under pressure; competent; reliable, adept.
With whom one is going steady.

examples.text: The footsteps were slow, but steady.
There was a steady increase in population.
examples.translation: 人口穩定地增加。

examples.text: When was the last time you had a steady job?
He was walking up the hill at a steady pace.
examples.translation: 他邁著穩健的步伐登上了山丘。

examples.text: The immigrants entered the country in a steady flow.
examples.translation: 移民川流不息地進入這個國家。

examples.text: My employment is not steady, only seasonal work.

etymology.text: From Middle English stedy, studi, stidiȝ, perhaps continuing Old English stæþþiġ, ġestæþþiġ (“steadfast, stable, firm, staid”), equivalent to stead + -y; or calquing Middle Low German or Middle Dutch stēdig. Cognate with Saterland Frisian stoadig (“steady”), West Frisian stadich (“slow”), Danish stedig, stadig, steeg, Swedish stadig, Icelandic stöðugur, German stätig, stetig.

senses.definition: Having a tendency to seek revenge when wronged, vengeful.
Punitive.

examples.text: Tom can be very vindictive.
examples.translation: 湯姆可以非常報復心強。

examples.text: Tom is feeling vindictive.
examples.translation: 湯姆正感到報復心強。

examples.text: Do not be so vindictive!
examples.translation: 別這麼報復心強！

examples.text: He became quite vindictive after his wife left him.
examples.translation: 妻子離開他後，他變得極度報復心強。

examples.text: Yuri wasn't a vindictive person at all.
examples.translation: 尤里根本不是個報復心強的人。

examples.text: More vindictive than jealous love.
examples.translation: 比嫉妒的愛更報復心強。

etymology.text: From Latin vindicta (“vengeance”) + -ive. Contrast Latin vindicātīvus.
etymology.native: 來自拉丁語 vindicta（報復）+ -ive。與拉丁語 vindicātīvus 相對。

senses.definition: Inclined to find fault or criticize.
Pertaining to, or indicating, a crisis or turning point.
Extremely important.
Relating to criticism or careful analysis, such as literary or film criticism.
Employing or related to textual criticism, particularly through a stemmatological comparison of all extant texts and reconstruction of the original.

Of a patient condition involving unstable vital signs and a prognosis that predicts the condition could worsen; or, a patient condition that requires urgent treatment in an intensive care or critical care medical facility.
In such a condition.
Likely to go out of control if disturbed, that is, opposite of stable.
Of the point (in temperature, reagent concentration etc.) where a nuclear or chemical reaction becomes self-sustaining.
Of a temperature that is equal to the temperature of the critical point of a substance, i.e. the temperature above which the substance cannot be liquefied.
Needing great discrimination to be correctly classified; easily confused.

examples.text: You're too critical of others' shortcomings.
Egyptian schools don't teach critical thinking.
She practices critical thinking every day.
I can't understand why you are so critical of him.
examples.translation: 我不明白為什麼你這麼批評他。

examples.text: Your mother is in critical condition.
examples.translation: 你母親現在情況危殆。

examples.text: The situation there was critical.
examples.translation: 那裡的情況很危急。

etymology.text: From Latin criticus + English -al.

senses.definition: The condition of being vindictive; a malevolent desire for revenge.

examples.text: We never ought to allow our instincts of justice to degenerate into mere vindictiveness.
examples.translation: 我們絕不應該讓我們的正義感淪為單純的報復心。

etymology.text: From vindictive + -ness.
etymology.native: 此詞由「報復的」加上表示狀態的後綴構成。

senses.definition: To add sauce to; to season.
To cause to relish anything, as if with a sauce; to tickle or gratify, as the palate; to please; to stimulate.
To make poignant; to give zest, flavour or interest to; to set off; to vary and render attractive.
To treat with bitter, pert, or tart language; to be impudent or saucy to.
To send or hand over.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Sauce the pasta before you serve it.
examples.translation: 上菜前先把醬汁淋在義大利麵上。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Middle English sauce, from Old French sause, from Vulgar Latin *salsa, noun use of the feminine of Latin salsus (“salted”), past participle of saliō (“to salt”), from sal. Doublet of salsa.
etymology.native: 「sauce」源自中世紀英文，來源為古法文 sause，再源自通俗拉丁文 *salsa，是拉丁文 salsus（意為「鹽味的」）的女性名詞用法，為 saliō（意為「鹽製」）的過去分詞，而 saliō 又來自 sal（鹽）。此詞與 salsa 為同源詞。

senses.definition: Something used to enhance the flavor of food, for example, salt or pepper, especially when added by the eater to taste rather than by the cook.

examples.text: Banana ketchup is a popular condiment in the Philippines.
examples.translation: 番茄醬是菲律賓流行的調味料。

examples.text: Failure is the condiment that gives success its flavor.
examples.translation: 失敗是賦予成功味道的調味料。

examples.text: Remember to check for any expired condiments and discard them.
examples.translation: 記得檢查是否有過期的調味料並丟棄。

examples.text: I add salt as a condiment to make my soup taste better.
examples.translation: 我加鹽作為調味料讓湯更好喝。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Many restaurants serve hot sauce as an optional condiment for customers.
examples.translation: 許多餐廳會提供熱辣醬作為顧客可選的調味料。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The dish required a judicious condiment to elevate its subtle aromatic profile.
examples.translation: 這道菜需要恰到好處的調味料來提升其微妙的芳香風味。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From late Middle English condiment, from Old French condiment, from Latin condimentum, from condīre (“to preserve, pickle, season”). See also condite and compare recondite.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 condiment，來自古法語 condiment，再來自拉丁語 condimentum，意為「保存、醃漬或調味」。

senses.definition: The act or process of irrigating, or the state of being irrigated; especially, the operation of causing water to flow over lands, for nourishing plants.

examples.text: The aquifer provides water for irrigation.
examples.translation: 地下水可供灌溉使用。

examples.text: Algeria needs to use proper irrigation techniques.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞需採用合適的灌溉技術。

examples.text: The Tuaregs use these wells for small-scale irrigation.
examples.translation: 圖阿雷格人利用這些水井進行小規模灌溉。

examples.text: Algeria needs to encourage the use of proper irrigation techniques.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞需鼓勵使用合適的灌溉技術。

examples.text: Algeria needs to use drip irrigation to improve crop yields.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞需採用滴灌技術以提高作物產量。

examples.text: In order to farm in this arid area, artificial irrigation is necessary.
examples.translation: 欲在這片乾旱地區耕作，必須依靠人工灌溉。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French irrigation, from Latin irrigatio.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀法語的灌溉，來自拉丁語 irrigatio。

senses.definition: An item of goods or supplies, especially food, obtained for future use.
The act of providing, or making previous preparation.
Money set aside for a future event.
A liability or contra account to recognise likely future adverse events associated with current transactions.
A clause in a legal instrument, a law, etc., providing for a particular matter; stipulation; proviso.
Regular induction into a benefice, comprehending nomination, collation, and installation.
A nomination by the pope to a benefice before it became vacant, depriving the patron of his right of presentation.

examples.text: Tom was in need of provisions.
Have you made provisions?
Tom steals provisions.
These provisions are flown in from Algiers.
The provisions ran out after a short time.
They took enough provisions for three years at sea.

etymology.text: From Middle English provisioun, from Old French provisïon, from Latin prōvīsiō (“preparation, foresight”), from prōvidēre (“provide”).

senses.definition: A natural or artificial means for the removal of fluids from a given area by its draining away.
A system of drains.
A downward wind.

examples.text: Heathers like good drainage.
examples.translation: 石南草喜歡排水良好的環境。

examples.text: The drainage is blocked.
examples.translation: 排水系統被阻塞了。

examples.text: We installed a new culvert to improve drainage.
examples.translation: 我們安裝了一條新的涵洞來改善排水。

examples.text: The drainage is not sufficient.
examples.translation: 排水量不足夠。

examples.text: The drainage systems are not able to handle the water pressure.
examples.translation: 排水系統無法承受水壓。

examples.text: The spa offers lymphatic drainage massages.
examples.translation: 該溫泉提供淋巴引流按摩。

etymology.text: From drain + -age.
etymology.native: 由「drain」加上後綴「-age」組成。

senses.definition: Anything that sprinkles.
An irrigation device that sprays water into the air whilst moving back and forth.
senses.native: 噴灑裝置、噴灌器、灑水器

senses.definition: A heat-activated device that sprays water in the event of a fire, usually mounted on a ceiling.
A dance move in which the dancer places one hand on the head behind the ear, with elbow bent, stretches the other arm forwards and mimics the motions of an irrigation sprinkler with a rotary head.

examples.text: Tom turned off the sprinkler.
examples.translation: 湯姆關掉了灑水器。

examples.text: This building has sprinklers.
examples.translation: 這棟大樓有灑水器。

examples.text: Turn off the sprinklers.
examples.translation: 把灑水器關掉。

examples.text: She has a sprinkler system in her front yard.
examples.translation: 她前院有灑水系統。

examples.text: I thought this building had a sprinkler system.
examples.translation: 我以為這棟大樓有自動灑水系統。

examples.text: The sprinkler broke and the gardener had to use the hose again.
examples.translation: 灑水器壞了，園丁只好再用水龍頭。

etymology.text: From sprinkle + -er.
etymology.native: 由「灑」加表示工具的字尾組成。

senses.definition: The probability of a negative outcome to a decision or event.
The potential negative effect of an event, determined by multiplying the likelihood of the event occurring with its magnitude should it occur.
The magnitude of possible loss consequent to a decision or event.
A possible adverse event or outcome.
A type of adverse event covered under an insurance policy.
A thing (from the perspective of how likely or unlikely it is to cause an adverse effect).
A borrower (such as a mortgage-holder or person with a credit card).
A financial product (typically an investment).
An entity insured by an insurer.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: They identified the risk factors.
examples.translation: 他們確認了風險因素。

examples.text: I don't worry about the risk.
examples.translation: 我不擔心風險。

examples.text: The risk is too great.
examples.translation: 風險太大。

examples.text: We're all at risk.
examples.translation: 我們都處於危險之中。

examples.text: In order to do that, you have to take risks.
examples.translation: 要這麼做，你需要冒險。

examples.text: He saved my life at the risk of his own.
examples.translation: 他冒著生命危險救了我的命。

etymology.text: From earlier risque, from Middle French risque, from Old Italian risco (“risk”) (modern Italian rischio) and rischiare (“to run into danger”). Displaced native Old English pleoh (“risk”) and plēon (“to risk”).
etymology.native: 源自較早的（risque），來自中古法語（risque），再源自古義大利語（risco）「風險」（現代義大利語 rischio）與（rischiare）「冒險」。取代了古英語原有的（pleoh）「風險」與（plēon）「冒險」。

senses.definition: Food given to (especially herbivorous) non-human animals.
Something supplied continuously.
The part of a machine that supplies the material to be operated upon.
senses.native: 機器中供給加工材料的部分（供料器）

senses.definition: The part of a fountain pen that supplies ink to the nib.
senses.native: 鋼筆中向筆尖供應墨水的部分（墨水供應器）

senses.definition: The forward motion of the material fed into a machine.
senses.native: 送入機器的材料的前進運動（進料）

senses.definition: A meal.
A gathering to eat, especially in large quantities.
senses.native: 聚餐（尤指大量飲食的聚會）

senses.definition: antichronological sequence of posts or articles from a single source, especially as consumable on a platform other as originally published.
senses.native: （社群）來自單一來源的貼文或文章依時間倒序排列的資訊流

senses.definition: content intended for consumption by scrolling or swiping, especially as a home page and from multiple publishers followed or algorithmically curated
senses.native: 供人滑動瀏覽的內容（尤指首頁，來自多個發布者或由演算法推薦）

senses.definition: A straight man who delivers lines to the comedian during a performance.
senses.native: （喜劇）捧哏（在表演中為主角提供台詞的配角）

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Please feed the dog every day.
examples.translation: 請每天喂一下狗。

examples.text: Pandas feed on bamboo grass.
examples.translation: 熊貓以竹為食。

examples.text: These animals feed on grass.
examples.translation: 這幾種動物是吃草的。

examples.text: It's time to feed the sheep.
examples.translation: 是時候餵羊了。

examples.text: I feed my cat every morning and every evening.
examples.translation: 每天早晚，我給我的貓餵食。

examples.text: Tom had to remind Mary to feed the dog.
examples.translation: 湯姆不得不提醒瑪麗亞餵狗。

etymology.text: From Middle English feden, from Old English fēdan (“to feed”), from Proto-West Germanic *fōdijan, from Proto-Germanic *fōdijaną (“to feed”), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂- (“to guard, graze, feed”). Cognate with West Frisian fiede (“to nourish, feed”), Dutch voeden (“to feed”), Danish føde (“to bring forth, feed”), Swedish föda (“to bring forth, feed”), Icelandic fæða (“to feed”), and more distantly with Latin pāscō (“feed, nourish”, verb) through Indo-European. senses.definition: British form of inquiry.

examples.text: After a few weeks, my enquiry was finally dealt with.

examples.text: So, I phoned National Rail Enquiries yesterday afternoon.

etymology.text: From Middle English enquery, from the Old French verb enquerre, from Latin inquīrō, composed of in- (“in, at, on; into”) + quaerō (“to seek, look for”), of uncertain origin, but possibly from Proto-Italic *kʷaizeō, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷeh₂- (“to acquire”). The alternative form inquiry was subsequently respelled to conform to the original Latin spelling, as opposed to the Old French spelling.
etymology.native: 「enquery」源自中世英文，來源為古法文動詞 enquerre，再源自拉丁文 inquīrō，由 in-（「在、於、向」）+ quaerō（「尋求、找尋」）組成，其詞源不明，但可能來自原始伊特魯里亞語 *kʷaizeō，而該詞又可能源自原始印歐語 *kʷeh₂-（「取得」）。另一形式「inquiry」則因應拉丁文原拼法，後改寫以符合拉丁文拼法，而非古法文拼法。

etymology.text: From scape + goat; coined by English biblical scholar and translator William Tyndale, interpreting Biblical Hebrew עֲזָאזֵל (“azazél”) (Leviticus 16:8, 10, 26), from an interpretation as coming from עֵז (ez, “goat”) and אוזל (ozél, “escapes”). etymology.native: 此詞源自「scape」與「goat」，由英國聖經學者與翻譯家威廉·譚代爾創製，用以翻譯希伯來文「עֲזָאזֵל」（azazél），出自利未記16:8、10、26，意指由「עֵז」（ez，「山羊」）與「אוזל」（ozél，「逃脫」）組成。最早見於1530年。可參見英文詞「scapegrace」與「scapegallows」。

etymology.text: From Old English port, borrowed from Latin portus (“port, harbour”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *pértus (“crossing”) (and thus a distant doublet of ford). The directional sense, attested since at least the 1500s, derives from ancient vessels with the steering oar on the right (see etymology of starboard), which therefore had to moor with their left sides facing the dock or wharf. Doublet of fjard, fjord, firth, ford, and Portus.

senses.native: （縫帆）頂針，套在手掌上的金屬圓盤，用來推針穿過帆布

senses.definition: The broad flattened part of an antler, as of a full-grown fallow deer; so called as resembling the palm of the hand with its protruding fingers.
senses.native: （鹿角）掌狀部，成年黇鹿鹿角寬扁的部分

senses.definition: The flat inner face of an anchor fluke.
Synonym of hand, any of various units of length notionally derived from the breadth of the palm, formalized in England as 4 inches and now chiefly used for the height of horses
senses.native: 掌（長度單位），源自手掌寬度，英制定為四英寸，今主要用於量馬高

senses.definition: Any of various units of length notionally derived from the length of the palm from the wrist to the base of the fingers.
senses.native: （長度單位）掌，源自手掌長度的各種單位

examples.text: An A6 notebook is just a little bigger than a palm.
examples.translation: 一個A6的本子大概就比巴掌大一點。

examples.text: I can place the palms of my hands on the floor without bending my knees.
examples.translation: 我不彎膝也能把手掌平放在地上。

etymology.text: From Middle English palme, from Old English palm, palma (“palm-tree, palm-branch”), from Latin palma (“palm-tree, palm-branch, palm of the hand”), from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥h₂meh₂, *pl̥h₂emeh₂ (“palm of the hand”), from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat”). Cognate with Dutch palm, German Palme, Danish palme, Icelandic pálmur (“palm”).

senses.definition: A fanciful impulse, or sudden change of idea.
A large capstan or vertical drum turned by horse power or steam power, for raising ore or water, etc., from mines, or for other purposes.
A bird, the Eurasian wigeon.

examples.text: He indulges all her whims.
examples.translation: 他滿足她所有的任性。

examples.text: It's just a whim of yours.
examples.translation: 這只是你的任性。

examples.text: He can't make decisions like that on a whim.
examples.translation: 他不能隨便就做這種決定。

examples.text: At work they are at the whim of the boss.
examples.translation: 在公司裡，他們完全聽從主管的安排。

examples.text: This is not a whim; it’s a deep, personal choice.
examples.translation: 這不是任性；這是深層的個人選擇。

examples.text: On a whim, he learnt the periodic table off by heart.
examples.translation: 他隨便一想，就把週期表背熟了。

etymology.text: Clipping of whim-wham.
etymology.native: whim-wham 的縮略形式。

senses.definition: Mental apprehension of whatever may be known, thought, or imagined; idea, concept.
A sentiment; an opinion.
Any small article used in sewing and haberdashery, either for attachment to garments or as a tool, such as a button, zipper, or thimble.
An invention; an ingenious device; a knickknack.
Inclination; intention; predisposition; disposition.
Pretentiousness or overambition.
Sense; mind.

examples.text: Futurology includes notions of probabilities.
It challenged my preconceived notions.
He has some pretty strange notions.
His notion is that planes are safer than cars.
What on earth put such a notion into your head?
We had no notion of leaving our hometown.

etymology.text: From Latin nōtiō (“a becoming acquainted, a taking cognizance, an examination, an investigation, a conception, idea, notion”), from nōscō (“to know”). Compare French notion. See know.

senses.definition: Something to play with, especially as intended for use by a child.
A thing of little importance or value; a trifle.
A simple, light piece of music, written especially for the virginal.
Love play, amorous dalliance; fondling.
A vague fancy, a ridiculous idea or notion; a whim.
An old story; a silly tale.
A headdress of linen or wool that hangs down over the shoulders, worn by elderly women of the lower classes.
An inferior graffiti artist.
A gun.
The penis.
The vagina.
A watch.
A small jar (about an inch across) used to hold prepared opium.
A small ball of opium (about the size of a pea).

examples.text: The children are playing with toys.
examples.translation: 小孩們在玩玩具。

examples.text: This toy car runs on batteries.
examples.translation: 這個玩具汽車是裝電池的。

examples.text: He gathered his toys together.
examples.translation: 他收起了他的玩具。

examples.text: This factory produces toys.
examples.translation: 這個工廠製造玩具。

examples.text: He deprived my little sister of all her toys.
examples.translation: 他把我妹妹的玩具都搶走了。

examples.text: It was her little sister that broke her toy.
examples.translation: 她的玩具是被她妹妹弄壞的。

relations.native: 非他也非她者；生物；被非人化的存在

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English toye (“amorous play, piece of fun or entertainment”), probably from Middle Dutch toy, tuyg (“tools, apparatus, utensil, ornament”) as in Dutch speel-tuig (“plaything, toy”), from Old Dutch *tiug, from Proto-West Germanic *tiugī̆, *teug, from Proto-Germanic *teugą (“stuff, matter, device, gear, lever”, literally “that which is drawn or pulled”), from Proto-Germanic *teuhaną (“to lead, bring, pull”), from Proto-Indo-European *dewk- (“to pull, lead”).

senses.definition: A playful activity that may be unstructured; an amusement or pastime.
A particular instance of playing a game.
In some games, a point awarded to the player whose cards add up to the largest sum.
Something that resembles a game with rules, despite not being designed.
An exercise simulating warfare, whether computerized or involving human participants.
A questionable or unethical practice in pursuit of a goal.
Wild animals hunted for food.
A flock of swans, especially as kept for hunting purposes (or, originally, a group of any animals kept for such purpose).
An activity described by a set of rules, especially for the purpose of entertainment, often competitive or having an explicit goal.
A school subject during which sports are practised.
Part of a set during which one player continuously serves (at least four rallies must be won to win a game, at least six games must be won to win the set).
That which is gained, such as the stake in a game.
The number of points necessary to win a game.
The equipment that enables such activity, particularly as packaged under a title.
One's manner, style, or performance in playing a game.
A field of gainful activity, as an industry or profession.
The music industry.
The ability to seduce or woo someone, usually by strategy.
Lovemaking, flirtation.
Prostitution. (Now chiefly in on the game.)

examples.text: We enjoyed watching the baseball game.
examples.translation: 我們喜歡看棒球比賽。

examples.text: Tom is always playing video games.
examples.translation: 湯姆總是在玩電視遊樂器。

examples.text: Everybody plays the game of love.
examples.translation: 大家都玩愛情遊戲。

examples.text: Which game are you talking about?
examples.translation: 你在說哪個遊戲？

examples.text: The baseball game was called off due to rain.
examples.translation: 棒球比賽因為天雨取消了。

examples.text: Whatever game I play with you, you never win.
examples.translation: 無論我和你玩甚麼遊戲，你也總是輸。

etymology.text: From Middle English game, gamen, gammen, from Old English gamen (“sport, joy, mirth, pastime, game, amusement, pleasure”), from Proto-West Germanic *gaman, from Proto-Germanic *gamaną (“amusement, pleasure, game", literally "participation, communion, people together”), from *ga- (collective prefix) + *mann- (“man”); or alternatively from *ga- + a root from Proto-Indo-European *men- (“to think, have in mind”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（game、gamen），來自古英語（gamen）「運動、歡樂、消遣、遊戲」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*gamaną）「娛樂、遊戲」，字面意為「參與、共處」，由集合字首（*ga-）加（*mann-）「人」組成；或另說來自原始印歐語（*men-）「想」。

senses.definition: A state of being pleased or contented; gratification.
A person, thing or action that causes enjoyment.
Sexual enjoyment.
One's preference.
The will or desire of someone or some agency in power.

examples.text: He lives for nothing but pleasure.
examples.translation: 他生活除了享樂之外沒別的了。

examples.text: Reading gives me great pleasure.
examples.translation: 閱讀帶給我巨大的快樂。

examples.text: It's our pleasure.
examples.translation: 這是我們的榮幸。

examples.text: Few things give us as much pleasure as music.
examples.translation: 很少有東西像音樂一樣帶給我們這麼多的快樂。

examples.text: Did you go abroad for pleasure or on business?
examples.translation: 你去國外是玩兒還是出差？

examples.text: "Thank you for your help." "It's my pleasure."
examples.translation: 「謝謝你的幫助。」　「不用謝。」

etymology.text: From Early Modern English pleasur, plesur, alteration (with ending accommodated to -ure) of Middle English plaisir (“pleasure”), from Old French plesir, plaisir (“to please”), infinitive used as a noun, conjugated form of plaisir or plaire, from Latin placeō (“to please, to seem good”), from the Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂-k- (“wide and flat”). Related to Dutch plezier (“pleasure, fun”). More at please.

senses.definition: Violent derangement of mind; madness; insanity.
Excessive or unreasonable desire; insane passion affecting one or many people; fanaticism.
The state of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, arousal, and/or energy levels.
senses.native: 異常亢奮、易怒的情緒、興奮或能量狀態

examples.text: Manias can be alarming.
examples.translation: 狂躁症可能令人擔憂。

examples.text: Something about big cities triggers mania in me.
examples.translation: 某些關於大城市的因素會在我身上引發狂躁。

examples.text: I don't understand all the soccer mania.
examples.translation: 我不完全明白所有的足球狂熱。

examples.text: He has mania for sports cars.
examples.translation: 他對賽車車的狂熱令人印象深刻。

examples.text: I get hypomanic, but rarely does this become full-blown mania.
examples.translation: 我會有輕度躁鬱，但這很少發展成完全發作的狂躁症。

examples.text: This is pure and sterile mania of protagonism for its own sake.
examples.translation: 這是純粹且無菌的、為本身而存在的 protagonism 狂熱。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin mania, from Ancient Greek μανία (manía, “madness”).
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 mania，來自古希臘語 μανία（madness）。

senses.definition: A contract which binds a person to work for another, under specified conditions, for a specified time (often as an apprentice).
A contract relating to lending (typically for issuing a bond), a real estate transaction, or a bankruptcy that imposes additional conditions on one or both parties.
A document, written as duplicates separated by indentations, specifying either of the above contracts.
An indentation; a recess.

examples.text: The indenture required me to work 40 hours weekly for a year.
examples.translation: 此契約規定我須每周工作四十小時，持續一年。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The indenture specifies my duties, hours, and end date clearly.
examples.translation: 契約明確列明我的職責、時數與終止日期。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: I must follow the indenture’s terms or face penalties.
examples.translation: 我必須遵守契約條款，否則將面臨懲罰。

examples.text: The indenture binds me to work under specific conditions for a year.
examples.translation: 契約約束我於特定條件下服役一年。

examples.text: This indenture includes clauses on pay, hours, and termination.
examples.translation: 此契約包含薪資、時數與終止條款。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The indenture is legally binding and enforceable in court.
examples.translation: 契約具法律效力，可於法院執行。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Anglo-Norman endenture, from Old French endenteure, from endenter (“to dent”). The name of the contract derives from the irregular dent-shaped cut (indentation) used to prove the authenticity of the two parts, similar to a chirograph.
etymology.native: 此詞源自盎格魯-諾曼語 endenture，來源於古法語 endenteure，又源自 endenter（意為「齒狀凹陷」）。合約之名來自於用不規則的齒狀凹陷（凹痕）來證明兩部分真實性，類似於手寫契約。

senses.definition: To bind a person under such a contract.
To indent; to make hollows, notches, or wrinkles in; to furrow.

examples.text: Though age may creep on, and indenture the brow.
examples.translation: 雖年歲漸長，亦不免契約刻皺眉間。

etymology.text: From Anglo-Norman endenture, from Old French endenteure, from endenter (“to dent”). The name of the contract derives from the irregular dent-shaped cut (indentation) used to prove the authenticity of the two parts, similar to a chirograph.
etymology.native: 此詞源自盎格魯-諾曼語 endenture，來源於古法語 endenteure，又源自 endenter（意為「齒狀凹陷」）。合約之名來自於用不規則的齒狀凹陷（凹痕）來證明兩部分真實性，類似於手寫契約。

senses.definition: Confidence in or reliance on some person or quality.
Dependence upon something in the future; hope.
Confidence in the future payment for goods or services supplied; credit.
That which is committed or entrusted; something received in confidence; a charge.
That upon which confidence is reposed; ground of reliance; hope.
The condition or obligation of one to whom anything is confided; responsible charge or office.
The confidence vested in a person who has legal ownership of a property to manage for the benefit of another.

An arrangement whereby property or money is given to be held by a third party (a trustee), on the basis that it will be managed for the benefit of, or eventually transferred to, a stated beneficiary; for example, money to be given to a child when he or she reaches adulthood.
A group of businessmen or traders organised for mutual benefit to produce and distribute specific commodities or services, and managed by a central body of trustees.
Affirmation of the access rights of a user of a computer system.
Trustworthiness, reliability.

examples.text: You shouldn't trust people like this.
examples.translation: 您不應該信任這樣的人。

examples.text: He's the only friend I trust.
examples.translation: 他是我唯一信任的朋友。

examples.text: They didn't trust each other.
examples.translation: 他們彼此不信任。

examples.text: No one trusts him any more.
examples.translation: 再沒有人相信他了。

examples.text: I don't trust him any more.
examples.translation: 我不再相信他了。

examples.text: I suggest that you don't trust Tom too much.
examples.translation: 我建議你別太相信湯姆。

etymology.text: From Middle English trust, trost (“trust, protection”). Long considered a borrowing from Old Norse traust (“confidence, help, protection”), from Proto-Germanic *traustą, but the root vocalism is incompatible, so trust has come to be considered a reflex of an unattested Old English *trust, from a rare zero-grade Proto-Germanic variant of the same root also attested in Middle High German getrüste (“host”). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *deru- (“be firm, hard, solid”).

senses.definition: A proposal that has been made.
the verbal act of offering
something offered (as a proposal or bid)
a usually brief attempt
Something put forth, bid, proffered or tendered.
An invitation to enter into a binding contract communicated to another party which contains terms sufficiently definite to create an enforceable contract if the other party accepts the invitation.

examples.text: English has a lot of idiomatic expressions to offer.
examples.translation: 英語有很多慣用語。

examples.text: Following a wave of other recent sports simulations, this release offers ball game fans a more authentic management experience.
examples.translation: 在多款體育類模擬遊戲陸續登場後，這款作品為熱愛球類運動的玩家帶來更真實的管理體驗。

relations.native: 連接河流或水域與大海的水道（如河口三角洲的水道）

etymology.text: From Middle English offer, from Old English offrian (“offer or make a sacrifice”) rather than from Old French offre (“offer”), from offrir (“to offer”), from Latin offerō (“to present, bring before”). Compare North Frisian offer (“sacrifice, donation, fee”), Dutch offer (“offering, sacrifice”), German Opfer (“victim, sacrifice”), Danish offer (“victim, sacrifice”), Icelandic offr (“offering”). See verb below.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（offer），來自古英語（offrian）「獻祭」，而非來自古法語（offre）；兩者最終都源自拉丁語（offerō）「呈獻」。比較荷蘭語（offer）「祭品」、德語（Opfer）「受害者、犧牲」。

senses.definition: Synonym of lease (an interest in land, its related contract or the document containing that contract); more commonly used when a lease is short-term or has a periodic rent that is not merely nominal.

examples.text: If your tenancy is being threatened, contact us.
examples.translation: 如果您的租約受到威脅，請聯絡我們。

examples.text: Your tenancy is being terminated.
examples.translation: 您的租約已被終止。

examples.text: A tenancy agreement is a legally binding document between a landlord and their tenant.
examples.translation: 租約是房東與房客之間具有法律約束力的文件。

examples.text: I have a tenancy agreement with my landlord.
examples.translation: 我與我的房東有租約。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: My family shares the same tenancy in this house.
examples.translation: 我的家人在同一棟房子裡共享租約。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The new tenant will start his tenancy next week.
examples.translation: 新房客下週開始他的租約。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From tenant + -cy.
etymology.native: 來自 tenant 加上 -cy 詞尾。

senses.definition: To create or edit the layout of a document.
Change a document so it will fit onto a different type of page.
To prepare a mass storage medium for initial use, erasing any existing data in the process.

examples.text: I just formatted my computer.
I've formatted your hard disk by mistake.
examples.translation: 我不小心格式化了你的硬碟。

examples.text: I lost weeks of work when I inadvertently formatted my hard drive.
Format this letter so it can be printed out.
Please format this disk before entering data!

etymology.text: Via French format and German Format, from New Latin liber fōrmātus (“book fashioned”), from fōrmō (“to shape, fashion”).

senses.definition: to identify by or divide into classes; to categorize
to declare something a secret, especially a government secret
To make classy

examples.text: Automated systems can classify news articles.
examples.translation: 自動化系統可以為新聞文章分類。

examples.text: Please classify these books by subject.
examples.translation: 請把這些書依主題分類。

examples.text: We should classify them before throwing them out.
examples.translation: 我們在扔掉之前得分類。

examples.text: These can be classified roughly into three types.
examples.translation: 這些大致可以分成三類。

examples.text: One can classify books into good ones and bad ones.
examples.translation: 書可以分成好書和壞書。

examples.text: Is Algeria classified as a middle-income country?
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞被歸類為中等收入國家嗎？

etymology.text: From French classifier. By surface analysis, class + -ify.
etymology.native: 源自法語；表面上可拆為「類別」加「使成為」字尾。

senses.definition: To be in harmony about an opinion, statement, or action; to have a consistent idea between two or more people.
To give assent; to accede.
To yield assent to; to approve.
To make a stipulation by way of settling differences or determining a price; to exchange promises; to come to terms or to a common resolve; to promise.
To resemble; to coincide; to correspond; to tally.
To suit or be adapted in its effects; to do well.
To correspond to (another word) in a grammatical category, such as gender, number, case, or person.
To consent to a contract or to an element of a contract.

examples.text: I don't agree with you smoking.
examples.translation: 我不贊成你吸菸。

examples.text: I couldn't agree with you more.
examples.translation: 我再同意你不過了。

examples.text: I'm starting to agree with you.
examples.translation: 我開始同意你的想法了。

examples.text: It's strange that Ken doesn't agree with us.
examples.translation: 很奇怪肯竟然沒有同意我們。

examples.text: This account does not agree with the facts.
examples.translation: 報告和事實不相符。

examples.text: It is strange for Ken not to agree with us.
examples.translation: 肯不同意我們，是件奇怪的事。

etymology.text: From Middle English agreen, from Old French agreer (“to accept or receive kindly”), from a gré (“favorably”), from Latin ad (“to”) + gratum (“pleasing”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gʷerH- (“to welcome, greet, praise”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（agreen），來自古法語（agreer）「欣然接受」，源自（a gré）「樂意地」，再上溯至拉丁語（ad）「向」加（gratum）「令人愉悅的」，最終來自原始印歐語（*gʷerH-）「歡迎、稱讚」。

senses.definition: To dictate policy.
To control or direct according to rule, principle, or law.
To adjust (a mechanism) for accurate and proper functioning.
To put or maintain in order.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Melatonin helps to regulate circadian rhythms.
Emotions are hard to regulate.
Zucchini regulates digestion.
Traffic lights are used to regulate traffic.
examples.translation: 交通燈是用來控制交通的。

examples.text: Rice prices are regulated by the government.
Many countries try to regulate the birth rate.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin regulatus, perfect passive participle of regulō (“to direct, rule, regulate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from regula (“rule”), from regō (“to keep straight, direct, govern, rule”). Compare regle, rail. Displaced native Old English metegian.

senses.definition: To form a line; to fall into line.
To store (data) in a way that is consistent with the memory architecture, i.e. by beginning each item at an offset equal to some multiple of the word size.
To organize a linear arrangement of DNA, RNA, or protein sequences which have regions of similarity.
To identify entities that refer to the same real-world object in different knowledge bases.
To adjust to a line; to range or form in line; to bring into line.
To organize in a consistent, defined way, perhaps in an abstract sense.
senses.native: 使有系統地整理、一致化

senses.definition: To identify (oneself) with, match, or support the behaviour, thoughts, etc. of another person, organization, or country.
senses.native: 使（自己）與他人、組織或國家的立場一致，或表示認同與支持

examples.text: Align the jars.
We can use braces to align your teeth better.
Align all the soldiers for their daily checkup.
Align yourself with the Will to Unify...
Make sure you align the faucet properly before installing.
I tried to align the pieces of metal perfectly together before soldering them.

etymology.text: From Middle English alynen, alinen (“copulate”), from Middle French aligner, from Old French alignier, from a- + lignier, from Latin lineare (“make straight or perpendicular”), from the noun linea (“line”), from līneus (“flaxen; flaxen [thing]”), from līnum (“flax”), likely ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *līnom (compare linen).

senses.definition: To cry out, as in sorrow or anguish.
To weep, lament persistently or bitterly.
To make a noise like mourning or crying.
To lament; to bewail; to grieve over.
To perform with great liveliness and force.
Synonym of wale (“to choose; to select”).

examples.text: The sirens are wailing.
examples.translation: 警報聲在鳴叫。

examples.text: The sirens wailed.
examples.translation: 警報聲曾鳴叫過。

examples.text: She was wailing when her son passed away.
examples.translation: 她兒子過世時正在哭喊。

examples.text: The baby wailed because it was hungry.

etymology.text: c. 1300, Middle English weilen, waylen (“to sob, cry, wail”), from Old Norse væla (“to wail”), from væ, vei (“woe”), from Proto-Germanic *wai (whence also Old English wā (“woe”) (English woe)), from Proto-Indo-European *wáy.

etymology.text: c. 1300, Middle English weilen, waylen (“to sob, cry, wail”), from Old Norse væla (“to wail”), from væ, vei (“woe”), from Proto-Germanic *wai (whence also Old English wā (“woe”) (English woe)), from Proto-Indo-European *wáy.
etymology.native: 1300年中世英文 weilen, waylen（「哭泣、哀嚎」），源自古諾斯語 væla（「哀嚎」），自 væ, vei（「悲慘」），源自古高地德語 *wai（亦見古英語 wā（「悲慘」）），自印歐語系 *wáy。

etymology.text: A back-formation from lamentation or else from Middle French lamenter and its etymon Latin lāmentor (“to wail, weep”), from lāmentum (“wailing, moaning, weeping”); with formative -mentum, from the root *la-, probably ultimately imitative. Also see latrare.
etymology.native: 源自中法語 lamenter 或拉丁語 lāmentor，後者來自 lāmentum（哭號、呻吟），詞根 *la- 可能為擬聲詞。另見 latrare。

senses.definition: The act of complaining.
A grievance, problem, difficulty, or concern.
In a civil action, the first pleading of the plaintiff setting out the facts on which the claim is based.
In criminal law, the preliminary charge or accusation made by one person against another to the appropriate court or officer, usually a magistrate.
A bodily disorder or disease; the symptom of such a disorder.

etymology.text: From Middle English compleynte, from Anglo-Norman compleint, from Old French compleindre, eventually from Latin planctus (whence plaint).

senses.definition: The U.S. Republican Party.
Of the lower-frequency region of the (typically visible) part of the electromagnetic spectrum which is relevant in the specific observation.

senses.definition: Of a red color charge.
Amerind; relating to Amerindians or First Nations.

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English red, from Old English rēad, from Proto-West Germanic *raud, from Proto-Germanic *raudaz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rowdʰós, from *h₁rewdʰ- + *-ós.

senses.definition: Having a deep red colour.
Immodest.

examples.translation: 請給我這八個深紅色的蘋果。

examples.text: The acer leaf was the perfect shade of crimson.
examples.translation: 那棵楓樹的葉子呈現完美的深紅色。

examples.text: The crimson flowers will bloom in January.
examples.translation: 深紅色的花朵將在一月開花。

etymology.text: Late Middle English cremesyn, from obsolete French cramoisin or Old Spanish cremesín, from Arabic قِرْمِز (qirmiz), from Classical Persian کرمست (kirmist), from Middle Persian; see Proto-Indo-Iranian *kŕ̥miš. Cognate with Sanskrit कृमिज (kṛmija). Doublet of kermes; also see carmine.
etymology.native: 源於古法語 cramoisin 或舊西班牙語 cremesín，後者來自阿拉伯語 qirmiz，再源自中古波斯語；與梵語 kṛmija 同源。

senses.definition: A root (of a number or quantity).
In logographic writing systems such as the Chinese writing system, the portion of a character (if any) that provides an indication of its meaning, as opposed to being wholly phonetic.
Any component of a logographic character, whether used for indexing or not, whether semantic or not.
In Celtic languages, the basic, underlying form of an initial consonant which can be further mutated under the Celtic initial consonant mutations.
In Semitic languages, any one of the set of consonants (typically three) that make up a root.
A group of atoms, joined by covalent bonds, that take part in reactions as a single unit.
A free radical.

Given an ideal I in a commutative ring R, another ideal, denoted Rad(I) or √, such that an element x ∈ R is in Rad(I) if, for some positive integer n, xⁿ ∈ I; equivalently, the intersection of all prime ideals containing I.
Given a ring R, an ideal containing elements of R that share a property considered, in some sense, "not good".
The intersection of maximal submodules of a given module.
The product of the distinct prime factors of a given positive integer.
A member of the most progressive wing of the Liberal Party; someone favouring social reform (but generally stopping short of socialism).
A member of an influential, centrist political party favouring moderate social reform, a republican constitution, and secular politics.
A person with radical opinions.

examples.translation: 今天的激進也許是明天的老生常談。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English radical, from Latin rādīcālis (“of or pertaining to the root, having roots, radical”). Compare grassroots.

A student or player on a sports team at the University of Louisville.
A deep red color, somewhat less vivid than scarlet, the traditional colour of a Catholic cardinal's cassock. (same as cardinal red)
A woman's short cloak with a hood, originally made of scarlet cloth.

Cognate with Saterland Frisian bläidich, blöidig, blouderch (“bloody”), West Frisian bloedich (“bloody”), Dutch bloedig (“bloody”), German Low German blödig (“bloody”), German blutig (“bloody”), Danish blodig (“bloody”), Swedish blodig (“bloody”), Faroese blóðigur (“bloody”), Icelandic blóðugur (“bloody”). etymology.native: 14世紀，經法語與拉丁語由古希臘語 ἀγωνία（agōnía，意為「競賽、競爭、掙扎」）來，源自 ἀγών（agṓn，意為「比賽」）。特指臨死前的掙扎（mortal agony）自1540年代開始。表面分析為 agon + -y。

senses.definition: Intense pleasure.

etymology.text: From Old French estaise (“ecstasy, rapture”), from Latin ecstasis, from Ancient Greek ἔκστασις (ékstasis), from ἐξίστημι (exístēmi, “to displace”), from ἐκ (ek, “out”) and ἵστημι (hístēmi, “to stand”).

senses.definition: A true desire sustained or prolonged.
Any great, strong, powerful emotion, especially romantic love or extreme hate.
Fervor, determination.
An object of passionate or romantic love or strong romantic interest.
Sexual intercourse, especially when very emotional.
The suffering of Jesus leading up to and during his crucifixion.
A display, musical composition, or play meant to commemorate the suffering of Jesus.
Suffering or enduring of imposed or inflicted pain; any suffering or distress.
The state of being acted upon; subjection to an external agent or influence; a passive condition

senses.definition: The main character, or one of the main characters, in any story, such as a literary work or drama.
A leading person in a contest; a principal performer.
An advocate or champion of a cause or course of action.

Execution (in the judicial sense).

etymology.native: 源自中古英語（deth、deeth），來自古英語（dēaþ），再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*dauþuz），最終來自原始印歐語（*dʰówtus）。參見（die）。

A state of restlessness and agitation, often accompanied by a distressing sense of oppression or tightness in the stomach.
Any anxiety disorder, especially generalized anxiety disorder.

senses.definition: People who are old; old beings; the older generation, taken as a group.

Cognate with Dutch kreupel, Low German Kröpel, German Krüppel, Old Norse kryppill.
etymology.native: 「cripel」源自中古英語，來源為古英語「crypel」，再溯自原始日耳曼語「*krupilaz」，意為「行動困難者」，源自原始印歐語「*grewb-」，意為「彎曲、爬行」，而「*ger-」則意為「彎曲、扭曲」，與「creep」相關。與荷蘭語「kreupel」、下德語「Kröpel」、德語「Krüppel」、古諾斯語「kryppill」同源。
