senses.definition: A hanging down of the head; a drooping posture; a limp appearance.

An awkward, heavy, clownish fellow.

etymology.text: Unclear. Perhaps from Middle English slugge, from Old Norse slókr (“lazy fellow”). See also Swedish sloka (“to slouch, wilt”), related to Swedish slak (“slack, soft and flexible”) and Latin laxus (“loose, slack”).

senses.definition: To receive and transfer; to have pass through one's hands; hence, to buy and sell.

To use the hands.

senses.definition: Free from emotional or mental disturbance.
Calm; without motion or sound.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

etymology.text: From Middle English silence, from Old French silence, from Latin silentium (“silence”), from silēns (“quiet, silent”, present participle of silēre) + -ium. Displaced native Old English swīġe and sālnes.

senses.definition: The quality or state of being still.
Habitual silence or quiet; taciturnity.

etymology.text: From Middle English stilnesse, from Old English stilnes (“stillness, quiet; absence of noise or disturbance, release, relaxation; silence, abstention from speech; absence of disturbance or molestation, tranquility, peace, security; that which appeases”), equivalent to still + -ness.

The shrub or small tree that bears the fruit.

etymology.text: The noun is derived from Middle English pome-garnet, pome-garnete, pome garnate, pome granat, pome-granate (“pomegranate fruit; pomegranate tree; pomegranate seeds (?)”) [and other forms], from Anglo-Norman pome gernate, pomme gernette, Middle French pomme granade, pomme granate, pomme grenade, and Old French pome grenade, pome grenate, pomme grenate [and other forms] (modern French grenade), probably from Italian pomogranato, pomo granato (though apparently first attested later), and then eithe
etymology.native: 這個名詞源自中古英語 pome-garnet、pome-garnete、pome garnate、pome granat、pome-granate（意為「石榴果實；石榴樹；石榴籽 (?)」），以及盎格魯-諾曼語 pome gernate、pomme gernette、中古法語 pomme granade、pomme granate、pomme grenade，和古法語 pome grenade、pome grenate、pomme grenate（現代法語 grenade），可能來自義大利語 pomogranato、pomo granato（雖看似最早出現於後期），再由 eithe

etymology.text: From folk + lore, coined by British writer William Thoms in 1846 to replace terms such as "popular antiquities". Thoms imitated German terms such as Volklehre (“people's customs”) and Volksüberlieferung (“popular tradition”). Compare also Old English folclar (“popular instruction; homily”) and West Frisian folkloare (“folklore”).
etymology.native: 由英國作家威廉·湯姆斯於 1846 年造詞，用以取代「流行古物」等術語。他模仿了德國術語如 Volklehre（人民的習俗）和 Volksüberlieferung（流行的傳統）。

senses.definition: A humanoid figure made with large snowballs stacked on each other. Human traits like a face and arms may be fashioned with sticks (arms), a carrot (nose), and stones or coal (eyes, mouth).

A playing card with the rank of eight.
An attractive but heartless man.

senses.definition: A surrounding area or place (especially of an urban settlement); an environment.

etymology.text: From Middle English enviroun (“round about in a circle or ring; all around”) [and other forms], from Anglo-Norman enviroun, environ [and other forms], and Middle French enviroun, environ [and other forms], from Old French environ (“around, surrounding; about, approximately, roughly”) (modern French environ), from en- (prefix meaning ‘in; into’) + viron (“circuit; circumference, compass; country round about”) (though first attested later) (from virer (“to bear, turn, veer”) (either from Latin gȳr
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 enviroun（意為「環繞、圈繞」），來自盎格魯-諾曼語 enviroun、environ，以及中古法語 enviroun、environ，再源自古法語 environ（意為「周圍、環繞；大約、粗略」），由 en-（前綴，意為「在…內」）+ viron（意為「迴圈、周長、周圍地區」）構成，而 viron 本身源自拉丁語 virer（意為「轉向、偏轉」）

Nearly; approximately; with close correspondence in quality, manner, degree, quantity, or time; almost.
Here and there; around; in one place and another; up and down.

etymology.text: From Middle English alyve, alive, alife, olive, olife, on live, on life, from Old English on līfe (“alive”, literally “in life" or "in (the) body”), from on (“on, in”) + līfe, dative singular of līf (“life”). In this sense, replaced Old English cwic (whence English quick). Equivalent to a- + life. Compare Dutch in leven (“alive”, literally “in life”), German am Leben (“alive”, literally “at life" or "at living”).

senses.definition: Yielding, pliant; docile; ready or apt to learn; not froward.

etymology.text: From Middle English toward, from Old English tōweard, from Proto-West Germanic *tōward, equivalent to to + -ward. senses.definition: Gradual reduction over time.

examples.text: He needed to taper off venlafaxine.

etymology.text: From Middle English taper, from Old English tapor (“taper, candle, wick of a lamp”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Latin papyrus (“papyrus", used in Mediaeval times to mean "wick of a candle”); If so, it is a doublet of papyrus; but compare Old French taper (“taper, slender candle or light”). Alternatively, of Celtic origin related to Irish tapar (“taper”), Welsh tampr (“a taper, torch”); further compare Sanskrit तपती (tápati, “(it) warms, gives out heat, is hot; (it) heats”). More at tepid.

examples.text: I understand that this sounds far-fetched, but in order to understand Exodus you have to see the bigger picture.
examples.translation: 我理解這聽起來不太可能，但要了解《出埃及記》，必須看清大局。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin Exodus, borrowed from Ancient Greek Ἔξοδος (Éxodos), from ἔξοδος (éxodos, “departure”), from ἐξ- (ex-, “out”) + ὁδός (hodós, “path, road”).
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 Exodus，該詞又來自古希臘語 Ἔξοδος，由前綴 ἐξ-（「出」）加上ὁδός（「道路」）組成。

senses.definition: Green foliage or verdure.
Foliage used as decoration.
Marijuana.

examples.text: The spring greenery has appeared.
examples.translation: 春天的綠意已現

examples.text: You like greenery.
examples.translation: 你喜歡綠意

examples.text: He loves greenery.
examples.translation: 他愛綠意

examples.text: What is the size of this district's greenery area?
examples.translation: 這片小區的綠地面積有多少？

examples.text: There's a lot of greenery in Tokyo Midtown!
examples.translation: 東京中心區綠意盎然！

examples.text: There is less crime in apartment buildings surrounded by trees and greenery.
examples.translation: 環繞樹木與綠意的公寓大樓犯罪率較低

etymology.text: From green + -ery.
etymology.native: 由 green + -ery 組成。

senses.definition: A person who is severely impaired or deficient in some non-physical way.
A shortened wooden stud or brace used to construct the portion of a wall above a door or above and below a window.
A rocky shallow in a stream.
Scrapple.
A person who has severely impaired physical abilities because of deformation, injury, or amputation of parts of the body.

examples.text: He returned from war a cripple.
examples.translation: 他從戰爭中歸來，受傷

etymology.text: From Middle English cripel, crepel, crüpel, from Old English crypel (“crippled; a cripple”), from Proto-Germanic *krupilaz (“tending to crawl; a cripple”), from Proto-Indo-European *grewb- (“to bend, crouch, crawl”), from Proto-Indo-European *ger- (“to bend, twist”), equivalent to creep + -le. Cognate with Dutch kreupel, Low German Kröpel, German Krüppel, Old Norse kryppill.
etymology.native: 「cripel」源自中古英語，來源為古英語「crypel」，再溯自原始日耳曼語「*krupilaz」，意為「行動困難者」，源自原始印歐語「*grewb-」，意為「彎曲、爬行」，而「*ger-」則意為「彎曲、扭曲」，與「creep」相關。與荷蘭語「kreupel」、下德語「Kröpel」、德語「Krüppel」、古諾斯語「kryppill」同源。

senses.definition: To scatter in different directions.
To break up and disappear; to dissipate.
To disseminate.
To separate rays of light, etc., according to wavelength; to refract.
senses.native: 將光線等按波長分開；折射

senses.definition: To distribute throughout.

examples.text: How do trees disperse their seeds?
examples.translation: 樹木如何傳播種子？

examples.text: We dispersed from each other.
examples.translation: 我們彼此分散開來。

examples.text: Fungi disperse spores.
examples.translation: 真菌散佈孢子。

examples.text: The bank robbers dispersed in all directions.
examples.translation: 銀行強盜四處逃竄。

examples.text: The police used tear gas to disperse the crowd.
examples.translation: 警方使用催淚瓦斯驅散人群。

examples.text: The first men lived dispersed, and cities did not exist yet.
examples.translation: 最初的人們分散而居，城市尚未存在。

etymology.text: From Middle French disperser, from Latin dispersus, past participle of dispergō (“to scatter abroad, disperse”), from dis- (“apart”) + spargō (“to scatter”); see sparse.
etymology.native: 源自中法語的 disperser，來自拉丁語 dispergō（「四處散佈」），由 dis-（「分開」）與 spargō（「撒灑」）組成。

senses.definition: To destroy completely; to reduce to nothing radically; to put an end to.
To pull up by the roots.
eradicated

examples.text: Algeria has eradicated many diseases.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞已根除許多疾病。

examples.text: They tried to eradicate my culture.
examples.translation: 他們試圖根除我的文化。

examples.text: The savage in man is never quite eradicated.
examples.translation: 人性中的野性從未完全被根除。

examples.text: The US attempted to eradicate Native Americans.
examples.translation: 美國曾試圖根除美洲原住民。

examples.text: Algeria should eradicate illegal dumps.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞應根除非法垃圾場。

examples.text: It is urgent to eradicate poverty in Africa.
examples.translation: 必須緊急根除非洲的貧困。

etymology.text: From Middle English eradicaten (“to eradicate”), from eradicat(e) (“eradicated”, past participle of eradicaten) + -en (verb-forming suffix), borrowed from Latin ērādīcātus, the perfect passive participle of ērādīcō (“to uproot, root out; to anihilate, eradicate”), from ē- (“out”) + rādīx (“root”) + -ō (verb-forming suffix). See also radish.
etymology.native: 此詞源於中世紀英語，由拉丁語組成，意為拔除根部。

senses.definition: To deprive of inhabitants.
To devastate or lay waste somewhere.
To abandon or forsake something.
To make someone sad, forlorn and hopeless.
senses.native: 使某人悲傷、絕望且無希望

examples.text: Mary's explanations enchanted me and desolated me all at once.

relations.native: 摧毀大片區域內眾多或所有事物

etymology.text: From Middle English desolat(e). See Etymology 2 and -ate (adjective-forming suffix) for more.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 desolat(e)。請參閱詞源 2 和 -ate（形容詞構成後綴）以獲取更多資訊。

senses.definition: To get in the way of; to hinder.

examples.text: He was impeded in his work.
examples.translation: 他在工作中受到阻礙。

examples.text: A stalled car impedes traffic in the left lane.
examples.translation: 一輛故障的汽車阻擋了左側車道的交通。

examples.text: I hope it doesn't impede my online classes.
examples.translation: 我希望它不會干擾我的線上課程。

examples.text: Obstructions near doors can impede people in an emergency.
examples.translation: 門附近的障礙物可能會在緊急情況下阻礙人們通行。

examples.text: He has tried to impede an official investigation.
examples.translation: 他試圖阻擋官方調查。

examples.text: Storms at sea impeded our progress.
examples.translation: 海上的風暴阻礙了我們的進度。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin impediō (“to shackle”), from pēs (“foot”) (compare pedestrian). First attested use as a verb was in William Shakespeare's Macbeth, see quotations.
etymology.native: 此詞源自拉丁語 impediō，由 pēs（腳）組成。該動詞最早於莎士比亞的《麥克白》中出現。

senses.definition: To cause to fail; to frustrate, to prevent.
To place (something) across (another thing); to position crosswise.
To hinder or obstruct by placing (something) in the way of; to block, to impede, to oppose.
To move (something) across or counter to; to cross.

examples.text: He's always thwarting my nefarious plans.
Tom tried to thwart Mary's plans.
Tom thwarted everything he could.
You've thwarted my plans for the last time!
Once again, my plans have been thwarted.
A moat was dug around the castle to thwart attackers.

etymology.text: From Middle English thwerte, from the adjective thwert (“obstinate, perverse”), from Old Norse þvert, neuter of þverr (“transverse”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語，來自形容詞「頑固的、乖張的」，來自古諾斯語「橫向的」的中性形式。

senses.definition: To hold in or hold back; to keep in check; restrain.
To recuse.

examples.text: I should act, yet fear inhibits me from doing so.
Fear can inhibit success.
It won't do to be so inhibited when you go up on stage.
He noticed that this drug seemed to inhibit bacterial growth.
The passive-aggressive behavior of the English teacher inhibits effective communication.
Some claim that taxing the rich inhibits job creation.

etymology.text: From Latin inhibitus, perfect passive participle of inhibeō (“to hold in, check, restrain”), from in (“in, at, on”), + habeō (“to have, hold, keep”).
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語「抑制」的完成被動分詞，由「在內」加「持有、保持」組成。

senses.definition: A male child.
A male servant, slave, assistant, or employee, particularly
A male submissive.
A male non-human animal, especially, in affectionate address, a male pet, especially a dog.
A former low rank of various armed services; a holder of this rank.
A male (tree, gene, etc).
A young man.
A son of any age.
A male human younger than the speaker.
A male human of any age, as opposed to a "girl" (female human of any age).
A male of low station, (especially as pejorative) a worthless male, a wretch; a mean and dishonest male, a knave.
A younger such worker.
A male camp follower.
A male friend.
Heroin.
Any tangible object close to one's person; often used in emphatic forms such as bad boy.
A non-white male servant regardless of age, particularly as a form of address.
Any non-white male, regardless of age.

examples.text: That boy denies stealing the bicycle.
examples.translation: 那個男孩否認偷了腳踏車。

examples.text: That class has 15 boys and 28 girls.
examples.translation: 那個班有15名男孩和28名女孩子。

examples.text: The boy denied stealing the bicycle.
examples.translation: 那個男孩否認偷了腳踏車。

examples.text: The boy enjoyed painting a picture.
examples.translation: 這個男孩喜歡繪畫。

examples.text: They rescued the boy from drowning.
examples.translation: 他們救了這個男孩，使他免於淹死。

examples.text: That boy put on his sneakers and ran outside.
examples.translation: 那個男孩穿上了他的運動鞋，跑向外面。

etymology.text: From Middle English boy /boye (“servant, commoner, knave, boy”), from Old English *bōia (“boy”), from Proto-West Germanic *bōjō, from Proto-Germanic *bōjô (“younger brother, young male relation”), from Proto-Germanic *bō- (“brother, close male relation”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰā-, *bʰāt- (“father, elder brother, brother”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語「僕人、平民、小子、男孩」，來自古英語，上溯至原始日耳曼語「弟弟、年輕男性親屬」，再追溯至原始印歐語「父親、兄長」的字根。

senses.definition: To speak (words) with a spasmodic repetition of vocal sounds.
To expel a gas with difficulty.

examples.text: Why are you stuttering?
examples.translation: 你為什麼在結巴。

examples.text: Tom is stuttering.
examples.translation: Tom在結巴。

examples.text: I am stuttering.
examples.translation: 我在結巴。

examples.text: How is it you speak with such a stutter?
examples.translation: 你怎麼說這樣的口吃？

examples.text: When she began to stutter, her classmates couldn't help laughing.
examples.translation: 她一開始結巴，她的同學們就忍不住笑了。

examples.text: Talk slowly and you won't stutter that much.
examples.translation: 慢慢說，就不會那麼結巴了。

etymology.text: From Middle English stutten, stoten (“stutter”); cognate with Dutch stotteren (“stutter”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 stutten、stoten（意為「結巴」）；與荷蘭語 stotteren 同源。

senses.definition: A speech disorder characterized by stuttering.
One who stutters.

examples.text: I have a stutter.

etymology.text: From Middle English stutten, stoten (“stutter”); cognate with Dutch stotteren (“stutter”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 stutten、stoten（意為「結巴」）；與荷蘭語 stotteren 同源。

senses.definition: To waver or be unsteady; to weaken or trail off.
senses.native: 搖擺或站不穩；變弱或漸行漸遠

senses.definition: To stammer; to utter with hesitation, or in a weak and trembling manner.
senses.native: 口吃；以猶豫、微弱且顫抖的方式說話

senses.definition: To fail in distinctness or regularity of exercise; said of the mind or of thought.
senses.native: 失去清晰度或規律性；用於形容心智或思想

senses.definition: To stumble.
To lose faith or vigor; to doubt or abandon (a cause).
senses.native: 失去信心或活力；懷疑或放棄（某種信念）

senses.definition: To hesitate in purpose or action.
senses.native: 在目的或行動上猶豫不決

senses.definition: To cleanse or sift, as barley.

examples.text: The stars never falter.
examples.translation: 星星從未搖擺不定。

examples.text: You must not falter.
examples.translation: 你絕不能搖擺不定。

examples.text: He faltered at the last second, costing them the game.
examples.translation: 他在最後時刻猶豫了一下，導致他們輸掉了比賽。

examples.text: We can't allow ourselves to falter.
examples.translation: 我們不允許自己搖擺不定。

examples.text: Her voice always falters when she mentions her late father.
examples.translation: 她一提到已故的父親，聲音就會顫抖。

examples.text: We never saw him hesitate or falter.
examples.translation: 我們從沒見過他猶豫或搖擺不定。

etymology.text: From Middle English falteren (“to stagger; be unsteady, tremble, quiver; to stammer; be entangled, get caught”), further origin unknown. Probably from a North Germanic source such as Old Norse faltrask (“to hesitate, be puzzled, be encumbered”). May also be a frequentative of fold, although the change from d to t is unusual.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 falteren（「踉蹌；站不穩、顫抖、發抖；口吃；糾結」），起源不明。可能來自北日耳曼語源，如古諾斯語 faltrask（「猶豫、困惑、受困」）。也可能源自 fold 的頻繁化形式，但從 d 變為 t 的情況並不常見。

senses.definition: A short, high-pitched sound, as of two objects rubbing together, or the sounds made by mice and other small animals.
senses.native: 短促的高音，如兩物摩擦或鼠類等小動物發出的聲音

senses.definition: A card game similar to group solitaire.
senses.native: 類似群組獨贏的紙牌遊戲

senses.definition: A narrow squeak.

examples.text: Don't talk to your mom like that, pip squeak!
examples.translation: 別對你媽媽那樣說話，Pip Squeak！

examples.text: The door to the kitchen squeaks too loudly.
examples.translation: 廚房那扇門吱嘎聲太響了。

examples.text: The squeak of shoes on powdery snow.
examples.translation: 鞋子在粉雪上發出吱嘎聲。

examples.text: We heard a sharp squeak indicating that the glass window had broken suddenly.
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: A delicate squeak pierced the silence, signaling the subtle movement of unseen creatures.
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Only a seasoned craftsman could discern the precise squeak indicating imminent structural failure.
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

relations.native: 發出尖銳聲音或吱嘎聲的
發出尖銳聲音或吱嘎聲的
發出尖銳聲音或吱嘎聲的

morphemes.native: 短促的高音、如兩物摩擦或鼠類等小動物發出的聲音

etymology.text: An allusion to the newspaper cartoon strip Pip, Squeak and Wilfred.
etymology.native: 這是指向《Pip、Squeak 和 Wilfred》漫畫條的典故。

senses.definition: A spasm of the diaphragm, or the resulting sound.
A case of the hiccups; the condition of having the spasms of hiccupping; singultus; diaphragmatic myoclonus.
Any spasm or sudden change.
A minor obstacle or setback.

examples.text: I hiccup a lot.
examples.translation: 我經常打嗝。

examples.text: I have hiccups.
examples.translation: 我打嗝了。

examples.text: I often hiccup.
examples.translation: 我經常打嗝。

examples.text: Hiccups are caused by spasms of the diaphragm.
examples.translation: 打嗝是由橫膈膜痙攣引起的。

examples.text: And to make matters worse, I have the hiccups.
examples.translation: 更糟糕的是，我打嗝了。

examples.text: Drink some water to get rid of your hiccups.
examples.translation: 喝點水可以止住你的打嗝。

etymology.text: From earlier hickop, alteration of earlier hicket, hyckock, from hic (onomatopoeic) + -ock (diminutive suffix).
etymology.native: 源自較早的hickop，為hicket與hyckock的變體，來自hic（擬聲詞）+ -ock（縮小詞尾）

senses.definition: To pelt with rocks; to stone.
To move gently back and forth.
To sway one's body as a stim.
senses.native: （自我刺激行為）身體前後搖晃

senses.definition: To cause to shake or sway violently.
senses.native: 使（某物）劇烈搖晃或擺動

senses.definition: To sway or tilt violently back and forth.
senses.native: 劇烈地前後擺動或傾斜

senses.definition: To be washed and panned in a cradle or in a rocker.
senses.native: 在搖籃或搖床中淘洗（礦砂）

senses.definition: To disturb the emotional equilibrium of; to distress; to greatly impact (most often positively).
senses.native: 擾亂（某人）的情緒平衡；使震撼（多為正面影響）

senses.definition: To do well or to be operating at high efficiency.
senses.native: 表現出色或高效率運作

To make love to or have sex (with).
To play, perform, or enjoy rock music, especially with a lot of skill or energy.
senses.native: 演奏或享受搖滾樂（尤指高超或熱情）

senses.definition: To thrill or excite, especially with rock music.
senses.native: 使（人）興奮、激動（尤指以搖滾樂）

To wear (a piece of clothing, outfit etc.) successfully or with style; to carry off (a particular look, style).

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: If the van is rocking, it needs new shocks.

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English rocke, rokke (“rock formation”), from Old English *rocc (“rock”), as in Old English stānrocc (“high stone rock, peak, obelisk”), and also later from Anglo-Norman roque, (compare Modern French roc, roche, rocher), from Medieval Latin rocca (attested 767), of uncertain origin, sometimes said to be of Celtic (in particular, perhaps Gaulish) origin (compare Breton roc'h). Related also to Middle Low German rocke (“rock ledge”). One suggestion is that it derives from Vulg
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 rocke, rokke（岩層），來自古英語 *rocc（岩石），如古英語 stānrocc（高聳石岩、峰頂、方尖碑），亦源自盎格魯-諾曼語 roque（比較現代法語 roc, roche, rocher），來自中世紀拉丁語 rocca（767年有記載），起源不明，有說源自凱爾特語（特別是高盧語）（比較布列塔尼語 roc'h）。亦與中古低德語 rocke（岩縫）相關。有一說認為源自 Vulg

senses.definition: A slope or inclination.
A jousting contest. (countable)
An attempt, run, or bid for something; commonly with a sense of bold defiance or against steep odds.
A thrust, as with a lance.
A tilt hammer.
A penalty triggered when a player physically shakes, lifts, or bangs a pinball machine too violently in an attempt to influence the path of the ball.
The inclination of part of the body, such as backbone, pelvis, head, etc.
senses.native: 身體部位的傾斜角度，如脊椎、骨盆等

senses.definition: The controlled vertical movement of a camera, or a device to achieve this.
senses.native: 相機的垂直控制移動或實現此功能的裝置

senses.definition: A state of frustration and worsened performance resulting from a series of losses.
A canvas covering for carts, boats, etc.
Any covering overhead; especially, a tent.

examples.text: The tilt of the earth's axis is the reason for the season.
examples.translation: 地球軸線的傾斜是季節形成的原因。

examples.text: The tower had a pronounced tilt.
I tilt my head. Not the pawn, but the knight?
examples.translation: 我歪頭。不是兵，而是騎士？

etymology.text: From Middle English tilte, from Old English *tyltan, *tieltan (“to be unsteady”), related to the adjective tealt (“unsteady”), from Proto-West Germanic *talt, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *del-, *dul- (“to shake, hesitate”), see also Dutch touteren (“to tremble”), North Frisian talt, tolt (“unstable, shaky”). Cognate with Icelandic tölt (“an ambling pace”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 tilte，來自古英語 *tyltan 或 *tieltan（「不穩固」），與形容詞 tealt 相關。

senses.definition: Any naturally occurring solid material that has a (more or less) definite chemical composition and characteristic physical properties; especially, an inorganic and crystalline one.
Any inorganic material (as distinguished from animal or vegetable).
Any inorganic element that is essential to nutrition.
Mineral water.
A soft drink, particularly a single serve bottle or can.
A mine or mineral deposit.
A poisonous or dangerous substance.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: China will buy minerals from Algeria.
examples.translation: 中國將從阿爾及利亞購買礦物。

examples.text: They're not rocks. They're minerals.
examples.translation: 它們不是岩石，而是礦物。

examples.text: Fruits are rich in vitamins and minerals.
examples.translation: 水果富含維生素和礦物質。

examples.text: A mine is where you find precious minerals.
examples.translation: 礦裡能找到寶貴的礦物質。

examples.text: This food contains all the minerals without which our bodies would not function.
examples.translation: 這食物中含有所有的礦物質, 若沒有這些礦物質我們的身體將無法正常運作。

examples.text: Algeria is a country abundant with minerals.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞是一個礦產豐富的國家。

etymology.text: From Middle English mineral, borrowed from Old French mineral, (French minéral), from Medieval Latin minerale, from minera (“ore”), probably ultimately derived from Latin mina (“ore, mine”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 mineral，借自古法語 mineral（法語 minéral），再來自中世紀拉丁語 minerale，源自 minera（礦石），可能最終源自拉丁語 mina（礦石、礦山）。

senses.definition: To support oneself on the feet in an erect position.
To rise to one’s feet; to stand up.
To act as an umpire.
To undergo; withstand; hold up.
To be a candidate (in an election).
To remain valid.
To oppose, usually as a team, in competition.
To cover the expense of; to pay for.
To have or maintain a position, order, or rank; to be in a particular relation.

examples.translation: 在多重引導電腦上安裝多少作業系統，就需要多少授權嗎？

examples.text: Tom's driver's license will expire next month.
examples.translation: 湯姆的駕駛執照下個月到期。

examples.text: I am licensed to practice law in this state.
examples.translation: 我有資格在本州從事法律實務。

etymology.text: From Middle English licence, licens, lisence, lissens, licance, from Old French licence, from Latin licentia (“license”), from licens, present participle of licere (“to be allowed, be allowable”); compare linquere, Ancient Greek λείπω (leípō, “leave”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 licence、lens、lisence、lissens、licance，來自法文 licence，再來自拉丁文 licentia（許可），源自 licens（licere「被允許」的現在分詞）；可與拉丁文 linquere、古希臘文 λείπω（leípō，「離開」）相比。

senses.definition: An artifact or document rendering something allowed or legal.
A learner's permit.
A pompano of the species Trachinotus falcatus.
Formal permission.

examples.text: The question permits of only one interpretation.
The two birds built a nest without a building permit.
examples.translation: 這兩隻鳥在沒有建築許可的情況下築了巢。

examples.text: Tom got his learner's permit yesterday, so he's out with his father practicing driving.
A construction permit can be obtained from the town offices.

etymology.text: From Middle English permitten, borrowed from Middle French permettre, from Latin permittō (“give up, allow”), from per (“through”) + mittō (“send”).

senses.definition: To grant or establish a charter.
To lease or hire something by charter.
senses.native: 依契約租賃或租用某物

senses.definition: (of a peace officer) To inform (an arrestee) of their constitutional rights under the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms upon arrest.
senses.native: （對執法人員而言）在逮捕時告知被逮捕者其憲法權利

examples.text: Charter schools are a grift.
examples.translation: 契約學校是一場騙局。

examples.text: I want to charter a bus.
examples.translation: 我想包車。

examples.text: The charter flight is to take off at three.
examples.translation: 包機將於三點起飛。

examples.text: They chartered planes to airlift their employees.
examples.translation: 他們包租飛機將員工空運回去。

examples.text: We've got a charter flight waiting to take us to Boston.
examples.translation: 我們有一班包機等待帶我們前往波士頓。

examples.text: The party charter passes with twenty-one votes against and four abstentions.
examples.translation: 黨章以二十一票反對、四票棄權通過。

etymology.text: From Middle English charter, chartre, borrowed from Old French chartre, from Latin chartula (diminutive of charta). See chart. Doublet of chartula.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 charter，chartre，借自舊法語 chartre，來自拉丁語 chartula（charta 的縮小詞）。與 chartula 為雙胞胎詞。

senses.definition: To let one have as a suitable share of something.
To forgo bothering with, to let slide.
To present something as possible or reasonable.
senses.native: 提出某事是可能或合理的

senses.definition: To permit, to give permission to.
To not bar or obstruct.
To acknowledge, accept the truth of; to concede; to accede to an opinion; to say something one agrees on in the context of a larger disagreement or reluctance.
senses.native: 承認；同意（某說法），尤指在整體有異議時讓步

senses.definition: To grant (something) as a deduction or an addition; especially to abate or deduct.
senses.native: （作為扣除或增加而）給予；扣除

senses.definition: To make an allowance, to take into account when making plans.
To render physically possible.
To decide (a request) in favour of the party who raised it; to grant victory to a party regarding (a request).
senses.native: （對請求）作出有利於提出方的裁定；准予

senses.definition: To praise; to approve of; hence, to sanction.
To sanction; to invest; to entrust.
To like; to be suited or pleased with.

examples.text: Smoking isn't allowed in this room.
examples.translation: 這房間是禁止吸煙的。

examples.text: You aren't allowed in this room.
examples.translation: 你不能進這個房間。

examples.text: She allowed him to go alone.
examples.translation: 她允許他一個人去。

examples.text: Tom said that Mary isn't allowed to do that.
examples.translation: 湯姆說瑪麗不可以做那種事。

examples.text: I hope that your parents will allow us to marry.
examples.translation: 希望你父母會讓我們結婚吧。

examples.text: No one is allowed to translate this sentence.
examples.translation: 無人准翻譯此句。

etymology.text: From Middle English allowen, alowen, a borrowing from Anglo-Norman allouer, alouer, from Medieval Latin allaudāre, merged with alouer, from Medieval Latin allocō (“to assign”). Doublet of allaud (via allaudāre) or allocate (via allocāre).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（allowen、alowen），借自英法語（allouer、alouer），來自中世紀拉丁語（allaudāre），並與來自中世紀拉丁語（allocō）「分配」的（alouer）合流。與（allaud）、（allocate）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: A completed curriculum of study in tertiary education.
A unit of measurement of angle equal to ¹⁄₃₆₀ of a circle's circumference.
A unit of measurement of temperature on any of several scales, such as Celsius or Fahrenheit.
The sum of the exponents of a term; the order of a polynomial.
The number of edges that a vertex takes part in; a valency.
A stage of rank or privilege; social standing.
A ‘step’ in genealogical descent.
The amount that an entity possesses a certain property; relative intensity, extent.
The dimensionality of a field extension.
The number of logical connectives in a formula.
senses.native: （邏輯）公式中邏輯連接詞的個數

senses.definition: The curvature of a circular arc, expressed as the angle subtended by a fixed length of arc or chord.
A unit of measurement of latitude and longitude which together identify a location on the Earth's surface.
Any of the stages (like positive, comparative, superlative, elative) in the comparison of an adjective or an adverb.
A step on a set of stairs; the rung of a ladder.
An individual step, or stage, in any process or scale of values.
One's relative state or experience; way, manner.

examples.text: Water freezes at 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
examples.translation: 水在華氏32度結成冰。

examples.text: Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius.
examples.translation: 水在攝氏零度時結冰。

examples.text: It's very hot here, it's 26 degrees.
examples.translation: 這裡很熱，溫度是 26 度。

examples.text: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
examples.translation: 水在攝氏100度沸騰。

examples.text: It was 36 degrees in Boston today.
examples.translation: 今天波士頓到了36度。

examples.text: To what degree are you interested in baseball?
examples.translation: 你喜歡棒球到什麼程度？

etymology.text: From Middle English degre, borrowed from Old French degré (French: degré), itself from Latin gradus, with the prefix de-.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（degre），借自古法語（degré），再源自拉丁語（gradus），加上字首（de-）。

senses.definition: The quality of being brothers or brotherly; brotherhood.
A group of people associated for a common purpose.
A social organization of male students at a college or university; usually identified by Greek letters.

examples.text: Why should I join a fraternity?
examples.translation: 為何要加入兄弟會？

examples.text: Tom is in a college fraternity.
examples.translation: 湯姆是大學兄弟會的一員。

examples.text: Welcome to the fraternity.
examples.translation: 歡迎加入兄弟會。

examples.text: As time passed, the fraternity grew bigger.
examples.translation: 隨著時間流逝，兄弟會越辦越大。

examples.text: Fraternity is like the truth. Where is it?
examples.translation: 兄弟會就像真理，它在哪裡？

examples.text: "Liberty, equality, fraternity" is a French motto.
examples.translation: 「自由、平等、博愛」是法國的格言。

etymology.text: From Middle English fraternite, borrowed from Old French fraternité, from Latin frāternitās, ultimately from frāter (“brother”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 fraternite，借自古法文 fraternité，來自拉丁文 frāternitās，最終源自拉丁文 frāter（「兄弟」）。

senses.definition: A group sharing common characteristics, such as the same language, law, religion, or tradition.
A residential or religious collective; a commune.
The condition of having certain attitudes and interests in common.
A group of interdependent organisms inhabiting the same region and interacting with each other.
A group of people interacting by electronic means for educational, professional, social, or other purposes; a virtual community.
A feeling of togetherness or connectedness, common identity or of possessing a similar outlook, perspective and purpose with some group of people.

A local area within a county or county borough which is the lowest tier of local government, usually represented by a community council or town council, which is generally equivalent to a civil parish in England.
senses.native: （威爾斯的）社區：最基層的地方行政區

senses.definition: Common enjoyment or possession; participation.
Common character; likeness.
Commonness; frequency.

examples.text: Asian communities are very differentiated.
examples.translation: 亞洲社群極具差異性。

examples.text: Everybody in the community loved Fadil.
examples.translation: 社區裡的每個人都很喜愛法迪爾。

examples.text: He lives in a segregated community.
examples.translation: 他居住在分隔的社區。

examples.text: Do you take part in any community activities?
examples.translation: 你參加社團活動嗎？

examples.text: The community is made up of individuals.
examples.translation: 社會是由個人組成的。

examples.text: Tom is part of the LGBTQ+ community.
examples.translation: 湯姆是LGBTQ+群體中的一員。

etymology.text: From Late Middle English communite, borrowed from Old French communité, comunité, comunete (modern French communauté), from Classical Latin commūnitās (“community; public spirit”), from commūn(is) (“common, ordinary; of or for the community, public”) + -itās. By surface analysis, commun(e) + -ity. Displaced native Old English ġemǣnsċipe. Doublet of communitas.
etymology.native: 源自晚期中古英語（communite），借自古法語（communité、comunité，現代法語 communauté），來自古典拉丁語（commūnitās）「共同體、公共精神」，由（commūnis）「共同的」加（-itās）組成。表面分析為（commune）加（-ity）。取代了古英語原有的（ġemǣnsċipe）。與（communitas）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: The act of associating.
The state of being associated; a connection to or an affiliation with something.
Any relationship between two measured quantities that renders them statistically dependent (but not necessarily causal or a correlation).
A group of persons associated for a common purpose; an organization; society.
Relationship between classes of objects that allows one object instance to cause another to perform an action on its behalf.
A benevolent overseas Chinese organization of popular origin for overseas Chinese individuals with the same surname, geographical origin, location, trade or business.

examples.text: The association counts thirty members.
examples.translation: 這個協會有三十個會員。

examples.text: Our Berber-language association has 140 members.
There are 30 members in the association.
No one may be compelled to belong to an association.
examples.translation: 不可以強迫任何人加入某個協會。

examples.text: Are there a lot of associations in your city?
I benefited much from my association with him.

relations.native: 創傷性聯合反應防止法

etymology.text: From Latin associātiō, from associō (perhaps via French association). Morphologically associate + -ion.

senses.definition: An entity having legal personality, and thus able to own property and to sue and be sued in its own name; a corporation.
A team; a group of people who work together for a common purpose.
A unit of approximately sixty to one hundred and twenty soldiers, typically consisting of two or three platoons and forming part of a battalion.
Companionship.
One or more social visitor(s) or companion(s).
One or more other person(s) who are nearby, are approaching, or are (e.g. covertly) watching, especially if they may have hostile intentions (like adversaries or rivals).
an institution created to conduct business
small military unit; usually two or three platoons
the state of being with someone
organization of performers and associated personnel (especially theatrical)
a social or business visitor
a social gathering of guests or companions
Any business, whether incorporated or not, that manufactures or sells products (also known as goods), or provides services as a commercial venture.
A group of performing artists who put on shows together.
The crew of a ship.
A unit of firefighters and their equipment.
An intelligence service.
A specific aircraft or its airline, usually used in air traffic communications to refer conveniently to another aircraft operated by the same airline.
A small group of birds or animals.
The members of a partnership business who are not listed in the company's name; unnamed individuals in an entourage or other group.
senses.native: （合夥事業中）未列名的合夥人；同行的人

examples.text: The company cancelled the meeting.
examples.translation: 公司取消了會議。

examples.text: Tom works for an American company.
examples.translation: 湯姆給一家美國公司幹活。

examples.text: The company suffered big losses.
examples.translation: 公司遭受了巨大的損失。

examples.text: The company manager decided on the work plan.
examples.translation: 公司的經理確定了工作計劃。

examples.text: That company is managed by my older brother.
examples.translation: 那家公司由我的哥哥經營。

examples.text: He holds an important position in the company.
examples.translation: 他在公司裡身兼要職。

etymology.text: From Middle English companye (“a team; companionship”), from Old French compaignie (“companionship”) (Modern French: compagnie), possibly from Late Latin *compania, but this word is not attested. Old French compaignie is equivalent to Old French compaignon (Modern French: compagnon) + -ie. More at companion.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（companye）「團隊、陪伴」，來自古法語（compaignie）「陪伴」，可能來自未見記載的後期拉丁語（*compania）。古法語詞相當於「同伴」（compaignon）加字尾（-ie）。另見（companion）。

senses.definition: Someone who wipes.
Something, such as a towel, that is used for wiping.
Something, such as a windscreen wiper, that is designed for wiping.
A movable electric contact in some devices.
A program or process that erases data.
A junior role in the engine room of a ship, someone who wipes down machinery and generally keeps it clean.
A hybrid fish variety artificially bred from eggs of striped bass (Morone saxatilis) fertilized with white bass (Morone chrysops) sperm, or the opposite combination.
An impertinent young man.

examples.text: The wipers don't work.
examples.translation: 雨刷不工作了。

examples.text: How often do wiper blades need to be replaced?
examples.translation: 雨刷片多久需要更換一次？

examples.text: These scratches are caused by the wipers.
examples.translation: 這些刮痕是由雨刷造成的。

examples.text: Shouldn't you turn your windscreen wipers off?
examples.translation: 你不該關掉雨刷嗎？

examples.text: Windscreen wipers are useless against ice.
examples.translation: 雨刷對冰完全無用。

examples.text: Gabriel saw the bus’s windshield wipers move.
examples.translation: 加百利看到公車的雨刷在移動。

etymology.text: From wipe + -er.
etymology.native: 由 wipe + -er 組成。

senses.definition: The act of touching physically; being in close association.
The establishment of communication (with).
Someone who can be contacted, or with whom one is in communication.
A device designed for repetitive connections.
The situation of being within sight of something; visual contact.
A nodule designed to connect a device with something else.
A means of communication with a person, especially in the form of a telephone number.
A contact lens.
Contact juggling.
The plane between two adjacent bodies of dissimilar rock.

examples.text: Tom made contact with Mary's ghost.
examples.translation: 湯姆與瑪麗的鬼魂取得了聯繫。

examples.text: Did you find your contact lenses?
examples.translation: 你找到你的隱形眼鏡了嗎？

examples.text: This is my contact information.
examples.translation: 這些是我的聯絡方式。

examples.text: These are my contact details.
examples.translation: 這些是我的聯絡方式。

examples.text: I've tried to contact Tom.
examples.translation: 我試過去聯絡湯姆。

examples.text: When you arrive in Osaka, please contact me.
examples.translation: 你來到大阪的時候請跟我聯絡。

relations.native: 本地人與外來文化接觸之前時期的
敞開的、無遮蔽的（因此易受傷害或易受影響）

etymology.text: From Latin contactus, from contingō (“to touch on all sides”), from tangō (“to touch”). Used in English since the 17th century.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語（contactus），來自（contingō）「四面接觸」，源自（tangō）「觸碰」。自十七世紀起用於英語。

senses.definition: Something recurring across a genre or type of art or literature; a motif.
A figure of speech in which words or phrases are used with a nonliteral or figurative meaning, such as a metaphor.
An addition (of dialogue, song, music, etc.) to a standard element of the liturgy, serving as an embellishment.
A tangent space meeting a quartic surface in a conic.
A short cadence at the end of the melody in some early music.
A pair of complementary hexachords in twelve-tone technique.
senses.native: 十二音技法之補充六音組

senses.definition: A cantillation pattern, or one of the marks that represents it.
Any of the ten arguments used in skepticism to refute dogmatism.
A particular instance of a property (such as the specific redness of a rose), as contrasted with a universal.
The reciprocal of a node on a surface.

examples.text: Airships are a common trope in steampunk works.
examples.translation: 飛艇是蒸汽朋克作品中常見的設定。

examples.text: Chinese characters are made up of common tropes.
examples.translation: 中文字符由常見設定構成。

examples.text: Many of the tropes of modern antisemitism were invented by czarist authorities in Imperial Russia.
examples.translation: 現代反猶太主義的許多設定，是由沙皇時代的帝俄政府所創造。

examples.text: I spent hours reading about media tropes.
examples.translation: 我花了數小時閱讀關於媒體設定的資料。

examples.text: This story has a classic love triangle trope.
examples.translation: 這個故事有經典的三角戀設定。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The film repeats the same villain trope.
examples.translation: 這部電影重複相同的反派設定。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Latin tropus, from Ancient Greek τρόπος (trópos, “a manner, style, turn, way; a trope or figure of speech; a mode in music; a mode or mood in logic”), related to τροπή (tropḗ, “solstice; trope; turn”) and τρέπειν (trépein, “to turn”); compare turn of phrase. The verb is derived from the noun.
etymology.native: 「tropus」源自拉丁語，源自古希臘語 τρόπος（trópos，意為「方式、風格、轉折、方法」；亦指修辭格或音樂模式；邏輯中的模式」），與 τροπή（tropḗ，意為「夏至、修辭轉折、轉折」）及 τρέπειν（trépein，意為「轉動」）相關；可與「phrase 的轉折」對照。此動詞源自名詞。

senses.definition: Something that is representative of all such things in a group.
Something that serves to illustrate or explain a rule.
Something that serves as a pattern of behaviour to be imitated (a good example) or not to be imitated (a bad example).
A person punished as a warning to others.
senses.native: 殺雞儆猴的對象；被懲罰以儆效尤的人

senses.definition: A parallel or closely similar case, especially when serving as a precedent or model.
An instance (as a problem to be solved) serving to illustrate the rule or precept or to act as an exercise in the application of the rule.

examples.text: You should learn from his example.
examples.translation: 你該拿他當榜樣。

examples.text: Let's look at some examples first.
examples.translation: 先看一些範例。

examples.text: Can you think of any examples?
examples.translation: 你想得到例子嗎？

examples.text: Please give us some examples.
examples.translation: 可以舉幾個例子嗎？

examples.text: Give me a different example.
examples.translation: 給我另一個例子。

examples.text: Could you make an example to reify your idea?
examples.translation: 你能舉例說明你的想法嗎?

relations.native: 實例教訓；活生生的教訓

etymology.text: From Middle English example, exaumple, from Old French example, essaumple, from Latin exemplum (“sample, pattern, specimen, copy for imitation, etc.”, literally “what is taken out”); see exempt. Doublet of exemplum and sample. Displaced native Middle English forebisne, from Old English forebȳsn; and Middle English bisne, from Old English bȳsn (modern English bizen).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（example、exaumple），來自古法語（example、essaumple），再源自拉丁語（exemplum）「樣本、模範」，字面意為「被取出的東西」；參見（exempt）。與（exemplum）、（sample）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: An occasion; an order of occurrence.
A case offered as an exemplification or a precedent; an illustrative example.
One of a series of recurring occasions, cases, essentially the same.
A specific occurrence of something that is created or instantiated, such as a database, or an object of a class in object-oriented programming.
A dungeon or other area that is duplicated for each player, or each party of players, that enters it, so that each player or party has a private copy of the area, isolated from other players.
An individual copy of such a dungeon or other area.
An independent server on a decentralised social network, such as Mastodon.
Urgency of manner or words; an urgent request; insistence.
A token; a sign; a symptom or indication.
That which is urgent; motive.
A piece of evidence; a proof or sign (of something).

examples.text: Take, for instance, your family problems.
Which instance is it?
This is an instance of modern British life.
Let's learn something, like a language for instance!
I can give you several instances.
For instance, "delight" is the opposite of "sorrow."

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French instance, from Latin īnstantia (“a being near, presence, also perseverance, earnestness, importunity, urgency”), from īnstāns (“urgent”); see instant.

senses.definition: Of or pertaining to the tropics, the equatorial region between 23 degrees north and 23 degrees south.
From, or similar to, a hot, humid climate.
Pertaining to tropical geometry.
Pertaining to, involving, or of the nature of a trope or tropes; figurative, metaphorical.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: The tropical sun glared down relentlessly.
examples.translation: 熱帶太陽毫不留情地怒目而視。

examples.text: Visualize yourself on a tropical beach.
examples.translation: 想像你自己在一片熱帶海灘上。

examples.text: Heathers can grow in tropical climates.
examples.translation: 石楠可以在熱帶氣候中生長。

examples.text: This is a tropical storm. It'll be over soon.
examples.translation: 這是熱帶風暴，很快就會過去。

examples.text: Tropical rainforests are a cause for concern.
examples.translation: 熱帶雨林的狀況令人擔憂。

examples.text: The area is covered with tropical rainforest.
examples.translation: 這個地區被熱帶雨林覆蓋。

etymology.text: From tropic + -al.
etymology.native: 由「熱帶」加形容詞字尾組成。

senses.definition: To start (a fire).
To set fire to; to set burning.
To illuminate; to provide light for when it is dark.
senses.native: 照亮；在黑暗中提供光源

senses.definition: To become ignited; to take fire.
To attend or conduct with a light; to show the way to by means of a light.
To make (a bonus) available to be collected by hitting a target, and thus light up the feature light corresponding to that bonus to indicate its availability.
senses.native: 透過擊中目標使獎勵可被收集，並點亮對應的獎勵燈（點亮）

senses.definition: To unload a ship, or to jettison material to make it lighter.
senses.native: 卸除（船的）貨物，或拋棄物料以減輕重量

senses.definition: To lighten; to ease of a burden; to take off.
To leave; to depart.

etymology.text: From Middle English park, from Old French parc (“livestock pen”), from Medieval Latin parcus, parricus, from Frankish *parrik (“enclosure, pen, fence”). Cognate with Dutch perk (“enclosure; flowerbed”), Old High German pfarrih, pferrih (“enclosure, pen”), Old English pearroc (“enclosure”) (whence modern English paddock), Old Norse parrak, parak (“enclosure, pen; distress, anxiety”), Icelandic parraka (“to keep pent in under restraint and coercion”). etymology.text: Borrowed from Italian miniatura (“manuscript illumination”), from miniare (“to illuminate”), from Latin miniō (“to colour red”), from minium (“red lead, minium”). Not related to minimum, minor or min (which are all from a different root, *mi-n-), though the sense development may have been influenced by association with them or sound symbolism.
etymology.native: 「miniatura」源自義大利語，意為「手抄本裝飾」，由「miniare」（意為「照亮」）衍生，而「miniare」又來自拉丁語「miniō」（意為「染紅」），再往上溯源於拉丁語「minium」（紅鉛礦）。此詞與「minimum」、「minor」或「min」無關，雖語義演變可能受其聯想或音韻符號影響。

etymology.text: Etymology unclear. Attested in the sense “to stroll” from the 1660s; noun sense “a stroll” attested 1828. Likely from earlier term meaning “to muse”, late 15th century, from late Middle English santren, of unknown origin. Competing theories exist:
etymology.native: 詞源不明。1660年代開始用於「散步」之意；「散步」的名詞用法則見於1828年。可能源自15世紀晚期的詞，意為「沉思」，來自中古英語santren，其來源未知。另有其他說法。

senses.definition: A wandering on foot; an idle and leisurely walk; a ramble; a saunter.

examples.text: South Africa's foremost wine connoisseur strolls through the cool, musty interior of the wine cellar he manages in Johannesburg.

etymology.text: Borrowed from German strollen, seemingly from Alemannic German strollen; related to Strolch (“vagabond; rascal”) and strolchen.

etymology.text: From Middle English trotten, from Old French trotter, troter (“to go, trot”), from Medieval Latin *trottō, *trotō (“to go”), from Frankish *trottōn (“to go, run”), from Proto-Germanic *trudōną, *trudaną, *tradjaną (“to go, step, tread”), from Proto-Indo-European *dreh₂- (“to run, escape”). Cognate with Old High German trottōn (“to run”), Modern German trotten (“to trot, plod”), Gothic 𐍄𐍂𐌿𐌳𐌰𐌽 (trudan, “to tread”), Old Norse troða (“to walk, tread”), Old English tredan (“to step, tread”). Doublet
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 trotten，來自舊法語 trotter, troter（「行走、奔跑」），來自中世紀拉丁語 *trottō, *trotō（「行走」），來自弗蘭克語 *trottōn（「行走、奔跑」），來自原始日耳曼語 *trudōną, *trudaną, *tradjaną（「行走、步伐、踩踏」），來自原始印歐語 *dreh₂-（「奔跑、逃離」）。與舊高地德語 trottōn（「奔跑」）、現代德語 trotten（「小跑、蹣跚」）同源，古哥特語 𐍄𐍂𐌿𐌳𐌰𐌽 (trudan, 「踩踏」），舊諾斯語 troða（「行走、踩踏」），舊英語 tredan（「步伐、踩踏」）。雙胞胎詞根。

senses.definition: A mammal of the order Primates, comprising of apes (including humans), monkeys, lemurs, tarsiers, lorisids, and galagos.

In the Orthodox Church, the presiding bishop of an ecclesiastical jurisdiction or region. Usually, the expression primate refers to the first hierarch of an autocephalous or autonomous Orthodox church. Less often, it is used to refer to the ruling bishop of an archdiocese or diocese.
In the Anglican Church, an archbishop, or the highest-ranking bishop of an ecclesiastic province.

etymology.native: 最早見於1876年，源自法文primate，由拉丁文prīmās、prīmātis（意為「首領、最優秀者」）派生而成，與第二條詞源相同。此名稱源自人們認為靈長類動物是哺乳動物中最高級的類群。

senses.definition: To cover (a window) with a curtain; to hang curtains.
To hide, cover or separate as if by a curtain.

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English curtine, from Old French cortine, from Late Latin cōrtīna (“curtain”), a calque from Ancient Greek.

senses.definition: A curtain; a drapery.

senses.definition: A dress made from an entire piece of cloth, without having pieces cut away as in a fitted garment.
senses.native: 披掛式服裝，由整塊布料製成、不經裁剪的服裝

examples.text: She adjusted the drape of her skirt.

etymology.text: From Middle English drape (“a drape”, noun), from Old French draper (“to drape; to full cloth”), from drap (“cloth, drabcloth”), from Late Latin drappus, drapus (“drabcloth, kerchief”), a word first recorded in the Capitularies of Charlemagne, probably from Frankish *drapi, *drāpi (“that which is fulled, drabcloth”, literally “that which is struck or for striking”), from Proto-Germanic *drapiz (“a strike, hit, blow”) and Proto-Germanic *drēpiz (“intended for striking, to be beaten”), both from *

senses.definition: The act of inhibiting.
A personal feeling of fear or embarrassment that stops one behaving naturally.
The process of stopping or retarding a reaction.
A writ from a higher court to an inferior judge to stay proceedings.
A recusal.

examples.text: She dropped all inhibitions.
examples.translation: 她放下了所有戒心。

examples.text: The music will help you lose your inhibitions.
examples.translation: 音樂能幫你放下戒心。

examples.text: Tom is truly free from inhibition.
examples.translation: 湯姆真的完全無戒心。

examples.text: Tom lies without any inhibition.
examples.translation: 湯姆毫不顧忌地撒謊。

examples.text: She's prepared to argue without inhibition.
examples.translation: 她準備好無戒心地爭辯。

examples.text: Alcohol lowers inhibitions.
examples.translation: 酒精會降低戒心。

etymology.text: From Middle English inhibicioun, inhibicione from Old French inibicion, from Latin inhibitio.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 inhibicioun、inhibicione，來自古法文 inibicion，源自拉丁文 inhibitio。

senses.definition: In low spirits from loss of hope or courage.

examples.text: Tom was despondent.
examples.translation: 湯姆感到絕望。

examples.text: Tom is despondent.
examples.translation: 湯姆感到絕望。

examples.text: Those close to her say she was despondent.
examples.translation: 與她親近的人說，她當時感到絕望。

examples.text: He was despondent over the turn of events.
examples.translation: 他對事件的轉折感到絕望。

examples.text: Millions of Russians feel cheated and despondent.
examples.translation: 數百萬俄羅斯人感到被欺騙且絕望。

examples.text: They seemed really despondent to find that their project didn't boost profits like they thought it would.
examples.translation: 他們發現自己的計畫並未如預期般提升利潤，顯得真的絕望。

etymology.text: From Latin dēspondēns, from the verb despondere (“to give up, to abandon”).
etymology.native: 來自拉丁語 dēspondēns，源自動詞 despondere（意為「放棄、拋棄」）。

senses.definition: Of or pertaining to religious ceremonies and rites; (generally) religious in nature; sacred.
Characterized by or performed with appropriate or great ceremony or formality.
Deeply serious and sombre; grave.
Inspiring serious feelings or thoughts; sombrely impressive.
Cheerless, gloomy, sombre.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: It was pretty solemn.
examples.translation: 這事相當肅穆。

examples.text: Roy looked solemn as I told him the story.
examples.translation: 羅伊聽我講完故事後顯得十分肅穆。

examples.text: A solemn wisp of smoke rose from the shattered city.
examples.translation: 一縷莊嚴的煙霧從破碎的城市升起。

examples.text: It's the wedding tomorrow. Everything must look very solemn.
examples.translation: 明天就是婚禮，一切必須看起來非常莊嚴。

examples.text: The king addressed the court with solemn authority.
examples.translation: 國王以莊嚴的權威向法庭發話。

examples.text: It is so easy to be solemn; it is so hard to be frivolous.
examples.translation: 變得莊嚴很容易，變得輕浮卻很難。

etymology.text: From Middle English solempne, solemne (“performed with religious ceremony or reverence; devoted to religious observances, sacred; ceremonious, formal; of a vow: made under a religious sanction, binding; religious celebration, celebration of a feast day; famous, well-known; important; grand, imposing; awe-inspiring, impressive; grave, serious; dignified; enunciated or held formally”) [and other forms], from Old French solempne, solemne (“serious, solemn”) [and other forms], or from its etymon Lat
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 solempne，意為「以宗教儀式或敬意執行；致力於宗教活動；神聖」等義。

senses.definition: One who lives alone, or in solitude; an anchorite, hermit or recluse.
The state of being solitary; solitude

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Bears are solitary animals.
examples.translation: 熊是一種獨居動物。

examples.text: I like a solitary walk.
examples.translation: 我喜歡一個人散步。

examples.text: Robert led a very simple and solitary lifestyle.
examples.translation: 羅伯特過著極為簡樸孤獨的生活。

examples.text: He became solitary since his mother died.
examples.translation: 他母親去世後便過著孤獨的生活。

examples.text: Snow leopards are solitary when not raising cubs.
examples.translation: 雪豹在育幼時並非群居，而是獨居。

examples.text: Here and there, a solitary tree provided shade.
examples.translation: 偶爾，一棵孤零零的樹提供陰涼。

etymology.text: From Middle English solitarie, borrowed from Latin sōlitārius. Doublet of solitaire.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 solitarie，借自拉丁文 sōlitārius，為 solitaire 的同義詞。

senses.definition: Living or being by oneself; alone; having no companion present
Performed, passed, or endured alone.
Not much visited or frequented; remote from society
Single; individual; sole.
Not inhabited or occupied; without signs of inhabitants or occupation; desolate; deserted
Gloomy; dismal, because of not being inhabited.
Not associated with others of the same kind.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: The old man lived a solitary life in a small cabin by the lake.
examples.translation: 那位老人在湖邊的小木屋裡過著獨居的生活。

examples.text: Carpenter bees are solitary.

etymology.text: From Middle English solitarie, borrowed from Latin sōlitārius. Doublet of solitaire.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 solitarie，借自拉丁文 sōlitārius，為 solitaire 的同義詞。

senses.definition: Alone in a category.
Singularly superior; the best.
Without sibling; without a sibling of the same gender.
Mere.

examples.text: Only 3 out of the 98 passengers survived.
examples.translation: 98名乘客只有3人生還。

examples.text: There are only 80 Uyghurs in Switzerland.
examples.translation: 在瑞士只有８０個維族人。

examples.text: Only my mother really understands me.
examples.translation: 母親是唯一一個真正理解我的人。

examples.text: Her only hobby is collecting stamps.
examples.translation: 她唯一的興趣是集郵。

examples.text: Many people only speak one language.
examples.translation: 許多人只說一種語言。

examples.text: Lisa speaks not only English but also French.
examples.translation: 麗薩不但會說英文，而且會說法文。

etymology.text: From Middle English oonly, only, from Old English ānlīċ, ǣnlīċ (“only; singular; solitary”), from Proto-Germanic *ainalīkaz. Cognate with obsolete Dutch eenlijk, German ähnlich (“similar”), Old Norse álíkr, Swedish enlig (“unified”). By surface analysis, on(e) + -ly.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（oonly），來自古英語（ānlīċ）「唯一的、獨自的」，經原始日耳曼語（*ainalīkaz）。與德語（ähnlich）「相似」同源。表面上可拆成「一」加字尾（one + -ly）。

senses.definition: Not accompanied by anything else; one in number.
Not married, and (in modern times) not dating or without a significant other.
Not divided in parts.
Designed for the use of only one.
Performed by one person, or one on each side.
Having only one rank or row of petals.
Simple and honest; sincere, without deceit.
Uncompounded; pure; unmixed.
Simple; foolish; weak; silly.

examples.text: She remained single all her life.
examples.translation: 她終生未婚。

examples.text: A single room with bath, please.
examples.translation: 我要一個帶浴室的單人房。

examples.text: He remained single all his life.
examples.translation: 他一生獨身。

examples.text: There are no single beds left.
examples.translation: 沒有單人床了。

examples.text: Not a single cloud could be seen in the sky.
examples.translation: 天上萬里無雲。

examples.text: Tom is single and has a three-year-old daughter.
examples.translation: 湯姆單身，有一個三歲的女兒。

etymology.text: From Middle English single, sengle, from Old French sengle, saingle, sangle, from Latin singulus, a diminutive derived from Proto-Indo-European *sem- (“one”). Akin to Latin simplex (“simple”). See simple, and compare singular.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（single、sengle），來自古法語（sengle），再源自拉丁語（singulus），是由原始印歐語（*sem-）「一」衍生的指小形式。與拉丁語（simplex）「簡單的」有關。參見（simple），並比較（singular）。

senses.definition: Remote from actual involvement (including cases where a person has retired from previously active involvement).
Unqualified or uninformed but yet giving advice, especially on technical issues, such as law, architecture, medicine, military theory, or sports; relating to such advice.

examples.text: These days I'm an armchair detective.
examples.translation: 最近我成了沙發偵探。

examples.text: He's just an armchair lawyer who thinks he knows a lot about the law because he reads a legal blog.
After the game, the armchair quarterbacks talked about what they would have done differently to win.

etymology.text: From arm + chair.
etymology.native: 由 arm 與 chair 組成。

senses.definition: To measure the depth of (water); to take a sounding of; to sound.
Often followed by out: to deeply understand (someone or something); to get to the bottom of.
To measure a depth; to sound.
To conduct an examination or inquiry; to investigate.
To encircle (someone or something) with outstretched arms; specifically, to measure the circumference or (rare) length of something.
To embrace (someone or something).

examples.text: I can’t for the life of me fathom what this means.
examples.translation: 我一生都無法理解這代表什麼意思。

etymology.text: From Middle English fathome, fadom, fadme (“unit of length of about six feet; depth of six feet for nautical soundings; (loosely) cubit; ell”) [and other forms], from Old English fæþm, fæþme (“encircling or outstretched arms, bosom, embrace; envelopment; control, grasp, power; fathom (unit of measurement); cubit”) [and other forms], from Proto-West Germanic *faþm (“outstretched arms, embrace; fathom (unit of measurement)”), from Proto-Germanic *faþmaz (“outstretched arms, embrace; fathom (unit o
etymology.native: 「fathom」源自中世英文 fathome、fadom、fadme，意為約六英尺長度或航海測深六英尺；亦可鬆散指「肘」或「肘長」。此詞源自古英語 fæþm、fæþme，意為「環抱之臂、胸膛、擁抱、包圍、掌控、力量」，再溯源自古西日耳曼語 *faþm，意為「伸展之臂、擁抱」或「測量單位」，更上溯至古德語 *faþmaz。

senses.definition: The act of returning.
The act of catching a ball after a punt and running it back towards the opposing team.
A throw from a fielder to the wicket-keeper or to another fielder at the wicket.
A short perpendicular extension of a desk, usually slightly lower.

The continuation in a different direction, most often at a right angle, of a building, face of a building, or any member, such as a moulding; applied to the shorter in contradistinction to the longer.
A return ticket.
An item that is returned, e.g. due to a defect.
An answer.
An account, or formal report, of an action performed, of a duty discharged, of facts or statistics, etc.; especially, in the plural, a set of tabulated statistics prepared for general information.
Gain or loss from an investment.
A report of income submitted to a government for purposes of specifying exact tax payment amounts; a tax return.
A carriage return character.
The act of relinquishing control to the calling procedure.
senses.native: （程式）返回：將控制權交回呼叫程序

senses.definition: A return value: the data passed back from a called procedure.
A return pipe, returning fluid to a boiler or other central plant (compare with flow pipe, which carries liquid away from a central plant).
A roadway along which foul air travels from the face on its way out of the mine.

examples.text: Please return the book by tomorrow.
examples.translation: 請明天前還書。

examples.text: The children returned home at dusk.
examples.translation: 夜幕降臨時，孩子們回家了。

examples.text: You should return what you borrow.
examples.translation: 有借有還。

examples.text: Finish your homework by the time they return.
examples.translation: 你要在他們回來之前把功課做完。

examples.text: He intends to return to the country earlier.
examples.translation: 他打算提前回國。

examples.text: The lost fishing boat made a safe return to harbour.
examples.translation: 迷路的漁船安全地返回了港口。

etymology.text: From Middle English returnen, retornen, from Anglo-Norman returner, from Old French retourner, retorner, from Medieval Latin retornare (“to turn back”), from re- + tornare (“to turn”). By surface analysis, re- + turn. Compare beturn. Displaced native Old English eftċierran, literally "eft-char".
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（returnen、retornen），來自英法語（returner），再源自古法語（retourner），來自中世紀拉丁語（retornare）「轉回」，由（re）- 加（tornare）「轉」組成。表面分析為（re）- 加（turn）。取代了古英語原有的（eftċierran）。

senses.definition: To convey (information, a message, news, etc.) using a telephone (noun sense 1).
To (attempt to) contact (someone) using a telephone.
To (attempt to) contact someone using a telephone; to make a telephone call.
To provide (a place) with a telephone system.
To transmit (sounds) over a distance.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Please let me know the result by telephone.
examples.translation: 請你打電話把結果告訴我。

etymology.text: The noun is derived from tele- (prefix meaning ‘from a distance’) + -phone (suffix denoting a device which makes a sound), modelled after German Telephon (“early apparatus converting sound into electrical signals”) (dated) (now German Telefon). The word was first used to refer to the modern device in 1876 by the Scottish-born Canadian-American engineer Alexander Graham Bell (1847–1922).
etymology.native: 這個名詞源自 tele-（表示「從遠處」的前綴）＋ -phone（表示「發出聲音的裝置」的後綴），仿照德語 Telephon（「早期將聲音轉換為電信號的裝置」）（舊用語）（現為德語 Telefon）。1876年，蘇格蘭出生的加拿大裔美國工程師亞歷山大·格雷厄姆·貝爾（1847–1922）首次用此詞指稱現代裝置。

senses.definition: Originally (music), a performing engagement by a musician or musical group; (by extension, film, television, theater) a job or role for a performer.
Any job, especially one that is freelance or temporary, or done on an on-demand basis.
senses.native: 任何工作，特別是自由職或臨時性工作，或是按需完成的工作

senses.definition: A demerit received for some infraction of a military deportment or dress code.
senses.native: 因違反軍規或制服規定而受到的懲罰記錄

senses.definition: Any unit of measurement having the SI prefix giga-.
senses.native: 具有前綴「吉加」的單位測量值

senses.definition: A top which is made to spin by tying a piece of string around it and then throwing it so that the string unwinds rapidly; a whipping-top.
senses.native: 一種由綁上繩子並拋出使繩子快速解開而旋轉的陀螺；鞭打陀螺

senses.definition: A person with an odd appearance; also, a foolish person.
senses.native: 外貌奇特的人；愚蠢的人

senses.definition: Fun; frolics.
A fanciful impulse; a whim; also, a joke.
A small, narrow, open boat carried in a larger ship, and used for transportation between the ship and the shore, another vessel, etc.
A similar rowing boat or sailboat, especially one used for racing; specifically, a six-oared sea rowing boat commonly found in Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly.
A two-wheeled carriage drawn by a single horse.
A frivolous, playful, or wanton young woman; a giglet or giglot.
Synonym of fishgig or fizgig (“a spear with a barb on the end of it, used for catching fish, frogs, or other small animals”).

examples.text: Tom and Mary do gigs together.

examples.translation: 教英語通常是失敗者和酒鬼的工作。

examples.text: Save for the cold in the hall, the gig was good.
examples.translation: 除了廳內有點冷，這場表演其實很精彩。

etymology.text: The etymology of the noun is unknown, but compare Old French gigue (“a fiddle”). The verb is derived from the noun.

senses.definition: Behaving in the manner of a moron; idiotic; stupid.
senses.native: 像白痴一樣行為；愚蠢的；笨拙的

senses.definition: Having a mental age of between seven and twelve years.
senses.native: 心智年齡在七至十二歲之間

examples.text: The moronic idea failed.
examples.translation: 那個愚蠢的點子失敗了。

etymology.text: From moron + -ic.
etymology.native: 由「白痴」加上後綴「-ic」組成。

senses.definition: Agitation; the state of being perturbed.
A small change in a physical system, or more broadly any definable system (such as a biological or economic system).
senses.native: 擾動，系統中的小幅變化或干擾

senses.definition: Variation in an orbit due to the influence of external bodies.

examples.text: Such observations showed him obvious examples of chemical perturbations of health.
examples.translation: 這些觀察結果讓他看到了健康受化學干擾的明顯例子。

examples.text: The term ‘distress’ connotes some degree of perturbation and emotional upset.
examples.translation: 「苦惱」一詞暗示了一定程度的干擾與情緒不安。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French perturbation, from Old French perturbacion, from Latin perturbatio.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀法語 perturbation，來自古法語 perturbacion，源自拉丁語 perturbatio。

senses.definition: A state of agitation or confusion; a flutter.
A state of slight drunkenness or tipsiness; also, the excitement caused by this state.
senses.native: 微醺或略醉的狀態；亦指由此產生的興奮感

senses.definition: Showiness, splendour.

examples.text: She was in a fluster.

etymology.text: The verb is probably from Middle English *flostren (implied in flostring, flostrynge (“agitation; blustering”)) from a Scandinavian (North Germanic) language; compare Icelandic flaustra (“to bustle”), flaustr (“a bustle; a hurry”). Compare Old English flustrian (“to weave, plait, braid”).
etymology.native: 此動詞可能源於中古英語 *flostren，與 flostring 或 flostrynge（「激動；吹噓」）有關，來自北日耳曼語言；可比較冰島語 flaustra（「忙亂」），flaustr（「忙亂；匆忙」）。可比較古英語 flustrian（「編織，編結」）。

senses.definition: Something unexpected.
A mess of feces, left by a pet or small child in an unexpected place or at an unexpected time.
The feeling that something unexpected has happened.

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: The surprise rendered her speechless.
examples.translation: 她驚訝得說不出話來。

examples.text: To my surprise, he easily came up with a plan.
examples.translation: 令我吃驚的是，他很容易就想出了一個方案。

examples.text: I was elated, ecstatic and extremely surprised that we were successful.
examples.translation: 我興奮、狂喜，又極度驚訝，我們居然成功了。

examples.text: "What a nice surprise," Tom said as he opened the door and saw Mary standing there.
examples.translation: 湯姆開門看見瑪麗站在那裡，說：「真是個驚喜！」

examples.text: Jason was a taciturn individual, so it was always a real surprise when he said anything.
examples.translation: 傑森是個沉默寡言的人，所以他一開口總是讓人很意外。

examples.text: It was a surprise to find out I owed twice as much as I thought.
examples.translation: 發現我欠的錢是我以為的兩倍，真是嚇了一跳。

etymology.text: From Middle English surprise, borrowed from Middle French surprise (“an overtake”), nominal use of the past participle of Old French sorprendre (“to overtake”), from sor- (“over”) + prendre (“to take”), from Latin super- + Latin prendere, contracted from prehendere (“to grasp, seize”). Doublet of suppli.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（surprise），借自中古法語（surprise）「追上」，是古法語（sorprendre）「追上」過去分詞的名詞用法，由（sor-）「超過」加（prendre）「拿」組成，源自拉丁語（super-）加（prendere，由 prehendere「抓住」縮約而來）。

senses.definition: The act of varying; a partial change in the form, position, state, or qualities of a thing.
A related but distinct thing.
The angular difference at the vessel between the direction of true north and magnetic north.
A line of play that differs from the original.
A technique where material is repeated with alterations to the melody, harmony, rhythm, timbre, texture, counterpoint or orchestration; but with some invariant characteristic, e.g. a ground bass.
The modification of a hereditary trait.
Deviation from the mean orbit of a heavenly body.

The situation where two or more linguistic forms appear in the same environment without a change in meaning, the choice of form being determined by factors of dialect, sociolect, register or simply the speaker's preference.
An infinitesimal perturbation applied to a function, typically denoted δf, used to probe how a functional changes.
The corresponding first-order change in a functional induced by such a perturbation, typically denoted δJ[f] and called the first variation.

examples.text: This story has infinite variations.
All the languages are subject to variations.
This does not mean that there is no variation.
Autism is a natural variation in the human condition.
This is a humorous variation of a proverb.
There is relatively little variation in temperature here.

etymology.text: From Middle French variation, from Old French variacion, from Latin variātiō, from vary + -ation.

senses.definition: A failure to function in an expected or complete manner. Usually refers to a disorder in a bodily organ (e.g. erectile dysfunction), a mental disorder, or the improper behavior of a social group.

examples.text: Tom suffers from erectile dysfunction.
examples.translation: 湯姆患有勃起功能障礙。

examples.text: You have erectile dysfunction.
examples.translation: 你有勃起功能障礙。

examples.text: Estrogen deficiency in men causes erectile dysfunction.
examples.translation: 男性雌激素缺乏會導致勃起功能障礙。

examples.text: Have you taken a medication for erectile dysfunction within the last 24 hours?
examples.translation: 你過去二十四小時內是否服用過治療勃起功能障礙的藥物？

examples.text: Viagra's impacts on erectile dysfunction were an unexpected — and lucrative — surprise.
examples.translation: 威而鋼對勃起功能障礙的影響是一個意外卻又有利可圖的驚喜。

examples.text: Doctors say his stomach has a dysfunction that needs fixing.
examples.translation: 醫生說他的胃有功能失調需要修復。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From dys- + function.
etymology.native: 由「dys-」與「function」組成。

To besmirch.

senses.definition: To commit a foul.
To hit outside of the baselines.
To hit a ball outside of the baselines.
senses.native: 把球擊出壘線之外（界外球）

senses.definition: To become clogged.
To become entangled.
To come into contact or collide with.

examples.translation: 他犯規了，因為他推倒了對方。

examples.text: Bale was fouled, and his team was awarded a free kick.
examples.translation: 貝爾被犯規了，球隊獲得了任意球。

examples.text: The sanctity of this place has been fouled.
examples.translation: 此處的聖潔已被玷汙。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English ffoul, foul, foull, fowel, fowle, fuyle, voul, vul, from Old English fūl (“foul, dirty, unclean, impure, vile, corrupt, rotten, stinking, guilty”), from Proto-West Germanic *fūl, from Proto-Germanic *fūlaz (“foul, rotten”), from Proto-Indo-European *puH- (“foul, rotten”).

A (usually accidental) contact between a bowler and the lane before the bowler has released the ball.
senses.native: （保齡球）球員在放球前身體或腳觸及球道（通常為意外）

senses.definition: A foul ball, a ball which has been hit outside of the base lines.
senses.native: （棒球）界外球（擊出壘線外的球）

senses.definition: A tangle or entanglement.

examples.text: The umpire called the ball foul.

examples.text: It was a hard foul, but I was just trying to stop him from pushing forward.
examples.translation: 那球是硬的，但我只是想阻止他前衝。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English ffoul, foul, foull, fowel, fowle, fuyle, voul, vul, from Old English fūl (“foul, dirty, unclean, impure, vile, corrupt, rotten, stinking, guilty”), from Proto-West Germanic *fūl, from Proto-Germanic *fūlaz (“foul, rotten”), from Proto-Indo-European *puH- (“foul, rotten”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 ffoul、foul、foull、fowel、fowle、fuyle、voul、vul，來自古英語 fūl（意為汙穢、不潔、腐敗、臭味、有罪），源自古西日耳曼語 *fūl，再溯源自古德語 *fūlaz（意為腐敗、臭味），最終源自印歐語系 *puH-（意為腐敗、臭味）

Light in color, pale, particularly with regard to skin tone but also referring to blond and red hair.
Just.
Adequate, reasonable, or decent, but not excellent.
Favorable to a ship's course.
Favorable, pleasant.
Not overcast; cloudless; clear.
Free from obstacles or hindrances; unobstructed; unencumbered; open; direct; said of a road, passage, etc.
Without sudden change of direction or curvature; smooth; flowing; said of the figure of a vessel, and of surfaces, water lines, and other lines.
Between the baselines.
Taken direct from an opponent's foot, without the ball touching the ground or another player.
Not a no ball.
Of a coin or die, having equal chance of landing on any side, unbiased.
Beautiful, of a pleasing appearance, with a pure and fresh quality.

senses.native: 腐敗的，特別是有腐肉般的惡臭

senses.definition: Vile, disgusting.
Morally corrupt.
Totally objectionable.

examples.text: It is very unpleasant to live near a place with putrid waste.
examples.translation: 住在有腐爛廢棄物的地方附近非常不舒服。

examples.translation: 下水道管裡的腐臭氣味讓每個人感到噁心。

senses.definition: A person whose sexual habits are not considered acceptable.
One who has been perverted; one who has turned to error, or adopted a twisted sense of values or morals.

examples.text: She's dating a pervert.
examples.translation: 她正在跟一個變態交往。

examples.text: Gustavo must have known John was a pervert.
examples.translation: 古斯塔沃一定知道約翰是個變態。

examples.text: Those perverts were trying to spy on us while we changed clothes!
examples.translation: 那些變態在我們換衣服時還想偷看我們！

etymology.text: From Old French pervertir, itself from the Latin pervertō.
etymology.native: 來自古法語 pervertir，本身源自拉丁語 pervertō。

senses.definition: One who is degenerate, who has fallen from previous stature; an immoral or corrupt person.
senses.native: 墮落者，失去昔日地位之人；不道德或不潔淨的人

examples.text: Though my uncle is homeless, I don't think he is a degenerate.
examples.translation: 雖然我的叔叔無家可歸，但我認為他並非墮落者。

examples.text: There remain great fears of seeing the clashes degenerate into massacres.
examples.translation: 人們仍擔心衝突會惡化為屠殺。

examples.text: In the cult of degenerates, acts of decency, kindness and modesty could be seen as acts of apostasy.
examples.translation: 在墮落者崇拜中，端莊、仁慈與謙遜的行為可被視為異端行為。

etymology.text: Learned borrowing from Latin dēgenerātus. See -ate (adjective-forming suffix) for more.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 dēgenerātus 的借詞。請參閱 -ate（形容詞構成綴尾）以獲取更多資訊。

senses.definition: To place bias upon; to influence.
To give a bias to.

examples.text: I'm not biased.

examples.text: They admitted that they were biased.

Tom told Mary that he thought she was biased.

senses.definition: To put into a new and improved form or condition; to restore to a former good state, or bring from bad to good; to change from worse to better.
To return to a good state; to amend or correct one's own character or habits.
To form again or in a new configuration.

examples.text: Esther's family is Reform Jewish.
Nothing will stop Algeria's economic reforms.
This product contains reformed meat.
The regiment reformed after surviving the first attack.
The Church reformed me.

etymology.text: From Middle English reformen, from Old French reformer, from Latin reformo, reformare. As a noun since 1660s, from French réforme.

senses.definition: To give power, strength, or vigour to (oneself or someone, or to something); to strengthen.
To increase the nutritional value of (food) by adding ingredients, especially minerals or vitamins.
To increase the defences of (an army, soldiers, etc.), or put (it or them) in a defensive position.
To add spirits to (wine) to increase the alcohol content.
To undergo, or cause to undergo, fortition.
To support (one's or someone's opinion, statement, etc.) by producing evidence, etc.; to confirm, to corroborate.
senses.native: 支持（意見、陳述等）以提供證據；證實，核實

senses.definition: To impart fortitude or moral strength to (someone or their determination, or something); to encourage.
senses.native: 賦予（某人或其決心，或某事物）勇氣或道德力量；鼓勵

senses.definition: To make (something) defensible against attack by hostile forces.
senses.native: 使（某物）能抵禦敵對部隊的攻擊

senses.definition: To make (something) structurally strong; to strengthen.
senses.native: 使（某物）結構上更堅固；加強

senses.definition: To provide (a city, a fortress, an army, etc.) with equipment or soldiers.

examples.text: Russian positions in Crimea are well fortified.
examples.translation: 俄羅斯在克里米亞的陣地防禦良好。

examples.translation: 這座城市除了這一側外，其他方面都加強了防禦。

etymology.text: From Late Middle English fortifien, fortfien (“to strengthen (a castle, etc.) from attack; to strengthen (an army, etc.); to strengthen (a person), aid, support; to reinforce, support; to improve; to increase the efficacy of”), from Old French fortifier (modern French fortifier), from Late Latin fortificāre (“to strengthen, fortify”), from Latin fortis (“powerful, strong”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰerǵʰ- (“to ascend, rise up; to be elevated or up high”) or *dʰerǵʰ- (“to be firm; ro
etymology.native: 源於中世紀晚期法語，意為「使城堡免受攻擊；使軍隊或人變強；支援、強化；改善功效」，最終源自印歐語根，含「上升」或「堅固」之意。

examples.translation: 在語言學中，「體」一詞指的是動詞所表示的行為如何延展於時間之中。

etymology.native: 源自中法語 denoter，來自拉丁語 denotare，由 de-（完全）與 notare（標記）組成。

Something that pollutes; a pollutant.
Moral or spiritual corruption; impurity, degradation, defilement.
The desecration of something holy or sacred; defilement, profanation.
The ejaculation of semen outside of sexual intercourse, especially a nocturnal emission.

examples.text: Because there's pollution in the cities.

This village is free from air pollution.
examples.translation: 這座村沒有空氣汙染。

examples.text: The talks will deal with the problem of pollution.

examples.text: Industrialization often goes hand in hand with pollution.

etymology.text: From Middle English pollucioun, pollucion (“desecration, impurity”), from Anglo-Norman pollutiun, Middle French pollution, pollucion, and their source, post-classical Latin pollūtiō (“defilement, desecration; nocturnal emission”) (4th century), from the participial stem of polluō (“to soil, defile, contaminate”), from por- (“before”) + -luō (“to smear”), related to lutum (“mud”) and luēs (“filth”). senses.definition: Arousing or likely to arouse controversy.
Engaging in or given to controversy; disputatious, argumentative.

examples.translation: 他挑起爭議性高的話題，製造紛爭。

senses.definition: Tending to inflame or provoke somebody.
Relating to, causing, or caused by inflammation.

examples.text: His inflammatory comments caught everyone off guard.
examples.translation: 他煽動性的言論讓大家措手不及。

examples.translation: 別再這麼煽動性了。

examples.translation: 克隆氏症和潰瘍性結腸炎等發炎性腸道疾病極為疼痛，並可能導致大腸直腸癌。

examples.text: We don't allow inflammatory or provocative content in this forum.
examples.translation: 我們不允許這個論壇出現煽動性或挑釁性的內容。

senses.definition: Causing harm in a stealthy, often gradual, manner.
Intending to entrap; alluring but harmful.
