examples.text: The loud noise was such an irritant that I could not sleep at all.
examples.translation: 那陣刺耳的噪音是一種如此大的刺激，讓我完全無法入睡。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From French irritant, equivalent to irritate + -ant.
etymology.native: 源自法語 irritant，等同於 irritate 加上 -ant。

senses.definition: That which has the quality of eating or wearing away gradually.
Any solid, liquid or gas capable of irreparably harming living tissues or damaging material on contact.

examples.text: The cheapest of nepenthes are often the most corrosive.
examples.translation: 最便宜的萼葉塔花通常腐蝕性最強。

etymology.text: From Old French corrosif.
etymology.native: 源自中古法語的 corrosif 一詞。

senses.definition: Synonym of reflash.

examples.text: The rekindle of their romance surprised everyone.
examples.translation: 他們舊情復燃，讓大家都很意外。

etymology.text: From re- + kindle.
etymology.native: 由「re-」加上「kindle」組成。

senses.definition: To render young again.
senses.native: 返老還童、恢復活力、使變得年輕

senses.definition: To give new energy or vigour to; to revitalise.
senses.native: 賦予新能量或活力；使復甦

examples.text: He came back from Algeria rejuvenated.
examples.translation: 他從阿爾及利亞回來時精神煥發。

examples.text: Algiers needs to be rejuvenated.
examples.translation: 阿爾及爾需要復甦。

examples.text: Tebboune ambitions to rejuvenate the Algerian state.
examples.translation: 泰布恩希望使阿爾及利亞國家復甦。

examples.text: Between friends, to have a heart-to-heart is really rejuvenating.
examples.translation: 朋友之間，大家談談心，非常爽快。

examples.text: The Algerian economy needs to be rejuvenated.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞經濟需要復甦。

examples.text: A lot of these soils are destroyed from growing tobacco. So, growing a crop like millet helps rejuvenate them.
examples.translation: 許多土壤因種植菸草而遭破壞，因此種植小米有助於使它們復甦。

etymology.text: From re- (“again”) + Latin iuvenis (“young”) + -ate (verb-forming suffix). Compare Old French rejuvener.
etymology.native: 源自「再次」加上拉丁語「青年」及動詞後綴，與古法語 rejuvener 相比。

senses.definition: An unremarkable, ordinary human being.
A person with no magical or supernatural powers or properties.
senses.native: 無魔法或超自然能力或屬性的人

senses.definition: A person considered to be "normal", part of the mainstream culture, outside the subculture, not part of the elite group.
senses.native: 被視為「正常」的人，屬於主流文化，不在次文化中，也不在精英群體中

senses.definition: A person who is not a Satanist.
The world outside fandom; the normal, mainstream world.
senses.native: 粉絲圈之外的世界；正常的、主流的世界

examples.text: I reflect on the beauty that surrounds us, even in the mundane.
examples.translation: 我反思著環繞在我們身邊的美，即使在平凡之中。

relations.native: 世俗的；屬世的；褻瀆的；粗俗的（與天界相對）

etymology.text: From Middle English mondeyne, from Old French mondain, from Late Latin mundānus, from Latin mundus (“world”). Compare Danish mondæn.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 mondeyne，來自舊法語 mondain，來自晚拉丁語 mundānus，來自拉丁語 mundus（世界）。與丹麥語 mondæn 相比。

senses.definition: The act of kneading something.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Give the dough a knead.
examples.translation: 把麵團揉一揉。

etymology.text: From Middle English kneden, from Old English cnedan, from Proto-West Germanic *knedan, from Proto-Germanic *knudaną, from Proto-Indo-European *gnet- (“to press together”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 kneden，後者來自古英語 cnedan，再源自日耳曼語族 *knedan，最終來自印歐語系 *gnet-（「壓合」之意）。

senses.definition: To honor; to hold in high esteem; to praise or worship.
To raise in rank, status etc., to elevate.
To elate, or fill with the joy of success.
senses.native: 使興奮或充滿成功的喜悅

senses.definition: To refine or subtilize.

examples.text: The Lord be most exalted!
examples.translation: 願主至高無上！

examples.text: The party will continue to exalt their hero.
examples.translation: 該黨將繼續尊崇他們的英雄。

examples.text: All these details exalted my young imagination.
examples.translation: 這些細節激發了我年輕的想像力。

examples.text: Whoever degrades himself will be exalted.
examples.translation: 無論如何貶低自己，終將被尊崇。

examples.text: In Buddhism, an exalted being is not so emotional.
examples.translation: 在佛教中，高潔者並不那麼情緒化。

examples.text: The illusion which exalts us is dearer to us than ten thousand truths.
examples.translation: 我們比萬千真理更愛那讓我們陶醉的幻象。

etymology.text: From Middle English exalten, from Old French exalter, from Latin exaltō.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 exalten，來自舊法式 exalter，再來自拉丁語 exaltō。

senses.definition: To be in the habit of choosing something rather than something else; to favor; to like better.
To present or submit (something) to an authority (now usually in "to prefer charges").
To advance, promote (someone or something).
To put forward for acceptance; to introduce, recommend (to).

examples.text: Compared to baseball, I prefer soccer.
examples.translation: 相比棒球，我更喜歡足球。

examples.text: No, I still prefer eating vegetables.
examples.translation: 不，我還是喜歡吃蔬菜。

examples.text: I would prefer the second sentence.
examples.translation: 我會更傾向於第二句話。

examples.text: He prefers football to baseball.
examples.translation: 他喜歡足球勝過棒球。

examples.text: Would you prefer milk or coffee?
examples.translation: 你喜歡牛奶還是咖啡?

examples.text: Which one do you prefer, this one or that one?
examples.translation: 你喜歡哪一塊？這塊還是那塊？

etymology.text: From Middle English preferren, from Anglo-Norman preferer, from Latin praeferō. Displaced native Old English foresettan and foreberan. Doublet of prelate. See also infer, relate and refer, delate and defer, as well as collate and confer among others.

senses.definition: A person who displays nostalgia for something.

examples.text: What's something that makes you feel nostalgic?
examples.translation: 有什麼東西會讓你感到懷舊嗎？

etymology.text: From nostalgia + -ic.
etymology.native: 由「懷舊」加上後綴「-ic」組成。

senses.definition: To destroy (someone or something) completely, leaving no trace; to annihilate, to wipe out.
To hide (something) by covering it; to conceal, to obscure.
To make (a drawing, text which is printed or written, etc.) indecipherable, either by erasing or obscuring it; to blot out, to efface, to delete.
To impair the function and/or structure of (a body cavity, vessel, etc.) by ablating or occluding it (in the latter case, chiefly by filling it with tissue).
senses.native: 阻塞或填塞（體腔、血管等）

senses.definition: To cancel (a postage stamp) with a postmark so it cannot be reused.
To be destroyed completely, leaving no trace.
Of a body cavity, vessel, etc.: to close up or fill with tissue; of perfusion or a pulse: to cease owing to obstruction.
senses.native: 閉合或填塞；因阻塞而停止

examples.text: Everything should be obliterated.
examples.translation: 一切事物都應被抹去。

examples.text: Let his name be obliterated!
examples.translation: 讓他之名被抹去！

examples.text: It's time to obliterate those walls of yours!
examples.translation: 現在是摧毀你那些牆壁的時候了！

examples.text: The tsunami obliterates everything in its path.
examples.translation: 颶風將沿途一切摧毀殆盡。

examples.text: The tank was obliterating everything around it.
examples.translation: 坦克正將周圍的一切摧毀殆盡。

examples.text: Can nuclear weapons obliterate asteroids?
examples.translation: 核武器能摧毀小行星嗎？

etymology.text: (start of 17th century) From earlier obliterat, learned borrowing from Latin obliterātus, oblitterātus (“having been blotted out, effaced, erased; having been forgotten”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix, of participial origin)). Obliterātus and oblitterātus are respectively the perfect passive participles of obliterō and oblitterō (“to blot out, efface, erase, obliterate; to cause to be forgotten”), probably either:
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 oblitterātus，意為「被塗黑、被刪去」，是 oblitterō 的完成被動分詞。

senses.definition: To be more important than; to outweigh.
To cause an imbalance in (something) by means of excess weight or numbers.
senses.native: 以過重的重量或數量造成失衡

senses.definition: To throw (someone or something) off balance; to cause to capsize.
senses.native: 使（某人或某物）失去平衡；使其傾覆

senses.definition: To lose one's balance; to fall over.

examples.text: It is not desirable to overbalance the budget.
examples.translation: 不應該讓預算失衡。

examples.text: My mom's advice is very important and overbalances my dad's opinion.
examples.translation: 我母親的建議非常重要，甚至超過了我父親的看法。

examples.text: The heavy rain overbalanced the sun, making everything look dark.
examples.translation: 大雨遮擋了陽光，使一切看起來陰暗無光。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The cost of living has started to overbalance our family budget completely.
examples.translation: 生活成本開始完全超出我們的家庭預算。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Her fear of spiders is stronger and overbalances her love for cats.
examples.translation: 她對蜘蛛的恐懼比愛貓的感情更強，甚至壓倒了這份愛意。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The new technology costs too much money and overbalances our savings.
examples.translation: 新技術費用太高，已經完全超出我們的儲蓄。

etymology.text: From over- + balance.
etymology.native: 由「over-」加上「balance」組成。

senses.definition: Excess of weight or value; something more than an equivalent.

examples.text: The ephemeral nature of fame often overbalances the enduring value of true artistry.
examples.translation: 名聲的短暫性往往壓倒了真正藝術的持久價值。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From over- + balance.
etymology.native: 由「over-」加上「balance」組成。

senses.native: 某些雙唇花（如龍膽）喉嚨中的突起

senses.definition: The palate of an animal, as an item of food.
senses.native: 動物的口腔，作為食物項目

senses.native: 分辨並欣賞不同味道的能力

senses.definition: Taste or flavour, especially with reference to wine or other alcoholic drinks.

examples.translation: 他確實是全心全意地享受美食與腹飽。

examples.text: Tom bought a palate of mac and cheese.
examples.translation: 湯姆買了一盤義大利麵配起司。

examples.text: He smacked his tongue against his palate.
examples.translation: 他將舌頭抵住上顎發出聲音。

examples.text: If you don't have any teeth, your palate will suffer.
examples.translation: 如果你沒有牙齒，你的口腔頂部會受損。

examples.text: Salmon has been delighting the human palate since prehistoric times.
examples.translation: 鮭魚自史前時代起就讓人們愛不釋口。

examples.translation: 那個阻礙音不是卷舌音，因為舌頭底部沒有觸碰到口腔頂部。

etymology.text: From Middle English palate, from Latin palātum (“roof of the mouth, palate”), perhaps of Etruscan origin.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 palate，來自拉丁語 palātum（意指口腔頂部、顎），可能源自伊特魯利亞語。

senses.definition: To relish; to find palatable.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: The chef can palate the soup.
examples.translation: 主廚能品嚐這鍋湯的味道。

etymology.text: From Middle English palate, from Latin palātum (“roof of the mouth, palate”), perhaps of Etruscan origin.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 palate，來自拉丁語 palātum（意指口腔頂部、顎），可能源自伊特魯利亞語。

senses.definition: To sing a lullaby to.

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: She will lullaby the baby to sleep.
examples.translation: 她會哼搖籃曲哄寶寶入睡。

senses.definition: Of, from, or similar to fish.
Suspicious; inspiring doubt.
Of a drag queen or a trans woman: appearing very feminine and resembling a cisgender woman.
senses.native: 指變性皇后或跨性別女性：外表極具女性化特徵，酷似異性戀女性

examples.text: This sounds fishy.
examples.translation: 這是可疑的。

examples.text: There's something fishy going on here.
examples.translation: 這裡似乎有些可疑之處。

examples.text: There's something fishy about this.
examples.translation: 這事有點不對勁。

examples.translation: 她母親一定聞到了什麼不對的氣息。

examples.translation: 如果東西聞起來不對，就快跑吧！

examples.translation: 我早就覺得那個傢伙有點可疑。

etymology.native: 源自中古英語 fishi 或 fischey，由 fish 加上 -y 構成。

Relating to rural life and scenes, in particular of poetry.
senses.native: 與鄉村生活及景緻有關，尤指詩歌

examples.translation: 他說：「有些學校更擅長為兒童提供牧養支持。」

examples.translation: 簡·奧斯汀的鄉村小說中，並未出現拿破崙橫掃歐洲的舞曲。

examples.translation: 半遊牧的牧民。

examples.translation: 一種牧業經濟。

examples.translation: 這片鄉村風景有起伏的山丘和一個小村落。

examples.text: Only a rustic retreat offers such genuine pastoral serenity today.
examples.translation: 唯有鄉間隱逸處能提供如此真正的寧靜。

etymology.text: From Middle English pren, from Old English prēon, from Proto-Germanic *preunaz (compare Icelandic prjónn (“pin, knitting-needle”), Danish pryne (“needle, eel-spear”)), of uncertain origin, but perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *brewn- (“protrusion, tip, edge”) (compare Lithuanian briaunà (“edge”), Albanian brez (“belt, girdle”)). Cognate with German Pfriem.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 pren，來自古英語 prēon，源自原始日耳曼語 *preunaz，可能來自原始印歐語 *brewn-（突出、尖端、邊緣）。與德語 Pfriem 同源。

senses.native: 用於固定兩塊木材等的長方形凹槽；燕窩槽

senses.definition: A piece of wood hafted into a long stick, and serving to beat out mortar.
senses.native: 安裝在長棍上的木柄，用於敲出灰漿

senses.native: 一種堅硬的石材，用於鋪設路面

examples.translation: 他給我了一萬日元的扣減金。

examples.text: In America 'rebate' is widely recognized, generally as an incentive where makers give back directly to consumers.
examples.translation: 在美國，「rebate」廣為認知，通常指製造商直接向消費者提供獎勵。

senses.definition: A device (now often electrical) used to goad livestock into moving.
A prick or stab with such a pointed instrument.

senses.definition: A poke.

senses.native: 新教徒，即羅馬天主教徒所稱之者，指信仰上屬於新教傳統之人，或因其政治意識形態（如愛爾蘭聯合主義或北愛爾蘭保皇黨）而被視為新教徒者

examples.text: Don't prod your food with your fork like that.
examples.translation: 別用叉子那樣戳你的食物。

examples.text: A few prods and he'll start talking, just watch.
examples.translation: 再戳幾下，他就會開始說話了，看著吧。

examples.text: The cat prods the ball away from me.
examples.translation: 貓把球從我腳邊踢開。

examples.text: I must prod him to realize the danger he faces.
examples.translation: 我必須催促他意識到他所面臨的危險。

examples.text: Tom's so lazy that you have to prod him repeatedly to get him to do his share of the work.
examples.translation: 湯姆太懶惰了，你得反覆催促他才能讓他完成自己的工作。

examples.text: "It's your turn," she reminded me, giving me a prod on the shoulder.
examples.translation: 「該你輪到了，」她提醒我，並拍了拍我的肩膀。

etymology.text: Alteration of earlier brod (perhaps through influence of poke; compare prog), from Middle English brodden (“to goad, incite, urge; to sprout”), from brod (“goad, nail; shoot, sprout”), from Old Norse broddr (“shaft, spike, thorn”), from Proto-Germanic *bruzdaz. Cognate with Icelandic broddur, Danish brod. Doublet of brad. Or, from or influenced by sound symbolism.
etymology.native: 源自較早的 brod，可能受 poke 影響（與 prog 相比），來自中古英語 brodden（「刺、激勵、催促；發芽」），源於 brod（「刺、釘子；莖、芽」），再源於古諾斯語 broddr（「軸心、尖刺、荊棘」），最終源自原始日耳曼語 *bruzdaz。與冰島語 broddur、丹麥語 brod 同源，亦為 brad 的雙胞胎詞。或受音韻象徵影響而成。

senses.definition: A number of domestic animals assembled together under the watch or ownership of a keeper.
Any collection of animals gathered or travelling in a company.
senses.native: 一群聚集或共同旅行的動物

senses.definition: A crowd, a mass of people or things; a rabble.
A collection of things, especially vehicles.
Someone who keeps a group of domestic animals.

examples.text: Benedito's herd helped fertilize the fields.
examples.translation: 本尼迪托的牲畜群幫助肥沃了田地。

examples.text: Benedito protected his herd from predators.
examples.translation: 本尼迪托保護他的牲畜群免受掠食者侵害。

examples.text: The herd dog understands Carlos's signals.
examples.translation: 牧犬懂得卡洛斯的手勢信號。

examples.text: Carlos knew every animal in his herd by name.
examples.translation: 卡洛斯知道牠群中每隻動物的名字。

examples.text: Gazelles sleep and graze together in a herd.
examples.translation: 羚羊成群地在草原上一起睡覺和吃草。

examples.text: It's time for the Tuaregs to transfer their herds to the valley.
examples.translation: 圖阿雷格人該把他們的牲畜轉移到山谷去了。

etymology.text: From Middle English herde, heerde, heorde, from Old English hierd, heord (“herd, flock; keeping, care, custody”), from Proto-West Germanic *herdu, from Proto-Germanic *herdō (“herd”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kerdʰ- (“file, row, herd”). Cognate with German Herde, Danish hjord, Swedish hjord. Non-Germanic cognates include Albanian herdhe (“nest”) and Serbo-Croatian krdo.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 herde，來自古英語 hierd，再追溯至原始日耳曼語與印歐語根。此詞與德語、丹麥語等相關語言中的詞同源，非日耳曼語系中亦有相連詞彙。

senses.definition: To unite or associate in a herd; to feed or run together, or in company.
senses.native: 將人或物聚集成群；共同放牧或同行

senses.definition: To unite or associate in a herd
To manage, care for or guard a herd
senses.native: 管理、照顧或守護一群牲畜

senses.definition: To associate; to ally oneself with, or place oneself among, a group or company.
senses.native: 結盟；與某群體聯合或加入其中

senses.definition: To move, or be moved, in a group. (of both animals and people)
senses.native: 成群移動或被移動（適用於動物與人）

senses.definition: To act as a herdsman or a shepherd.
senses.native: 擔任牧人或牧羊人的工作

senses.definition: To form or put into a herd.
To move or drive a herd.

examples.text: Benedito's herd moved slowly up the mountain.
examples.translation: 本尼迪托的牲畜群緩慢地沿著山脊上行。

examples.text: On alighting at the station, we were all herded over the footbridge and through a side exit.

etymology.text: From Middle English herde, heerde, heorde, from Old English hierd, heord (“herd, flock; keeping, care, custody”), from Proto-West Germanic *herdu, from Proto-Germanic *herdō (“herd”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kerdʰ- (“file, row, herd”). Cognate with German Herde, Danish hjord, Swedish hjord. Non-Germanic cognates include Albanian herdhe (“nest”) and Serbo-Croatian krdo.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 herde，來自古英語 hierd，再追溯至原始日耳曼語與印歐語根。此詞與德語、丹麥語等相關語言中的詞同源，非日耳曼語系中亦有相連詞彙。

senses.definition: To pass through the pores or interstices of; to penetrate and pass through without causing rupture or displacement; applied especially to fluids which pass through substances of loose texture
To enter and spread through; to pervade.

examples.text: A bad smell permeated the room.
examples.translation: 一股難聞的氣味滲透了整個房間。

examples.text: Tom permeated our lives.
examples.translation: 湯姆滲透進我們的生活裡。

examples.text: The air was permeated by the smell of the sea.
examples.translation: 空氣中充斥著海的氣息。

examples.text: Information processing permeates all aspects of life.
examples.translation: 資訊處理滲透於生活的各個面向。

examples.text: Everything here is permeated by the spirit of history.
examples.translation: 這裡的一切都充滿了歷史精神。

examples.text: Mammeri's presence still permeates Algeria's cultural scene.
examples.translation: 馬默里的影響力至今仍滲透在阿爾及利亞的文化界。

etymology.text: First attested in 1656; borrowed from Latin permeātus, perfect passive participle of permeō (“to pass through”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (noun-forming suffix).
etymology.native: 最早見於 1656 年，源自拉丁語 permeātus，為 permeō（「穿過」）的完成時被動分詞。

senses.definition: A watery by-product of milk production.
Liquid that has passed through a filtration system.

examples.text: The spirit of giving and kindness that permeates during Christmas is something I truly adore.
examples.translation: 聖誕節期間充滿了慷慨與善良的精神，這是我真正愛慕的。

etymology.text: First attested in 1656; borrowed from Latin permeātus, perfect passive participle of permeō (“to pass through”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (noun-forming suffix).
etymology.native: 最早見於 1656 年，源自拉丁語 permeātus，為 permeō（「穿過」）的完成時被動分詞。

senses.definition: The act or an instance of puncturing.

A hole in a vehicle's tyre, causing the tyre to deflate.

examples.translation: 他的手臂上有兩個小孔，那是蛇牙刺穿皮膚的地方。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Late Latin punctūra.

senses.definition: To pierce; to break through; to tear a hole.
To destroy the vitality or strength of.

examples.text: His car's tyre was punctured.
examples.translation: 他的車胎被刺破了。

examples.text: This tyre is punctured.
examples.translation: 這隻輪胎已經刺破了。

examples.text: The petrol containers have been punctured.
examples.translation: 汽油容器已被刺破。

examples.text: Mark punctured the tires of Jessica's van.
examples.translation: Mark 刺破了 Jessica 的貨車輪胎。

examples.text: He broke two ribs and punctured his lung.
examples.translation: 他摔斷兩根肋骨，並刺破肺臟。

examples.text: The tire punctured and Gunter crashed.
examples.translation: 輪胎刺破後，Gunter 撞車了。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Late Latin punctūra.
etymology.native: 源自晚拉丁語 punctūra。

senses.definition: The act of quenching something; the fact of being quenched.
The abnormal termination of operation of a superconducting magnet, occurring when part of the superconducting coil enters the normal (resistive) state.
senses.native: 超導磁體異常停止運作

senses.definition: A rapid change of the parameters of a physical system.

examples.translation: 那瓶汽水解了我們的渴。

etymology.text: From Middle English quenchen, from Old English cwenċan, from Proto-Germanic *kwankijaną.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 quenchen，再源自古英語 cwenċan。

senses.definition: To make (something) even, inactive or ineffective.
To make (a territory, etc.) politically neutral.
senses.native: 使（地區等）在政治上保持中立

senses.definition: To make (an acidic or alkaline substance) chemically neutral.
senses.native: 使（酸性或鹼性物質）化學上呈中性

senses.definition: To kill.

examples.text: Alkalis neutralize acids.
examples.translation: 鹼性物質可中和酸性物質。

examples.text: Flavio can try using antibiotics to neutralize the bacteria.
examples.translation: Flavio 可以嘗試使用抗生素來消滅細菌。

examples.text: Make sure every hostile has been neutralized.
examples.translation: 請確保所有敵對單位都已消滅。

examples.text: The antidote neutralized the toxin.
examples.translation: 解毒劑中和了毒素。

examples.text: The treaty neutralized the small republic.
examples.translation: 該條約使小共和國陷入孤立。

examples.text: Her optimism neutralizes his gloom.
examples.translation: 她的樂觀主義抵消了他的悲觀情緒。

relations.native: 神經化（誤植，應為 neutralize 之類推詞）
一種以嘲弄或諷刺方式模仿其他作品或表演的演出

etymology.text: From French neutraliser (first attested in 1642). By surface analysis, neutral + -ize.
etymology.native: 源於法語 neutraliser（首次見於 1642 年）。由中性加上 -ize 構成。

senses.definition: To cause to have a polarization.
To cause a group to be divided into extremes.

examples.text: Tom bought a pair of polarized sunglasses.
examples.translation: 湯姆買了一副偏光太陽眼鏡。

examples.text: These polarized sunglasses are great for driving.
examples.translation: 這副偏光太陽眼鏡開車時效果很好。

examples.text: In Algeria, politics is polarized.
examples.translation: 在阿爾及利亞，政治已分極化。

examples.text: A polarized plug has two blades with one wider than the other.
examples.translation: 分極化插頭有兩片刀片，其中一片較寬。

examples.text: Do not defeat the safety purpose of the polarized or grounding-type plug.
examples.translation: 不要破壞分極化或接地型插頭的安全功能。

examples.text: It was never my intent to be divisive or polarizing.
examples.translation: 我從未有意製造分裂或分極化的局面。

relations.native: 使分成兩個對立的派別

etymology.text: From French polariser, equivalent to polar + -ize.
etymology.native: 源自法語 polariser，等同於 polar 加上 -ize。

senses.definition: Inactive, quiet, at rest.
Not sounded; silent.
Non-proliferating.

examples.text: His normally quiescent demeanor hid a storm of ideas beneath the surface.
examples.translation: 他平時安詳的舉止掩蓋了表面下翻湧的思緒。

examples.text: The patient remained quiescent, showing no signs of distress or movement.
examples.translation: 病人保持安靜，未顯出任何痛苦或動作的跡象。

examples.text: The volcano had been quiescent for centuries, but scientists still monitored it closely.
examples.translation: 該火山數百年來一直處於平靜狀態，但科學家仍密切監控它。

examples.text: The bats were quiescent at that time of day, so we slowly entered the cave.
examples.translation: 蝙蝠在那個時段處於安靜狀態，因此我們緩慢地進入洞穴。

examples.text: The quiescent level of centimeter wave-length solar radiation.
examples.translation: 厘米波長太陽輻射的平靜水平。

examples.text: The quiescent melancholy of the town.
examples.translation: 這座城市那沉靜的憂愁。

relations.native: 牛角麵包、新月形麵包、可頌

etymology.text: Learned borrowing from Latin quiēscēns, quiēscentem.
etymology.native: 此詞源自拉丁語 quiēscēns 與 quiēscentem，意為「休息」或「安靜」。

senses.definition: Biotic material that releases fragrant smoke when burnt, often used in religious rites or for aesthetic reasons.
The fragrant smoke released by burning incense (sense 1).
senses.native: 焚香所釋出的香氣濃煙

senses.definition: Homage; adulation.

examples.text: It smells like incense in here.
examples.translation: 這裡聞起來有股香味的味道。

examples.text: What kind of incense is this?
examples.translation: 這是什麼樣的香火？

examples.text: They do not like incense.
examples.translation: 他們不喜歡香火。

examples.text: A lot of these old books smell of incense.
examples.translation: 許多這些舊書都散發著香味的氣息。

examples.text: When you go visit the grave, don't forget to bring incense and candles, oh, and flowers too.
examples.translation: 當你去拜訪墳墓時，別忘記帶香火和蠟燭，還有花。

examples.text: In the Nigerian city of Maiduguri, the popular incense kaaji is a cherished, local tradition.
examples.translation: 在尼日利亞的馬迪古里市，流行的香火 kaaji 是當地珍貴的傳統。

relations.native: 有刺激性的；令人氣憤的

etymology.text: From Middle English encens, from Old French encens (“sweet-smelling substance”) from Late Latin incensum (“burnt incense”, literally “something burnt”), neuter past participle of incendō (“to set on fire”). Compare incendiary. Doublet of incienso. Displaced native Old English rēcels.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 encens，來自舊法語 encens（「芳香物質」），後者來自晚拉丁語 incensum（「燃燒的香火」，字面意思為「被燒的東西」），是 incendō（「點火」）的中性過去分詞。與 incendiary 相比。與 incienso 同源。對應古英語 rēcels。

etymology.text: From Middle English agayn, from Old English onġēan (“against, again”), from Proto-West Germanic *in gagin, from Proto-Germanic *in gagin. etymology.text: First use appears c. 1513 in the writings of Robert Fabyan. etymology.native: 首次出現約於 1513 年羅伯特·法比安之著作中。此義源自中古英語 repryen（「送回監禁」），可能來自中古法語 reprendre；與 reprise 為同源詞。

etymology.text: From Late Middle English elongat, elongate (“kept away; different or remote in nature”, adjective), borrowed from Late Latin ēlongātus (“having been stretched out, elongated; prolonged, protracted; having been kept aloof, removed”) + Middle English -at (suffix forming participles). Ēlongātus is the perfect passive participle of ēlongō (“to prolong, protract; to keep aloof, remove; to depart, withdraw”), from Latin ē- (a variant of ex- (prefix meaning ‘away; out’)) + longus (“extended, long, prol
etymology.native: 源於中世紀晚期英語 elongat 或 elongate（意指「被置於遠處；性質不同或遙遠」的形容詞），借自中世紀晚期拉丁語 ēlongātus（意指「被拉伸、伸長；延長；被置於高處、移開」）加上中古英語 -at 分詞後綴。ēlongātus 是動詞 ēlongō（意指「延長、拖延；置於遠處、移開；離去、撤回」）的完成時被動分詞，該動詞來自拉丁語前綴 ē-（ex- 的變體，意為「向外」）加上 longus（意指「延伸、長、多餘」）。

examples.translation: 好奇心被激起後，他問了一個問題。

etymology.text: The verb is borrowed from French piquer (“to prick, sting; to anger, annoy; (reflexive) to get angry; to provoke, stimulate; (reflexive) to boast about”), from Middle French piquer, picquer (“to prick, sting; to anger, annoy; (reflexive) to get angry”), from Old French piquer (“to pierce with the tip of a sword”), from proto-Romance or Vulgar Latin *pīccare (“to sting; to strike”) or *pikkāre, and then either:
etymology.native: 此動詞源自法語 piquer（「刺、刺痛；生氣、煩擾；反身用法：發怒；激發；反身用法：自誇」），來自中古法語 piquer, picquer（「刺、刺痛；生氣、煩擾；反身用法：發怒」），來自古法語 piquer（「用劍尖刺穿」），源自原始羅曼語或通俗拉丁語 *pīccare（「刺痛；擊打」）或 *pikkāre，然後分為：

senses.definition: To speak in generalities, or in vague terms.
To infer or induce from specific cases to more general cases or principles.
To spread throughout the body and become systemic.
To derive or deduce (a general concept or principle) from particular facts.
senses.native: 從特定事實推導出一般概念或原則

examples.text: Don't generalize your personal problems.
examples.translation: 不要將個人問題泛化。

examples.text: You can't just generalize like that.
examples.translation: 你不可以這樣泛泛而談。

examples.text: The new findings don't generalize very well.
examples.translation: 新發現的結論很難推廣。

examples.text: Tom's mind excels at abstracting and generalizing.
examples.translation: 湯姆擅長抽象思維與概括。

examples.text: It's a mistake to generalize Muslims as terrorists.
examples.translation: 將穆斯林一概視為恐怖分子是錯誤的。

examples.text: Don't generalize individual behavior to an entire group.
examples.translation: 不要把個人行為上升到集體。

etymology.text: From general + -ize.
etymology.native: 由「一般」加上「化」構成。

senses.definition: To free or deprive of illusion; to disenchant.

examples.text: We were disillusioned with the result.
examples.translation: 我們對結果感到幻滅。

examples.text: I'm disillusioned with everything.
examples.translation: 我對一切事物都感到幻滅。

examples.text: He said he was disillusioned with Christianity.
examples.translation: 他說他對基督教感到幻滅。

examples.text: He became disillusioned with his life in France.
examples.translation: 他因在法國的生活而感到幻滅。

examples.text: I was disillusioned at his married life.
examples.translation: 我對他的婚姻生活感到失望。

examples.text: He became more and more disillusioned with politics.
examples.translation: 他對政治越來越感到幻滅。

etymology.text: From dis- + illusion: literally, the removal or undoing of illusion.
etymology.native: 由 dis- 加上 illusion 組成，字面意思是移除或解除虛妄。

senses.definition: The act of revealing or disclosing.
Something dramatically disclosed.
A manifestation of divine truth.
Something that is revealed.
Something that turns out to be a great success.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: The revelation took everyone by surprise.
examples.translation: 這個啟示讓所有人感到意外。

examples.text: The company is still smarting from the revelations.
examples.translation: 該公司仍因這些揭露而耿耿於懷。

examples.text: His extensive knowledge of music was a revelation to us.
examples.translation: 他對音樂的廣泛知識讓我們感到驚訝。

examples.text: Zoroastrianism is based on the revelations of the Persian prophet Zarathustra, or Zoroaster in Greek.
examples.translation: 祆教基於波斯先知扎拉圖施特拉（希臘語稱之為佐羅亞斯特）的啟示。

examples.text: Another source of surprise has been the revelation that Pluto’s thin atmospheric haze has many more layers than previously thought.
examples.translation: 另一個令人驚訝的消息是，冥王星稀薄的大氣層霧霾比先前認為的要多得多層次。

examples.text: The revelation of the culprits' identities was cathartic for the populace.
examples.translation: 揭露兇手的身份對民眾來說是一種宣洩。

etymology.text: From Middle English revelacioun, from Old French revelacion, from Latin revēlātiō (“disclosure”), from revēlō (“to disclose”), re (“again”) + vēlō (“to cover”); by surface analysis, revelate + -ion.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 revelacioun，來自舊法語的 revelacion，再源自拉丁語 revēlātiō（披露），由 revēlō（揭露）組成，re 表示「再次」加上 vēlō（覆蓋）。

senses.definition: Passed on as an inheritance, by last will or intestate.
Of a title, honor or right: legally granted to somebody's descendant after that person's death.
Of a disease or trait: passed from a parent to offspring in the genes.
Of a person: holding a legally hereditary title or rank.
senses.native: 持有合法世襲的頭銜或爵位

senses.definition: Of a ring: such that all submodules of projective modules over the ring are also projective.
senses.native: 指環：其所有項式模的子模也是項式模的

senses.definition: Of a property of graphs: such that if G has the property, so must every induced subgraph of G.
senses.native: 圖論性質：若圖具有此性質，則其任何誘導子圖也必具有此性質

examples.text: Her face is really swollen, but she says that it isn't the mumps. Apparently, it's some unknown hereditary disease.
examples.translation: 她的臉腫得很厲害，但她說這不是麻疹。顯然，這是某種未知的遺傳性疾病。

examples.text: Duke is a hereditary title which was created in Norman times.
examples.translation: 公爵是一個世襲爵位，始創於諾曼時期。

examples.text: Haemophilia is hereditary in his family.
examples.translation: 血友病在他的家族中具有遺傳性。

examples.text: The aristocratic dynasty's hereditary succession ensured uninterrupted power for generations.
examples.translation: 貴族王朝的世襲繼承制度確保了數代人的權力未斷。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: No, infertility isn't hereditary.
examples.translation: 不，不孕症並非遺傳的。

examples.text: Alopecia is often hereditary.
examples.translation: 斑禿症通常是遺傳的。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English hereditarie, from Latin hērēditārius, from hērēditās (“inheritance”), from hērēs (“heir”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 hereditarie，來自拉丁語 hērēditārius，意為「繼承」，再源自 hērēs（繼承人）。

senses.definition: A hereditary ruler; a hereditary peer in the House of Lords.
senses.native: 世襲公爵；上議院中的世襲貴族

examples.text: The noble house maintained its hereditary dominion through unwritten royal decrees.
examples.translation: 貴族家族透過無文字的王室詔令維持其世襲統治權。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English hereditarie, from Latin hērēditārius, from hērēditās (“inheritance”), from hērēs (“heir”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 hereditarie，來自拉丁語 hērēditārius，意為「繼承」，再源自 hērēs（繼承人）。

senses.definition: A large medical facility, usually in a building with multiple floors, where seriously ill or injured patients are given extensive medical or surgical treatment.
A building founded for the long-term care of its residents, such as an almshouse.
A place of lodging.

examples.text: She went to the hospital yesterday.
examples.translation: 她昨天去了醫院。

examples.text: That white building is a hospital.
examples.translation: 那棟白色的建築物是一家醫院。

examples.text: Tom called every hospital in town.
examples.translation: 湯姆給鎮上的每家醫院都打去了電話。

examples.text: Please take me to the hospital.
examples.translation: 請帶我去醫院。

examples.text: I went to the hospital to have my eyes tested.
examples.translation: 我到醫院去檢查了眼睛。

examples.text: He was kind enough to take me to the hospital.
examples.translation: 他好心地把我送到醫院。

etymology.text: From Middle English hospital, hospitall, from Old French hospital (Modern French hôpital), from Late Latin hospitālis, hospitāle (“hospice, shelter, guesthouse”), from noun use of Latin hospitālis (“hospitable”), from hospes (“host, guest”). Doublet of hotel and hostel. Displaced native Middle English lechehous, from Old English lǣċehūs (literally “doctor house”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（hospital、hospitall），來自古法語（hospital，現代法語 hôpital），再源自晚期拉丁語（hospitālis、hospitāle）「招待所、庇護所」，是拉丁語（hospitālis）「好客的」的名詞用法，來自（hospes）「主人、客人」。與（hotel）、（hostel）為雙式詞。取代了中古英語原有的（lechehous），其源自古英語（lǣċehūs）「醫生之家」。

senses.definition: Previous caution or care; caution previously employed to prevent misfortune or to secure good.
A measure taken beforehand to ward off evil or secure good or success; a precautionary act.
senses.native: 事先採取的預防措施，以避開災禍或確保好運；預防行動

examples.text: Boldi still observed some precautions.
examples.translation: Boldi 仍遵守一些預防措施。

examples.text: We have to take every precaution.
examples.translation: 我們必須採取一切預防措施。

examples.text: We need to take some precautions against fire.
examples.translation: 我們需要針對火災採取一些預防措施。

examples.text: Observe all warnings, precautions and instructions.
examples.translation: 遵守所有警告、預防措施及說明。

examples.text: During an epidemic, observe the proper precautions.
examples.translation: 在流行病期間，請遵守正確的預防措施。

examples.text: That seems to be a sensible precaution.
examples.translation: 那似乎是一個合理的預防措施。

etymology.text: From French précaution, Latin praecautio, from praecavere, praecautum (“to guard against beforehand”); prae (“before”) + cavere (“be on one's guard”). See pre-, and caution.
etymology.native: 源自法文 précaution，拉丁文 praecautio，來自 praecavere（事先警戒）；prae（在...之前）加上 cavere（保持警惕）。參見前綴 pre- 及 caution。

senses.definition: To enclose, as in a case.

examples.text: My feet were encased in mud.
examples.translation: 我的腳被泥封住了。

examples.text: The box is too small to encase the big gift.
examples.translation: 這個盒子太小，無法裝下這份大禮物。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: We need to encase the wires before they get wet.
examples.translation: 我們需要在線纜受潮前將其包覆起來。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The doctor will encase the broken bone with metal.
examples.translation: 醫生將用金屬將骨折處包覆固定。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Can you help me encase this fragile vase safely?
examples.translation: 你能幫我安全地包覆這隻易碎花瓶嗎？
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The new law requires all data to be securely encased.
examples.translation: 新法規定所有資料必須安全地加以封裝。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From en- + case.
etymology.native: 由 en- 加上 case 組成。

senses.definition: A polypeptide hormone that regulates carbohydrate metabolism (in various animals including humans).
Any exogenous preparation of this hormone for use as a medication.
senses.native: 此荷爾蒙作為藥物使用的任何外源性製劑

senses.definition: Any exogenous preparation of this hormone or its analogues for use as a medication.
senses.native: 此荷爾蒙或其類似物的任何外源性製劑，用於藥物治療

examples.text: Insulin is produced by the pancreas.
examples.translation: 胰島素由胰臟製造。

examples.text: The insulin was making her fat.
examples.translation: 那胰島素讓她變胖了。

examples.text: The pancreas produces enzymes as well as insulin.
examples.translation: 胰臟除了製造胰島素外，還分泌酵素。

examples.text: The pancreas is a large gland that produces insulin.
examples.translation: 胰臟是一個大型腺體，負責製造胰島素。

examples.text: Apart from insulin, the pancreas also produces enzymes.
examples.translation: 除了胰島素外，胰臟還分泌酵素。

examples.text: Have you been keeping up a normal diet since the last shot of insulin?
examples.translation: 你最後一次注射胰島素之後有正常飲食嗎？

etymology.text: From Latin īnsula (“island”) (named for the islets of Langerhans, where insulin is produced) + -in.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 īnsula（島嶼），因朗格漢斯島（胰島素產生處）而得名，加上 -in 詞尾。

senses.definition: A simple monosaccharide (sugar) with a molecular formula of C₆H₁₂O₆; a principle source of energy for cellular metabolism.

examples.text: My glucose levels went down.
examples.translation: 我的血糖下降了。

examples.text: Tom is glucose-deprived.
examples.translation: 湯姆缺乏葡萄糖。

examples.text: Your blood glucose levels are too high.
examples.translation: 您的血糖水平太高了。

examples.text: The sucrose molecule is comprised of glucose and fructose.
examples.translation: 蔗糖分子由葡萄糖和果糖組成。

examples.text: Whoever lost a bag with a glucose meter inside, contact this address.
examples.translation: 誰丟了裝有血糖儀的袋子，請聯絡此地址。

examples.text: The relationship between epilepsy and glucose metabolism was established more than 85 years ago.
examples.translation: 關於癲癇與葡萄糖代謝的關係已確立超過 85 年。

etymology.text: From French, from Ancient Greek γλεῦκος (gleûkos, “wine, must”). By surface analysis, gluco- + -ose; note that -ose is derived from the word glucose.
etymology.native: 源自古希臘語，由前綴「gluco-」加上後綴「-ose」組成。

senses.definition: A sugar, starch, or cellulose that is a food source of energy for an animal or plant.
Any food rich in starch or other carbohydrates.
senses.native: 富含澱粉或其他醣類的食物

examples.text: It is important to eat carbohydrates.
examples.translation: 攝取醣類很重要。

examples.text: Cellulose is a carbohydrate.
examples.translation: 纖維素是一種醣類。

examples.text: Galactose is a carbohydrate.
examples.translation: 半乳糖是一種醣類。

examples.text: Food is comprised of protein, carbohydrates, and fats.
examples.translation: 食物由蛋白質、醣類和脂肪組成。

examples.text: Spaghetti is high in carbohydrates.
examples.translation: 義大利麵富含醣類。

examples.text: Do you know anything about complex carbohydrates?
examples.translation: 你對複合碳水化合物有什麼瞭解嗎？

etymology.text: From their general formula Cₙ(H₂O)ₙ; they were once thought to be hydrates of carbon.
etymology.native: 因其通式為 Cₙ(H₂O)ₙ；過去曾認為它們是碳的水合物。

senses.definition: To reproach with contemptuous words; to deride, to mock, to taunt.
To say in a mocking or taunting manner.
To make a mocking remark or remarks; to jeer.
senses.native: 發出戲謔的評論或話語；嘲諷

senses.definition: To accord or agree.

examples.text: Something here doesn't jibe.
examples.translation: 這裡有些東西不對勁。

examples.text: I'm tired of your anti-science jibe from your religion.
examples.translation: 我厭倦了你宗教中那些反科學的嘲諷了。

examples.text: His criticism of the Thai people doesn't jibe at all with my experience of them.
examples.translation: 他對泰國人的批評完全與我的經驗不符。

examples.text: The rude and arrogant son of the famous actor used to indulge in jibes at other people's expense.
examples.translation: 那位著名演員的粗魯傲慢之子過去常藉他人之過頭發笑。

examples.text: He jibed at me for being late again today.
examples.translation: 他因我再次遲到而對我發笑。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Don't let him jibe at you when you are sad.
examples.translation: 當你傷心時，別讓他嘲笑你。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: Uncertain; possibly from Old French giber (“to engage in horseplay; to play roughly in sport”). Compare English jib (“usually of a horse: to stop and refuse to go forward”), Old Norse geipa (“to talk nonsense”).
etymology.native: 可能源自舊法語 giber（「從事嬉戲；在運動中粗魯地玩耍」）。比較英語 jib（通常指馬：停止並拒絕前行），以及古諾斯語 geipa（「胡言亂語」）。

senses.definition: The preying of one animal on others.
The action of attacking or plundering.

examples.text: Several species of Wētā are under threat from predation by birds and reptiles, and habitat loss.
examples.translation: 幾種 Wētā 物種正面臨鳥類與爬行動物的捕食威脅，且棲息地正在流失。

examples.text: Predation happens when strong animals eat weaker ones.
examples.translation: 捕食發生在強壯動物吃掉弱小的動物時。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: This type of predation is very dangerous for babies.
examples.translation: 這種類型的捕食對嬰兒來說非常危險。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Natural predation keeps the population of animals balanced.
examples.translation: 自然的捕食能維持動物族群的平衡。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: We must protect endangered species from human predation.
examples.translation: 我們必須保護瀕危物種免受人類捕食的侵害。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The cycle of predation ensures that weak animals die.
examples.translation: 捕食循環確保了弱小的動物會死亡。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin praedātiō, praedātiōnis, from praedor (“pillage, plunder”), from praeda (“plunder, spoils”).
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 praedātiō，由 praedor（掠奪）衍生，該詞又來自 praeda（戰利品）。

senses.definition: A publication, such as a newspaper or magazine, that is issued with a printed date later than the date of issue.
senses.native: 出版日期晚於發行日期的刊物，如報紙或雜誌

examples.text: Such a temporal displacement predates any known astronomical record.
examples.translation: 這種時間位移早於任何已知的天文紀錄。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From pre- + date.
etymology.native: 由「前」加上「日期」組成。

senses.definition: To participate in a foray.
To do or attempt something outside one's typical area of expertise.
senses.native: 在自己專長的範疇之外嘗試做某事

senses.definition: To scour an area for goods as part of a foray.
senses.native: 為了進行一次探索而搜尋該區域的貨物

examples.text: Scientists' forays into politics.
examples.translation: 科學家們涉足政治的嘗試。

examples.text: He led a brave foray across the river to rescue his friend.
examples.translation: 他勇敢地渡河前往營救朋友。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: This avant-garde foray into digital art challenges conventional perceptions of beauty.
examples.translation: 這場前衛的數位藝術嘗試挑戰了傳統的美學觀念。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Based on initial data analysis, the collared bears rarely forayed outside the park.
examples.translation: 根據初步數據分析，頸帶熊很少離開公園範圍。

examples.text: The diplomat's subtle foray into diplomatic negotiations resolved the long-standing dispute.
examples.translation: 那位外交官在談判中採取的微妙策略解決了長期爭端。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The poet's enigmatic foray into metaphysical philosophy puzzled the discerning critics.
examples.translation: 那位詩人涉足形而上學哲學的探索讓敏銳的評論家感到困惑。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Middle English forrayen (“to pillage”), a back-formation of forrayour, forreour, forrier (“raider, pillager”), from Old French forrier, fourrier, a derivative of fuerre (“provender, fodder, straw”), from Frankish *fōdar (“fodder, sheath”), from Proto-Germanic *fōdrą (“fodder, feed, sheath”), from Proto-Indo-European *patrom (“fodder”), *pat- (“to feed”), *pāy- (“to guard, graze, feed”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 forrayen（「洗劫」），是 forrayour 等詞的派生形式，源於古法語 forrier，後者來自 fuerre（飼料、乾草），再追溯至日耳曼語族及印歐語族的原始詞根。

senses.definition: A building for recreational use such as a hunting lodge or a summer cabin.
A local chapter of some fraternities, such as freemasons.
senses.native: 某些兄弟會（如自由之愛社）的地方分會

senses.definition: A local chapter of a trade union.
A rural hotel or resort, an inn.
senses.native: 鄉間旅館或度假屋，即客棧

senses.definition: A beaver's shelter constructed on a pond or lake.
senses.native: 海狸在池塘或湖泊中建造的庇護所

senses.definition: A den or cave.
The chamber of an abbot, prior, or head of a college.
senses.native: 修道院長、司鐸長或學院長的房舍

senses.definition: The space at the mouth of a level next to the shaft, widened to permit wagons to pass, or ore to be deposited for hoisting; called also platt.
senses.native: 水平井口旁寬敞的空間，供車輛通行或堆放礦石以便提升；亦稱平台

senses.definition: A collection of objects lodged together.

senses.definition: A relationship of resemblance or equivalence between two situations, people, or objects, especially when used as a basis for explanation or extrapolation.
The proportion or the equality of ratios.

The correspondence of a word or phrase with the genius of a language, as learned from the manner in which its words and phrases are ordinarily formed; similarity of derivative or inflectional processes.
senses.native: 詞語與語言天才之對應，如從其詞語與片語通常形成之方式所學；派生或變位過程之相似性

examples.text: It was an inappropriate analogy.
examples.translation: 這是一個不當之類比。

examples.text: Your analogy isn't correct.
examples.translation: 您的類比不正確。

examples.text: Such an analogy is inappropriate in this case.
examples.translation: 此類比於此情境而言並不恰當。

examples.text: I see no analogy between your problem and mine.
examples.translation: 我看不出您之問題與我之間有何類比。

examples.text: I don't understand the analogy.
examples.translation: 我不懂此類比之意。

examples.text: Mary tried to explain fractions to Tom by using a pie as an analogy.
examples.translation: 瑪麗試著用蛋糕作為類比，向湯姆解釋分數。

etymology.text: From Latin analogia, from Ancient Greek ἀναλογίᾱ (analogíā), from ἀνα- (ana-) + λόγος (lógos, “speech, reckoning”).
etymology.native: 源自古希臘語 ἀναλογίᾱ，由前綴 ἀνα- 與 λόγος 組成。

senses.definition: Extremely precise or specific, especially regarding location.

examples.text: A GPS device can pinpoint your location anywhere in the world.
examples.translation: 無論你在世界的哪一個角落，你都可以使用全球定位儀來找出你的所在。

examples.text: The machine assembles parts at high speed and with pinpoint accuracy.
examples.translation: 這台機器高速且精準地組裝零件。

examples.text: We need to find the precise pinpoint location of the leak.
examples.translation: 我們需要找到洩漏的確切位置。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From pin + point.
etymology.native: 由「針」與「點」組合而成。

senses.definition: To identify or locate (someone or something) precisely or with great accuracy.

examples.text: The cause hasn't been pinpointed.
examples.translation: 原因尚未被釐清。

examples.text: The investigators tried to pinpoint the source of the flames.
examples.translation: 調查人員試圖找出火源。

etymology.text: From pin + point.
etymology.native: 由「針」與「點」組合而成。

senses.definition: A hobby or recreational or leisure pursuit.
That which calls one away from one's regular employment or vocation.
senses.native: 從正職工作或職業中抽離的事物

senses.definition: Pursuits; duties; affairs which occupy one's time; usual employment; vocation.
The calling of a case from an inferior to a superior court.
senses.native: 將案件從下級法院移送至上級法院

senses.definition: A calling away; a diversion.

examples.text: Skiing is his winter avocation.
examples.translation: 滑雪是他的冬季副業。

examples.text: His avocation is photography.
examples.translation: 他的副業是攝影。

examples.text: Gardening became her beloved avocation.
examples.translation: 園藝成了她最愛的副業。

examples.text: They tended their flocks and herds together, and carried on all their avocations in common.
examples.translation: 他們共同放牧群畜，並一起從事所有副業活動。

examples.text: Learning languages is my avocation. I don't get paid for it.
examples.translation: 學習語言是我的副業，但我沒有因此領薪。

examples.text: Painting is my main avocation, and I sell some pictures online.
examples.translation: 繪畫是我的主要副業，我會在網路上出售一些作品。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Latin āvocātiō (“a distraction”), from āvocō (“to call off, distract”).
etymology.native: 源於拉丁語 āvocātiō（「分心」），來自動詞 āvocō（「叫離、分散」）。

senses.definition: A part, portion, or subdivision.
One of the principal divisions of executive government

A territorial division; a district; especially, in France, one of the districts into which the country is divided for governmental purposes, similar to a county in the UK and in the USA. France is composed of 101 départements organized in 18 régions, each department is divided into arrondissements, in turn divided into cantons.
A distinct course of life, action, study, or the like.
A specified aspect or quality.
One of the divisions of instructions
A military subdivision of a country
Act of departing; departure.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Kelly carries the news department.
examples.translation: 凱利主持新聞部門。

examples.text: I'm the youngest in my department.
examples.translation: 在我的單位，我是最年輕的。

examples.text: Please call the fire department.
examples.translation: 請叫消防員。

examples.text: She got out of the taxi at the department store.
examples.translation: 她在百貨公司門前下了的士。

examples.text: Go to the history department or education department.
examples.translation: 去歷史系或者教育系。

examples.text: There is a bookstore in front of the department store.
examples.translation: 百貨商店前有個書店。

etymology.text: From Middle English departement (“ceasing, end”), from Middle French département. Later senses borrowed from Modern French département. Doublet of département.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（departement）「停止、結束」，來自中古法語（département）。後來的詞義借自現代法語（département）。與（département）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: To order (a drug or medical device) for use by a particular patient (under licensed authority).
To specify by writing as a required procedure or ritual; to lay down authoritatively as a guide, direction, or rule of action.
To develop or assert a right; to make a claim (by prescription).
senses.native: 主張權利；提出請求（依據慣例）

senses.definition: To become invalidated or unenforceable by prescription, to lapse
senses.native: 因過期而失效或無法執行

examples.text: The doctor has prescribed you medicine.
examples.translation: 醫生給您開了藥。

examples.text: The dermatologist prescribed me a cream.
examples.translation: 皮膚科醫生給我開了一罐藥膏。

examples.text: I'm going to prescribe some antibiotics.
examples.translation: 我要開一些抗生素。

examples.text: The doctor prescribed two acetaminophen‑caffeine tablets for me.
examples.translation: 醫生給我開了兩粒酚咖片。

examples.text: I was prescribed several prophylactic drugs.
examples.translation: 我接受了幾種預防性藥物治療。

examples.text: If Tom doesn't take the prescribed medicine, his state of health might deteriorate.
examples.translation: 如果湯姆不服用處方藥，他的健康狀況可能會惡化。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin praescrībere, from prae- (“before, in front”) and scrībere (“to write”).
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 praescrībere，由 prae-（「在前」）與 scrībere（「書寫」）組成。

senses.definition: In the nature of a conjecture, or based on a conjecture.

examples.text: Theories about the extinction of dinosaurs are still highly conjectural.
examples.translation: 關於恐龍滅絕的理論至今仍充滿推測成分。

etymology.text: From conjecture + -al.
etymology.native: 由「推測」加上後綴「-al」組成。

senses.definition: A product resulting from a process, event, or course of action.
A solid that exits the liquid phase of a solution.
senses.native: 從溶液中析出的固體（沉澱物）

examples.text: The chemist filtered the precipitate from the solution.
examples.translation: 化學家從溶液中濾出沉澱物。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Latin praecipitātus, perfect passive participle of praecipitō (“throw down, hurl down, throw headlong”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix) for more), from praeceps (“head foremost, headlong”) (praecipit- in its oblique stem), from prae (“before”) + -ceps (“headed”).
etymology.native: 源於拉丁語 praecipitātus，為 praecipitō（拋下、投擲、頭朝下墜落）的完成時被動分詞。

senses.definition: Of or relating to sight; visual.
Designed to assist or enhance sight
Of or relating to optics.
Of or relating to visible light.
Incorporating light-sensitive devices.

examples.text: This is an optical illusion.
examples.translation: 這是一場光學幻覺。

examples.text: It's an optical illusion.
examples.translation: 這是一場光學幻覺。

examples.text: Lenses with two distinct optical powers are also called "bifocals".
examples.translation: 具有兩種不同光學屈光力的鏡片也稱為「雙光鏡」。

examples.text: This looks longer than that, but it is an optical illusion.
examples.translation: 這看起來比那長，但這其實是一場光學幻覺。

examples.text: An optical illusion makes the second object look larger than the first.
examples.translation: 光學幻覺會讓第二個物體看起來比第一個大。

examples.text: The use of optical instruments with this product will increase eye hazard.
examples.translation: 使用此產品的光學儀器會增加眼睛受傷害的風險。

relations.native: 聽眾；大型聆聽或觀看表演、演說等的人群

etymology.text: From optic + -al.
etymology.native: 由「光學」加上後綴「-al」組成。

senses.definition: A site for mining stone, such as limestone, or slate.
An animal, often a bird or mammal, which is hunted.
senses.native: 被獵捕的動物，通常是鳥類或哺乳動物

senses.definition: An object of search or pursuit.
A diamond-shaped tile or pane, often of glass or stone.
senses.native: 菱形地磚或窗格，通常由玻璃或石材製成

senses.definition: A part of the entrails of a hunted animal, given to the hounds as a reward.
senses.native: 獵獲動物的內臟，作為獎勵給獵犬食用

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: I have no quarry with you.
examples.translation: 我對你沒有興趣。

examples.text: He drowned in a quarry.
examples.translation: 他死在採石場裡。

examples.text: There's a rock quarry ten miles west of town.
examples.translation: 鎮西十英里處有一處石礦場。

examples.text: The old quarry is now a popular swimming hole.
examples.translation: 那座舊採石場現在是一個受歡迎的游泳孔洞。

examples.text: There is a rock quarry just north of town.
examples.translation: 鎮北邊有一處石礦場。

examples.text: We used to love to go swimming in the quarry, but it was always a little scary.
examples.translation: 我們過去愛去礦坑游泳，但總覺得有點可怕。

etymology.text: From Middle English quarere, from Medieval Latin quarreria (1266), literally a “place where stones are squared”, from Old French quarrière (compare modern French carrière), from Vulgar Latin *quadraria, from Latin quadrō (“to square”), itself from quadra (“a square”), from quattuor (“four”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kʷetwóres (“four”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 quarere，來自中世紀拉丁語 quarreria（1266 年），字面意思為「將石頭切割成方塊的地方」，源自舊法語 quarrière（比較現代法語 carrière），來自通俗拉丁語 *quadraria，來自拉丁語 quadrō（「切成正方形」），本身來自 quadra（「正方形」），來自 quattuor（「四」），最終源於原始印歐語 *kʷetwóres（「四」）。

senses.definition: To increase in number or spread rapidly; to multiply.

examples.text: We let destitution proliferate.
examples.translation: 我們讓貧窮蔓延。

examples.text: The sentences proliferate like rabbits. But it's good.
examples.translation: 這些句子像兔子一樣大量繁殖，但很好。

examples.text: Anti-Berber racism is proliferating.
examples.translation: 反柏柏爾種族主義正在蔓延。

examples.text: The flowers proliferated rapidly all spring.
examples.translation: 花朵在整個春天迅速大量繁殖。

examples.text: Pizza parlors proliferate in this area.
examples.translation: 披薩店在這個地區大量出現。

examples.text: We must not proliferate nuclear arms.
examples.translation: 我們不得大量製造核武。

etymology.text: Back-formation from proliferation.
etymology.native: 此詞由「proliferation」回削而成。

senses.definition: To restore consciousness, vigor, or life to.
To regain consciousness.

examples.text: The doctors tried to resuscitate Martino.
examples.translation: 醫生試圖讓馬丁諾蘇醒過來。

examples.text: Alberto managed to resuscitate Isabella.
examples.translation: 阿爾貝托成功讓伊莎貝拉蘇醒過來。

examples.text: The attempt to resuscitate Tom failed.
examples.translation: 嘗試讓湯姆蘇醒過來失敗了。

examples.text: Tom has a do-not-resuscitate order.
examples.translation: 湯姆有「不蘇醒」的指示。

examples.text: Can he resuscitate the dead?
examples.translation: 他能讓死者蘇醒嗎？

examples.text: The EMTs are trying to resuscitate Tom.
examples.translation: 急救人員正試圖讓湯姆蘇醒過來。

etymology.text: From Latin resuscitātus, past participle of resuscitō (“to raise up again, revive”), from re- (“again”) + suscitō (“to raise up”), from sub- (“up, under”) + citō (“to summon, rouse”).
etymology.native: 源於拉丁語 resuscitātus，為 resuscitō 的過去分詞（意即「再次抬起」），由 re-（再次）與 suscitō（抬起）組成，後者來自 sub-（上、下）與 citō（召喚、喚醒）。

senses.definition: After the death of someone.
In reference to a work, published after the author's death.
senses.native: 死後發表的、死後出版的

senses.definition: Born after the death of one's father.
Taking place after one's own death.
In reference to a musical opus, published or initially performed after the composer's death.

examples.text: Most of his posthumous fame came from his autopsy results.
examples.translation: 他死後的名聲主要來自於他的屍檢結果。

examples.text: His memoirs were his posthumous revenge on enemies he dared not take on alive.
examples.translation: 他的回憶錄是他對那些他不敢生時對抗的敵人死後的報復。

examples.text: Posthumous orphans never even knew their fathers.
examples.translation: 死後孤兒從未見過他們的父親。

examples.text: A posthumous award.
examples.translation: 一項死後獎項。

examples.text: A posthumous book.
examples.translation: 一本死後出版的書籍。

examples.text: A posthumous daughter.
examples.translation: 一位死後出生的女兒。

etymology.text: From Latin posthumus, a variant spelling of postumus, superlative form of posterus (“coming after”), the ⟨h⟩ added by association with humus (“ground, earth”) referring to burial.
etymology.native: 源於拉丁語 posthumus，由 posterus 演變而來，h 是與 humus（土地）相關聯的拼寫變化。

senses.definition: An elliptical galaxy.
An elliptical trainer.

examples.text: The elliptical is a very powerful tool for developing cardio fitness. Unfortunately, few people know how to actually use it.

etymology.text: From elliptic + -al, from Ancient Greek ἐλλειπτικός (elleiptikós), from ἐλλείπω (elleípō, “I leave out, omit”).
etymology.native: 源自希臘文，意為「遺漏」或「省略」。

senses.definition: To apply tension to an object before some other event or process.
senses.native: 在另一事件或過程發生前對物件施力

senses.definition: To apply tension to reinforcing strands before concrete is poured in.
senses.native: 在澆灌混凝土前對加強鋼絲施力

examples.text: Workers must pretension the cables before use.
examples.translation: 工人必須在使用前對鋼纜施加預張力。

etymology.text: From Middle English pretencioun, pretensioun, from Medieval Latin prētēnsiō.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 pretencioun 或 pretensioun，來自中世紀拉丁語 prētēnsiō。

senses.definition: Of a cave passage, to end in a sump, or to fill completely with water on occasion.
senses.native: 洞穴通道終結於水坑，或偶爾完全被水淹沒

examples.text: We discovered a new passage, but it sumped after 100 metres.
examples.translation: 我們發現了一條新通道，但它在一百公尺處被水淹沒。

examples.text: This low passage sumps quickly after moderate rainfall.
examples.translation: 這條低窪通道在適度降雨後會迅速積水。

etymology.text: From Middle English sompe, either from Middle Dutch somp, sump or Middle Low German sump from Old Saxon *sump, from Proto-West Germanic *sump, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *sumpaz. Doublet of swamp.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 sompe，可能來自中古荷蘭語 somp 或中低地德語 sump，最終源自原始日耳曼語 *sumpaz，與 swamp 同源。

senses.definition: To exclude; to specify as being an exception.
To take exception, to object (to or against).

examples.text: I take a walk every day except when it rains.
examples.translation: 除了雨天我每天都散步。

examples.text: I find most people annoying — present company excepted, of course!

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French excepter, from Latin exceptus.

senses.definition: The act or principle of compensating.
Something which is regarded as an equivalent; something which compensates for loss.
The extinction of debts of which two persons are reciprocally debtors by the credits of which they are reciprocally creditors; the payment of a debt by a credit of equal amount.
A recompense or reward for service.
An equivalent stipulated for in contracts for the sale of real estate, in which it is customary to provide that errors in description, etc., shall not avoid, but shall be the subject of compensation.

The relationship between air temperature outside a building and a calculated target temperature for provision of air or water to contained rooms or spaces for the purpose of efficient heating. In building control systems, the compensation curve is defined to a compensator for this purpose.
The ability of one part of the brain to overfunction in order to take over the function of a damaged part (e.g. following a stroke).

examples.text: You may be entitled to compensation.
Daniel is entitled to compensation.
I promise you every possible compensation.
The US should pay compensation to Vietnam.
Felix's lawyer got him full and fair compensation.
Elias paid a hefty sum of compensation money.

etymology.text: From Middle English compensacioun, from Old French compensacion, from Latin compensātiōnem, accusative singular of compensātiō. Equivalent to compensate + -ion.

senses.definition: A product sold under a generic name.
senses.native: 以通用名稱銷售之產品

senses.definition: A wine that is a combination of several wines, or made from a combination of several grape varieties.
senses.native: 由多種葡萄酒混合而成，或來自多種葡萄品種釀造之酒

senses.definition: A term that specifies neither male nor female.
senses.native: 指既不指男性也不指女性之詞語

senses.definition: The part of a toponym that identifies the feature's type.

examples.text: "What's the generic term for a muppet?" "Puppet?" "Hmmm..."
examples.translation: 「木偶的通用術語是什麼？」 「木偶？」 「嗯……」

etymology.text: From Middle French générique, from Latin genus (“genus, kind”) + -ic.
etymology.native: 源自中法語 générique，由拉丁語 genus（種類）加上 -ic 構成。

senses.definition: To make or become supple.
To make compliant, submissive, or obedient.

examples.text: These boots are not yet suppled by frequent use.
examples.translation: 這雙靴子尚未因頻繁穿著而變得柔韌。

etymology.text: From Middle English souple, from Old French souple, soupple (“soft, lithe, yielding”), from Latin supplic-, supplex (“suppliant, submissive, kneeling”), of uncertain formation. Either from sub + plicō (“bend”) (compare complex), or from sub + plācō (“placate”). More at sub-, placate.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 souple，來自舊法式 souple, soupple（柔軟、輕盈、順從），源自拉丁語 supplic-, supplex（乞求者、服從者、跪著的人）。

senses.definition: To join items together, or to coat them with solder.
To join things as if with solder.
senses.native: 像焊接一樣將事物連接起來

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: I was soldering the pipes.
examples.translation: 我正在焊接水管。

examples.text: Are you soldering?
examples.translation: 你正在焊接嗎？

examples.text: Tom soldered the wires with his soldering iron.
examples.translation: 湯姆用他的焊槍焊接了電線。

examples.text: He hasn't started soldering the electronic components on the printed circuit board yet.
examples.translation: 他尚未開始在電路板上焊接電子元件。

examples.text: I tried to align the pieces of metal perfectly together before soldering them.
examples.translation: 我試著在焊接前將金屬片完美對齊。

examples.text: Modern soldering techniques require precise temperature control for optimal alloy fusion.
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Middle English souder, soudere, soudur (noun), from Old French soldure, soudeure (noun), from Old French souder, solder (“to solder”, verb) (> Middle English souden (“to solder”)), from Latin solidāre (“make solid”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 souder、soudere 或 soudur，來自舊法式 soldure 或 soudeure，再源自舊法式 souder（動詞），最終來自拉丁語 solidāre。

senses.definition: To join two materials (especially two metals) together by applying heat, pressure and filler, either separately or in any combination.
To make something by welding.
To bind together inseparably; to unite closely or intimately.
To wield.

examples.text: Tom welded the two pipes together.
examples.translation: 湯姆將兩根管子焊接在一起。

examples.text: Tom said that he thought Mary knew how to weld.
examples.translation: 湯姆說他認為瑪麗知道如何焊接。

examples.text: You can get good welds with this welder.
examples.translation: 使用這台焊機可以獲得良好的焊接品質。

examples.text: These boxes were made with steel plates welded together.
examples.translation: 這些箱子是用鋼板焊接而成的。

examples.text: Sorry, I can't show you how to weld with your left hand.
examples.translation: 抱歉，我無法用左手示範如何進行焊接。

examples.text: Weld the outer edge to match the one provided on the plate.
examples.translation: 將外邊緣焊接以匹配板上提供的樣式。

etymology.text: From Middle English welde, wolde, from Old English *weald, weard, variant form of wād, Proto-West Germanic *waiʀd, from Proto-Germanic *waizdaz. Alternatively reborrowed from or contaminated by Anglo-Norman wold, wolde (compare Old French guaide). Doublet of woad. Dutch wouw is derived from the same basic form with -l-.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 welde 或 wolde，來自古英語 *weald 等詞，與 woad 同源。

senses.definition: A burst, split, or break.
A social breach or break, between individuals or groups.
A break or tear in soft tissue, such as a muscle.

Cognate with Danish glente, Swedish glänta, Norwegian Nynorsk gletta (“to peep, look”), Middle High German glinzen; compare also Swedish glinta (“to slip, slide, gleam, shine”), Swedish glimt (“flash, glint, glimpse”), Norwegian Ny

examples.text: The nautilus is a mollusk that uses jet propulsion to roam the ocean deep.

examples.text: This is the first time solar propulsion has been successfully demonstrated in Earth's orbit.

examples.text: Researchers at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory raced drones controlled by artificial intelligence (A.I.) against a professional human pilot.
examples.translation: NASA 噴氣實驗室的研究人員讓由人工智慧控制的無人機與專業飛行員進行競賽。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Medieval Latin propulsio, propulsionis, from the past participle of Latin propello (“to drive forward, drive forth, drive away, drive out”).

senses.native: 受詛咒或遭教會權威譴責者

examples.text: That cult makes people believe things that are anathema to them.

examples.text: He is an anathema to me.
examples.translation: 他是我的極度厭惡之物。

examples.text: The teacher said this behavior is anathema in our class.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Late Latin anathema (“curse, person cursed, offering”), itself a borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀνάθεμα (anáthema, “something dedicated, especially dedicated to eternal damnation”), from ἀνατίθημι (anatíthēmi, “to set upon, offer as a votive gift”), from ἀνά (aná, “upon”) + τίθημι (títhēmi, “to put, place”). The Ancient Greek term was influenced by Hebrew חרם (herem), leading to the sense of "accursed," especially in Ecclesiastical writers.
etymology.native: 此詞源自晚拉丁語，本來自古希臘語，後受希伯來語影響而具「被詛咒」之意。

senses.definition: A typically aquatic blood-sucking annelid of the subclass Hirudinea, especially Hirudo medicinalis.
A person who derives advantage from others in a parasitic fashion.
A healer.
The vertical edge of a square sail.
The aft edge of a triangular sail.
A glass tube designed for drawing blood from damaged tissue by means of a vacuum.
A physician.

senses.definition: Characteristic of a burden; arduous or demanding

examples.text: The tax is burdensome for the companies.
examples.translation: 對這些公司來說，稅收相當繁重。

examples.text: I appreciated her kindness, while I feel it burdensome.
examples.translation: 我感激她的善意，但也覺得這令人感到負擔。

examples.translation: 英國本土劃分為四十八個儀式郡。

examples.text: Archeologists have found a Roman ceremonial chariot near Pompeii.
examples.translation: 考古學家在龐貝古城附近發現了一輛羅馬儀式戰車。

etymology.text: From Middle English cerymonial, from Latin caerimōniālis. Morphologically ceremony + -al or -ial.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語，來自拉丁語。由儀式加上詞綴構成。

senses.definition: To season with condiments.
To pickle.

examples.text: The fridge is overloaded with condiments.
examples.translation: 冰箱裝滿了調味品。

examples.text: Return condiments and spices to their designated spots.
examples.translation: 將調味料與香料放回指定位置。

examples.text: Ketchup and mustard are condiments.
examples.translation: 番茄醬與黃芥末是調味料。

examples.text: Spices and condiments should be arranged in an orderly manner.
examples.translation: 香料與調味料應整齊排列。

examples.text: One of the most popular condiments in the U.S. is in short supply thanks to the coronavirus pandemic.
examples.translation: 美國最流行的調味料之一因冠狀病毒疫情而供應短缺。

examples.text: Mustard and ketchup are condiments.
examples.translation: 黃芥末與番茄醬是調味料。

etymology.text: From late Middle English condiment, from Old French condiment, from Latin condimentum, from condīre (“to preserve, pickle, season”). See also condite and compare recondite.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 condiment，來自古法語 condiment，再來自拉丁語 condimentum，意為「保存、醃漬或調味」。

senses.definition: Not allowing sound through.

examples.text: The room windows are not soundproof.
examples.translation: 房間的窗戶沒有隔音效果。

examples.text: These walls aren't soundproof.
examples.translation: 這些牆壁不具備隔音功能。

examples.text: The windows in the rooms are not soundproof.
examples.translation: 房間的窗戶沒有隔音效果。

examples.text: How effective are soundproof windows?
examples.translation: 隔音窗有多有效？

examples.text: The contestant was placed in a soundproof booth so he could not receive help from the audience.
examples.translation: 參賽者被安置在隔音隔間內，以免受到觀眾的干擾。

examples.text: A soundproof room.
examples.translation: 一間隔音室。

etymology.text: From sound + -proof.
etymology.native: 由「聲音」加上「防...」組成。

senses.definition: To make resistant to transmitting sound.

examples.text: We soundproofed our basement and use it as a recording studio.
examples.translation: 我們對地下室做了隔音處理，並用作錄音室。

examples.text: It's a guest room equipped with soundproofing with an emphasis on privacy.
examples.translation: 這是一間配備隔音設施且注重隱私的客房。

examples.text: When my home had an extension built I only had this room fitted with soundproofing and an internal lock.
examples.translation: 當我家擴建時，這間房只裝設了隔音設施和內部鎖。

examples.text: We soundproofed the room so we couldn't hear the road noises; unfortunately we couldn't hear the fire alarm either.
examples.translation: 我們對房間做了隔音處理，這樣就聽不到路過的噪音；不幸的是，也聽不到火警鈴聲。

examples.text: Proust had his apartment soundproofed.
examples.translation: 普魯斯特將他的公寓做了隔音處理。

etymology.text: From sound + -proof.
etymology.native: 由「聲音」加上「防...」組成。

senses.definition: Curved like the inner surface of a sphere or bowl.
Not convex; having at least one internal angle greater than 180 degrees.
senses.native: 非凸形；至少有一個內角大於 180 度

senses.definition: Satisfying the property that all segments connecting two points on the function's graph lie below the function.
senses.native: 滿足函數圖上任意兩點連線皆位於函數下方的性質

senses.definition: Hollow; empty.

examples.text: The bowl of the hat is concave and fits my head.
examples.translation: 帽子的碗狀部分是凹形的，很合我的頭型。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Concave is the antonym of convex.
examples.translation: 凹形是凸形的反義詞。

etymology.native: 源於中古英語 concave，再源自舊法語 concave，最終來自拉丁語 concavus。

senses.definition: A concave surface or curve.
The vault of the sky.
One of the celestial spheres of the Ptolemaic or geocentric model of the world.
senses.native: 托勒密或地心說世界模型中的天體球層之一

senses.definition: An element of a curved grid used to separate desirable material from tailings or chaff in mining and harvesting.
senses.native: 礦業與採收中用於分離有用礦物與廢石的曲線網格元素

senses.definition: An indentation running along the base of a surfboard, intended to increase lift.
senses.native: 衝浪板底部的一道凹槽，用以增加升力

senses.definition: An indented area on the top of a skateboard, providing a position for foot placement and increasing board strength.
senses.native: 滑板頂部的一處凹陷區域，供腳放置並增強板面強度

senses.definition: A playing card made concave for use in cheating.
senses.native: 為作弊而製作的凹形撲克牌

examples.text: You will need a concave lens to take those photos.
examples.translation: 您需要一個凹面鏡來拍攝那些照片。

examples.text: Concave curbs make little sense.
examples.translation: 凹形的路緣石毫無意義。

examples.text: The moon's orbit is always concave toward the sun.
examples.translation: 月球繞太陽的軌道總是朝向太陽呈凹形。

examples.text: In the past, a woman was only attractive if her corset created a concave curve.
examples.translation: 過去，只有當束腰衣創造出凹形曲線時，女性才具有吸引力。

examples.text: Aristotle makes [Fire] to move to the concave of the Moon. - Thomas Salusbury (1661).
examples.translation: 亞里士多德使 [火] 移動至月球的凹面。——湯瑪斯·薩勒斯伯里（1661）。

examples.text: The moon looks concave in this strange photograph tonight.
examples.translation: 今晚這張奇怪的照片中，月亮看起來是凹形的。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Middle English concave, from Old French concave, from Latin concavus.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 concave，再源自舊法語 concave，最終來自拉丁語 concavus。

senses.definition: To render concave, or increase the degree of concavity.
senses.native: 使呈凹形，或增加凹的程度

examples.text: The workers can concave the surface.
examples.translation: 工人可以把表面磨成凹面。

etymology.text: From Middle English concave, from Old French concave, from Latin concavus.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 concave，再源自舊法語 concave，最終來自拉丁語 concavus。

senses.definition: Amazement or horror that confounds the faculties, and incapacitates for reflection; terror, combined with amazement; dismay.

examples.text: I learned with consternation that my fears had come to pass.
examples.translation: 我得知恐懼成真時感到極度震驚。

examples.text: The consternation was general.
examples.translation: 驚恐之情普遍存在。

examples.text: He looked at me with consternation, saying that he must put a comma somewhere.
examples.translation: 他帶著驚恐看著我，說必須加個逗號。

examples.text: Tom looked in consternation at the stain on his shirt.
examples.translation: 他驚恐地看著衣服上的汙漬。

examples.text: The teacher looked at me with great consternation when I failed.
examples.translation: 我考砸時，老師滿臉驚恐地看著我。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: My parents were full of consternation when they found the mess.
examples.translation: 他們發現亂七八糟後，父母充滿驚恐。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From French consternation, from Latin consternātiō. By surface analysis, consternate + -ion.
etymology.native: 源自法語 consternation，再源自拉丁語 consternātiō。字面分析為 consternate 加上 -ion。

senses.definition: The awn of barley or other types of corn.
senses.native: 麥穗或其他類玉米的芒

senses.definition: An ailment; trouble; illness.

examples.text: O what can ail thee, knight-at-arms, alone and palely loitering?

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English eilen, from Old English eġlan, eġlian (“to trouble, afflict”), from Proto-West Germanic *aglijan, from Proto-Germanic *aglijaną (“to trouble, vex”), cognate with Gothic 𐌰𐌲𐌻𐌾𐌰𐌽 (agljan, “to distress”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 eilen，來自古英語 eġlan、eġlian（「困擾、折磨」），源自原始西日耳曼語 *aglijan，來自原始日耳曼語 *aglijaną（「困擾、煩惱」），與哥特語 agljan 同源。

senses.definition: To take the place of; to replace, to supersede.
To uproot, to remove violently.

examples.text: Will artificial intelligence supplant human intelligence?
examples.translation: 人工智慧會取代人類智慧嗎？

examples.text: Islam supplanted Christianity and animism in North Africa.
examples.translation: 伊斯蘭教已取代北非的基督教與萬靈教。

examples.text: Chinese and Korean tourists have supplanted Japanese tourists in the last few years.
examples.translation: 近年來，中國與韓國遊客已取代日本遊客成為主流。

examples.text: The Hawaiian language is threatened with extinction, having been largely supplanted by English.
examples.translation: 夏威夷語面臨滅絕危機，因已被英語大規模取代。

examples.text: Arabic anciently supplanted Ancient Egyptian, both languages belonging to the Afro-Asiatic language family.
examples.translation: 阿拉伯語曾取代古埃及語，兩者同屬亞非語系。

examples.text: Christianity's main connection to Judaism throughout history has been its attempt to eradicate and supplant it.
examples.translation: 基督教歷史上與猶太教的主要連結，在於試圖消滅並取代後者。

etymology.text: From Middle English supplanten, supplaunten, from Old French supplanter, from Latin supplantō (“trip up”), from sub (“from below, under”) + planta (“sole”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 supplanten，來自舊法式 supplanter，再源自拉丁語 supplantō（「絆倒」），由 sub（「從下方」）與 planta（「腳底」）組成。

senses.definition: Having the same or very similar nature, personality, tastes, habits or interests.
Friendly or sociable.
Suitable to one’s needs.
Agreeable to one's disposition.

examples.text: All of our neighbors are congenial individuals and always up for a social gathering.
examples.translation: 我們所有的鄰居都是親切友善的人，總是樂於參加社交聚會。

examples.text: The syncretist, the mystic, the devotee, the puritan, would find a congenial climate in these regions of Asia Minor.
examples.translation: 融合主義者、神秘主義者、信徒、清教徒，在小亞細亞這些地區都能找到合適的氛圍。

examples.text: A congenial atmosphere to work in.
examples.translation: 一個令人愉悅的工作環境。

examples.text: Two congenial spirits united … by mutual confidence and reciprocal virtues.
examples.translation: 兩個性格相投的人因彼此的信任與美德而結合……

examples.text: My new friend is very congenial and makes me feel happy.
examples.translation: 我這位新朋友非常親切，讓我感到快樂。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: We had a congenial time playing games together yesterday.
examples.translation: 昨天我們一起玩游戲度過了一段愉快的時光。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From con- + genial.
etymology.native: 由前綴 con- 與 genial 組成。

Having lost good or desirable qualities; hence also having bad character or habits, base, immoral, corrupt.
senses.native: 品質喪失；故亦指性格或習慣不良、卑鄙或不道德

senses.definition: Having lost functionality in general.

senses.native: 多個定義域元素對應於範圍中的單一元素

senses.definition: Qualitatively different, usually simpler, than typical objects of its class.
senses.native: 質上不同，通常比其類別的典型物件更簡單

senses.definition: Having multiple different (linearly independent) eigenvectors.
senses.native: 擁有多個不同的（線性獨立）特徵向量

senses.definition: Having the same quantum energy level.
senses.native: 具有相同的量子能量層級

examples.text: The cells began to degenerate.
examples.translation: 細胞開始退化。

examples.text: Don't allow your muscles to degenerate.
examples.translation: 不要讓你的肌肉退化。

examples.text: Standards of art are slowly degenerate.
examples.translation: 藝術標準正逐漸退化。

examples.text: Live can so easily degenerate into something sordid and vulgar.
examples.translation: 生活很容易淪為猥瑣粗俗的東西。

examples.text: Cultures in which people refuse to sing in their own language are degenerate cultures.
examples.translation: 拒絕用本國語言唱歌的文化是退化文化。

examples.text: Authorities had initially authorized the march, but reversed themselves on Monday, citing fears it would degenerate into violence.
examples.translation: 當局最初批准了遊行，但於星期一反悔，引用擔心會惡化為暴力的理由。

relations.native: 非退化的（此處依詞根應為未退化，但依上下文對比應指恢復或相反狀態，通常譯為：非退化的）

etymology.text: Learned borrowing from Latin dēgenerātus. See -ate (adjective-forming suffix) for more.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 dēgenerātus 的借詞。請參閱 -ate（形容詞構成綴尾）以獲取更多資訊。

To cause to lose good or desirable qualities.
senses.native: 使喪失良好或理想的品質

examples.translation: 我們之間的東西正在退化。

examples.translation: 會議惡化為一場殘酷的混戰。

examples.text: His condition continued to degenerate even after admission to hospital.
examples.translation: 他的狀況即使在入院後仍持續惡化。

examples.text: Conditions in the slums degenerated.
examples.translation: 貧民窟的情況惡化了。

senses.native: 此植物萃取的黃色色素或染料

etymology.native: 源於中古英語 welde 或 wolde，來自古英語 *weald 等詞，與 woad 同源。
